data.title: Convert register_v3_pool to Result + V3 cascade
data.body:
Same shape as V2 but with `RegisterV3PoolError` (from task 1) and the V3
spec helpers: `validate_v3_sqrt_price(sqrt_price_x96)?`,
`validate_v3_tick(tick)?` (where present on the params),
`validate_v3_fee(fee)?`, `validate_v3_tick_spacing(tick_spacing)?`.

Update non-test callsites (propagate via `?`):
`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs` (V3 register
callsite), `reorg_coordinator.rs`. Update the
`UniswapEngine::register_v3_pool` `#[cfg(test)]` helper to
`.expect("test setup: V3 registration")`, preserving `-> u64`. Grep to
refresh line numbers before editing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `register_v3_pool` returns `Result<u64, RegisterV3PoolError>`; no
  `assert!` remains in the function body.
- All non-test callsites compile (use `?`).
- The `#[cfg(test)]` engine helper preserves `-> u64`.
- Red: tests for `sqrt_out_of_range` (`MAX_SQRT_RATIO` and below
  `MIN_SQRT_RATIO`), `tick_out_of_range`, `fee_too_large`
  (`>= 1_000_000`), and `tick_spacing_out_of_range` assert the typed
  `SpecViolation` variant.
- Green: implementation passes.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot` green
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-bot --all-targets` clean

# 24KNGF — `register_v3_pool → Result` + V3 cascade

## Outcome
`BotState::register_v3_pool` is now `Result<u64, RegisterV3PoolError>`. Four V3 spec validators fire up-front (before the `seed_from_store` snapshot step — `seed_from_store` only overrides `tick_data`/`coverage` and never touches the validated immutable-config / current-state scalars):

- `validate_sqrt_price(params.sqrt_price_x96)` (`TickMath`-bounded `<uint160, MAX_SQRT_RATIO>`)
- `validate_tick(params.tick)` (`int24`, `[MIN_TICK, MAX_TICK]`)
- `validate_v3_fee(params.fee)` (`< 1_000_000`, V3 factory)
- `validate_tick_spacing(params.tick_spacing)` (`[1, 32_767]`)

The `assert!` duplicate-address panic becomes `Err(RegisterV3PoolError::AlreadyRegistered { address })`.

## Cascade
Same shape as MSTAT2 (V2). The `~50 test callsites` went through one of three paths:

- `UniswapEngine::register_v3_pool` `#[cfg(test)]` engine helper: now `self.core.write().register_v3_pool(params).expect("test setup: V3 registration")`, preserving `-> u64`. ~30 test callsites in `uniswap_engine/tests.rs` + 2 in `diagnostic.rs` go through this helper and remain unchanged.
- `BotState::register_v3_pool` direct test calls in `mod.rs` (14), `log_dispatcher.rs` (1), `reorg_coordinator.rs` (1), `uniswap_engine/tests.rs` (1): patched with `.expect("test setup: V3 registration")`. A Python-bracket-walk script handled the multi-line `&RegisterV3PoolParams { ... }` literal form + the helper-defn tail (no trailing `;`) specially.
- PyO3 wrapper `degenbot_python::bot::mod::PyBot::register_v3_pool`: stop-gap `.map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(format!("V3 pool registration failed: {e:?}")))`. The typed `map_register_v3_err` Python exception hierarchy is task **F2EVV6** (it bumps the V3 wrapper, the V2 wrapper, and introduces the shared `PoolRegistrationError` base class all together).

## Red/Green
7 new tests in `bot_core::tests`:
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_duplicate_address_as_already_registered`
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_sqrt_price_at_max_as_spec_violation`
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_sqrt_price_below_min_as_spec_violation`
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_tick_below_min_as_spec_violation`
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_fee_at_max_as_spec_violation`
- `register_v3_pool_rejects_tick_spacing_out_of_range_as_spec_violation`
- `register_v3_pool_accepts_in_spec_params` (green companion at every validator's accept boundary)

## Validation
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot --lib`: 369 (was 362; +7 new), all green.
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-bot --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo fmt -p degenbot-bot -p degenbot_rs --check`: clean.
- `cargo build --example standalone_consumer`: clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`: OK (no `pyo3` in core crates; only the `degenbot-python` wrapper touches `pyo3`).
- `cargo test -p degenbot_rs --test python_integration`: 16/16 green.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -k "register_v3 or v3_pool or v3register"`: 32 passed, 4 skipped.

## Followups
- **F2EVV6** (blocked-by this task): replace the V2 + V3 stop-gap `PyValueError` mappers with the typed `PoolRegistrationError` hierarchy + `map_register_v2_err` / `map_register_v3_err` (mirroring `map_register_v4_err`). The stop-gap surfaces `RegisterV{2,3}PoolError` to Python as an opaque `PyValueError({:?})`; the typed mapper will give Python a class hierarchy to catch against, matching the V4 precedent.
- **RNZQUO** (final audit + ADR note) still gated on K3IICB + F2EVV6.

data.body:
# Dead Python state mirrors cleanup

## Scope
Per transition-guide §2.3 smell #4, several Python state mirrors are candidate
dead weight now that Rust owns pool state. Goal: delete the mirrors once
verified dead (no back-compat layer).

## In-scope
- `src/degenbot/types/state_cache.py` (`StateCache[PoolState]` deque + lock)
- Per-family `*_pool_state.py`: `uniswap/v{2,3,4}_pool_state.py`,
  `curve/stableswap_pool_state.py`, `aerodrome/v2_pool_state.py`,
  `types/abstract/pool_state.py`
- The `release_python_state()` seam in `bot.py` (the hot loop already drops
  these — proof they are scaffolding once Rust owns canonical state)
- Retained parity/equivalence test harnesses vs Rust implementations per
  §4.3 oracle-retirement protocol

## Non-goals
- Migrating a responsibility that is genuinely `stays-python` (I/O, `Fraction`
  display) — only deleting verifiable dead mirrors.
- Breaking the construction-time Python pool objects needed for encoding until
  the encoding epic lands.

## Constraints
- `rg` the symbol's live consumers before deletion; if zero outside the module
  + its own tests, delete. Retain as parity oracle only while unrouted
  (§4.3 — delete with it at cutover).

# Publisher/subscriber → Rust core

## Scope
The pub/sub notification system is pure-Python. Per `AGENTS.md` it is on the
migration path. Goal: a Rust-owned pub/sub core; Python delegates.

## In-scope
- `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py` — `Publisher` / `PublisherMixin` /
  `Subscriber` protocols + `_notify_subscribers`
- Every pool class composing the mixin:
  `uniswap/v{2,3,4}_liquidity_pool.py`, `curve/curve_stableswap_liquidity_pool.py`,
  `aerodrome/pools.py`, `balancer/pools.py`, `balancer/stable_pools.py`
- The `WeakSet` subscriber registry + `AbstractPublisherMessage` shapes
- Consumers of state-change notifications (trackers, builders)

## Rust status
- No Rust pub/sub core exists today.
- The hot loop drops Python pools after `release_python_state()`, so pub/sub is
  *not* on the hot path — but it IS on the construction/discovery path and the
  AGENTS.md vision names it explicitly.

## Non-goals
- Replacing the pump's `tokio::sync::watch` block channel (a different, already
  Rust-owned mechanism).
- Keeping Python-side mirrors of Rust state (the rubric smell #4).

data.title: Phase 0: set WAL + busy_timeout + synchronous=normal on the Python SQLite open path
data.body:
## Body

Prerequisite bug-fix, ships standalone and first. Latent concurrency hazard unrelated to Rust — close it regardless of the migration.

**Problem.** `get_scoped_sqlite_session` (`src/degenbot/database/operations.py`) opens an engine with NO PRAGMAs:
- no `journal_mode` (so a DB not created via `create_new_sqlite_database` sits in default rollback-journal mode — readers block on an active write, `SQLITE_BUSY` with no timeout),
- no `busy_timeout` (a concurrent writer/reader surfaces `SQLITE_BUSY` immediately),
- no `synchronous`.

WAL mode is currently set ONLY at fresh-DB creation (`create_new_sqlite_database:81`, `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`). Existing DBs opened normally never get WAL set by the open path (though a once-set WAL is file-persistent in the header).

**Fix.** In `get_scoped_sqlite_session` (the normal open path) set, on every connection, via SQLAlchemy `connect_args` / `event.listens_for` on `"connect"`:
- `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;`  (idempotent — file-persistent once set, but cheap to re-assert)
- `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;`  (per-connection — must be set every time)
- `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;`  (per-connection)

Use the SQLAlchemy `event.listens_for(Engine, "connect")` pattern so every pooled connection gets the PRAGMAs (not just the first). Do NOT set `query_only` on the Python writer's own connection (it needs to write).

**Non-goals.** No Rust. No cutover. No reader/writer split. Pure hygiene that also de-risks the later hybrid period.

**AC.**
- [ ] `get_scoped_sqlite_session`-opened connections observe WAL + busy_timeout=5000 + synchronous=NORMAL (assert via a test that opens a session and reads the PRAGMAs).
- [ ] `create_new_sqlite_database`'s existing WAL set still passes (no regression — it can keep its explicit set or rely on the shared open path; prefer keeping the canonical assertion there).
- [ ] Existing tests green; no behavior change for single-process usage.
- [ ] Documented one-liner in the open path docstring/concurrency note.

**Why first.** The hybrid read/write period (Rust reader ≠ Python writer) is only safe if BOTH opens honor WAL+busy_timeout. Shipping this Python fix first means the production DBs are WAL-on by the time any Rust read connection touches them.

## Plan / Implementation notes
- Touch ONLY `src/degenbot/database/operations.py` (`get_scoped_sqlite_session`).
- Add a small test asserting the PRAGMAs are set on a normally-opened session.
- TDD: red-green. The setting is a one-event-listener change; the test is the bulk of the value (proves the PRAGMAs survive pooling).

Phase 0 complete. Edited only `src/degenbot/database/operations.py` (`get_scoped_sqlite_session`).

Changes:
- Added `event` to SQLAlchemy imports.
- Registered an `event.listens_for(engine, "connect")` listener that runs on EVERY pooled connection: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`, `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL`. Per-connection PRAGMAs (busy_timeout, synchronous) are re-asserted each connect; WAL is re-asserted (idempotent, file-persistent). Did NOT set query_only (Python path writes).
- Added a concurrency-note docstring on the open path.
- Left `create_new_sqlite_database` untouched (its explicit WAL assertion still holds — no regression).

TDD: wrote failing test first (`tests/database/test_operations.py`) asserting PRAGMAs on a normally-opened session AND that they survive pooling across 3 sequential sessions. Confirmed red (`journal_mode=delete`), then green after the listener.

Tests:
- `tests/database/test_operations.py`: 2 new tests, both green.
- `just test-python` full suite: 3026 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failures.
- `just lint` + `just format`: clean.
- Test properly disposes its engine (no unclosed-connection ResourceWarning contributing to flaky unraisable-warning noise in the full suite).

data.title: Fix: ReserveInitialized must link the GHO token vToken FK (§4.2 divergence #8 — precondition for ULDUAC guard)
data.body:
# Fix: ReserveInitialized must set `aave_gho_tokens.v_token_id` when the asset IS the GHO token

## The divergence (found by U5YIBG §4.2 ReserveInitialized investigation)
The Python's `_process_reserve_initialized_event` (`event_handlers.py:689-698`) links the GHO vToken FK when the new asset's underlying IS the GHO token:
```python
gho_asset = get_gho_asset(session, market)
if asset_address == gho_asset.token.address:
    gho_token_entry = session.scalar(select(AaveGhoToken).where(...))
    gho_token_entry.v_token_id = v_token.id
```

The Rust OMITS this:
- `resolve_reserve_initialized` (`config_dispatch.rs:410`) does NOT take `gho_asset` — it can't compare the underlying against the GHO token address.
- `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn` (`write.rs:1179`) does NOT touch `aave_gho_tokens.v_token_id` (the only `aave_gho_tokens` UPDATEs are the Upgraded clear at `:1286` + the DiscountRateStrategy apply at `:1691`).

## Why DEFECT + why it interacts with ULDUAC
`gho_asset.v_token_address` (the value the ULDUAC discount-dispatch guard compares `decoded.v_token_address` against) is resolved via the `aave_gho_tokens.v_token_id` FK → `erc20_tokens.address` join (`aave.rs:84`: "addresses resolved via the `erc20_tokens` FK joins"). If a fresh ReserveInitialized registers the GHO asset + the FK is never set, `gho_asset.v_token_address` stays `None` → the ULDUAC guard returns `Ok(None)` (skips ALL discount events) for the fresh-init GHO asset. So #8 is a precondition for ULDUAC's guard to function on the fresh-init path — without it, the Rust SILENTLY DROPS all GHO discount config for a freshly-registered GHO asset.

## The fix (resolved placement)
- Thread `gho_asset: Option<&AaveGhoAsset>` (or the resolved GHO token address + gho_token_id) into `resolve_reserve_initialized`.
- After the vToken erc20 row is created (`get_or_create_erc20_token_on_conn`), if the new asset's underlying == the GHO token address, set the FK: `UPDATE aave_gho_tokens SET v_token_id = ? WHERE id = ?` (in `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn` or the resolve fn — mirror the Python's placement).
- Mirror the Python's guard: the FK is set ONLY when `asset_address == gho_asset.token.address`.
- Add `#[cfg(test)]` covering the GHO-asset ReserveInitialized path (the FK is set) + the regular-reserve path (the FK is untouched).

## §4.3 retirement gate
CZM7TI (the retire) MUST NOT delete the Python FK-link until this fix lands. Sequenced: U5YIBG → ULDUAC → this task → CZM7TI.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the regular-reserve path (non-GHO asset) — it's divergence-free.
- The GHO-asset ReserveInitialized identity (parity) test is banked AFTER this fix lands (the #8 fix sets the FK; then the GHO-asset path is byte-identical to the Python).

data.title: Aave writer PyO3 seam: bind get_or_create_* + apply_* + decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap (Sub-step B of AZGJUN/RQXEKH)
data.body:
# Aave writer PyO3 seam — bind `get_or_create_*` + `apply_*` + `decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` (Sub-step B of AZGJUN/RQXEKH)

## Goal
- Land **Sub-step B** of the three-layer cutover for the Aave V3 lending-market DB writers: wrap the 14 already-landed Rust core writer fns in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs` (Sub-step A, RQXEKH) as PyO3 `#[pyfunction]`s in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/`, register them in `c_api.rs`, and add `.pyi` stubs. **No business logic in the binding layer** — pure arg-extraction → GIL release → core call → result wrap (three-layer Sub-step B, ADR-005).

## Context
- **RQXEKH premature close.** Sub-step A landed: `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs` (1,536 lines) exposes the full writer surface (`get_or_create_*` × 7, `apply_*` × 7, `decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap`, `update_erc20_token_metadata`). Re-exported at `degenbot-db/src/lib.rs:70`. **`RQXEKH` was marked `done`, but Sub-steps B + C never landed.** This is one of five sibling tasks (under AZGJUN) that together complete the port.
- **The QJSCA5 precedent to mirror.** The V3/V4 liquidity-updater PyO3 seam (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/liquidity_updater.rs`) is the canonical shape:
  - Module-level `#[pyfunction]`s taking `database_path: PathBuf` (NOT a writer pyclass); the Python shell decodes raw `LogReceipt`s into a `#[pyclass]` event record and delegates.
  - `py.detach()` wraps the DB I/O (no GIL held during the apply loop).
  - The writer uses `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(path)` (`degenbot-db/src/connection.rs:132`) — the write-capable variant of `open` (`query_only` is NEVER set on the write path; SLHSM4 binding #2). The reader (`open`) stays read-only.
- **The two seam homes.** `update_erc20_token_metadata` already lives on `PyBotIo` (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs:236`) taking `database_path`. **Two reasonable shapes for the new bindings** (impl decision):
  1. **Mirror the QJSCA5 precedent:** module-level `#[pyfunction]`s in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/aave.rs` (the existing Aave seam module, currently read-only — extend it). `db_get_or_create_e_mode_category(database_path, market_id, category_id) -> int`, `db_apply_collateral_configuration_changed(database_path, ...)`, etc.
  2. **Co-locate on `PyBotIo`** alongside `update_erc20_token_metadata` (one writer façade). Discouraged: bloats `PyBotIo` with 13 domain methods, breaks the per-domain module convention (`db/aave.rs`, `db/discovery.rs`, `db/liquidity_updater.rs`).
  - **Preferred: option 1** (mirror precedent; keep the writer seam in `db/aave.rs`).
- **TheRpc-coupling carve-out (already handled by the core).** `get_or_create_erc20_token` + `get_or_create_user` would normally need on-chain metadata (name/symbol/decimals / GHO discount). The Rust core fns already take these as caller-supplied `Option` params (Python driver computes them via `raw_call` + passes them in) — `degenbot-db` has no `degenbot-rpc` dep. The PyO3 seam exposes these `Option` params directly; the Python driver stays the RPC authority.
- **Rubric (§2.1).** Hot=warm/bulk (per-block chunk backfill); GIL=held during pure CPU work (the bit-decode + get-or-create lookup are fast but `py.detach()` per the precedent wraps the apply loop); type=int/Address/U256/config-bitmaps (pure typed); I/O=substrate; eco=none. Standalone constraint: `cargo add degenbot` consumers need Aave writes from a Rust crate (the PyO3 seam is the Python-facing half; a standalone Rust consumer calls the core fns directly — already true).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/aave.rs` (extended) gains `#[pyfunction]` wrappers for all 14 Sub-step-A fns:
  - 7 `get_or_create_*` → `db_get_or_create_e_mode_category`, `db_get_or_create_asset_config`, `db_get_or_create_user_collateral_config`, `db_get_or_create_user`, `db_get_or_create_erc20_token`, `db_get_or_create_collateral_position`, `db_get_or_create_debt_position` (signatures mirror `write.rs` args; `Option` params for the RPC-coupling carve-outs).
  - 7 `apply_*` → `db_apply_collateral_configuration_changed`, `db_apply_e_mode_category_added`, `db_apply_emode_asset_category_changed`, `db_apply_asset_collateral_in_emode_changed`, `db_apply_reserve_used_as_collateral`, `db_apply_user_e_mode_set`, `db_apply_price_oracle_updated`, `db_apply_asset_source_updated`.
  - `db_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap(config_bitmap: int) -> dict` (pure CPU — still `py.detach()` for consistency; returns a dict whose keys match the Python `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` oracle 1:1, so callers and the parity test are unchanged).
- [ ] Each `#[pyfunction]` is registered in `c_api.rs` (mirror the `liquidity_updater` registration pattern).
- [ ] `.pyi` stubs added for all 14 under `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi` (signature-complete; mirror the existing `db_apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` style).
- [ ] Each function opens a write handle via `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(&path)` per call (NOT held across calls — matches `liquidity_updater`'s per-call open + the write.rs docstring's "locked connection" model).
- [ ] `py.detach()` wraps the DB I/O (substrate) — no GIL during write apply.
- [ ] **Zero `pyo3` in `degenbot-db`** (the core fns already are; verify with `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` after landing).
- [ ] **No Python cutover in this task** — Sub-step B only. The Python callers in `cli/aave/db_*.py` / `event_handlers.py` keep using the ORM (they're cut over in the sibling C-slice tasks). Add a `tests/test_aave_writer_seam_parity.py` smoke that calls each new pyfunction with fixture args against an in-memory write handle and asserts the row landed (proves the seam works in isolation, not via the Python driver).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (the `write.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` parity is already green; the seam tests are in `tests/rust/` PyO3-wrapped Python tests).
- `just test-rust-python` — the new `tests/test_aave_writer_seam_parity.py` smoke (in-memory `DegenbotDb` opened for writes; each pyfunction round-trips).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — `degenbot-db` stays pyo3-free.
- `just lint-rust` + `just lint-python` (the `.pyi` addition). `just format`.

## Non-goals
- The Rust core (`write.rs`) — Sub-step A, already landed (RQXEKH).
- The Python cutover (`cli/aave/db_*.py`, `event_handlers.py`) — Sub-step C, siblings.
- The `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch — `stays-python` (AZGJUN scope `MPS3U7`).
- The Aave read-back seam (`PyDatabasePositionQuery`) — landed (OKKMG5); this task does NOT touch it (different pyclass, read-only path).
- §4.2 red-green parity against the Python driver — that's the parity-gate sibling; this task's smoke only proves the seam works in isolation.

## Sequencing
- **Unblocks:** the two C-slice siblings (db-shell cut + handler cut) — both wait on the seam landing before they can cut over.
- **Depends on:** none (the core `write.rs` already landed in RQXEKH's Sub-step A).

- [ ] `py.detach()` wraps the DB I/O (substrate) — no GIL during write apply.

- [ ] **No Python cutover in this task** — Sub-step B only. The Python callers in `cli/aave/db_*.py` / `event_handlers.py` keep using the ORM (they're cut over in the sibling C-slice tasks). Add a `tests/test_aave_writer_seam_parity.py` smoke that calls each new pyfunction with fixture args against an in-memory write handle and asserts the row landed (proves the seam works in isolation, not via the Python driver).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (the `write.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` parity is already green; the seam tests are in `tests/rust/` PyO3-wrapped Python tests).
- `just test-rust-python` — the new `tests/test_aave_writer_seam_parity.py` smoke (in-memory `DegenbotDb` opened for writes; each pyfunction round-trips).

## Non-goals

- The Python cutover (`cli/aave/db_*.py`, `event_handlers.py`) — Sub-step C, siblings.
- The `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch — `stays-python` (AZGJUN scope `MPS3U7`).
- The Aave read-back seam (`PyDatabasePositionQuery`) — landed (OKKMG5); this task does NOT touch it (different pyclass, read-only path).
- §4.2 red-green parity against the Python driver — that's the parity-gate sibling; this task's smoke only proves the seam works in isolation.

## Sequencing
- **Unblocks:** the two C-slice siblings (db-shell cut + handler cut) — both wait on the seam landing before they can cut over.
- **Depends on:** none (the core `write.rs` already landed in RQXEKH's Sub-step A).
---

## Role shift — 2026-07-04 (re-scope to mirror run_pool_update)

The per-fn cutover plan this seam was built for is **abandoned** (two-writer
hazard — see RQXEKH body). This task stays `done` and committed (commit
`67d009c3`), but its role shifts:

- **NOT the cutover path.** The 14 pyfunctions each open
  `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(database_path)` per call + commit immediately —
  a second writer on the SQLite file while the `aave_update` driver's
  SQLAlchemy session holds an open mid-chunk transaction. Unsafe for the
  cutover; fine for single-threaded parity cross-check (no concurrent session).
- **Building-block source:** task `CXRGX4` extracts `_on_conn` free-function
  variants from the `write.rs` `&self` methods these pyfunctions wrap. The

data.title: DB updater atomicity hardening: restore single-transaction chunk invariant
data.body:
## Goal

The pool updater's chunk loop has a **correctness regression** vs `main`: the "process complete chunk before commit" atomicity invariant was shattered during the migration of writes into the Rust core. Restore (and enforce structurally) a single-transaction-per-chunk so that an interrupt mid-chunk rolls the whole chunk back atomically — leaving `last_update_block` and the committed pool/liquidity data consistent.

## Background — the regression

On `main`, the chunk loop (`src/degenbot/cli/pool.py`) open was a **single atomic transaction**:
- One shared SQLAlchemy `session` threaded through every update call.
- Updaters did `session.add(...)` / `session.execute(...)` — never `commit()`.
- The `last_update_block` stamp was a dirty ORM attribute on the same session — uncommitted until chunk end.
- **One `session.commit()` at chunk end** durably persisted pool rows + liquidity updates + the stamp together. Ctrl-C mid-chunk → the whole transaction rolled back → `last_update_block` still pointed at the previous chunk end → restart re-processed the chunk cleanly with no duplicates.

In the current tree, the inner calls were migrated to the Rust core without preserving this invariant:
- `db_upsert_v3_pools` / `db_upsert_v2_pools` / `db_upsert_v4_pools` open their **own** connection via `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes`, and `upsert_v3_pools` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/discovery.rs`) does **per-row autocommit `execute()` with no `transaction()` wrapper** — pool rows are durable immediately, mid-chunk, on a separate connection from the stamp.
- `db_apply_v3_liquidity_updates` / `db_apply_v4_liquidity_updates` — separate connection again.
- `db_set_exchange_last_update_block` — separate connection again.
- The `session.commit()` on the Python side now only commits whatever the SQLAlchemy session still owns (the stamp, partially), while the pool writes were already committed by Rust earlier.

**Consequence:** pool writes and the `last_update_block` stamp live in separate transactions on separate connections. An interrupt in the gap between "Rust commits the pools" and "Rust commits the stamp" → pools durably present, stamp stale → restart refetches the same `PoolCreated` events → `UNIQUE constraint failed: pools.address, pools.chain`. Worse: the `last_update_block` ground truth no longer actually bounds the committed pool data — this is a **correctness regression**, not just a duplicate-insert annoyance.

User-observed symptom: `uv run degenbot pool update` interrupted around block 12M, restarted → `ValueError: sqlite error: UNIQUE constraint failed: pools.address, pools.chain`.

## Scope

Restoring the invariant in a way that is **structurally enforced** (not just convention) and consistent with ADR-005 (Rust owns the writes; Python is a thin shell). The chunk's writes — pool upserts, liquidity updates, `last_update_block` stamp — must be a single SQLite transaction. An interrupt rolls back the whole chunk. Restart is idempotent.

This epic includes: (1) the research/invariant write-up that pins down the exact contract + names the approach; (2) the implementation tasks derived from that research.

## Out of scope

- Auto-heal-on-open (ADR-011 non-goals).
- The broader "move all DB interaction into Rust" program — only the pool updater chunk path is in scope here.
- Performance work unrelated to correctness.

data.title: CLI DB I/O migration to Rust core (Alembic retained through 0.6.x)
data.body:
# CLI DB I/O migration to the Rust core (Alembic retained through 0.6.x)

Migrate the remaining CLI database I/O — the `exchange activate/deactivate`
write path — to route through the Rust core (`degenbot-db` + PyO3 seams),
and build + prove the schema-cutover mechanism that lets a production
Alembic-stamped DB cross from Alembic ownership into Rust ownership. Alembic
and `src/degenbot/migrations/` are **retained through the 0.6.x point
releases** so that `pip` users can upgrade a stale database through the final
Alembic revision; dropping the Alembic dependency and retiring the legacy
conversion is gated to a **0.7 release** (tracked as a blocked placeholder
task here, executed in a later epic).

## Non-goals

- **Aave CLI write path** (`aave extract`, activate, the `db_*` helpers in
  `src/degenbot/cli/aave/`). Scoped to a separate epic — it needs new
  Aave-row Rust substrate that does not exist yet.
- **Aave CLI reads** (`position show` / `market show` / `risk`), which already
  delegate to the existing `PyDatabasePositionQuery` read seam, stay as-is.
- **`pool update` residual ORM reads** (`active_chains`, `active_exchanges`
  SELECT, the V4 `pool_manager_in_db` lookup). These are loop-orchestration
  reads that do not cross the staleness boundary fixed by the
  `db_fetch_exchange` ground-truth readback. Disposition: **stays-python**.
  Do not "migrate" them — they are not on the critical write path.
- **0.7 retirement execution.** The actual deletion of the Alembic
  dependency, `src/degenbot/migrations/`, the `ALEMBIC_HEAD` constant, and
  the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `ensure_schema` happens in 0.7,
  not in this epic. This epic only *builds and proves* the cutover path.

## Constraints

- **Alembic must stay live and shippable through 0.6.x.** No task in this
  epic (other than the 0.7-gated placeholder) may delete or stub
  `src/degenbot/migrations/`, remove the `alembic` or `sqlalchemy`
  dependency from `pyproject.toml`, delete `DatabaseSessionManager`, or
  remove the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `migrate.rs::ensure_schema`.
- **The Rust core never writes schema to an Alembic-stamped DB.** The
  `query_only=on` invariant on the `AlembicCurrent` path is preserved.
- **The cutover is opt-in during 0.6.x** via an explicit
  `degenbot database cutover` command. Automatic cutover-on-open is a 0.7
  concern, not built here. Rationale: an unannounced schema-ownership flip
  on first open is a surprising, hard-to-rollback action for a production
  DB; an explicit command lets users cutover deliberately, and lets the
  pytest exercise the full boundary deterministically.
- **Standalone-Rust constraint (AGENTS.md).** Anything a
  `cargo add degenbot` consumer needs to build an MEV bot must live in a
  core crate. The `upsert_exchange` / `set_exchange_active` /
  `upsert_pool_manager` / `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned` functions belong
  in `degenbot-db`, not the PyO3 wrapper.

## Key decisions (resolved during planning)

1. **Aave write path excluded** — separate epic (new Aave Rust substrate).
2. **Two end-states, version-gated.** During 0.6.x the DB stays
   Alembic-stamped; the Rust core reads Alembic-owned tables via
   `query_only=on`. The 0.7 release retires Alembic (drops dep +
   `migrations/` + `ALEMBIC_HEAD` + the `alembic_version` branch) after a
   production cutover release has given every pip user a path across the
   boundary.
3. **Cutover is opt-in via `degenbot database cutover`** during 0.6.x (see
   Constraints). The pytest proves the full boundary; production execution
   is a human decision.
4. **Documentation surfaces: ADR-010, top-level `AGENTS.md`, the epic body
   you are reading, and a pytest that migrates a stale Alembic-tagged DB
   through the cutover boundary.**

## Forbidden-until-0.7 kill list (guard against premature removal)

No task before the 0.7-gated retirement placeholder may touch any of:

- `src/degenbot/migrations/` (the Alembic migration scripts)
- the `alembic` and `sqlalchemy` entries in `pyproject.toml`
  `[project.dependencies]`
- `DatabaseSessionManager` and the SQLAlchemy `models/` package
- the `ALEMBIC_HEAD` constant in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`
- the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `migrate.rs::ensure_schema`
- the `DegenbotDb::open` `query_only=on` setting on the `AlembicCurrent` path

An implementing agent that sees these imports fall out of use mid-epic MUST
leave them in place and note them in the task completion summary; removal is
exclusively the 0.7 retirement task's responsibility.

## Goal
Render per-candidate `[sim-fail]` lines from `outcome.failures`, surfacing path_id + path_type + bucket + fail_index + the decoded revert + a hop token summary.

data.title: Goal
data.body:
## Body
New module `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/heal.rs`, re-exported from `ops.rs` + `lib.rs`. **Zero `pyo3`** (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`).

## The 7-step operation (owned by `heal_database`)
1. **Inspect** old DB state (read-only open). If `rust_owned`, no-op → return `already_rust_owned`. If unrecognized (no `alembic_version` AND no `_degenbot_db_schema_version` AND tables present but not the degenbot schema) → `DbError::UnrecognizedSchema`.
2. **Build** fresh DB at a temp path via `db_create_new_database` (the coherent head schema — same primitive `create_new_sqlite_database` uses).
3. **Copy** all rows old → new, table-by-table in **FK-dependency order** (parents before children): `erc20_tokens` → `exchanges` → `pool_managers` → `pools` → subclass tables (`uniswap_v2_pools`, `aerodrome_v2_pools`, …) → `liquidity_positions` → `initialization_maps` → `managed_pool_*` → aave tables → …. Order derived from FOREIGN KEY declarations in the head schema (static topological sort, a Rust constant in `heal.rs`).
4. **Apply column mapping** per table (see below), **preserving PK `id` values** so FK references survive.
5. **Reset `sqlite_sequence`** to max copied id per table (autoincrement continues correctly post-heal).
6. **Stamp** new DB `RustOwned` directly. Do NOT stamp Alembic head on the heal path (skip that step of `db_create_new_database`, or drop `alembic_version` before stamping — cleaner to skip). No `alembic_version` table on the new DB.
7. **Verify** per-table row counts: old read count == new read count. Refuse swap on mismatch → `DbError::HealVerificationFailed`.
8. **Atomic swap**: `rename(new, live)`; preserve old as `*.bak` (`rename(old, old.bak)` — or copy first if the temp path is on a different filesystem so rename isn't atomic). On any failure mid-heal, live DB untouched; clean up partial new file.

## Column-mapping auto-derivation (NOT a hand-maintained 43-entry constant)
Derive at heal-time from `PRAGMA table_info(old)` vs `PRAGMA table_info(new db_create_new_database)`. Three action classes:
- **Added-after** (column on new, absent on old): fill with column default / NULL.
- **Renamed** (column on old under name X, on new under name Y): map the read. Disambiguated via an explicit `RENAME_OVERRIDES: &[(table, old_col, new_col)]` constant covering the rename migrations (`6a77c4e07151` rename_column, `a4f59783919f` rename_pool_hash_column, `5c8805573ab3` convert_pool_hash_to_text type-change). Consult migration history ONLY for this disambiguation.
- **Dropped** (column on old, not on new): ignore the read.

Auto-derivation survives future head-schema drift; the constant is small and explicit.

## `HealReport`
```rust
pub struct HealReport {
    pub old_state: SchemaState,       // alembic_current | alembic_stale | rust_owned
    pub rows_copied: HashMap<String, u64>,
    pub bak_path: PathBuf,
```

data.title: Rust standalone BalanceTransfer ignores paired BT scaled amount
data.body:
## Goal

`dispatch_balance_transfer` (rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/transaction_processor.rs:528ish) previously iterated the op's `scaled_events` (= the ERC20 CollateralTransfer event, no index) and dispatched a `ScaledTokenTransfer` chunk event using the ERC20's UNDERLYING amount as `scaled_amount` with `transfer_index = 0`. The Python oracle instead pairs the ERC20 with its BalanceTransfer (BT) event (already in `op.balance_transfer_events: Vec<&'a Log>`) and uses the BT's value (the SCALED balance moved) + the BT's index — see Python's `_match_paired_balance_transfer` in src/degenbot/cli/aave/transfers.py.

## Impact (silent wrong-value divergence → crash once balances mismatch)

* At liquidity_index =RAY (= 1.0), scaled == underlying, so this is invisible — the existing YUPSIB parity fixture (`test_standalone_transfer_then_withdraw_parity.py`) passed both pre- and post-NMWPI6 because of this RAY=1.0 coincidence.
* On mainnet (liquidity_index != 1.0), the standalone Transfer's debit was `underlying = scaled * index / RAY` (slightly larger than the position's credited scaled balance). This eventually exceeded the position balance -> crash `balance would go negative` at chunk 16491071-16501070 (block 16498232, position id=29; balance 10999704962418970004, delta -11000000547837008734).
* Surfaced only after NMWPI6 fixed the upstream supply word-extraction bug; previously masked because the user-as-int credit vastly exceeded any realistic Transfer delta (no wrong-side crash possible).

## Why YUPSIB + NMWPI6 alone didn't catch this

* YUPSIB (the deficit_coverage scavenger) was about whether the standalone op got created at all. The op WAS getting created correctly post-YUPSIB.
* NMWPI6 was about Supply/Borrow pool-event word extraction (word1 not word0). Different code path.
* This bug is in the standalone Transfer op's dispatch path (`dispatch_balance_transfer`), independent of YUPSIB / NMWPI6; the RAY=1.0 parity fixture couldn't see it because scaled == underlying.

## Python reference

`src/degenbot/cli/aave/transfers.py::_match_paired_balance_transfer`:
- For each standalone BalanceTransfer op, iterates `op.balance_transfer_events` (the paired BT Logs).
- Matches by `bt_token == token_address && bt_from == scaled_event.from_address && bt_to == scaled_event.target_address`.
- Decodes BT.data via `abi_decode(["uint256", "uint256"])` -> (scaled_amount, index).
- Returns (matched_event, scaled_amount, transfer_index).

`_process_collateral_transfer` (transfers.py:122):
- For the ERC20 CollateralTransfer event: skips if its logIndex matches an entry in `op.balance_transfer_events` (handled by the BT).
- For the BalanceTransfer scaled event: calls `_match_paired_balance_transfer` + uses the BT's scaled_amount + transfer_index.
- Effectively BOTH events in the op trace through `_process_operation`'s for-loop, but `_should_skip_collateral_transfer` drops the BalanceTransfer scaled (index-set) event when paired; only the ERC20 (index=None) event flows, with the BT's scaled_amount+index.

The Rust port collapsed both into `dispatch_balance_transfer` iterating `op.scaled_events` (= ERC20 only) — applying the ERC20's underlying + transfer_index=0 because the BT Log wasn't being decoded.

## Fix

In `dispatch_balance_transfer`, decode each standalone BalanceTransfer op's paired BT Log via a new `decode_balance_transfer_log` helper (returns `(from, to, token, value, index)`). Match against the ERC20 event by `token_address + from_address + target_address` (mirrors the Python semantic match). Override the chunk event's `scaled_amount` + `transfer_index` to the BT's value/index when paired; fall back to the ERC20 underlying + index 0 when not paired (the pre-fix behavior — shouldn't happen since `create_transfer_operations` always pairs an ERC20 with its BT when a match exists).

A new `override_transfer_with_paired_bt` helper applies the override on the `ScaledTokenTransfer` chunk event returned by `build_scaled_event_chunk_event` (which still resolves from-/to-position ids correctly).

## Test plan (Red/Green)

RED-first: extend the existing parity fixture `test_standalone_transfer_then_withdraw_parity.py` with a `2x-ray` parameter variant (liquidity_index = 2 * _RAY). At non-RAY index, the standalone Transfer's ERC20 underlying = 2 * _AMOUNT but the position holds only _AMOUNT (scaled balance credited by the Mint). Pre-fix: balance goes -1*_AMOUNT -> crash. Post-fix: dispatch_balance_transfer uses the BT's scaled amount (= _AMOUNT) -> SENDER end-state 0.

Fix the fixture's `value` semantics for Mint + Burn events: they are in UNDERLYING units (`amounts_match` checks `Mint.value - balance_increase == Supply.pool_amount`). The BT event's `value` IS the SCALED balance moved (per Aave V3 spec).

GREEN regression guards:
* parameterized parity test (`ray` + `2x-ray` variants) — both pass after the fix.
* the existing `ray` variant continues to pass (it was the only thing the existing YUPSIB parity could do at RAY=1.0 — it doesn't catch this class).
* Re-drive `--to-block 17000000` (the cold-boot gate): the chunk 16491071-16501070 no longer crashes.

## Out of scope

* Liquidation collateral transfers: the Python `_should_skip_collateral_transfer` ALSO has special handling for LIQUIDATION ops (skips ERC20, processes CollateralTransfer scaled). The Rust `dispatch_liquidation` handles those separately — not touched by this fix.
* The cold-boot path HLYWI6's broader balance correctness revisit — re-drive past the new fix to 17M as the next milestone before re-evaluating.

data.title: PyO3 PyChainlinkPriceFeed/PyAavePriceOracle seam; convert ChainlinkPriceContract/OraclePriceFetcher/Erc20Token.price to delegating shells
data.body:
## Goal
- Add a PyO3 seam (`#[pyclass] PyChainlinkPriceFeed` + `#[pyclass] PyAavePriceOracle` in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/oracle/` or `price/`) over the new `degenbot-price` core crate (sibling task), and convert the Python `ChainlinkPriceContract` (`src/degenbot/chainlink/price_feed.py`) and `OraclePriceFetcher` (`src/degenbot/aave/analysis/orchestrator.py`) into delegating shells. `Erc20Token._price_oracle`/`price` (`src/degenbot/erc20/erc20.py`) routes through the Rust `PyChainlinkPriceFeed`.

## Context
- Scope task: `XS57NO` (Epic `VNNYI6`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (PyO3 seam + Python cutover, rubric §3 B+C).
- §2.1: thin translator (extract args → `py.detach()` the RPC `eth_call` → wrap typed return). The Python `ChainlinkPriceContract`/`OraclePriceFetcher` shells retain their public API (`price` property, `fetch(asset_addresses)`) so callers (`Erc20Token.price`, `PositionAnalysisService.analyze_market`) are unchanged.
- `chainlink/CONTEXT.md` already notes the architecture debt: `ChainlinkPriceContract` reads `self._bot.provider` directly instead of receiving a `ProviderAdapter`/`PoolIO` — this cutover fixes that by routing through the Rust `Contract` (which holds the `AlloyProvider`).
- Deps: sibling `degenbot-price` core crate. The oracle address consumed by `AavePriceOracle` comes from `PositionQuery.get_oracle_address` — once `OKKMG5` (Epic `AZGJUN`) lands, that's a Rust call; until then the Python shell passes the resolved address in. NO hard cross-epic edge.
- KEY DISTINCTION: this task ports the MECHANISM's PyO3 surface. The CONSUMER valuation orchestration (`PositionAnalysisService`, path-ranking) stays-python (sibling task).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `#[pyclass] PyChainlinkPriceFeed { address, chain_id }` with `decimals`/`latest_round_data`/`price` mirroring `ChainlinkPriceContract`'s properties; `#[pyclass] PyAavePriceOracle { oracle_address }` with `fetch(asset_addresses) -> dict[Address,int]` matching `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch`'s shape + tolerant error handling. Registered in `c_api.rs`; `py.detach()` for the RPC I/O.
- Python `ChainlinkPriceContract` (and `chainlink/__init__.py`) delegates to `PyChainlinkPriceFeed`; the inline `provider.call_raw`/`abi_decode` bodies deleted. `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch` delegates to `PyAavePriceOracle`; the inline `raw_call`/`encode_function_calldata` loop deleted.

- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`tests/test_chainlink_price_feed.py`, `tests/erc20/test_erc20_token.py`, Aave analysis suite), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

- The `degenbot-price` core crate (sibling task).
- The Aave valuation CONSUMER (`PositionAnalysisService.analyze_market`, `core.py` calc) — stays-python (sibling task).
- Reading the `price_source` DB column (Epic `AZGJUN`/`OKKMG5`) — this seam takes the resolved oracle `Address` as an arg.
- Path-ranking by USD value / solver USD valuation — consumer concern.

data.title: Decision: reconcile stk_aave_balance underflow divergence (Rust strict-error+chunk-rollback vs Python permissive/negative)
data.body:
# Decision: reconcile the stk_aave_balance underflow divergence

## Origin
Surfaced by S3X2I2 (consistent with YMWN5V's Redeem apply). Pre-existing since YMWN5V; not introduced by S3X2I2.

## The divergence
- **Python** `process_stk_aave_transfer_event` / the Redeem handler: `assert from_user.stk_aave_balance >= 0` BEFORE the decrement, then applies — allows `stk_aave_balance` to go NEGATIVE (Python int, no underflow check on the apply itself).
- **Rust** `apply_stk_aave_redeem_on_conn` (YMWN5V, `write.rs:1880`) + `apply_stk_aave_transfer_on_conn` from-leg (S3X2I2, `write.rs:1957`): use `checked_sub(amount)` → returns `DbError` on underflow (amount > balance).

## The error-handling (why this matters beyond "stricter-correct")
The `checked_sub` error propagates via `ok_or_else` → `?` in the chunk loop (`run.rs:1274`/`1295` `apply_chunk_events_on_conn(...)?`) → the chunk transaction ROLLS BACK (the §3.4 `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn_rolls_back_on_injected_failure` test at `run.rs:1417` confirms). So a single Redeem/Transfer exceeding the tracked `stk_aave_balance` **fails the ENTIRE chunk → the bot stalls at that chunk** (can't advance).

## Why it's a CZM7TI blocker (per the user's principle: Rust must match Python before retirement)
Retiring the Python writer (CZM7TI) removes the permissive fallback. If the tracked `stk_aave_balance` ever drifts below the true balance (missed event, bad seed, reorg), a legitimate subsequent Redeem/Transfer would FAIL THE WHOLE CHUNK in the Rust (strict) where the Python would have continued (permissive, going negative). Post-CZM7TI, there's no Python fallback → the bot stalls.

NOTE: the Rust's strict-error is ALREADY live (post-YMWN5V). The stall risk exists NOW, not just post-CZM7TI. But CZM7TI removing the Python fallback makes it irrecoverable. So the reconciliation must land before CZM7TI retires the Python.

## The parity-test lens
The byte-IDENTITY parity tests (YMWN5V + S3X2I2) SIDESTEP the underflow by pre-seeding `from_balance >= amount` (so amount <= balance → no underflow → both agree). The divergence is in the UNEXERCISED edge case (amount > balance). The Python is "confirmed correct (replicates all positions deployment→tip)" — if drift never happens in practice (which the Python's confirmed-correctness implies), the underflow case is theoretical. But the Rust's stall-on-theoretical-case is a real production risk if drift EVER occurs.

## Options (user decision required)
- **(A) Allow signed balances in Rust (mirror the Python).** `stk_aave_balance` becomes a signed value (or the apply uses allow-negative semantics); the apply mirrors the Python's permissive behavior. Byte-IDENTITY even in the underflow case → no divergence → no stall risk. **Pro:** faithful to "match the Python" (the confirmed-correct reference); smallest code change. **Con:** masks state-sync drift (a silent wrong balance propagates through the analysis pipeline — the position-risk healthfactor calc reads these rows; the U5YIBG body explicitly warns about "silent state drift").
- **(C) Root-cause no-drift + keep strict-error.** Fix the state-sync so the tracked balance NEVER drifts (robust re-sync on startup, reorg handling, seed validation). Then strict-error never fires on legitimate events → parity maintained for all real events + the strict-error surfaces genuine bugs. **Pro:** preserves the Rust's stricter-correct behavior (surfaces drift rather than masking); no silent wrong balances. **Con:** big robustness investment; the divergence theoretically persists for the impossible-but-not-guaranteed-impossible drift case.

(Dropped (B) log+skip — it BREAKS parity: Rust skips the event, Python applies-and-goes-negative → not byte-identical. Not a parity-preserving option.)

## Recommendation
Lean (A) for faithfulness to "the Python is the confirmed-correct reference" + smallest change (mirror the Python's permissive behavior → byte-IDENTITY even in the edge case). The drift-masking concern is real but SECONDARY to the user's stated principle (Rust must match Python). If the user prioritizes "stricter-correct surfaces bugs" over "byte-IDENTITY with the reference," (C) is the alternative — but it's a much bigger investment + doesn't fully eliminate the theoretical divergence.

- If (A): `stk_aave_balance` allow-negative in the Rust apply fns (Redeem + Transfer from-leg); byte-IDENTITY parity test extended to exercise the underflow case (amount > balance → both go negative, match). - Do NOT change the Staked/Redeem/Transfer dispatch wiring (YMWN5V/S3X2I2 settled).
- Do NOT re-litigate the per-tx apply (GJQGKN settled).

## The parity-test lens

The divergence is in the UNEXERCISED edge case (amount > balance). But the Rust's stall-on-theoretical-case is a real production risk if drift EVER occurs.

## Options (user decision required)
- **(A) Allow signed balances in Rust (mirror the Python).** `stk_aave_balance` becomes a signed value (or the apply uses allow-negative semantics); the apply mirrors the Python's permissive behavior. Byte-IDENTITY even in the underflow case → no divergence → no stall risk. **Pro:** faithful to "match the Python" (the confirmed-correct reference); smallest code change. **Con:** masks state-sync drift (a silent wrong balance propagates through the analysis pipeline — the position-risk healthfactor calc reads these rows; the U5YIBG body explicitly warns about "silent state drift").
- **(C) Root-cause no-drift + keep strict-error.** Fix the state-sync so the tracked balance NEVER drifts (robust re-sync on startup, reorg handling, seed validation). Then strict-error never fires on legitimate events → parity maintained for all real events + the strict-error surfaces genuine bugs. **Pro:** preserves the Rust's stricter-correct behavior (surfaces drift rather than masking); no silent wrong balances. **Con:** big robustness investment; the divergence theoretically persists for the impossible-but-not-guaranteed-impossible drift case.

(Dropped (B) log+skip — it BREAKS parity: Rust skips the event, Python applies-and-goes-negative → not byte-identical. Not a parity-preserving option.)

## Recommendation
Lean (A) for faithfulness to "the Python is the confirmed-correct reference" + smallest change (mirror the Python's permissive behavior → byte-IDENTITY even in the edge case). The drift-masking concern is real but SECONDARY to the user's stated principle (Rust must match Python). If the user prioritizes "stricter-correct surfaces bugs" over "byte-IDENTITY with the reference," (C) is the alternative — but it's a much bigger investment + doesn't fully eliminate the theoretical divergence.

## Acceptance criteria
- User decides (A) or (C).
- If (A): `stk_aave_balance` allow-negative in the Rust apply fns (Redeem + Transfer from-leg); byte-IDENTITY parity test extended to exercise the underflow case (amount > balance → both go negative, match). Gates: `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `uv run pytest tests/aave/writer_parity/ -q`.
- If (C): robustness plan (re-sync, reorg, seed validation) — separate scoping.
- Resolves the divergence → unblocks CZM7TI (modulo its other deps).

## Sequencing
This task → CZM7TI (hard blocker: retiring the Python writer before this is reconciled = the Rust's strict-error could stall the bot on a drift, with no Python fallback).

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the Staked/Redeem/Transfer dispatch wiring (YMWN5V/S3X2I2 settled).
- Do NOT re-litigate the per-tx apply (GJQGKN settled).


## Resolution (user decision — RESOLVED, NO code change)

The user ruled: "a negative token balance is nonsensical. You may constrain the value to an unsigned Rust integer type like Alloy's U256 or similar. If a balance ever went negative that would be a terrible on-chain bug, simulating it would be the least of my concerns."

**Disposto: the Rust is ALREADY correct; the Python's permissive (signed `BigInteger`, allows-negative) behavior is a bug to NOT replicate. No reconciliation code change needed.**

Verification of the Rust's current behavior (no change required):
- The DB column `stk_aave_balance VARCHAR(78)` stores a decimal string of a U256.
- The Rust apply fn (`write.rs:1855` Redeem, `:1957` Transfer from-leg) reads it via `parse_decimal_u256` → `alloy::primitives::U256` (**unsigned**). A negative string would fail to parse (a leading `-` isn't a valid decimal digit) → the Rust can't even READ a negative balance.
- `checked_sub(amount)` on U256 → `DbError` on underflow (amount > balance) → the chunk transaction rolls back (§3.4 atomicity). It NEVER writes a negative.

The underflow-stall (chunk rollback on a catastrophic bug) is ACCEPTABLE — surfacing a catastrophic bug by stopping is the correct behavior.

So: no `stk_aave_balance` type change, no parity-test extension to exercise the underflow case, no signed-balance mirroring. The Rust's existing unsigned-U256 + checked_sub + chunk-rollback-on-underflow is the canonical-correct behavior. CZM7TI's blocker is cleared.

data.title: Divergence: ScaledTokenTransfer exceeds position balance (cluster shape, position 534)
data.body:
## Goal

After NMWPI6 (Supply/Borrow word-extraction fix) + 3MF5QM (standalone BalanceTransfer paired-BT scaled amount fix), the re-drive gets past chunk 16491071-16501070 (which held 16591170 last_update_block) and crashes 10 chunks later at chunk 16591071-16601070, position_id=534:

    balance would go negative (current=15826501534688837001, delta=-49735362329328235679)

Load-bearing observation: position_id=534's committed balance at last_update_block=16591070 (= with BOTH fixes already in effect when the chunks 16491071-16591070 committed) is 1.58*10^19 — realistic, not the user-as-int (~10^57) shape from pre-NMWPI6.

## Diagnostic trace (chunk 16591071-16601070 events around the crash)

    APPLY: ScaledTokenBurn { position: Debt, position_id: 219, balance_delta: -76379275788, ... }
    APPLY: ScaledTokenMint { position: Collateral, position_id: 534, balance_delta: 0, new_index: 1000594386508061719492494478 }
    APPLY: ScaledTokenTransfer { from_position_id: 534, to_position_id: 138,
                                 scaled_amount: 49735362329328235679,
                                 transfer_index: 1000594386508061719492494478 }
    NEGDBG: position_id=534 delta=-49735362329328235679 current=15826501534688837001 new=-33908860794639398678

Key observations:

- transfer_index = 1000594386508061719492494478 (a meaningful ~1.0006*RAY liquidity index, NOT 0). This means 3MF5QM's paired-BT override IS firing — `decode_balance_transfer_log` extracted a real BT log with both `value=49735362329328235679` and `index=1000594386508061719492494478` from its data.
- scaled_amount = 49735362329328235679 ≈ 3.1x position 534's balance (15826501534688837001).
- The preceding ScaledTokenMint (delta=0, new_index=matching the BT's index) looks like an INTEREST_ACCRUAL Mint emitted as part of a WITHDRAW's interest-then-burn sequence.
- The ScaledTokenBurn (Debt, position 219) just before suggests this chunk contains a REPAY transaction affecting position 219's debt + position 534's collateral.

## Likely shape

This is the THIRD divergence in the 16491070 -> 16601070 stretch (cluster shape):
1. W2S3WH scaled-token fetch staleness (resolved chunk 21 area).
2. 7UFMZX+B-YUPSIB scavenger theft + NMWPI6 word extraction + 3MF5QM paired-BT.
3. **THIS**: a `ScaledTokenTransfer` from p534's balance (~1.58*10^19) for `~4.97*10^19` — looking like a LiquidationCall's collateral transfer (the 76379275788 debt-burn preceding it talks to a smaller/aToken-aggregate liquidation scenario). The position's collateral balance is too small for the BT's `value` field by ~3.1x.

## Open questions (do NOT auto-fix without answers)

- Is this a LIQUIDATION (which `dispatch_balance_transfer` does NOT handle — the Python's `_should_skip_collateral_transfer` has explicit LIQUIDATION-only branches: ERC20 → skip, BT scaled → process)? If so, dispatch_balance_transfer is being called when the op should have been parsed as LIQUIDATION (not BALANCE_TRANSFER) — a CLASSIFICATION bug in operations_parser, not a math bug.
- Or is this a STANDALONE BalanceTransfer that legitimately wants to move 4.97*10^19 from a position that previously only had 1.58*10^19 — meaning a PRIOR chunk committed wrong values for position 534 (a retroactive divergence from before chunk 16591071)?
- Or is the position's current balance (1.58*10^19) UNDER-CREDITED — perhaps the preceding INTEREST_ACCRUAL Mint delta=0 should have credited accrued interest (which would have brought position 534's balance up to >= 4.97*10^19)? This points back at `dispatch_interest_accrual`'s `scaled_amount: Some(U256::ZERO)` assumption — does the Python oracle apply non-zero interest here?

## Action

File as a trackable divergence. AUTO-PROCEED PAUSED per the orchestrator's reassessment trigger (2-3 new divergences that each require fresh diagnostic scaffolding); the orchestrator is being consulted on whether to (a) investigate this 3rd divergence now, (b) write a parity fixture that exercises this scenario shape, OR (c) retarget toward building the BE474R (ii) on-chain-truth parity harness that would catch ALL of these via direct oracle comparison.

## Out of scope (already done)

- NMWPI6 (Supply/Borrow word1 fix) — commit 53255fc5.
- 3MF5QM (standalone BalanceTransfer paired BT scaled amount + index) — commit 213bc5f2.
- YUPSIB standalone test balance tightening — covered in commit 53255fc5.
- W2S3WH test balance tightening — covered in commit 53255fc5.

data.title: Drop 9 redundant leftmost-prefix FK indexes (Alembic migration + mirror)
data.body:
# Drop 9 redundant leftmost-prefix FK indexes

## Goal
- Drop 9 single-column FK indexes that duplicate the leftmost column of an existing UNIQUE/composite index, cutting write amplification + storage on the affected tables (incl. the largest: `managed_pool_liquidity_positions`, `managed_pool_initialization_maps`).

## Origin
Validated by spike `R3SR7L` (research complete). All 9 confirmed REDUNDANT via grep + EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (after drop, the planner picks the serving composite for every lone-column predicate; for #8/#9 the planner ALREADY picked the composite, so the single-col was pure dead weight).

## The 9 indexes to drop
1. `ix_aave_v3_asset_configs_asset_id` — served by `ix_aave_asset_config_asset` UNIQUE(`asset_id`)
2. `ix_aave_v3_assets_underlying_asset_id` — served by `ix_aave_assets_underlying_asset_market` UNIQUE(`underlying_asset_id`, `market_id`)
3. `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_collateral_position_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
4. `ix_aave_v3_debt_positions_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_debt_position_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
5. `ix_aave_v3_emode_categories_market_id` — served by `ix_aave_emode_category_market_cat` UNIQUE(`market_id`, `category_id`)
6. `ix_aave_v3_user_collateral_configs_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_user_collateral_config_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
7. `ix_pools_token0_id` — served by `ix_liquidity_pools_token_ids` (`token0_id`, `token1_id`) [non-unique; leftmost-prefix works on non-unique]
8. `ix_managed_pool_liquidity_positions_managed_pool_id` — served by UNIQUE(`managed_pool_id`, `tick`)
9. `ix_managed_pool_initialization_maps_managed_pool_id` — served by UNIQUE(`managed_pool_id`, `word`)

## CRITICAL: model-side change must be column-level, NOT alias-level (the trap)
The 9 indexes are SQLAlchemy `index=True` auto-declared on shared FK-column aliases (`ForeignKeyAaveAssetId`, `ForeignKeyTokenId`, `ForeignKeyAaveUserId`, `ForeignKeyAaveMarketId`, `ForeignKeyManagedPoolId`) reused across MULTIPLE tables. Naively stripping `index=True` from the alias would OVER-DROP the single-col index on sibling tables where that column is the **2nd** composite column (NOT a leftmost prefix) and is therefore genuinely needed (e.g. `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_asset_id`, `ix_pools_token1_id`, `ix_aave_v3_contracts_market_id`).

**Do NOT** strip `index=True` at the alias / shared-type level. Instead apply a column-level `index=False` override on each of the 9 specific columns in their model classes (`src/degenbot/database/models/aave.py` + `pools.py`). This neutralises the alias's `index=True` for that one column only.

Sibling indexes NOT in the list above are correctly EXCLUDED — verify none regress (they are the 2nd-column / no-composite cases).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/<new_rev>.py` whose `upgrade()` is 9× `op.drop_index(...)` and whose `downgrade()` is 9× `op.create_index(...)` (non-unique, single-column, mirroring the original definitions in `schema_head.sql`).
- [ ] `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`: the 9 `CREATE INDEX ix_...` lines removed; the serving UNIQUE/composite `CREATE INDEX` lines unchanged.
- [ ] `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`: `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bumped to the new revision id.
- [ ] `src/degenbot/database/models/{aave,pools}.py`: column-level `index=False` (or `mapped_column(..., index=False)`) on each of the 9 columns. Aliases themselves untouched.
- [ ] `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` spot-check on a fresh DB (post-migration): for the representative lone-column lookups (aave.rs:178, 243, 289; read.rs:416, 436), the planner picks the serving composite. Document the 5 plans in the task completion summary.
- [ ] No sibling single-col index (e.g. `ix_pools_token1_id`, `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_asset_id`, `ix_aave_v3_contracts_market_id`) was affected — verify via `sqlite_master` diff on a fresh DB.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (incl. the cutover `ensure_schema` / discovery schema-parity tests)
- `just test-rust` (the `degenbot-db` heal + writer parity tests assert schema shape)
- `just lint-rust` + `just format`
- Manual: `sqlite3 <fresh.db> ".indexes"` shows the 9 gone + siblings intact.
- Manual: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT ... WHERE managed_pool_id=?` on `managed_pool_liquidity_positions` returns the composite `ix_managed_pool_liquidity_positions_pool_id_tick` seek.

## Coordination note
If spike `ULMN4U` (drop boolean index `ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled`) also validates, COMBINE its drop into THIS migration (one Alembic revision carrying both R3SR7L + ULMN4U drops) rather than shipping two revisions — single `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bump. Decide when ULMN4U lands.

## Gating
0.6.x-safe (index drop via Alembic migration). NOT gated to 0.7.

data.body:
## Goal
- `#[pyclass]` `PyAnvilFork` under `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/fork/mod.rs`
  wrapping `degenbot_fork::AnvilFork`. Per the three-layer architecture (ADR-005):
  pyo3-only — arg extraction → GIL release → core call → result wrap. **Zero
  business logic in the wrapper.**
- `degenbot-python/Cargo.toml` adds `degenbot-fork = { path = "../degenbot-fork" }`.

## Surface
- `#[new]` constructor extracting the Python kwargs (fork_url, block_number,
  base_fee, storage_caching, ipc_path, etc.) → GIL release →
  `AnvilFork::try_spawn()` → wrap in `PyAnvilFork` (or `PyValueError` on spawn failure).
- Methods mirroring the Rust struct: `mine`, `reset`, `snapshot`, `revert`,
  `set_balance`, `set_code`, `set_nonce`, `set_storage_at`,
  `set_next_base_fee`, `set_next_block_timestamp`,
  `set_block_timestamp_interval`, `set_coinbase`. Each: extract args →
  `Python::allow_threads` → core call → convert result to Python types
  (HexBytes for bytes, int for U256, etc.).
- Async methods: expose as `async def` via pyo3's async support OR sync-only
  with a note (decide during impl; the alloy Provider is async, so the
  pyo3 wrapper spawns a tokio runtime or uses the existing one).
- `provider` property → returns the alloy Provider pyclass (for general RPC).
- `http_url`/`ipc_path` properties (if retained — see task FF4's design Q).

## Stub
- Update `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi` with the `PyAnvilFork` class stub
  (methods + types). RUF022-safe section (separate from the rpc_types/crypto
  stubs already there — different section, no `__all__` collision).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PyAnvilFork` compiles; `.pyi` stub updated.
- Wrapper contains zero business logic (pyo3 + delegation only).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` unaffected (wrapper is in degenbot-python,
  not a core).

## Validation Gates
- `cargo check -p degenbot-python`
- `just lint-rust`
- `just test-rust-python` (once Python shell lands in FF4)

## Result

`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/fork/mod.rs` (new, 390 lines) — single `#[pyclass(name = "AnvilFork")] PyAnvilFork` PyO3 seam wrapping the `degenbot-fork` core. Lives under `degenbot-python` (the PyO3 seam crate, gated).

### Surface (zero business logic — arg extract → GIL release → core call → result wrap)

- `__new__(**kwargs)` keyword-only constructor mirroring the legacy Python `AnvilFork.__init__` surface (fork_url/fork_block/fork_transaction_hash + mining_mode / mining_interval + storage_caching + base_fee + ipc_path + port + host + mnemonic + chain_id + anvil_opts). Releases GIL + spawns subprocess via `get_runtime().block_on`. Post-spawn state overrides (legacy `_overrides` kwargs) intentionally NOT exposed on the constructor — FF4's Python companion shell orchestrates them via the registered dev methods (`set_balance` / `set_code` / etc.) — keeps the FF3 surface minimal + avoids the borrow-lifetime trap when crossing the GIL-release boundary.
- `ipc_path` getter (forwarded to the FF2-small-follow-up core getter below).
- 12 sync dev-RPC methods: mine / reset / snapshot / revert / set_balance / set_code / set_nonce / set_storage_at / set_next_base_fee / set_next_block_timestamp / set_block_timestamp_interval / set_coinbase. Each uses the established `py.detach(|| get_runtime().block_on(async move { ... }))` pattern — sync chosen over async to match the `PyAlloyProvider` precedent.

### Side corrections (deferred to FF4)

- `provider` pyclass property — not exposed. Deferred to FF4's design call: it can re-construct an `AlloyProvider` over `AnvilFork.ipc_path` (replacing `self.w3`) or expose the core `DynProvider` directly via a new pyclass wrapper. FF3 delivers `ipc_path` so FF4 has what it needs.
- Async variants of the dev methods — module-doc-captured choice to mirror `PyAsyncAlloyProvider` shape later if needed.

### FF2 small follow-up (carried in the FF3 commit chain)

- Added `AnvilFork::ipc_path(&self) -> &str` getter on the `degenbot-fork` core (delegates to the underlying `AnvilInstance`'s resolved `--ipc` path) — additive, no semver break; the PyO3 seam needs it for the FF4 `provider` reconstruction design.
- Renamed `_instance` → `instance` field on `AnvilFork` (now read by the public `ipc_path()` method — `clippy::used_underscore_binding` requires).

### Commit chain

The work landed in two commits — the FF3 code in commit `672bc44b` (swept up into the sibling's episodic v2-math refactor `--no-verify` commit since they ran `git add -A` contemporaneously), and the ruff-lint fixes I had pending at that exact moment in `64d76304` (mnemonic literal → `...`, `revert(id:)` → `revert(snapshot_id:)` to satisfy `flake8-builtins-argument-shadowing`, plus the `uv sync`-driven Cargo.lock dangling-v2-math-entry cleanup).

### Validation gates

- `cargo check -p degenbot_rs` ✓
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot_rs --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo fmt --check -p degenbot_rs` ✓
- `ruff check` ✓ (post-`64d76304`)
- `ruff format --check` ✓
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` ✓ (the wrapper lives in `degenbot-python`, not a core)
- `cargo test -p degenbot-fork` ✓ (still 4/4 in-process anvil tests after the FF2-small-follow-up `ipc_path` getter)
- `just test-rust-python` — FF4's gate per FF3 task body.

    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Simulation → Rust core** migration so subsequent child
  tasks decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md`
  §2.1 criteria / §2.2 dispositions / §2.3 smells / §3 cutover discipline / §4 red-green
  parity + retirement).

## Context (responsibility boundary)
- The **Simulation** responsibility = everything between "engine solve results drained"
  and "profitable `tx_params` ready to submit". It reads engine results (`path_id`,
  `optimal_input`, `engine_profit`, `hop_outputs`, `consumed_inputs`, `solve_block` from
  `degenbot-python/src/bot/engine/result_channel.rs`), encodes each candidate into the
  `cmd_executor` command stream, builds `stateOverrides` (code injection + warmup slots),
  computes an EIP-2930 access list, dispatches `eth_simulateV1` with a 7-call balance-read
  pattern, classifies reverts, computes gross/net profit, and fans out in parallel.
- Today this lives ENTIRELY in Python:
  `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` (`simulate_one` L1857–L2437, `dispatch_profitable_results` L1653, `build_simulation_state_overrides` L416, `_compute_priority_fee` L1570, `PathSuppression` L509, `_load_executor_runtime_bytecode` L388, `encode_balanceof_calldata` L372) + `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` (`classify_revert`, `filter_thin_margin_results`, `format_sim_diag_line`). The Rust `degenbot-bot` pump/solve coordinator produces results and STOPS there — no simulation logic exists in any core crate.
- Canonical reading order applied: `AGENTS.md` (Architectural Vision → Rust is the engine,
  Python is the cockpit) → `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1/§2.2 →
  `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md` (standalone-core +
  zero-`pyo3`-in-cores) → `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §3 ("Rust is the engine,
  Python is the cockpit"), §17 (known-limitation: "Simulation, submission — today Python
  via `examples/`; on the migration path").
- Baseline gate: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (untouched by scoping).
- **Crate placement (recommended):** new core crate `degenbot-simulation` (pyo3-free;
  deps `alloy + degenbot-rpc + degenbot-core + degenbot-abi + degenbot-executor +
  degenbot-uniswap`), PyO3 wrappers in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/simulation/`.
  Mirrors the `degenbot-executor` precedent (the crate the WWC4DL epic lands). Keeps
  `degenbot-bot` focused on state/solve; simulation is a solve-results consumer. **Flag for
  `t-6486` confirmation** (consistent with the WWC4DL crate decision).

## Child-task split (port-now / partial rows → implementation tasks)

- **A1** → child: *`build_simulation_state_overrides` (stateOverrides dict: code injection + ETH/WETH funding + warmup-slot integration + WETH9 balanceOf override)*. Depends on `62H23D` (cross-epic WWC4DL warmup-slot math).
- **B1+B3+B4** → child: *Simulation RPC dispatch leaf: 7-call balanceOf + execute() calldata + SimulateV1Payload/StateOverride shape + `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList`* (typed consumer of `ZUZANP`; untyped `make_request` until typed lands → partial). - **C1+C2+C4** → child: *`simulate_one` orchestration + 7-call result parse + gross/net profit computation + `_compute_priority_fee` (market-aware age-decay fee) + int128 guard*. Depends on the A1 child + the B-leaf child + `SYI3PG` (cross-epic WWC4DL revert) + `YQORTM` (cross-epic WWC4DL encode).
- **D1+D2** → child: *`dispatch_profitable_results` fan-out + `PathSuppression` + categorization (gas-profitable/unprofitable/exception) + thin-margin filter integration*. Depends on the C1 child + `SYI3PG` (cross-epic WWC4DL thin-margin filter).

`stays-python` rows (A2 bytecode-load bootstrap, C6 revert param-decode diagnostic, D4 breakdown rendering, E1 sim-diag JSON, E2 revert-state dump) — NO child; flagged in the scope table so the next sweep does not re-litigate. Reference rows (A3, B2, C3, C5, D3, F1–F4) — provided by sibling epics/crates; consumed not re-scoped.

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **`ZUZANP` (RPC epic D3DIPE) is the critical path for the B-leaf.** The sim-dispatch leaf is `partial` until the typed `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList`/`eth_feeHistory` land (the untyped `make_request` exists, so an interim untyped-Rust cutover is possible — flag the sequencing with `t-6486`). Cross-epic child edge: B-leaf → `ZUZANP`.
2. **`_compute_priority_fee` shared with `SHT6GE`/`P7AMWR`.** The fee leaf feeds BOTH net-profit (simulation, gates dispatch) and the submitted tx's `maxPriorityFeePerGas` (P7AMWR). Scoped under this epic; `P7AMWR` should `ergo sequence`-depend on the fee child OR reference it. **Needs `t-6486` confirmation** (or a direct cross-epic child edge C-fee → `P7AMWR`'s submission leaf once `P7AMWR` scopes).
3. **Crate placement: `degenbot-simulation`?** Recommended new core crate (mirrors the `degenbot-executor` precedent from WWC4DL). **Confirm with `t-6486`** — consistent with the WWC4DL crate decision; alternatively fold into `degenbot-bot` (the state owner) though that bloats the solve crate.
4. **Float in `_compute_priority_fee` (C4).** The age-decay + target-fee use float→int truncate. Preserve the exact truncate semantics in the Rust port (§2.1 "type shape" — acceptable; document the float boundary).
5. **Diagnostics stay Python (E1/E2, C6, D4, A2).** Flagged `stays-python`; the next sweep should not re-litigate without a new driver (e.g. a hot-loop promotion of the revert param-decoder to structured return — then it would port alongside `SYI3PG`).
6. **`examples/` ownership.** The retired Python sim orchestration lives in `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` + `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`; the cutover retargets `simulate_one`/`dispatch_profitable_results` callsites + moves the parity corpus into `tests/rust/` per rubric §4.3.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose |
|----|-------|---------|
| `TCTUAW` | `build_simulation_state_overrides` (stateOverrides dict) | Code injection + ETH/WETH funding + warmup-slot integration (consumes `62H23D`) + WETH9 `balanceOf` 10-ETH override. |
| `PGA5S3` | Simulation RPC dispatch leaf | 7-call balanceOf + execute() calldata + `SimulateV1Payload` + `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList`/`eth_feeHistory` (typed consumer of `ZUZANP`; interim untyped `make_request`). |
| `YL2MTH` | `simulate_one` orchestration + profit + fee | Per-path async orchestration: encode → access-list → simulate → 7-call parse → classify revert (`SYI3PG`) → gross/net profit + `_compute_priority_fee` + int128 guard. |
| `5FB5MW` | `dispatch_profitable_results` fan-out + suppression | tokio `JoinSet` + `MAX_SIMULATE_CONCURRENT` semaphore + categorize (gas-profitable/unprofitable/exception) + `PathSuppression` + thin-margin filter (`SYI3PG`) integration. |

`stays-python` rows (no child): A2 (`_load_executor_runtime_bytecode` file-load bootstrap),
C6 (revert param-decode for `[sim-fail]` logs), D4 (`format_failure_breakdown` rendering),
E1 (`_emit_sim_diag`/`format_sim_diag_line` JSON), E2 (`_dump_state_for_revert` on-chain
state diagnostics). Reference rows (provided by sibling epics/crates, consumed not
re-scoped): A3 + C3 (`62H23D`/`fits_int128` via WWC4DL), B2 (`YQORTM` cmd-bytes), C5
(`SYI3PG` revert), D3 (`SYI3PG` thin-margin), F1–F4 (`make_request` + typed RPC leaves +
engine results + ABI encode/decode).

## Dependency edges (ergo `sequence`)

```
CROSS-EPIC (WWC4DL → 5LLJHX):                 CROSS-EPIC (D3DIPE → 5LLJHX):
  62H23D (warmup) ──► TCTUAW (A)                ZUZANP (typed RPC) ──► PGA5S3 (B)
  YQORTM  (encode) ──┬─► PGA5S3 (B)            CROSS-EPIC (WWC4DL → 5LLJHX):
                     └─► YL2MTH  (C)             SYI3PG (revert+filter) ──┬─► YL2MTH (C)
  SYI3PG  (revert) ──┴─► YL2MTH  (C)                                     └─► 5FB5MW (D)

INTRA-EPIC (5LLJHX):
  TCTUAW (A) ──► YL2MTH (C) ──► 5FB5MW (D)
  PGA5S3 (B) ──► YL2MTH (C)
```
`5FB5MW` (D, fan-out) gates on `YL2MTH` (C, simulate_one) + `SYI3PG`; `YL2MTH` (C) gates on
`TCTUAW` (A) + `PGA5S3` (B) + `YQORTM` + `SYI3PG`; `PGA5S3` (B) gates on `ZUZANP` (typed
RPC, cross-epic D3DIPE) + `YQORTM` (encode, cross-epic WWC4DL); `TCTUAW` (A) gates on
`62H23D` (warmup, cross-epic WWC4DL). The `PGA5S3` → `ZUZANP` edge is the critical-path
cross-epic dep; an interim untyped-`make_request` cutover is possible before `ZUZANP` lands.

data.title: [rpc] B3 — Factory rewrite: alloy-only, delete web3 branches
data.body:
## Goal
- `get_provider_from_config` becomes alloy-only; delete the web3 construction
  branches, `_fast_decode_rpc_response`, the middleware munging, the
  `optimize` param, and the `use_alloy`/`DEGENBOT_USE_ALLOY_PROVIDER` switch.

## Context
- `src/degenbot/provider/factory.py`: `get_provider_from_config` defaults
  `use_alloy` from env `DEGENBOT_USE_ALLOY_PROVIDER` (off by default) and
  branches to `Web3(HTTPProvider(...))` / `Web3(LegacyWebSocketProvider(...))` /
  `Web3(IPCProvider(...))` when off. `AlloyProvider(endpoint)` already handles
  all three schemes (http/ws/ipc — confirmed by the existing alloy branch).
- `get_async_provider_from_config` is already alloy-only — untouched.
- The `optimize` param only affects web3 (middleware clearing + fast JSON
  decode) — becomes vestigial; remove it.
- The chain-id enforcement stays (now via `AlloyProvider::get_chain_id`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `get_provider_from_config` constructs `AlloyProvider` unconditionally; no
  `Web3`/`HTTPProvider`/`IPCProvider`/`LegacyWebSocketProvider` references.
- `_fast_decode_rpc_response` deleted; `optimize`/`use_alloy` params deleted.
- Chain-id mismatch still raises `ValueError`.
- Callers of `optimize=`/`use_alloy=` updated.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (provider factory tests)
