data.title: dispatch_profitable_results fan-out + PathSuppression + categorization (gas-profitable/unprofitable/exception) + thin-margin filter integration
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **dispatch fan-out + suppression** to Rust: `dispatch_profitable_results` —
  cap concurrent sims at `MAX_SIMULATE_CONCURRENT`, fan out `simulate_one` across a tokio
  `JoinSet` (with a semaphore), gather results with exception tolerance, categorize into
  gas-profitable (net ≥ `MIN_PROFIT_NET`) vs gas-unprofitable (gross > 0, net below
  threshold) vs exception, integrate the thin-margin pre-filter (`SYI3PG`) + `PathSuppression`.
- This is the concurrency orchestration that owns the GIL release + the tokio fan-out
  over the per-path `simulate_one` leaf (sibling C-child).

## Context
- Scope task: `4JGPDW` (epic `5LLJHX`), rows D1/D2 (+ D3 reference, D4 stays-python).
- Rubric dispositions: D1 `port-now` (pure concurrency orchestration: tokio `JoinSet` +
  `MAX_SIMULATE_CONCURRENT` semaphore; categorization pure; the §2.1 "GIL?" win — owning
  the fan-out in Rust releases the GIL across the per-tx sim RPCs); D2 `port-now`
  (`PathSuppression` = `HashMap<path_id, fail_count>` + suppressed set, property-testable;
  small enough to fold in for clarity); D3 `done`-reference (`filter_thin_margin_results`
  = `SYI3PG`, cross-epic WWC4DL); D4 `stays-python` (`format_failure_breakdown` rendering
  of the tally dict to a log string — the buckets themselves port with the C-child).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core), `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md`
  §3.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` — `dispatch_profitable_results`
  L1653 + the fan-out L2450–L2517, `PathSuppression` L509–L578, the thin-margin pre-filter
  L2444–L2450, the categorization + summary log L2519–L2535.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-simulation` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `async fn dispatch_profitable_results(results, dispatcher_state, current_block,
  base_fee_next, min_profit_net, min_profit_margin_bps) -> DispatchOutcome` that:
  - applies `PathSuppression::is_suppressed` pre-filter,
  - applies `filter_thin_margin_results` (`SYI3PG`) pre-filter,
  - caps at `MAX_SIMULATE_CONCURRENT` + spawns `simulate_one` on a tokio `JoinSet` with a
    semaphore,
  - gathers with exception tolerance (logs first N, debug-rest),
  - categorizes gas-profitable / gas-unprofitable / exception,
  - returns the categories + the suppression/failure tallies.
- `PathSuppression` struct: `fail_count: HashMap<u64, u32>` + `suppressed: HashSet<u64>`;
  `PATH_SUPPRESS_THRESHOLD`; `record_success`/`record_failure`/`is_suppressed`/
  `is_path_blocked`; property tests (threshold, reset, suppress, re-prime).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: categorization buckets + suppression transitions vs the
  Python behavior over a fixture corpus.
- The summary-log RENDERING (`format_failure_breakdown`) stays Python (D4) — this leaf
  exposes the tally as a typed struct the Python companion renders.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example.
- Parity check vs the Python `dispatch_profitable_results` categorization (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- The per-path `simulate_one` + profit/fee computation — sibling C-child (`YL2MTH`).
- The sim RPC dispatch + stateOverrides — sibling B (`PGA5S3`) / A (`TCTUAW`).
- The thin-margin filter (`filter_thin_margin_results`) — `SYI3PG` (cross-epic WWC4DL).
- The summary-log rendering (`format_failure_breakdown`) — `stays-python` (D4).
- Transaction submission (the post-dispatch `submit`) — `SHT6GE`/`P7AMWR` (cross-epic).

## Dependencies
- Depends on the C-child `YL2MTH` (`simulate_one`) + `SYI3PG` (cross-epic WWC4DL,
  thin-margin filter).

data.title: Aave ScaledToken (aToken/vToken Mint/Burn/Transfer) apply fns + AaveChunkEvent variants
data.body:
## Goal
Port the **ScaledToken (aToken/vToken Mint/Burn/BalanceTransfer) apply fns** to `degenbot-db/src/write.rs` + extend `AaveChunkEvent` — the scaled-token sibling to CXRGX4/POOLAPPLY. Pure `write.rs` substrate (`_on_conn` variants, fixture-testable), mirroring CXRGX4's shape.

## Why this task exists
The Aave V3 `AaveV3ScaledTokenEvent` (Mint/Burn/BalanceTransfer) events drive aToken/vToken balance + last_index updates — the `token_processor.py` (958 lines) + `transfers.py` (203 lines) Python path. These interleave with Pool position events in the same chunk transaction (a Supply emits a Pool `Supply` event AND a scaled-token `Mint` event; the orchestrator must process both atomically). §3.4 two-writer hazard blocks partial coverage — sibling to POOLAPPLY, both prerequisite to `6SWY4R`.

## Event scope (this task) — `AaveV3ScaledTokenEvent` (3 events)
- `Mint(from, to, value)` — credit the `to` address's aToken/vToken balance; record the last_index applied. For `to` = the user's collateral position. For `from` = zero address (mint on deposit) OR the treasury (`MintedToTreasury` companion). Port the Python `token_processor.py::process_scaled_token_mint` logic exactly.
- `Burn(from, to, value)` — debit `from`'s balance; if `to` = zero address (burn on repay/withdraw) decrement the user balance; otherwise it's a transfer-burn (treasury burn). Port `process_scaled_token_burn`.
- `BalanceTransfer(from, to, value)` — aToken transfer between users (e.g. aToken sent to another address). Decrement `from`'s position, increment `to`'s position, update both users' `last_index` to the current asset `liquidity_index` (so the scaled-balance reconciliation is correct). Port `transfers.py`.

## The math (port from token_processor.py)
- **Scaled balance reconciliation** — the aToken tracks an external balance (ERC20 balanceOf). The DB position stores `scaled_balance` + `last_index`. On each event, the Python computes the delta in scaled terms using the asset's current `liquidity_index`, then updates `scaled_balance` + `last_index`. Port the exact reconciliation: the worker should read `token_processor.py`'s math before implementing; flag any index/reconciliation ambiguity (it's bitten ports before — the migration guide §4.2 warns about fee/retained-fraction conventions).
- **The scaled-amount pool revision** — `operations.py::SCALED_AMOUNT_POOL_REVISION` gates a behavior change in scaled-balance math (markets before/after the revision apply different rounding). Port the revision-aware branch.

## Scope (this task)
1. **`apply_scaled_token_mint_on_conn` / `apply_scaled_token_burn_on_conn` / `apply_scaled_token_transfer_on_conn`** in `write.rs` — `_on_conn` + thin `&self` wrappers (mirror CXRGX4). Each takes the position `id` (resolved by the orchestrator via `get_or_create_collateral_position_on_conn` / `get_or_create_debt_position_on_conn` — already landed in CXRGX4) + the event's typed fields.
2. **Extend `AaveChunkEvent`** with `ScaledTokenMint` / `ScaledTokenBurn` / `ScaledTokenTransfer` variants (carrying resolved `position_id: i64` + `amount: U256` + the asset's current `liquidity_index` for reconciliation — flag if the index should be re-fetched inside the apply fn vs passed in; the precedent's apply fns take pre-resolved ids, so passing the index is consistent).
3. **Extend `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`'s dispatch** + `AaveChunkWriteReport`'s counts.
4. **NO new ray-math** — reuse whatever POOLAPPLY established (this task depends on POOLAPPLY landing first so the ray-math home is settled).

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged)
ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Every apply writes through `_on_conn` on the caller's tx. On `Err`, whole-chunk revert. Unit tests assert commit-vs-rollback all-or-nothing for the scaled-token variants.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `apply_scaled_token_mint_on_conn` / `apply_scaled_token_burn_on_conn` / `apply_scaled_token_transfer_on_conn` exist in `write.rs`; `&self` wrappers preserved.
- [ ] `AaveChunkEvent` extended with the 3 scaled-token variants; dispatch + report counts updated.
- [ ] Unit tests: per-event apply correctness (fixture event → asserted DB row state, including the scaled-balance + last_index reconciliation) + one rollback atomicity test covering a scaled-token variant.
- [ ] The scaled-balance math matches `token_processor.py` byte-for-byte (the §4.2 U5YIBG cross-check will catch deviations, but the worker should self-verify against the Python before reporting DONE).
- [ ] `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just lint-rust`, `just format` all green.

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just test-rust-python`, `just lint-rust`, `just format`.

## Non-goals
- Pool position apply fns → sibling `POOLAPPLY` (this task depends on it for the ray-math home).
- GHO/stkAAVE/Rewards/ERC20-Transfer → sibling `SPECIALAPPLY`.
- Event decoders → sibling `AAVEDECODE`.
- The orchestrator → sibling `6SWY4R`.
- Python cutover → sibling `AVS4DR`.
- §4.2 parity → sibling `U5YIBG`.

## Dependencies
- `CXRGX4` (done) — `AaveChunkEvent` enum + `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` + the `get_or_create_*_position_on_conn` fns this task calls.
- `POOLAPPLY` (prerequisite) — establishes the ray-math home + the position-event apply pattern + the `ReserveDataUpdated` index-advance this task's reconciliation depends on.
- Depended on by: `6SWY4R`.

data.title: Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math (core leaf)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **simulation warmup-slot / `mapping_slot` storage-slot math** to Rust:
  `mapping_slot`, `_nested_mapping_slot`, `_keccak256`, and
  `compute_simulation_warmup_slots`.
- Produces the `eth_simulateV1` `stateDiff` overrides that replicate
  `cmd_executor.initialize()` (warms WETH9 `balanceOf(executor)` at slot 3 and
  PoolManager ERC6909 `balanceOf` at slot 4 nested-mapping slots for the WETH + native
  ids) so injected-runtime-bytecode simulations see warm storage.

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), rows C1–C2.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure Solidity-mapping storage-slot math —
  `keccak256(key ‖ base_slot)`; integer-only; property-testable). `_keccak256` is trivially
  `alloy::primitives::keccak256`.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`
  (standalone-core constraint), `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1,
  `contracts/README.md` "cmd_executor immutables" + "Code Injection"
  (`rust/CONTEXT.md` {Code Injection} documents the runtime-bytecode injection flow this
  feeds).
- The slot-computation is pure (executor-address / WETH-address / PoolManager-address →
  nested-mapping slots). The OUTPUT is an `eth_simulateV1`-specific dict
  (`{address: {"stateDiff": {slot_hex: value_hex}}}`); the dict shape may keep a thin
  Python adapter at the boundary, but the slot math lands in a core crate.
- Python oracle: `examples/cmd_stream.py` — `mapping_slot` L884–L891, `_nested_mapping_slot`
  L894–L916, `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` L919–L1054 (embeds the storage-layout
  knowledge: WETH9 `balanceOf` at slot 3; PoolManager C3-linearized ERC6909 `balanceOf`
  at slot 4 after `owner`/`pendingOwner`/`isOperator`/`protocolFeesAccrued`; ERC6909 id =
  `uint160(currency)` per `CurrencyLibrary.toId()`).
- Existing test: `tests/arbitrage/test_warmup_slots_gas.py` (414 lines) — the parity
  corpus.
- Parity required (§4.2) — the slot math must match the Python output exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `mapping_slot(base_slot: U256, key: U256) -> U256` and
  `nested_mapping_slot(base_slot, key1, key2) -> U256` over `alloy::primitives::keccak256`.
- `compute_simulation_warmup_slots(executor, weth, pool_manager) -> WarmupSlots` returning
  the three computed slots (WETH9 balance slot, PoolManager ERC6909 WETH-id slot, native-id
  slot) as a typed struct (the `eth_simulateV1` dict shape can be built in a thin PyO3
  wrapper).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests against `tests/arbitrage/test_warmup_slots_gas.py` fixture
  values (the WETH = `0xC02...` / PM = `0x0000...444c` mainnet slots are the canonical
  ground truth).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Byte-for-byte parity check vs the Python `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` output.

## Non-goals
- The cmd-stream opcodes / path composers — sibling tasks.
- The `eth_simulateV1` call itself (Simulation epic `5LLJHX`) — this task only computes
  the slot overrides.
- PyO3 wrapping (cutover task) — though a thin PyO3 adapter that turns the typed struct
  into the `stateDiff` dict is in-scope for the cutover task, not here.

## Dependencies
- Standalone (pure keccak math). No dep on the opcode/primitive leaf, but co-located in
  the same `degenbot-executor` core crate if created.

## Result — 62H23D done

**Crate chosen:** new pyo3-free core leaf `degenbot-executor` (`rust/crates/degenbot-executor/`) — as the orchestrator steered (executor-domain, the natural home for `HATTU7` opcodes later), NOT `degenbot-evm-math` (the warmup math is a Solidity-storage-layout concern, not generic EVM gas math). Wired into the workspace `members`, the umbrella `degenbot` crate (`pub use degenbot_executor;`), the `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` gate list, and a `[profile.release.package.degenbot-executor] codegen-units = 16`.

**Functions** (`rust/crates/degenbot-executor/src/lib.rs`):
- `pub fn mapping_slot(base_slot: U256, key: U256) -> U256` — `keccak256(key ‖ base_slot)` (key FIRST — the parity-sensitive point), both 32-byte big-endian. Ports `cmd_stream.py::mapping_slot` L884–L891.
- `pub fn nested_mapping_slot(base_slot, key1, key2) -> U256` — `mapping_slot(mapping_slot(base, k1), k2)` (double-keccak). Ports `_nested_mapping_slot` L894–L916; composition order verified against the oracle.
- `pub fn erc6909_id(currency: Address) -> U256` — `uint160(currency)` via a const `MASK_160` (low 160 bits); native id = 0.
- `pub fn compute_simulation_warmup_slots(executor, weth, _pool_manager) -> WarmupSlots` — returns the three slot ADDRESSES only (typed struct `{weth_balance, erc6909_weth, erc6909_native}`); the 1-wei warmed values + the `stateDiff` dict shape are the cutover-task PyO3 adapter (per the task's "stores the three computed slots" = slot addresses only — confirmed).
- consts `WETH9_BALANCE_OF_SLOT = 3`, `POOL_MANAGER_ERC6909_BALANCE_OF_SLOT = 4`.
- `_keccak256` is just `alloy::primitives::keccak256` (no wrapper) — the Python `_keccak256` is trivia.

**Parity fixtures** (3 fixture sets × 3 slots = 9 pinned U256 slot values + their `064x` hex), generated directly from the Python oracle `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` over the three executor addresses in the parity corpus:
- canonical mainnet WETH `0xC02…` / PoolManager `0x0000…444c` (ground truth from `test_warmup_slots_gas.py`).
- executors: `0xAA…AA` (the corpus `EXECUTOR_ADDRESS`), `0xDeAd…0001`, `0xDeAd…0002` (the `eth_simulateV1` test executors).
Each row asserts the Rust slot == the oracle slot AND the `{:064x}` hex == the `stateDiff` dict key hex the oracle emits. Cross-confirmed the dict slots exactly match the direct-fn outputs.

**TDD:** tests first (parity rows + layout invariants), watched RED (compile: MASK_160 const mis-built — read only 64 of 80 hex chars → wrong mask width → `erc6909_id` off + the nested WETH slot mismatched; a genuine layout bug, not a tautology, surfaced by the parity suite), fixed → GREEN.

**Tests** (8, all green): `parity_vs_python_oracle` (9 pinned slots×hex over 3 fixtures), `mapping_slot_layout_is_key_then_base_slot` (cross-checks the parity corpus's manual keccak at L271–278), `nested_mapping_slot_composition`, `nested_native_slot_is_double_hashed` (native ≠ single-level), `erc6909_id_is_uint160_of_currency` (+ native=0), 3 `proptest` properties (determinism, keccak spread, no-collision sweep).

**Gates (in-isolation, all PASS):**
- `cargo test -p degenbot-executor` — 8/8 green.
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-executor --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean (used the codebase's own `#![allow(clippy::doc_markdown)]` idiom for Solidity identifiers, matching `degenbot-{solidly,balancer,curve}-math`).
- `cargo fmt -p degenbot-executor -- --check` — clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — PASS (crate declares no `pyo3`).
- `cargo build -p degenbot` + `--example standalone_consumer` — umbrella re-export + standalone consumer build (ADR-005 standalone claim satisfied).

**Workspace gates:**
- `just test-rust` — GREEN workspace-wide (all crates incl. the new one).
- `just lint-rust` + `just fmt-check` — **BLOCKED by the parallel in-flight `degenbot-db` crate** (task `SLHSM4`, state `doing`): it has 55 clippy errors + unformatted files. This is concurrent agent work; my `degenbot-executor` crate passes every gate in isolation and I did not touch `degenbot-db`'s files. Flagging to the orchestrator so the gate can be re-run once `SLHSM4` lands.

**Non-goals honored:** no Python changes; Python oracle `examples/cmd_stream.py` retained as the §4.2 parity reference (not deleted); no `stateDiff` dict adapter / no `eth_simulateV1` call.

Result files: `rust/crates/degenbot-executor/src/lib.rs`, `rust/crates/degenbot-executor/Cargo.toml`.

data.title: Polish: IPC URL detection, make_request retry, eager WS/IPC connect, retry-config constant
data.body:
Bundle of four independent, low-risk fixes. May be committed as up to four
commits; track as one ergo task for simplicity since each is small.

## Goal
- `build_provider` IPC detection is explicit (not "anything without `://`").
- `make_request` does not blindly retry non-idempotent RPC methods.
- WS/IPC connect is no longer eagerly fatal at construction (matches HTTP's
  lazy-connect, retried-on-first-call behavior).
- `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` constant is no longer misleading (used as the actual
  default for `new`, or deleted).

## Context
- Sub-items (from the critical review):
  - **IPC detection (#4):** `else if !rpc_url.contains("://")` treats a typo
    like `localhost:8545` as an IPC path. Require `/`, `\\`, or `ipc://`.
  - **make_request retry (#5):** the raw escape hatch applies
    `retry_with_backoff` to any method, including `debug_*`/`trace_*`. Add a
    retry flag or a non-retried variant for non-idempotent methods.
  - **WS/IPC eager connect (#14):** `connect_ws`/`connect_ipc` `.await?` at
    construction; a transient outage fails provider build permanently while
    HTTP is lazy. Make WS/IPC lazy (connect on first call, retried) or add
    connect-time retry. Document the chosen approach in the task completion
    note.
  - **retry-config constant (#7):** `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 10` is exported
    but `new` callers pass `3`. Either make `new` default to the constant
    (per epic decision 6: constant becomes the actual default, with a
    builder/second constructor for override) or delete the constant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `build_provider` rejects `localhost:8545`-style strings with a clear
  `ConnectionFailed` ("unsupported scheme / not an IPC path") instead of
  silently routing to IPC. A path like `/tmp/anvil.ipc` or `\\.\pipe\x` still
  routes to IPC.
- `make_request` either takes an explicit retry flag
  (`make_request_no_retry` or `make_request(method, params, retry: bool)`)
  or defaults to no-retry for methods not in an idempotent allowlist
  (`eth_call`, `eth_getLogs`, `eth_getBlockByNumber`, etc.). Documented.
- WS/IPC providers connect lazily on first RPC call (retried via
  `retry_with_backoff`) OR construction retries the connect a bounded number
  of times. Chosen approach documented.
- `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` reflects the actual production default (callers no
  longer hardcode `3`); or the constant is removed and the default is
  inlined with a doc comment. `new(&rpc_url, 3)` call sites across
  `degenbot-bot` / `degenbot-python` / `degenbot-price` updated to the new
  signature or left passing the constant.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (URL-scheme detection tests; make_request retry-flag test)
- `just lint-rust`
- `just test-rust-python` if any call-site signatures change

data.title: drop 10 redundant indexes + add ix_pools_chain_kind (Alembic migration + ALEMBIC_HEAD bump)
data.body:
# Drop 10 redundant/dead-weight indexes + add `ix_pools_chain_kind` (Alembic migration + mirror + model changes)

## Goal
- Drop 9 single-column FK indexes that duplicate the leftmost column of an existing UNIQUE/composite index (spike-1).
- Drop 1 dead-weight boolean index with zero read predicates (spike-2).
- **Add 1 new composite index `ix_pools_chain_kind ON pools(chain, kind)`** to serve the chain-scoped construction-time reads that currently SCAN (spike-8).
- Net write-amplification: **NEGATIVE** (10 drops on big/hot tables >> 1 add on a small cold-write table).

## Bundling decision (spike-8)
spike-8 validated adding `ix_pools_chain_kind`. Folded into THIS migration as the 11th op — one Alembic revision carrying 10 drops + 1 add → one `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bump (vs. two migrations). Mechanically clean: both `op.drop_index` and `op.create_index` are index-DDL ops, no schema-rewrite difference. The downgrade is symmetric (`op.drop_index("ix_pools_chain_kind")` + 10 `op.create_index`s).

## Origin
Validated by two completed spikes under this epic:
- `R3SR7L` → indexes #1–#9 (all redundant leftmost-prefix duplicates)
- `ULMN4U` → index #10 (dead-weight hand-declared index, zero read predicates)

## The 10 indexes to drop + 1 to add

### Group A — redundant leftmost-prefix duplicates (origin: spike R3SR7L, ORM `index=True` cruft)
1. `ix_aave_v3_asset_configs_asset_id` — served by `ix_aave_asset_config_asset` UNIQUE(`asset_id`)
2. `ix_aave_v3_assets_underlying_asset_id` — served by `ix_aave_assets_underlying_asset_market` UNIQUE(`underlying_asset_id`, `market_id`)
3. `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_collateral_position_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
4. `ix_aave_v3_debt_positions_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_debt_position_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
5. `ix_aave_v3_emode_categories_market_id` — served by `ix_aave_emode_category_market_cat` UNIQUE(`market_id`, `category_id`)
6. `ix_aave_v3_user_collateral_configs_user_id` — served by `ix_aave_user_collateral_config_user_asset` UNIQUE(`user_id`, `asset_id`)
7. `ix_pools_token0_id` — served by `ix_liquidity_pools_token_ids` (`token0_id`, `token1_id`) [non-unique; leftmost-prefix works on non-unique]
8. `ix_managed_pool_liquidity_positions_managed_pool_id` — served by UNIQUE(`managed_pool_id`, `tick`)
9. `ix_managed_pool_initialization_maps_managed_pool_id` — served by UNIQUE(`managed_pool_id`, `word`)

### Group B — dead-weight hand-declared index (origin: spike ULMN4U)
10. `ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled` — boolean-column index, **zero read predicates filter on `enabled`** anywhere in the codebase (Rust or Python). Dead weight in practice.

### Group C — NEW index to ADD (origin: spike-8)
11. `ix_pools_chain_kind ON pools(chain, kind)` — serves chain-scoped construction-time reads that currently SCAN (see §"The add: `ix_pools_chain_kind`" below).

## Rationale corrections from the research (preserve in implementation notes)
- **Leftmost-prefix rule (Group A):** the original "lone-column predicate → KEEP" framing was theoretically WRONG. SQLite serves `WHERE A=?` from a composite on `(A,B)` just as well as a single-col on `A`. EXPLAIN confirmed no planner regression for #3/#4/#6 (the lone `user_id` predicates at aave.rs:178/243/289) after dropping — the planner picks the serving composite. Drop all 9.
- **Selectivity heuristic (Group B):** the original hypothesis ("planner prefers full scan over a 50%-selectivity boolean index") is FALSE for SQLite — SQLite picks the index regardless of selectivity at every N tested (100/1000/10000, incl. after ANALYZE and 90/10 skew). The deciding evidence for #10 is NOT selectivity but the total absence of any `WHERE enabled` predicate. Rationale in the migration comment must cite "no read predicate uses this index," NOT "low selectivity."

## CRITICAL model-side change has TWO distinct mechanics (the trap)

The implementation has TWO different model-side fixes depending on the index origin:

### Group A (#1–#9): column-level `index=False` override — NOT alias-level
These 9 come from SQLAlchemy `index=True` on SHARED FK-column aliases (`ForeignKeyAaveAssetId`, `ForeignKeyTokenId`, `ForeignKeyAaveUserId`, `ForeignKeyAaveMarketId`, `ForeignKeyManagedPoolId`) reused across MULTIPLE tables. Naively stripping `index=True` from the alias would OVER-DROP the single-col index on sibling tables where that column is the **2nd** composite column (NOT a leftmost prefix) and is therefore genuinely needed (e.g. `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_asset_id`, `ix_pools_token1_id`, `ix_aave_v3_contracts_market_id`).

**Do NOT** strip `index=True` at the alias / shared-type level. Apply a column-level `index=False` override on each of the 9 specific columns in their model classes (`src/degenbot/database/models/aave.py` + `pools.py`). This neutralises the alias's `index=True` for that one column only.

### Group B (#10): delete the standalone `Index(...)` block — NOT a column override
This index is a deliberate hand-declared `Index("ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled", AaveV3UserCollateralConfig.enabled)` block in `src/degenbot/database/models/aave.py:558-561`. The column itself (`enabled: Mapped[bool]` at aave.py:523) has NO `index=True` to flip. Just delete the `Index(...)` declaration block. (Original creation already in `migrations/versions/9c411aeeb15e_aave_v3_extend_schema.py:101`.)

Sibling indexes NOT in either list above are correctly EXCLUDED — verify none regress (2nd-column / no-composite cases).

## The add: `ix_pools_chain_kind` (Group C, from spike-8)

### Why (the EXPLAIN evidence)
`pools` has `UNIQUE(address, chain)` (`schema_head.sql:343` `ix_liquidity_pool_address_chain`) but `address` is LEFTMOST → `WHERE chain=?` alone CANNOT use it (leftmost-prefix gap). Chain-scoped reads SCAN at all row counts (100/1000/10000, confirmed by EXPLAIN). A `pools(chain, kind)` composite flips them to `SEARCH (chain=?)` (lone-`chain` predicate, by leftmost prefix) or `SEARCH (chain=? AND kind=?)` (the `chain + kind IN (...)` predicate shape used by `fetch_v3_pool_addresses` + `fetch_all_liquidity_maps`). The composite is strictly better than `(chain)` alone for the codebase's actual predicate shapes.

### What benefits + what DOESN'T (honest scope)
- **Benefits:** the direct `pools` reads — `fetch_pools_for_chain` (read.rs:318), `fetch_v3_pool_addresses` (snapshot.rs:357), the `fetch_path_graph_edges` V2/V3 branch (pathfinding.rs:128), the token-degree queries (pathfinding.rs:251/254/263/270).
- **Does NOT benefit:** the `fetch_all_liquidity_maps` JOIN (snapshot.rs:263) — the planner picks `SCAN lp → SEARCH p USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)`, joining FROM the `liquidity_positions` driving table TO `pools` via the rowid PK. `WHERE p.chain=?` on the JOIN side does NOT benefit from `pools(chain, kind)`. (Flagged for honesty; the index is for the direct reads, not the join.)

### All construction-time (not hot path)
Every chain-scoped read on `pools` is construction-time (snapshot build at startup, path-graph build once per arb-cycle). None are per-tx/per-block. So the benefit is a one-time cost-reduction at construction, NOT ongoing throughput.

### Write-amplification cost (negligible)
`pools` is small (per-chain thousands, not millions; even mainnet Uniswap V3 is ~20-30K pools total). Registration is COLD (`INSERT` only on `PoolCreated` events, a handful per day). Write-amp on `pools` is negligible vs. the impl-1 drops (which cut write-amp on `liquidity_positions`-scale tables with millions of rows). Net write-amp: NEGATIVE (10 drops >> 1 add on a cold-write table).

### Model-side: hand-declared `Index(...)`, NOT `index=True` on `chain`
Follow the SAME pattern as the existing deliberate composites (`ix_liquidity_pool_address_chain`, `ix_liquidity_pools_token_ids` are hand-declared `Index(...)` blocks at `pools.py:87`/`:94`). The `chain: Mapped[int]` column (`pools.py:62`) has NO `index=True` (do NOT add one — that would create a single-col `ix_pools_chain` that the composite already subsumes). Add a hand-declared `Index(...)` block:

```python
# In src/degenbot/database/models/pools.py, after the ix_liquidity_pools_token_ids block (~line 98):
Index(
    "ix_pools_chain_kind",
    LiquidityPoolTable.chain,
    LiquidityPoolTable.kind,
)
```

NOT unique (no constraint semantic — `(chain, kind)` is nowhere near unique).

### `pool_managers` DEFERRED (out of scope)
V4 has parallel chain-scoped reads on `pool_managers` (`fetch_path_graph_edges` V4, `fetch_v4_pool_hashes`, `fetch_all_liquidity_maps` V4) with the same leftmost-prefix gap (`UNIQUE(address, chain)`, `address` leftmost). By symmetry a `pool_managers(chain)` index would help — BUT `pool_managers` is even smaller than `pools` (one pool-manager per chain per protocol — tens of rows, not thousands). The absolute read benefit is microseconds; not worth a migration op. Defer; add only if a future workload proves otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/<new_rev>.py` whose `upgrade()` is 10× `op.drop_index(...)` (Groups A+B) **+ 1× `op.create_index("ix_pools_chain_kind", "pools", ["chain", "kind"])`** (Group C), and whose `downgrade()` is the inverse (1× `op.drop_index("ix_pools_chain_kind")` + 10× `op.create_index(...)` mirroring the original definitions in `schema_head.sql`). Migration comment cites the corrected rationale (leftmost-prefix rule for Group A; "no read predicate" for Group B — NOT "low selectivity"; "chain-scoped reads SCAN, composite serves `chain` + `chain+kind`" for Group C).
- [ ] `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`: 10 `CREATE INDEX ix_...` lines removed (Group A 9 lines + the Group B line at schema_head.sql:321); the serving UNIQUE/composite `CREATE INDEX` lines unchanged; **+ add `CREATE INDEX ix_pools_chain_kind ON pools (chain, kind);`** after line 344 (near the other `pools` indexes).
- [ ] `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`: `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bumped to the new revision id (one bump for all 11 ops).
- [ ] `src/degenbot/database/models/aave.py`:
  - column-level `index=False` on each of the 9 Group-A columns (collateral_positions.user_id, debt_positions.user_id, user_collateral_configs.user_id, asset_configs.asset_id, assets.underlying_asset_id, emode_categories.market_id). Aliases themselves untouched.
  - delete the standalone `Index("ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled", ...)` block at aave.py:558-561 (Group B #10).
- [ ] `src/degenbot/database/models/pools.py`: column-level `index=False` on `LiquidityPoolTable.token0_id`; **+ add hand-declared `Index("ix_pools_chain_kind", LiquidityPoolTable.chain, LiquidityPoolTable.kind)` block** (NOT `index=True` on `chain`) after the `ix_liquidity_pools_token_ids` block (~line 98).
- [ ] `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` spot-check on a fresh DB (post-migration): for representative lone-column lookups (aave.rs:178, 243, 289; read.rs:416, 436), the planner picks the serving composite. Document the 5 plans in the completion summary.
- [ ] No sibling single-col index (`ix_pools_token1_id`, `ix_aave_v3_collateral_positions_asset_id`, `ix_aave_v3_contracts_market_id`) affected — verify via `sqlite_master` diff on a fresh DB.
- [ ] Group C: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT address FROM pools WHERE chain=?1 AND kind IN ('uniswap_v3','sushiswap_v3','pancakeswap_v3','aerodrome_v3')` returns `SEARCH USING INDEX ix_pools_chain_kind (chain=? AND kind=?)` (not SCAN).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (incl. cutover `ensure_schema` / discovery schema-parity tests)
- `just test-rust` (degenbot-db heal + writer parity tests assert schema shape)
- `just lint-rust` + `just format`
- Manual: `sqlite3 <fresh.db> ".indexes"` shows the 10 gone + siblings intact.
- Manual: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT ... WHERE managed_pool_id=?` on `managed_pool_liquidity_positions` returns the composite seek.
- Manual: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT asset_id FROM aave_v3_user_collateral_configs WHERE user_id=?` still returns `USING INDEX ix_aave_user_collateral_config_user_asset` (the #10 `enabled` index was never the one serving this query).
- Manual: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT address FROM pools WHERE chain=? AND kind IN (...)` returns `SEARCH USING INDEX ix_pools_chain_kind`.

## Sequencing + Bundling decision
Bundled ULMN4U (spike-2) + `ix_pools_chain_kind` (spike-8) into this single migration (one `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bump carrying all 10 drops + 1 add = 11 index-DDL ops) rather than shipping three revisions. Sequenced after the three spikes (`R3SR7L`, `ULMN4U`, spike-8), all done.

## Gating
0.6.x-safe (index drop via Alembic migration). NOT gated to 0.7.

data.title: Retire web3py: wire the simulation & RPC Rust core through the cockpit
data.body:
The Architectural Vision (AGENTS.md) names two infrastructure pieces still
un-routed through the Rust core: **simulation** and **RPC**. This epic closes
both, then completes web3py's removal as a runtime dependency. It is one graph
so a follow-up session inherits the full scope: the boundary work (Pass A)
delivers the architectural win; the type/exception sweep (Pass B) drops the
`web3` dependency from `pyproject.toml`. web3py stops being on any hot path
after Pass A — Pass B deletes the dependency without changing behavior.

Two candidates drive Pass A:

- **Candidate 1 — wire the stranded `degenbot-simulation` crate through the
  cockpit.** A complete 3660-line Rust port (`simulate_one`,
  `dispatch_profitable_results`, `eth_simulateV1` dispatch, payload, calldata)
  exists with **zero consumers** — no Cargo dep from `degenbot-python`, no
  `c_api` entry, no pyi symbol. Meanwhile `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
  runs its own ~1900-line parallel Python copy (`simulate_one` = 846 lines,
  `dispatch_profitable_results` = 1055 lines). Sub-steps B (PyO3 seam) + C
  (route + delete the Python copy) were never executed. The crate's own module
  docs cite task IDs and reference the Python line ranges they port.
- **Candidate 2 — make `degenbot-rpc` the single RPC owner.** `PyBotIo` (the
  pyclass I/O façade pool builders receive) currently holds `Py<PyAny>` and
  GIL-round-trips every `get_block`/`call`/`get_logs` into the Python
  `ProviderAdapter` facade. The crate's own top-of-file doc (py_bot_io.rs:1–24)
  names this as the **14b/14c cutover**: swap the held `Py<PyAny>` for a direct
  `AlloyProvider` field + native method bodies. Separately, the polymorphic
  `ProviderAdapter`/`AsyncProviderAdapter` facade wraps three backends
  (`_Web3Adapter`/`_AlloyAdapter`/`_OfflineAdapter`); only alloy is real (and
  the async path is **already alloy-only**). Retire the wrapper + web3 backend;
  `Bot`/`AsyncBot` take the `AlloyProvider`/`AsyncAlloyProvider` pyclass
  directly.

Pass B is the mechanical-but-broad sweep that removes the `web3 ~= 7.14`
runtime dependency: replace `web3.types`/`web3.exceptions` imports with native
degenbot types/exceptions (~48 files), port `AnvilFork` + the two snapshot
modules off `Web3()`, and replace `web3.keccak(text=...)` selector sites with
`sol!`-typed calls or a degenbot keccak helper.

## Non-goals

- **Porting the DB-aware pool updaters to Rust.** The 5 pool hot-sync
  `make_request` sites in the example (reserves/slot0/liquidity/code — all
  sim-fail *diagnostics*, `try/except: pass`) are not pool-updater work; they
  route to existing typed `PyBotIo` fetchers in Pass A. The actual per-block
  pool-state updater migration is a separate Vision-named future epic.
- **Retiring the `AsyncProviderAdapter` Python class if residual
  `make_request` consumers remain.** Where Python still needs raw
  `make_request` after candidates 1+2 (AnvilFork until C3), the alloy pyclass
  already exposes `make_request` natively — Python calls the pyclass directly.
  The Python wrapper class retires in B4; the pyclass is the consumer's handle.
- **A backwards-compatibility layer for the retired wrapper / web3 backend.**
  AGENTS.md forbids it; breaking changes are scoped to the next release.
- **The Alembic/SQLAlchemy 0.7 kill list** (AGENTS.md) is unrelated and
  untouched.

## Constraints

- **Standalone-Rust-core constraint (AGENTS.md).** `degenbot-rpc` and
  `degenbot-simulation` are core crates — zero `pyo3` (enforced by
  `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`). No task may add `pyo3` to a core crate.
  `#[pyclass]`/`#[pyfunction]` live only in `degenbot-python`.
- **Never hold the `Dispatcher` lock across `.await`s.** The submission seam's
  convention (submit.rs:212). The sim seam's `&mut PathSuppression` touches are
  bookends (pre-filter + post-record) around the fan-out; the cutover extracts
  `PathSuppression` into its own `Arc<Mutex<…>>` so the sim seam holds *that*
  lock, not the `Dispatcher` lock, across the fan-out. See Key Decision 1.
- **PyO3 seam = arg-extract → GIL release → core call → result wrap.** No
  business logic in the wrapper layer (three-layer-transition.md §3.2). Mirror
  the existing `submission/` subtree exactly.
- **Red/Green TDD** for all behavioral changes (AGENTS.md).
- **The uv editable-installed `.so` is rebuilt by `uv` (not `cargo build`).**
  Do NOT manually rebuild with `cargo build` after Rust changes. Recovery:
  `uv sync --reinstall-package degenbot`.

## Key decisions (resolved during planning)

1. **`PathSuppression` is extracted out of `Dispatcher` into a standalone
   `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`.** It is currently an inline field of
   `Dispatcher` (not separately `Arc`'d), and `is_suppressed` takes `&mut self`
   (records the retry block on read). The submission crate's own doc comment
   on `PathSuppression` (dispatcher.rs:138) sanctions this: it is "owned by
   the Simulation epic (`5LLJHX` `5FB5MW`) per the `4JGPDW` scope — this module
   REFERENCES its shape." `PyDispatcher` holds **both**
   `Arc<Mutex<Dispatcher>>` and `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`. The sim seam
   takes the latter directly, so it never locks the `Dispatcher` across the
   sim fan-out (matching the submission seam convention). Submission stays
   unaffected: it touches `path_suppression` only via the same
   `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`.
2. **The sim seam's output is the submission seam's input shape.**
   `dispatch_profitable_py` emits `list[PySubmitCandidate]` directly (the
   `SimResult → PySubmitCandidate` join happens at result-wrap time in the
   wrapper, which has `SimulateContext.executor_address` + the originating
   candidate's `path_info` hops for `path_pools`). `PySimResult` stays
   internal. `gas_unprofitable` collapses to a count (the cockpit only logs
   it). This is the ergonomic win: the cockpit's per-block loop chains
   `dispatch_profitable_py → dispatch_and_submit_py` with no field reshuffling.
3. **`sol!` static ABI adoption** (per https://alloy.rs/guides/static-dynamic-abi-in-alloy/).
   `PyBotIo`'s typed fetchers currently hand-roll selectors + byte-decode.
   Pass A adopts `sol! { function getReserves() …; }` + `#[sol(rpc)]` in
   `degenbot-rpc` for the handful of fetcher ABIs (`getReserves`/`slot0`/
   `liquidity`/`balanceOf`/`totalSupply`/`allowance`), giving compile-time-safe
   typed calls (~10× faster than ethers, zero JSON). Not a blocker for web3py
   retirement (the fetchers already work); adopted as the ergonomic upgrade the
   boundary work implies.
4. **Scope split: Pass A (boundary) vs Pass B (type/exception sweep).** Pass A
   retires web3py from the runtime provider path and the example. Pass B drops
   the `web3` dependency. They are sequenced (A before B) so the ~48-file
   type/exception sweep follows the architectural win, not blocks it.
5. **The 4 example sim-fail diagnostic `make_request` sites (L2125–2180) route
   to existing `PyBotIo` typed fetchers** (`fetch_v2_reserves`,
   `fetch_v3_slot0_liquidity`), not to new `make_request` exposure. They are
   `try/except: pass` log lines, never load-bearing.

## Risk (highest-risk tasks)

- **A3 (`PathSuppression` extraction)** — touches the submission crate's
  `Dispatcher`. Mitigation: the doc comment sanctions it; TDD on the
  submission seam; the extractor keeps submission's access via the shared
  `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`.
- **B4 (retire the wrapper)** — broad blast radius on `Bot`/`AsyncBot`
  constructors + every construction site. Mitigated by B6 (test migration)
  proving correctness before C6 (dep removal) lands.
- **C3 (AnvilFork off web3)** — anvil RPC (`evm_mine`/`anvil_reset`/
  `evm_revert`/`evm_snapshot`) over alloy `make_request`; IPC behavior parity.
  Mitigation: keep AnvilFork's anvil *process* management as-is; only swap the
  IPC client from web3 to alloy.

## Existing ergo references

- The simulation crate's module docs cite simulation-epic task IDs `5LLJHX` /
  `5FB5MW` and scope `4JGPDW`. If those tasks exist in `.ergo`, the candidate-1
  tasks here are their PyO3-seam + routing completion (the unfinished sub-steps
  B + C). Reconcile/ reparent if appropriate during A1.

> Non-actionable narrative holder. The full epic vision, non-goals,
> constraints, key decisions, and risk assessment live in
> `.ergo/plan-retire-web3py-sim-rpc-core.md` (committed to the repo). This
> task exists only because `ergo plan --file` turns the leading markdown
> body into a child; it has no implementation work. See tasks A1–C6.

data.title: fix(db): delete stale liquidity rows on drained pool (parity with Python)
data.body:
# fix(db): delete stale liquidity rows on drained pool (parity with Python)

## This is a CORRECTNESS bug, not a perf issue
Surfaced during the F4N6DX perf review but it is a real data-correctness bug: ghost liquidity rows linger indefinitely on a fully-drained pool, then get re-read into the next apply's `tick_data` with stale non-zero liquidity → wrong base state → **compounding corruption**.

## Validated by spike `DWGD36` (research complete, verdict: INTENT A — real bug, fix the code)

### Root cause
`delete_stale_rows` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs`) early-returns `Ok(())` on `live_keys.is_empty()`, skipping the delete entirely:

```rust
if live_keys.is_empty() {
    // No live keys → delete ALL rows for this pool.
    return Ok(());   // ← DELETES NOTHING — contradicts the comment
}
// ... chunked `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1 AND {key_col} NOT IN (...)`
```

The comment claims "delete ALL"; the code deletes nothing. The pre-built `sql` passed by callers uses `NOT IN ({placeholders})` which would be a syntax error on empty input, so the early-return was likely added to avoid that — but it silently dropped the "delete all" semantic.

### Python parity oracle (the deciding evidence)
`0a431b97^:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py`, `apply_v3_liquidity_updates`:
```python
db_ticks = {position.tick for position in pool_in_db.liquidity_positions}
helper_ticks = set(current_tick_data)
if ticks_to_drop := db_ticks - helper_ticks:
    session.execute(delete(...).where(...pool_id..., .tick.in_(ticks_to_drop)))
```
On a drained pool: `helper_ticks = set()` → `ticks_to_drop = db_ticks - set() = db_ticks` (ALL existing rows) → truthy → **Python DELETES ALL existing tick rows**. Init-maps use the same complement-with-truthy pattern (`words_to_drop := db_words - helper_words`, filtered by `map_.bitmap != 0`). V4 mirrors V3 exactly. **Python deletes all on empty-live; Rust deletes nothing — pure parity violation.** The comment is RIGHT; the code is WRONG.

### Reachability (not a hypothetical edge case)
cl-math prunes zero-gross ticks (`rust/crates/degenbot-cl-math/src/cl_lib/liquidity_mapping.rs:250-253`): `if new_liquidity_gross == U128::ZERO { tick_data.remove(&current_tick); flip_tick(&mut tick_bitmap, ...); continue; }`. A pool fully drained (all positions burned to zero) → every tick removed from `tick_data` → `live_ticks = tick_data.keys().copied().collect()` is EMPTY in `persist_v3` → `delete_stale_v3_positions_on_conn(conn, pool_id, &[])` → the early-return triggers. cl-math's `flip_tick` zeros bitmap bits → empty `live_words` filtered by `bw.bitmap != U256::ZERO` → init-map delete early-returns too. A fully-drained pool is a normal market operation (a pool winding down).

### Downstream effect (compounding corruption)
Ghost rows are read back on the NEXT chunk's apply via `fetch_v3_liquidity_map_on_conn` (`liquidity_updater.rs:295`, `SELECT tick, liquidity_gross, liquidity_net FROM {LIQUIDITY_POSITIONS} WHERE pool_id = ?1`) called at `apply_v3_liquidity_updates_on_conn:444` → ghost rows reconstituted into `tick_data` with stale non-zero `liquidity_gross`/`liquidity_net` → liquidity map is WRONG → next apply mutates a WRONG base → compounding corruption. V4 mirror at line 502. Any swap-simulation / price consumer reading `fetch_v3/v4_liquidity_map` gets ghost ticks with stale liquidity → incorrect swap math.

### Why the existing parity test missed it
`rust/crates/degenbot-db/tests/fixtures/generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py:426-429` exercises a PARTIAL drain (one tick dropped via a 1.3M Burn; the second tick left live) → `live_ticks` non-empty → the early-return does not trigger. The empty-live path has zero coverage.

## The fix (small, self-contained)

Restructure `delete_stale_rows` to branch on `live_keys.is_empty()`:
- **empty** → `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col} = ?1` (no `NOT IN` clause; bind only `id_value`). This is the "delete all rows for this pool" semantic the comment always claimed.
- **non-empty** → the existing chunked `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1 AND {key_col} NOT IN (...)` path (unchanged).

Cleanest minimal shape: change `delete_stale_rows`'s signature to accept `(conn, table, id_col, key_col, id_value, live_keys)` instead of a pre-built `sql` string, and build the appropriate SQL internally. The 4 callers (`delete_stale_v3/v4_positions_on_conn` + `delete_stale_v3/v4_init_maps_on_conn`) already know these identifiers, so they pass table/id_col/key_col instead of a pre-built string. This:
- makes the empty/non-empty branch natural (no syntax-error avoidance),
- removes the `sql_placeholders_for`-replace hack in the chunk loop (a side-benefit overlap with spike `7UVVJI` — note this so 7UVVJI's scope can shrink to whatever remains),
- does NOT touch the `upsert_*_on_conn` early-returns (those ARE correct: empty `tick_data` → nothing to upsert).

### Call sites to change
- The 4 `delete_stale_*_on_conn` fns in `DegenbotDb` impl (`liquidity_updater.rs`): V3 positions, V3 init-maps, V4 positions, V4 init-maps.
- The `persist_v3`/`persist_v4` callers are UNCHANGED — they pass `live_ticks`/`live_words` as before.

### Do NOT touch
- `upsert_v3/v4_liquidity_positions_on_conn` early-return on `tick_data.is_empty()` — CORRECT (nothing to upsert). Only the DELETE path is bugged.

## TDD red-green order (IMPORTANT — do in this order)

1. **First regenerate the parity fixture from Python (the source of truth).** Extend `rust/crates/degenbot-db/tests/fixtures/generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py` with a FULL-DRAIN event sequence: a Mint that initializes 2 ticks, then Burns that drive BOTH ticks' gross to zero → `tick_data` empties → `live_ticks` empty. Regenerate `liquidity_updater_v3_expected.json` + `liquidity_updater_v4_expected.json` — these assert EMPTY positions/init-maps tables for the drained pool (matching the Python oracle's complement-delete-all semantics).
2. **Run the Rust parity test against the regenerated fixture** → it FAILS (ghost rows vs expected empty) — this is the RED.
3. **Apply the Rust fix** (restructure `delete_stale_rows` + 4 callers).
4. **Run again** → PASSES — GREEN.
5. **Add a focused direct in-crate Rust test** (`liquidity_updater.rs::mod tests` or a `tests/` integration test): build an in-memory DB, seed a pool with N tick rows, apply events that zero all ticks (`live_ticks` empty), assert `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM liquidity_positions WHERE pool_id=?` == 0 (and `initialization_maps`). Direct repro of the reachability path, independent of the parity fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `delete_stale_rows` restructured to branch on `live_keys.is_empty()` → empty issues `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1`, non-empty uses the chunked `NOT IN` path.
- [ ] Signature changed to `(conn, table, id_col, key_col, id_value, live_keys)`; 4 `delete_stale_*_on_conn` call sites updated.
- [ ] `upsert_*_on_conn` early-returns UNCHANGED (verified by reading the diff — no edits to those fns).
- [ ] Parity fixture regenerated from Python (full-drain event seq) + the regenerated `*_expected.json` assert empty tables for the drained pool.
- [ ] Rust parity test passes post-fix (and was demonstrably RED pre-fix — note the failing-plan output in the completion summary, or regenerate-then-`git stash`-the-fix to prove RED).
- [ ] New direct in-crate repro test: draining a seeded pool to zero → `COUNT(*) == 0` for both `liquidity_positions` and `initialization_maps` (V3 + V4 managed variants).
- [ ] The existing partial-drain parity case (`generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py:426-429`) still passes — no regression.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-db` green (incl. new parity case + new direct repro test).
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater` green (the chunk-atomicity contract test from BHF5BC + no-duplicate-writer from JZLTES — no write-path regression).
- `just test-python` green (`tests/rust/test_liquidity_updater_seam.py` parity test now covers full-drain).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings` clean (CI gate).
- `just test-rust` + `just test-python` + `just lint-rust` + `just format`.

## Sequencing + epic impact
- **Sequence `7UVVJI` (cosmetic rewrite of `liquidity_updater.rs`) AFTER this bugfix lands.** 7UVVJI must rewrite CORRECT code. Additionally, this fix's signature change (pre-built sql → table/id_col/key_col args) overlaps with 7UVVJI's "tidy the chunked placeholder rebuild" scope — note in 7UVVJI's task that the `sql_placeholders_for`-replace hack may already be gone after this fix, so 7UVVJI's scope may shrink.
- This is a correctness bug, not a perf issue, despite living in the F4N6DX perf epic. Small + self-contained (one helper + 4 callers + tests).

## Gating
0.6.x-safe (code fix, no schema change). NOT gated to 0.7. **Higher priority than the perf spikes** — correctness bug that compounds on every drained-pool apply.

## 6SRJRL — fix(db): delete stale liquidity rows on drained pool — DONE

### The bug
`delete_stale_rows` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs`) early-returned `Ok(())` on `live_keys.is_empty()`, deleting **nothing**, contradicting its own "delete ALL rows" comment. On a fully-drained pool (every tick pruned from `tick_data` → `live_ticks`/`live_words` empty in `persist_v3`/`persist_v4`), the stale seed rows lingered as ghosts and were re-read into the NEXT apply's base via `fetch_v3/v4_liquidity_map_on_conn` → compounding corruption. The early-return existed to dodge the `NOT IN ()` empty-placeholder SQL syntax error.

### The fix
Restructured `delete_stale_rows`'s signature from `(conn, sql, id_value, live_keys)` to `(conn, table, id_col, key_col, id_value, live_keys)`; it builds the SQL internally:
- **empty `live_keys`** → `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col} = ?1` (bare delete-all, no `NOT IN`).
- **non-empty** → the existing chunked `... NOT IN (...)` path (rebuilds placeholders per chunk — no more pre-built-`sql_placeholders_for`-`.replace` hack; side-benefit overlap with spike `7UVVJI`, whose scope can now shrink).

Updated the 4 callers (`delete_stale_v3/v4_positions_on_conn`, `delete_stale_v3/v4_init_maps_on_conn`) to pass table/id_col/key_col instead of a pre-built SQL string. `upsert_*_on_conn` early-returns UNCHANGED (verified — no edits to those fns).

### TDD (RED → GREEN)
RED-first via **direct in-crate Rust tests** (independent of the now-Rust-delegating Python shell — see "Oracle note" below). 2 levels × 2 variants = 4 new tests:
- `delete_stale_v3/v4_empty_live_deletes_all_rows` — direct call with `&[]` after seeding N tick/init-map rows → assert `COUNT(*) == 0`.
- `apply_v3/v4_full_drain_empties_tables_and_stamps_marker` — end-to-end through the public `apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates`: seed a position, Mint grows it + opens a second pair, two Burns fully drain EVERY tick (partial-drain `NOT IN` path exercised first via the first burn, full drain via the second) → assert positions + init-maps `COUNT(*) == 0` + marker stamped to the last event.

**RED evidence (pre-fix):** all 4 failed with `assertion left == right failed: left: 2, right: 0` (ghost rows = seeded `{-10, 10}` lingered; init-maps `{word -1, word 0}` lingered).
**GREEN (post-fix):** all 4 pass — `COUNT(*) == 0` for both positions + init-maps, V3 marker `(Some(102), Some(0))`, V4 marker `(Some(202), Some(0))`.

### Oracle note (deviation from the task body)
The task body assumed regenerating the parity fixture's `*_expected.json` from the Python generator would yield an independent (correct, empty) full-drain oracle. **That assumption no longer holds:** after task QJSCA5, `apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` in `cli/pool_updater_configs.py` are thin decode shells that delegate to the Rust core (`db_apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates`). Regenerating the fixture now runs the same (buggy-then-fixed) Rust under test, so it is no longer an independent oracle for this code path. (Also: the committed generator has a stale import `from degenbot.cli.pool import ...` — the symbols moved to `cli.pool_updater_configs`; the committed `*_expected.json` are frozen from a pre-migration independent Python implementation and remain valid as the partial-drain baseline.)

Therefore the RED was established via the **direct in-crate Rust tests** (fully independent of the delegating Python), which is exactly the task's step-5 deliverable. The existing frozen partial-drain parity fixture (`tests/liquidity_updater_parity.rs` + `tests/rust/test_liquidity_updater_seam.py`) is UNCHANGED and still passes — it continues to exercise the `NOT IN` partial-drain delete path (no regression). The `7UVVJI` cosmetic-rewrite task can note that the `sql_placeholders_for`-`.replace` hack is already gone.

### Validation gates (all green)
- `cargo test -p degenbot-db` — incl. 4 new tests + frozen parity test.
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater` — chunk-atomicity + no-duplicate-writer contracts intact.
- `just test-python` — 3223 passed, 30 skipped (incl. `test_liquidity_updater_seam.py` partial-drain parity).
- `just test-rust` — full suite green.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings` — clean (CI gate).
- `just lint-rust` + `just format` — clean.

### Orphaned / out-of-scope notes
- The committed generator's stale import + the now-circular Python-oracle nature of the full-drain fixture path are NOT fixed here (separate concern; 0.6.x-safe generator repair would invite silent corruption of the frozen independent partial-drain fixture). Left as-is per AGENTS.md's orphaned-symbol discipline.
- Files changed: `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs` only.

data.title: run_aave_update orchestrator: Aave RPC fetch+decode+apply+commit loop (mirror run_pool_update)
data.body:
## Goal
- Build the **`run_aave_update` Rust orchestrator** — the RPC-owning chunk loop that mirrors `run_pool_update` (`rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/run.rs:529`). Owns, per chunk: RPC fetch of Aave V3 events (GIL-free async, **no events cross the PyO3 boundary** — user decision 1a) → ABI decode into `AaveChunkEvent` (the typed enum from `WRUNAAVE`) → `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn(&tx)` under ONE `rusqlite::Transaction` → commit → stamp `last_update_block`. Exposed to Python via ONE `#[pyfunction] run_aave_update(...)` (mirror `run_pool_update` registration).

## Precedent (the proven shape to mirror exactly)
- `run_pool_update(database_path, chain_id, to_block, chunk_size, rpc_url, progress_callback, cancel_handle)` — `rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/run.rs:529`. Takes `rpc_url` (NOT events). Fetches the chain tip itself via `provider.get_block_number()`. Uses `degenbot_rpc::AlloyProvider` + `LogFetcher` for GIL-free async event fetch. Decodes into typed `ChunkInputs`. Calls `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn(&tx, ...)` under one `Transaction` opened via `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(database_path)`. Commits per chunk. Stamps `last_update_block` as the last write.
- The hard-to-test RPC boundary (fetch + decode) is separated from the pure transaction-semantics core (`apply_chunk_writes_on_conn`) precisely so the core is fixture-testable (run.rs module doc lines 36-41). Mirror this split.
- Python caller `cli/pool.py:152` passes only `rpc_url` — no events cross the boundary.

## Scope
1. **Aave V3 RPC fetch + ABI decode.** Aave V3 `IPool` event signatures for the event types the apply fns handle (`CollateralConfigurationChanged`, `EModeCategoryAdded`, `EModeAssetCategoryChanged`, `AssetCollateralInEmodeChanged`, `ReserveUsedAsCollateralEnabled`/`Disabled`, `UserEModeSet`, `PriceOracleUpdated`, `AssetSourceUpdated`, + the reserve-data updates the existing Python `_process_*` handlers cover). Mirror `fetch_v4_liquidity_logs_grouped` / `LogFetcher`. Aave V3 ABI lives in `degenbot-abi` if present, else add to the new `degenbot-aave-updater` crate (discover; flag if `degenbot-abi` is the wrong home).
2. **`run_aave_update(database_path, chain_id, market_id, to_block, chunk_size, rpc_url, progress_callback, cancel_handle) -> AaveUpdateReport`** — the orchestrator. Per market per chunk: fetch+decode → `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn(&tx, market_id, &events, chunk_end)` → commit → stamp. ONE `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes` per chunk, ONE `Transaction`. SIGINT handling via `cancel_handle` (mirror `cli/pool.py`'s `_on_sigint` + the core's cancel-detection).
3. **`#[pyfunction] run_aave_update`** in `degenbot-python/src/db/aave.rs` (or a new `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/aave_updater.rs` mirroring how pool-updater bindings are organized — discover the precedent). `py.detach()` around the whole loop (GIL released for RPC + DB I/O; only re-acquired to fire `progress_callback` — mirror `run_pool_update`'s `ProgressCallback` bridge from the liquidity_updater cutover). Registered in `c_api.rs`.
4. `.pyi` stub for `run_aave_update`.

## §3.4 atomicity invariant
- ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Failure mid-chunk → drop the tx → whole chunk reverts → `last_update_block` unchanged → restart re-processes clean. Idempotent re-run (a committed chunk's `last_update_block` is past the chunk start → skipped). Mirror run.rs doc lines 21-32.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `run_aave_update(...)` exists in `degenbot-aave-updater`, takes `rpc_url` (NOT events), fetches + decodes Aave V3 events itself, calls `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`, commits per chunk, stamps `last_update_block`.
- [ ] `#[pyfunction] run_aave_update` registered in `c_api.rs`; `.pyi` stub complete; `py.detach()` around the loop; `progress_callback` bridge mirrors the liquidity_updater precedent.
- [ ] `rg "events:|logs:|Vec<.*Event>" rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/` for any Aave-event-list pyfunction arg returns empty (no events cross the FFI boundary).
- [ ] Integration test mirror the precedent's RPC-integration shape (live RPC gated behind `#[ignore]` / anvil fork if present, OR a fixture-RPC-replay harness if the precedent has one — discover).
- [ ] `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green (the orchestrator is in `degenbot-aave-updater`, zero `pyo3`; only the `#[pyfunction]` is in `degenbot-python`).

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just format`.

## Non-goals
- The pure transactional apply core → `WRUNAAVE` (this task depends on it).
- Python `aave_update` shell cutover + deletion of the old writer pipeline → `SHELLAAVE`.
- §4.2 red-green parity gate → `U5YIBG`.
- The `aave_update` driver's `--dry-run` / `verify_all` / `backup_interval` orchestration — those stay in the Python shell (`SHELLAAVE`), `run_aave_update` is the per-market chunk engine the shell drives. Flag if a control feature can't stay in the shell cleanly.

## Dependencies
- `WRUNAAVE` (the apply core this orchestrator calls).
- `degenbot_rpc` (the RPC primitive — already a workspace crate, used by the pool updater).
- Depended on by: `SHELLAAVE`.

data.title: Route Python pub/sub consumers (engine_registry/CLI/test fakes) through the PySubscriberAdapter seam; consumer reaction bodies stay Python
data.body:
## Goal
- Convert the Python **pub/sub consumers** (classes/functions that subscribe to a `Publisher` to drive an update loop) into delegating shells that subscribe through the Rust `PoolStateSubscriber` seam (sibling mechanism task) instead of the Python `PublisherMixin`. These are the Python-orchestration consumers: the `FakeSubscriber` test helper pattern, the `engine_registry` subscribe-to-engine wiring, and any pool-state-driven update hooks. They stay **Python** (orchestration), but their *subscription* routes through Rust.

## Context
- Scope task: `I7KVKM` (Epic `2K2JP4`). Rubric disposition: **stays-python** (the consumers are orchestration/drivers), with their subscription *call* routed through the sibling Rust seam.
- §2.1 "Keep in Python" criteria: these consumers orchestrate update loops (subscribe → react → drive further Python I/O) — orchestration is a shell concern; the *mechanism* they use is the Rust one (sibling task). eco: they couple to Python async/CLI orchestration.
- KEY DISTINCTION (orchestrator's): MECHANISM = the dispatch/listener infra (sibling task, `port-now`). CONSUMERS = these orchestration subscribers (`stays-python`, this task routes their subscribe call only).
- Deps: sibling mechanism task (the `PySubscriberAdapter` / `subscribe_to_pool` seam they register through).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The Python consumer subscribe callsites (e.g. `engine_registry` WS subscribe, CLI update-loop subscriptions, `FakeSubscriber.subscribe` in tests) call the Rust seam (`PySubscriberAdapter`) when subscribing to a Rust-owned pool/token, instead of `Publisher.subscribe`.
- The consumer *reaction* bodies (what `notify` does — drive an update, record for assertion, etc.) stay Python and unchanged.
- `tests/fakes/subscribers.py::FakeSubscriber` updated to subscribe via the Rust seam when targeting a Rust-owned publisher (or kept dual-mode for Python-only publishers); `tests/types/test_publisher_mixin.py` + `test_pool_protocols.py` parity preserved.
- Parity (§4.2): consumers receive notifications in the same order/shape via the Rust seam as via the prior Python path.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (`tests/types/*`, `tests/fakes/`, `tests/arbitrage/*` consumer suites), `just test-rust-python`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The Rust pub/sub mechanism + `PySubscriberAdapter` (sibling task).
- The RPC WebSocket `eth_subscribe` subscribe loops (`engine_registry.subscribe`, `bot.py subscribe_blocks/logs`) — separate RPC concern.
- Porting consumer orchestration logic itself to Rust (it stays Python by disposition).

data.title: Unified verification policy for Rust updaters
4. V3 verify-core: `verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain` (degenbot-pool-updater)
data.body:
## Goal
- Compare a V3 pool's in-memory `(tick_data, tick_bitmap)` against on-chain `ticks(int24)`/`tickBitmap(int16)` at `block_number`; return a named divergence list. TDD-red-first against the pure mapping helper.
## Context
- `pub async fn verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain(provider, pool_address, tick_spacing, tick_data, tick_bitmap, block_number, scope: VerifyScope) -> Result<Vec<LiquidityDivergence>, RunError>` where `VerifyScope { ticks: &[i32] }` (Touched) or `All` derives the full tick set from `tick_data.keys()` + the bitmap-word set from `tick_bitmap`.
- On-chain: `ticks(tick)` returns `(uint128 gross, int128 net, …, bool initialized)`. Decode gross (word 0) + net (word 1); ignore init-flag except that a reverted/uninitialized tick (return len 0 / revert ⇒ `success=false`) means "tick absent on-chain" — if the in-memory map has the tick OR the bitmap has the bit set, that's a divergence (`ExtraTick`/`BitmapSetButUninitialized`).
- `tickBitmap(word)` → `uint256`; compare to `tick_bitmap[word].bitmap` (re-derive the word set from the in-memory ticks using `get_tick_word_and_bit_position(tick, tick_spacing)` so a tick with a set bit but no on-chain init is caught).
- Extract a pure `map_verify_results(expected: &TickData + &TickBitmap, scope, chain_results) -> Vec<LiquidityDivergence>` so the divergence logic is unit-testable offline (mirror the aave verify's `result_to_u256` + stride-map pattern). The on-chain batch is `multicall3_batch(provider, &calls, Some(block_number))`.
- Reuse the aave verify's `parse_u256`/`decode_uint256_return`/`build_call_data` shape (copy — they're 10-line helpers; don't create a shared dep).
- `LiquidityDivergence` enum variants: `TickGross`, `TickNet`, `BitmapWord`, `ExtraTick` (in-memory tick the chain lacks), `MissingTick` (chain tick the in-memory map lacks, when scope=All).
## Acceptance Criteria
- `verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain` returns `[]` when the in-memory map matches on-chain; non-empty named divergences otherwise.
- Pure `map_verify_results` unit-tested offline (no RPC) for each variant + the revert⇒absent mapping.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` passes (zero pyo3 in degenbot-pool-updater).
## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings`.

V3 verify-core done. `verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain(provider, pool_address, computed, block_number)` in degenbot-pool-updater/src/verify.rs compares the FULL in-memory (tick_data, tick_bitmap) against on-chain `ticks(int24)`/`tickBitmap(int16)` at block_number via multicall3_batch. Pure offline-testable helpers (ticks_calldata w/ sign-extension, tick_bitmap_calldata, decode_ticks_return, decode_bitmap_return, compare_tick, compare_bitmap_word) validated against an independent alloy DynSolValue encoder; LiquidityDivergence variants (TickGross/TickNet/BitmapWord/TickCallReverted/BitmapCallReverted). The ghost-row catch (in-memory gross 500, on-chain 0 -> TickGross) + drained-pool e2e comparison test GREEN.

Re-exported ComputedLiquidityUpdate + ApplyLiquidityAtTick/ApplyBitmapAtWord (cl-math U128/I256 flavor, aliased to dodge the snapshot U256-name collision) at degenbot-db root so the verifier has no direct cl-math dep (keeps the resolver clean under the rusqlite >=0.31 <1.0 bump). lib.rs re-exports verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain + LiquidityDivergence. clippy --all-features --deny warnings clean; 41 pool-updater tests pass; just check-no-pyo3-in-cores clean.

data.title: spike: remove redundant client sort in fetch_all_liquidity_maps V3
data.body:
# spike: remove redundant client sort in fetch_all_liquidity_maps V3

## Goal
- Confirm the V3 branch of `fetch_all_liquidity_maps` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/snapshot.rs`) does a redundant client-side re-sort that the SQL `ORDER BY` already satisfies, and that removing it preserves byte-identical parity vs the Python oracle.

## Hypothesis
The V3 SQL already does `ORDER BY p.address, lp.tick`. The Rust then loads rows into a `HashMap<Address, TickMap>`, then RE-SORTS the address keys (`keys.sort_by_key(|a| a.to_checksum(None))`) before rebuilding the result `Vec`. That client sort + HashMap round-trip is wasted work and discards row locality.

## What to investigate
1. Read the V3 branch of `fetch_all_liquidity_maps` in `snapshot.rs` + the parities `tests/parity.rs` / `tests/aave_parity.rs` to capture the EXACT expected output order (Python `get_all_liquidity_maps`).
2. Confirm the SQL `ORDER BY p.address` compares the stored checksummed VARCHAR — i.e. lexicographic on the checksum string — vs the Rust `sort_by_key(a.to_checksum(None))`. If both operate on the same string form, the client sort is provably redundant.
3. Check whether the V4 branch has the same redundant pattern (it uses a hand-rolled `key_order: Vec` instead of re-sorting — note whether the V3 branch could adopt the same streaming-into-ordered-Vec approach for free).
4. Confirm the parity fixture (`tests/fixtures/parity_expected.json` or equivalent) keys its V3 entries in address-sorted order, so removing the sort keeps the assertion green.

## Validation
- Verdict: client sort is redundant (DROP) or is load-bearing for some ordering subtlety the SQL does not guarantee (KEEP + explain).
- The exact parity fixture + assertion that proves the change is behaviour-preserving.

## Gating constraint
Rust-only change, no migration — actionable now (0.6.x).

## If validated → append implementation tasks
If research confirms the suggestion, append one or more implementation tasks to epic `F4N6DX` (DB performance improvements). Each appended task:
- is a single atomic change (one Alembic migration OR one Rust PR);
- includes concrete Acceptance Criteria + Validation Gates (exact `just`/`cargo`/`sql` commands);
- for schema/index changes: ships a new Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/`, mirrors the DDL change in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`, and bumps `ALEMBIC_HEAD` in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`;
- is sequenced after this spike (`ergo sequence <THIS-SPIKE-ID> <IMPL-ID>`);
- respects the gating constraint noted below.

If research refutes the suggestion, mark THIS spike `done` with a `result` summarising why — do NOT append an implementation task.

# spike-5: remove redundant client sort in fetch_all_liquidity_maps V3

## Verdict — DONE (REMOVE)
Verdict reached: DROP the `HashMap` round-trip + `keys.sort_by_key(|a| a.to_checksum(None))` re-sort in the V3 branch of `fetch_all_liquidity_maps` (snapshot.rs:285). The stored `pools.address` is already EIP-55-checksummed, so the SQL `ORDER BY p.address` and the client re-sort produce identical ordering — the client sort is dead work (restores faithful Python parity, which never re-sorted).

Full verdict recorded in spawned impl task ADTUMQ ("Validated by spike-5 — REMOVE (redundant, defensive over-engineering)").

Impl ADTUMQ remains `todo` — the code change is undone (snapshot.rs:285 still has the re-sort) and tracked separately there.
