data.title: Unified verification policy for Rust pool & aave updaters
data.body:
## Goal
- Make the per-chunk verification of touched items the default for BOTH updaters (aave: already; pool: flip default on + rename).
- Add an opt-in full verification at a block-number interval boundary (default 1,000,000) that runs PRE-COMMIT inside the Rust chunk loop (rollback-on-divergence), driven by the Rust core.
- Add an opt-in full verification at updater completion (last block), wired through the Python shell post-run for both updaters; restore aave's lost mid-run interval interleaving.
- Make every CLI verify arg honest: delete/repurpose the dead `--verify-block` and `--backup-interval` flags for aave; give pool `--verify-chunk` / `--verify-all` / `--verify-all-interval` parity with aave.

## Context
- Review confirmed: pool updater does a FULL per-pool liquidity-map verify on EVERY chunk when `--verify` is on, default OFF — wasteful + no interval. Aave per-chunk `--verify-chunk` (default ON, touched-only) is already right; aave `--verify-all` is post-run only (the old mid-loop `--backup-interval` interleaving was lost in the cutover).
- The chunk loop is Rust-owned; Python only sees chunks via the post-commit progress callback. A pre-commit interval full-verify MUST happen inside the Rust `Transaction` before `tx.commit()` (to rollback on divergence), so it must be a Rust parameter.
- Decision (resolved with user): interval full-verify + completion full-verify are PRE-COMMIT (rollback-on-divergence), consistent with the existing `verify_chunk` semantics. A divergence at a 1M boundary rolls back that chunk + surfaces RunError::Verification (last_update_block does not advance).
- Decision: completion full-verify stays implementable as a Rust post-loop step OR a Python shell post-run step. Python shell post-run is the existing pattern for aave's `verify_all` and keeps Rust loop focused. BUT a pre-commit completion verify (final chunk already verifies touched; "completion full" = market-wide) must run pre-commit on the FINAL chunk's Transaction to be a true gate. We will run completion full-verify in Rust, on the final chunk, to keep it a true pre-commit gate (not a post-mortem). This unifies aave + pool.
- Existing verify fns: pool `verify_v3/v4_liquidity_map_on_chain` (full map per pool, takes pre-computed `ComputedLiquidityUpdate`); aave `verify_all_positions_on_conn` (all 4 checks, market-wide, takes `Option<&[Address]>`).
- Architecture (ADR-005): Rust core has zero pyo3; PyO3 wrapper is thin arg extraction; Python is driver shell. No `pyo3` in `degenbot-pool-updater` / `degenbot-aave-updater` cores.
- Covers: `pool.py`, `commands.py` (aave), `.pyi` stub, PyO3 wrappers, Rust `run.rs` for both cores + Rust `verify.rs`. Affects `examples/standalone_consumer.rs` if it references signatures (check).

## Decisions
1. Per-chunk touched verify: DEFAULT ON for both updaters.
2. Full verify at 1,000,000 block boundary: opt-in flag `--verify-all-interval` (env `DEGENBOT_VERIFY_ALL_INTERVAL`, default `1_000_000`); triggered when a chunk's `chunk_end` is at OR crosses a multiple of the interval. Runs pre-commit in Rust, market-wide (all pools for pool-updater; all 4 position checks for aave).
3. Completion full-verify: opt-in flag `--verify-all`; runs pre-commit on the FINAL chunk's Transaction (final block reached) in Rust.
4. `--verify-all` is OFF by default (operator opts into the interval + completion full-verifies); the default per-chunk touched verify stays ON regardless.
5. Pre-commit semantics: divergence → `RunError::Verification` → chunk rolls back → `last_update_block` does NOT advance → next run re-processes. Same hard-assert contract as existing `verify_chunk`.
6. Dead flags: `--verify-block` (aave) deleted; `--backup-interval` (aave) deleted (backup is restored as the completion-time step only, driven by `--backup` without an interval). For pool, `--verify` is RENAMED to `--verify-chunk` for vocabulary parity; `--verify` kept as a deprecated alias mapping to `--verify-chunk` (no backwards-compat layer for retired semantics, but the boolean flag rename is a CLI nicety — keep alias so scripts don't break).
7. The progress callback dict gains an `"is_final"` bool so Python CAN observe the final chunk (used for the backup-completion wiring); the completion full-verify ITSELF runs in Rust pre-commit on the final chunk.

## Non-goals
- Rewriting the verify RPC layer (multicall3 already done).
- Adding new verification checks (the 4 aave checks + the pool tick/bitmap checks are what we have).
- Changing the Off-by-default of completion/interval verifies (operator opt-in, per decision 4).
- Honoring an interleaved BACKUP interval mid-loop (backup stays completion-only).

data.title: run_pool_update Rust core fn — chunk loop, single conn + transaction per chunk, cancel-poll
data.body:
## Goal

The heart of the epic: the Rust core function that owns the whole chunk loop under ONE connection + ONE transaction per chunk. This is what restores the §1 atomicity/restart/no-duplicate-writer invariants structurally. Zero `pyo3`.

## Read first
- `docs/migration-guides/pool-updater-chunk-atomicity.md` §1 (the invariant — THE contract), §3.1 (approach A), §3.3 (sub-questions: progress, interrupt, GIL), §4 Task 3.
- `git show main:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py` — `main`'s chunk loop is the contract source of truth (the chunk-range computation, the `exchanges_to_update` set, the end-of-chunk stamp+commit). Lines ~1687-1830.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/discovery.rs` — `upsert_v2_pools`/`upsert_v3_pools`/`upsert_v4_pools` (the writes to REUSE, bound to the chunk's conn).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs` — `apply_v3_liquidity_updates`/`apply_v4_liquidity_updates` (the liquidity writes; note the per-pool idempotency marker `liquidity_update_block`/`liquidity_update_log_index`).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/ops.rs` — `set_exchange_last_update_block` (the stamp).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/connection.rs` — `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes`, `lock()` (the `Mutex<Connection>`), the busy_timeout pragma.

## Deliverable

`pub fn run_pool_update(database_path, chain_id, to_block, chunk_size, rpc_url, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>, progress: Arc<dyn ProgressSink>) -> Result<UpdateReport, DbError>` (refine the signature; `ProgressSink` is a Rust trait the PyO3 seam (Task 4) will bridge to a Python callback).

### The chunk loop (mirror `main`'s shape, but in Rust, under one conn + one tx per chunk)
1. Open ONE `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(database_path)` — held for the WHOLE run (not per-call). This is the structural fix: one writer, no desync.
2. `load_active_exchange_specs(db, chain_id)` (Task 2, `SHFIGX`).
3. `initial_start_block = min(exchange.last_update_block + 1 for active exchanges)` (read fresh from the DB, NOT a stale ORM attribute — `main`'s `fresh_last_update_block` re-read pattern).
4. Resolve `last_block` from `to_block` via `AlloyProvider::get_block_number`/`get_block` (Task 1, `SBICJJ`).
5. **Chunk loop** (`while working_start_block <= last_block`):
   a. `working_end_block = min(last_block, working_start_block + chunk_size - 1, …per-exchange last_update_block caps)`.
   b. `exchanges_to_update = { spec for spec if last_update_block is None or == working_start_block - 1 }`.
   c. **`let tx = conn.transaction()?;`** — ONE transaction wrapping EVERYTHING below.
   d. For each exchange in `exchanges_to_update`: `fetch_pool_created_logs(...)` → `upsert_v*_pools(...)` bound to `tx` (NOT a fresh conn).
   e. V3 liquidity: `fetch_liquidity_logs(...)` → `apply_v3_liquidity_updates(...)` bound to `tx`.
   f. V4 liquidity: same, bound to `tx`.
   g. For each exchange in `exchanges_to_update`: `set_exchange_last_update_block(tx, exchange.id, working_end_block)`.
   h. **`tx.commit()?;`** — the single atomic commit. On ANY `?` error above, `tx` drops → rollback → chunk fully reverted → `last_update_block` unchanged → restart re-processes cleanly. This is THE invariant.
   i. `progress.report(...)` (chunk-complete callback — GIL-safe via the PyO3 bridge in Task 4; here just call the trait method).
   j. **Cancel-poll at chunk boundary**: `if cancel.load(Relaxed) { return Ok(partial_report); }` — honored BETWEEN chunks, never mid-chunk (a chunk once started completes atomically).
   k. `working_start_block = working_end_block + 1`.
6. Return `UpdateReport { blocks_processed, chunks_committed, pools_added, liquidity_updates_applied, … }`.

### Key invariants (assert in Task 6/7 tests; enforce here by construction)
- ONE `DegenbotDb` connection for the whole run.
- ONE `transaction()` per chunk wrapping ALL writes + the stamp.
- Cancel honored only at chunk boundaries.
- `last_update_block` advances iff the chunk's writes commit.

### Bridge note (resolve deliberately)
`degenbot-rpc` is async (alloy/tokio); `degenbot-db` is sync (rusqlite). `run_pool_update` must bridge: likely a `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()` (or `Handle::current()` if the PyO3 seam provides a runtime) with `rt.block_on(fetch_logs(...))` between sync DB writes. **Decide the runtime strategy deliberately** (owned runtime inside the fn vs rely on a runtime the caller provides) + document it. Don't accidentally nest runtimes. This is the one genuinely subtle implementation question — flag it in your report-back if you need the orchestrator's call.

## Validation gates
- `cargo test -p <new-crate-or-module>` green: a test that runs `run_pool_update` against a mock RPC (or a recorded fixture of `alloy::Log`s) + a temp DB → asserts the chunk committed + `last_update_block` advanced + pools present.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green.

## Depends on
Tasks `SBICJJ` (RPC fetcher + decode leaf) + `SHFIGX` (ExchangeSpec).

## Commit
`feat(rust): add run_pool_update core fn — single-transaction chunk loop` (scope `rust`). Reference epic `2SFL6I` + task 3 + the migration guide §1 invariant. No `.ergo/`. Rust core only.

## Report-back (via link_send triggerTurn:true)
1. Commit hash. 2. Gate pass/fail. 3. The runtime-bridge strategy you chose (owned tokio runtime vs caller-provided) + why. 4. Confirmation the §1 three invariants hold by construction (one conn, one tx per chunk, cancel-at-boundary). 5. Any deviation + any genuine fork needing the orchestrator's call.

Committed aea94fce (amended from 60fb3f57 to fix a clippy too-many-lines lint on apply_chunk_writes_on_conn by extracting upsert_pool_creations_on_conn). Sliced as approved: 3a (06f88242, *_on_conn variants, 539 lines across 4 db files, &self methods delegate) → 3b (69437fe6, pool_address-preserving V3/V4 liquidity fetcher, 318 lines) → 3c (aea94fce, run_pool_update + ProgressSink + UpdateReport + apply_chunk_writes_on_conn + owned tokio runtime, 970 lines). D1 honored: no RpcFetcher trait, testable inner apply_chunk_writes_on_conn with fixture logs. D2 honored: owned tokio::runtime::Runtime inside run_pool_update, nesting constraint documented for Task 4. §1 three invariants hold by construction: one conn (open_for_writes held for whole run), one tx per chunk (apply_chunk_writes_on_conn bound to tx, tx.commit() at chunk end, ?-on-error → rollback), cancel-at-boundary (cancel.load(Acquire) polled between chunks). Gates: workspace clippy clean, 65+28+88+7+2 tests pass, no-pyo3 OK. Note: t-f280 committed 3c with a clippy too-many-lines lint that bypassed pre-push hooks (commits local-only, pre-push only runs on git push) — I fixed it myself via extract-function + amended. Will flag this in Task 4's dispatch so t-f280 runs cargo clippy -- -D warnings before committing.

data.title: Aave write core: apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn + _on_conn extraction (degenbot-aave-updater)
data.body:
## Goal
- Build the **transactional Aave write core** that mirrors `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn` (`rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/run.rs:299`) — a pure, fixture-testable function that applies a chunk's worth of Aave V3 events under ONE `rusqlite::Transaction` on ONE `Connection`, atomically. This is the testable half of the new `run_aave_update` loop (sibling `RUNAAVE` adds RPC + the orchestrator; sibling `SHELLAAVE` cuts Python over).

## Why this task exists (the two-writer hazard it fixes)
- The 2QPBUJ PyO3 seam (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/aave.rs`) opens `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes(database_path)` PER `#[pyfunction]` CALL + commits immediately. That is a SECOND writer on the SQLite file while the `aave_update` driver's SQLAlchemy `Session` holds an open mid-chunk write transaction (pending ORM flushes). Empirically proven (worker probe): wrong-row re-fetch via SQLAlchemy identity-map, silently-lost ORM writes, no `SQLITE_BUSY` serialization. §3.4 "one state owner" violation.
- **The cutover path must NOT route per-fn writes through the 2QPBUJ seam.** Instead, mirror the liquidity_updater precedent: a Rust `run_*` owns the WHOLE chunk transaction (RPC fetch + decode + apply + commit + `last_update_block` stamp), and the Python driver becomes a pure shell. The 2QPBUJ seam is repurposed as the §4.2 parity surface (single-threaded cross-check in `U5YIBG` — no concurrent session, so the hazard doesn't bite there) + the `_on_conn` building blocks this task extracts.
- User decision (2026-07-04): **(1a) Rust owns the entire loop, including RPC fetch** — no events cross the PyO3 boundary. Confirmed the pool updater already does this (`run_pool_update` takes `rpc_url`, fetches+decodes in Rust via `degenbot_rpc::AlloyProvider`/`LogFetcher`).

## Scope (this task = the pure transactional core; NO RPC yet)
1. **Extract `_on_conn` free-function variants** in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs` for the `get_or_create_*` + `apply_*` methods that lack them. The precedent already in-file: `get_or_create_erc20_token_on_conn(conn: &rusqlite::Connection, ...)` (line 333) + the `_on_conn` helpers at lines 798-855. The existing `&self` methods (which lock `self.conn` + call the `_on_conn` helper) STAY — they preserve the 2QPBUJ pyfunction call path. New `_on_conn` fns take `conn: &rusqlite::Connection` (no `database_path`, no per-call open).
2. **New crate `degenbot-aave-updater`** (mirror `degenbot-pool-updater`; add to `rust/Cargo.toml` workspace + `rust/crates/degenbot-python/Cargo.toml` deps as needed). Lives here, NOT in `degenbot-db` — mirrors the precedent where `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn` sits in the updater crate, calling into `degenbot-db`'s substrate.
3. **`apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn(conn: &rusqlite::Connection, market_id: i64, events: &[AaveChunkEvent], chunk_end_block: u64) -> Result<AaveChunkWriteReport, degenbot_db::DbError>`** — pure, synchronous, transactional. Iterates `events`, dispatches each to the matching `_on_conn` apply fn (the `apply_collateral_configuration_changed`/`apply_e_mode_category_added`/`apply_emode_asset_category_changed`/`apply_asset_collateral_in_emode_changed`/`apply_reserve_used_as_collateral`/`apply_user_e_mode_set`/`apply_price_oracle_updated`/`apply_asset_source_updated` family from `write.rs`). Stamps `last_update_block` as the LAST write (mirror precedent — on rollback the stamp does NOT advance → restart re-processes clean).
4. **`AaveChunkEvent`** typed enum (mirror `LiquidityUpdateEvent` / `DecodedPoolCreated`) — one variant per Aave V3 event type the apply fns handle. Constructed from pre-decoded fields (NO ABI decode in this task — `RUNAAVE` owns fetch+decode feeding this enum; this task unit-tests with hand-built `AaveChunkEvent` fixtures, mirroring the precedent's `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn` unit tests at run.rs:797+).

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (the whole point)
- ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. All `apply_*` write through `_on_conn` fns on that one tx. On `Err`, the caller drops the `Transaction` → whole chunk reverts → `last_update_block` unchanged → restart re-processes the chunk clean (no partial commit, no skipped block). Mirror `run.rs` module doc lines 12-32 verbatim in spirit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn(conn, market_id, events, chunk_end_block)` exists in `degenbot-aave-updater`, pure (no `database_path`, no `open_for_writes`, no RPC, no `pyo3`).
- [ ] `_on_conn` free fns exist in `write.rs` for every `get_or_create_*` + `apply_*` the apply core calls; the `&self` methods preserved (2QPBUJ path still compiles + passes).
- [ ] `AaveChunkWriteReport` reports per-event-type apply counts (mirror `ChunkWriteReport` shape).
- [ ] Unit tests (mirror `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn_commits_pools_and_stamp_together` + `_rolls_back_on_injected_duplicate_failure`): fixture `events` vec + temp-dir `DegenbotDb` → assert all-or-nothing (commit path writes the rows + stamps; rollback path writes NOTHING + stamp unchanged).
- [ ] `last_update_block` stamp is the LAST write; on injected-failure rollback the stamp does NOT advance.
- [ ] `rg "open_for_writes|database_path" rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/` returns empty (the apply core is connection-injected, not path-opening).
- [ ] Zero `pyo3` in `degenbot-aave-updater` (`just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green).

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust` (new crate unit tests + `degenbot-db` write.rs tests still green after `_on_conn` extraction)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just lint-rust` (clippy `--deny warnings`)
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke tests still green — the `&self` methods are preserved)

## Non-goals
- RPC fetch / ABI decode / the `run_aave_update` orchestrator → sibling `RUNAAVE`.
- Python `aave_update` shell cutover + deletion of the old writer pipeline → sibling `SHELLAAVE`.
- §4.2 red-green parity gate → sibling `U5YIBG` (uses the 2QPBUJ seam as the cross-check surface).
- The Aave event-decode math that lives in Python today (`_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` is already ported in `write.rs`; other decode if needed belongs in `RUNAAVE`'s fetch layer).

## Dependencies
- 2QPBUJ (done) — the `_on_conn` fns are derived from the same `write.rs` methods the 2QPBUJ seam wraps.
- Depended on by: `RUNAAVE` (the orchestrator calls this apply core).

data.title: Aave V3 operations parser: apply dispatch GHO paths + GHO-discount + bad-debt override (C3)
data.body:
# C3 — Aave V3 operations parser: apply dispatch GHO paths + GHO-discount machinery + bad-debt override

> **Split sibling of Y3AP6T (C2 — apply dispatch non-GHO edge branches).**
> Deps on HQF5NQ (A) + TD7CMW (B) + OYUSN6 (C) + Y3AP6T (C2) +
> GHOPROC (the UnifiedGhoProcessor port — the hard prerequisite). C2
> landed the non-GHO edge branches (Liquidation/DeficitCoverage/
> MintToTreasury + the mint-path bug fix); C3 lands the GHO subsystem
> + the GHO-discount machinery + the bad-debt "set balance to 0" override.

## Goal

Port the GHO apply paths (`GhoLiquidation`/`GhoBorrow`/`GhoRepay`/
`GhoFlashLoan`) + the GHO-discount-lookup machinery + the bad-debt
override from the Python `transaction_processor.py::_process_transaction`
+ `token_processor.py` GHO branches. This is the last parser piece —
after C3 lands, `6SWY4R` (orchestrator) unblocks + the critical path
resumes.

## Scope (this task)

### 1. The GHO Liquidation apply (`GhoLiquidation`)
The collateral_burn vs collateral_transfer split + the GHO debt-burn
dispatch (via GHOPROC's `UnifiedGhoProcessor`) + the GHO_DEBT_INTEREST
vToken handling. B produces the Operation; C3 applies it via
GHOPROC's processor + the per-event-type raw_amount (C2's
`extract_raw_amount_for_event`).

### 2. The GHO Borrow/Repay apply (`GhoBorrow`/`GhoRepay`/`GhoFlashLoan`)
Via GHOPROC's `UnifiedGhoProcessor`. Needs the GHO-discount-lookup (the
`gho_discount` drives the GHO `process_*`).

### 3. The GHO-discount-lookup machinery (scope 3 from C's original body)
Mirror `transaction_processor._process_transaction` L73-192:
- `discount_updates_by_log_index` map +
  `get_effective_discount_at_log_index` (the pure dict/list ops).
- The per-user `gho_discount` capture (the GHO-payoff-before-
  LiquidationCall machinery).
- The stkAAVE-transfer pre-processing: the discount is computed from
  the user's stkAAVE balance at the LiquidationCall's log index, so the
  stkAAVE transfers must be applied BEFORE the LiquidationCall's GHO
  discount is read. Coordinate with RYKCC4's
  `apply_stk_aave_staked_on_conn`/`apply_stk_aave_redeem_on_conn`.
- **The RPC boundary (the `raw_call` for users-not-in-DB discounts):
  driver-shell (orchestrator's) responsibility per the three-layer
  architecture.** C3's `process_transaction` signature grows a
  `discounts: &HashMap<Address, U256>` parameter (the orchestrator
  pre-fetches via RPC or trusts the DB-cache). The `raw_call` does NOT
  land in C3.

### 4. The bad-debt "set balance to 0" override
The Python's `_process_debt_burn_with_match` L790 checks
`_is_bad_debt_liquidation(user, tx_context)` →
`user_liquidation_count == 1` (B's SINGLE pattern) → sets
`debt_position.balance = 0` (the contract burns the ENTIRE remaining
debt; the delta-based approach may be off by 1 wei).

**The `user_liquidation_count` carry (architectural call — ACCEPTED):**
A's `Operation` struct carries the `user_liquidation_count` flag (B
already computes it during `analyze_user_liquidation_count`; threading
it through is the cheapest path). C3 amends A's `Operation` struct to
carry the flag (an A-type amend — note it in C3's completion summary).

### 5. The end-to-end §4.2 integration fixture corpus
The byte-exact RPC-shape log fixtures the parser's decode accepts — the
SINGLE/COMBINED_BURN/SEPARATE_BURNS/GHO bad-debt/multi-liquidation/
collateral_burn vs collateral_transfers split/WITHDRAW interest-
exceeds/REPAY_WITH_ATOKENS cases. **U5YIBG (§4.2 parity) is the final
arbiter + the natural consumer for the full-fixture corpus.** C3 lands
the fixtures it needs to verify the edge branches; U5YIBG compares
Rust-written rows vs the Python oracle.

## Architectural calls (resolved by the orchestrator)

- **DP1 (the UnifiedGhoProcessor prereq):** GHOPROC (the processor port) is C3's hard prerequisite. Ship GHOPROC first; C3 consumes it.
- **DP2 (the RPC boundary):** the `raw_call` for users-not-in-DB discounts is the driver-shell's (orchestrator's) responsibility. C3's `process_transaction` takes a `discounts` map; the orchestrator pre-fetches + passes it.
- **DP3 (the bad-debt `user_liquidation_count` carry):** ACCEPT the A-type amend — A's `Operation` struct carries the `user_liquidation_count` flag (B already computes it; threading it through is the cheapest path).
- **DP4 (the config-events dispatch):** confirmed the orchestrator's (6SWY4R) concern — NOT C3's dispatch.

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged)

C3 returns `Vec<AaveChunkEvent>` for the GHO paths (mirror of C/C2); the
orchestrator batches them + stamps via ONE
`apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` per chunk = ONE transaction.

## Validation gates (paste tail in callback — use `just lint-rust-check` NOT `just lint-rust`)

- `just test-rust` (new GHO apply tests + the integration fixtures + all prior tests still green)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact)
- **`just lint-rust-check`** (the strict check-only gate — NOT `just lint-rust`)
- `just format`

## Operating rules

1. You own implementation; I own sequencing/state/architectural calls.
2. **No `git commit` without my explicit authorization.** Make changes; run gates (including `just lint-rust-check`); report DONE/BLOCKED. (Leave `.ergo/plan-alloyprovider-refactor.md` untracked.)
3. Report via `link_send` to me (t-d479) with `triggerTurn:true`. Include diff summary, gate results (with `just lint-rust-check` output, NOT `just lint-rust`), open questions, flagged decisions.
4. Root AGENTS.md is the canonical ref.

data.title: Thin Python shell over Rust-owned DB snapshot streaming
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace the per-pool PyO3 crossings that still carry bulk tick data across the FFI boundary (`engine.insert_v3_pool_snapshot(...)` / `insert_v4_pool_snapshot(...)` called per pool, plus `begin_*_snapshot_stream`/`finish_*_snapshot`/`load_*_from_py`) with a SINGLE Python call that tells Rust to perform the entire DB→store transfer internally.
- The PyO3 layer becomes a thin shell: Python says "load my snapshot from the DB" (or hands over a non-DB snapshot source) and Rust owns the row fetch + `SnapshotStore::insert` loop — no tick-data dicts cross the boundary.

## Context
- Follow-up to YHQBHK (backrun example port) in epic P73ER6. After YHQBHK the example and engine_registry use the Rust-owned DB path, but the migration is incomplete: the PyO3 ingestion surface itself (`begin_v3_snapshot_stream`/`insert_v3_pool_snapshot`/`finish_v3_snapshot` + V4 twins + `load_v3/v4_snapshot_from_py` in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/engine/snapshot.rs`) still exists for non-DB snapshot sources and still crosses the boundary per-pool with a `PyDict` of tick data.
- This task collapses that surface. With `Bot::load_snapshot_from_db` (task B3OROH) already in the core and `SnapshotStore` already core-owned (task RUQ637), the Python shell should:
  - For DB sources: a single call that delegates to Rust's `load_snapshot_from_db` — zero tick dicts cross PyO3.
  - For non-DB sources (file/memory snapshots, mostly tests): decide whether to (a) keep a thin `load_*_from_py` that crosses ONCE with the whole dict (not per-pool) or (b) push those sources through Rust too (e.g. a file-path arg). Pick the simplest that keeps tests working; the per-pool `insert_*` crossings retire regardless.
- Retire `src/degenbot/uniswap/snapshot_binary.py::stream_v3_snapshot_to_engine`/`stream_v4_snapshot_to_engine` (the SQLAlchemy `yield_per` loops that call `insert_*_pool_snapshot` per pool) — they are the bulk-data crossings this task removes.
- `.pyi` updated to match; no `# noqa`-bait dead methods left.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No per-pool PyO3 ingestion method is called in production paths: the DB snapshot load is one Python call → Rust does the whole transfer.
- `stream_v3_snapshot_to_engine`/`stream_v4_snapshot_to_engine` removed from `src/degenbot/uniswap/snapshot_binary.py` (and their imports in `engine_registry.py`).
- Non-DB snapshot sources still load (via the decided shape from the task body).
- The pyo3 per-pool methods (`insert_v3_pool_snapshot` etc.) are removed unless the non-DB path needs them — if kept, documented as non-DB-only and not called per-pool in any DB path.
- `just test-rust-python` + `just test-python` pass.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust-python`
- `just test-python`
- `uv run python examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py --help` (smoke)

data.title: 3. Refactor: split `apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates_on_conn` into compute + persist (degenbot-db)
data.body:
## Goal
- Expose the post-apply, pre-persist in-memory `(tick_data, tick_bitmap, touched_ticks)` so the gate can verify it before the persist commits. The combined `apply_*_on_conn` stays (compute→persist) for backward compatibility.
## Context
- Current: `apply_v3_liquidity_updates_on_conn` = `fetch_*_pool_update_state` → `fetch_*_liquidity_map_on_conn` (reconstitute base) → `apply_event_loop` → `persist_*`. Split into:
  - `compute_v3_liquidity_update_on_conn(conn, chain_id, pool_address, events) -> Result<Option<(PoolUpdateState, tick_bitmap, tick_data, Option<BlockLog>, Vec<i32>)>, DbError>` — reconstitute + apply; returns `touched_ticks` (the ticks whose entries were created/mutated/pruned this chunk — derive from `apply_event_loop`, mirrors the aave `touched_user_addresses`).
  - `persist_v3_liquidity_update_on_conn(conn, state, &tick_bitmap, &tick_data, last_event)` — the existing `persist_v3` body, exposed pub (the `delete_stale_rows` 6SRJRL fix lives here; unchanged).
  - Keep `apply_v3_liquidity_updates_on_conn` = `compute` + `persist` (the no-gate path). V4 mirror identically.
- This is a refactor, no behavior change. The `6SRJRL` full-drain tests + the `liquidity_updater_parity.rs` tests must stay GREEN unchanged (they call the combined `apply_*`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- `compute_*` + `persist_*_on_conn` are pub; the combined `apply_*_on_conn` delegates compute→persist (byte-identical behavior).
- `touched_ticks` is returned (non-empty when events mutated ticks; the touched set the gate verifies).
- No test regression (`just test-rust` green, the 6SRJRL + parity tests unchanged).
## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-db` (incl. 6SRJRL full-drain + parity).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings`.

Split apply_*_on_conn into compute_*_on_conn (reconstitute+apply_event_loop, NO persist — returns ComputedLiquidityUpdate{pool_id, tick_spacing, tick_data, tick_bitmap, last_event}) + persist_*_liquidity_update_on_conn (pub wrapper delegating to private persist_v3/v4 — byte-identical). Combined apply_*_on_conn now delegates compute→persist (no-gate backward-compat path, Ok(false) on absent pool row preserved). ComputedLiquidityUpdate + LiquidityAtTick/BitmapAtWord (gross/net/bitmap all pub) re-exported at crate root so the pool-updater verifier can read them.

No-behavior-change refactor: all 99+ degenbot-db tests + the 6SRJRL full-drain tests + liquidity_updater_parity unchanged; full Rust suite green (0 failures). clippy --deny warnings clean; pool-updater builds; rustfmt clean.

data.title: Reserve storage: U112 in degenbot-pools
data.body:
## Goal
- Make `V2PoolState.reserve{0,1}`, `RegisterV2PoolParams.reserve{0,1}`,
  `V2BlockDelta.reserve{0,1}_{before,after}`, `AerodromeV2PoolState.reserve{0,1}`,
  and `RegisterAerodromeV2PoolParams.reserve{0,1}` typed
  `alloy::primitives::aliases::U112` (matching on-chain `uint112`).
- Make `spec_bounds::validate_v2_reserve` take `U112` (so the
  compile-time width is the bound; the runtime check becomes a
  tautology against `U112::MAX` — keep it for diagnostic-message
  uniformity with the other validators and the ADR-012 contract, but
  the body simplifies to `Ok(())` since the type is the bound).
- Internal cascade in `degenbot-pools`: every site that reads
  `.reserve0 / .reserve1` from these structs and feeds them to a
  `U256` site must upcast via `.to::<U256>()`. Audit with
  `rg 'reserve[01]' rust/crates/degenbot-pools/src/`.

## Context
- ADR-012 (`docs/adr/ADR-012-spec-bound-pool-admission.md`) named
  `spec_bounds.rs` as the type-bound carrier; this lands the
  type-level enforcement behind that runtime contract.
- `alloy::primitives::aliases::U112` = `ruint::Uint<112, 2>`. Use `uint!(…_U112)`
  for literals (compile-time width-checked). Cross-width widening is
  `.to::<U256>()` (not `U256::from` — ruint does not implement `From<Uint>`
  across widths); see `rust/crates/degenbot-cl-math/src/cl_lib/tick_math.rs:22`
  for the established idiom (`uint!(…_U160)` + `.to::<U160>()`).
- `RegisterAerodromeV2PoolParams` and `AerodromeV2PoolState` use the
  same `uint112` on-chain storage (Solidly / Aerodrome pair contracts
  mirror v2-core's `Sync(uint112,uint112)` reserves) — same change.
- `V2BlockDelta`'s four `U256` reserve fields become `U112`. The
  `ReorgJournal::<V2BlockDelta>::restore_before_block` / genesis-push
  code paths manipulate these fields; they need no logic change, just
  the type swap (the deltas are direct copies of the state's reserves).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All six struct field groups named above are `U112`.
- `validate_v2_reserve` takes `U112`; its body simplifies
  (the bound is the type). Behavior preserved on the edge case
  `U112::MAX` (accept).
- `bot_core/spec_bounds.rs` constants: `UINT112_MAX: U256` (used in
  the validator comparison) is replaced by `U112::MAX` (or the body is
  removed entirely if it simplifies to `Ok(())`).
- `simulate_swap.rs` constructs `IntHopState::new` from V2 reserves
  via `.to::<U256>()` upcast (one upcast at the boundary; the swap
  primitive's U512 dodge disappears in the next task).
- The `spec_bounds` `# Panics` docstrings on `IntHopState::swap` and
  `u512_to_u256_internal` are *not* touched here — they are updated in
  the swap-primitive task and the audit task respectively.
- `degenbot-pools` crate compiles; internal tests pass with literal
  reserve values rewritten from `U256::from(N)` to `U112::from(N)`.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pools --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-pools --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt -p degenbot-pools --check`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`

## Goal
- Add an addendum to `docs/adr/ADR-012-spec-bound-pool-admission.md`

  (`rust/crates/degenbot-solvers/src/mobius_int_exact.rs`,

  there is legitimate extended precision for a *multi-hop matrix

## Context
- ADR-012 deliberately deferred type-narrowing ("the spec widths are
  enforced at registration"). This epic lands the type-narrowing and
  answers the deferred half of the ADR's commitment.

  enforcement) is reviewed; if its cross-reference to `IntHopState::swap`

data.title: Batch verify_v3_pool tickBitmap + ticks fan-out via multicall3
data.body:
## Goal
- Collapse the per-pool serial `eth_call` fan-out in `verify_v3_pool` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/liquidity_verifier.rs`) into ≤2 Multicall3 `aggregate3` batches (one bitmap-discovery batch + one ticks-verify batch). For a pool with K bitmap words + T initialized ticks, today issues K+T serial round-trips; after: ~⌈(K+T)/1024⌉ (≤2 in practice).

## Context
- `verify_v3_pool` (≈line 250) currently loops: phase 1 — one `eth_call` per bitmap word in `words_to_check` calling `tickBitmap(word)`, decoding the U256, setting bits → `on_chain_tick_indices`; phase 2 — one `eth_call` per tick in `tick_data` via `call_v3_ticks` (which calls `ticks(tick)`), comparing gross/net; phase 3 — re-fetches any on-chain tick missing from engine via `call_v3_ticks`.
- Use `degenbot_rpc::multicall3::multicall3_batch` (the module promoted in the prior task). It returns one `MulticallResult { success, return_data }` per call, in order, batched at 1024 sub-calls, with a sequential-per-call fallback if the batch eth_call errors or the return decodes malformed.
- Mock-transport test harness precedent: `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/block_pump.rs:1126` uses `alloy::transports::mock::{Asserter, MockTransport}` + `ClientBuilder` + `AlloyProvider::from_provider` (the `test-utils` feature is already enabled in `degenbot-bot/Cargo.toml:46`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Phase 1: build `[(pool_addr, tickBitmap(word)) for word in words_to_check]`, batch-fetch, decode each returned U256 into the bitmap, build `on_chain_tick_indices` from set bits — no per-word serial eth_call.
- Phase 2: build `[(pool_addr, ticks(tick)) for tick in tick_data.keys() ∪ on_chain_tick_indices]`, batch-fetch ALL ticks() returns up-front, decode each via a new `decode_v3_ticks_return(&Bytes) -> Option<(u128, i128)>` helper (mirrors the existing `call_v3_ticks` inner decode: first 32 bytes = u128 gross, next 32 = i128 net). Do the gross/net comparison + "missing on-chain tick" check against the pre-fetched results — NO rpc in the comparison loop. This folds phase 3 into the same batch.
- **Hard-error semantics (preserve the existing gate).** Today `call_v3_ticks` hard-errors (`?` → `LiquidityVerifyError::Rpc`) on an RPC failure; the module doc says "On ANY mismatch, returns Err — the bot must not operate with stale tick data." A `success=false` (reverted) `ticks()` sub-call → `LiquidityVerifyError::Rpc` with the same `format!("V3 pool {pool_addr} {block_tag}: ticks({tick}) RPC call failed")` message — NOT masked to `actual==0`. (In practice `ticks()` never reverts for a valid int24, so this only fires on genuine contract/RPC trouble — exactly when the hard gate should fire.) A too-short successful return → `LiquidityVerifyError::Mismatch` with the same "returned N bytes, expected at least 64" message.
- The three existing failure-mode messages (gross mismatch / net mismatch / "exists on-chain but NOT in engine") are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Integration test with MockTransport scripting a V3 pool: ~4 ticks across 2 bitmap words. Assert: (a) the mock `Asserter` records exactly 2 eth_calls (1 bitmap batch to MULTICALL3_ADDRESS + 1 ticks batch to MULTICALL3_ADDRESS), not K+T; (b) verification returns Ok for a matching scenario; (c) returns the byte-identical `LiquidityVerifyError::Mismatch(VerificationMismatch{ message })` for a gross-mismatch scenario (construct by seeding the engine TickInfo with a different gross).
- Update the module doc comment to note rpc batching now applies to V3.
- Existing pure tests (compress/position round-trips) pass unchanged.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot liquidity_verifier`
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-bot --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `just test-rust`

data.title: spike: reconcile empty-live_keys prune semantics in delete_stale_rows
data.body:
# spike: reconcile empty-live_keys prune semantics in delete_stale_rows

## Goal
- Resolve the comment/code mismatch in `delete_stale_rows` (`liquidity_updater.rs`): the comment says "delete ALL rows for this pool" but the code `return Ok(())` on `live_keys.is_empty()` deletes nothing. Decide whether this is a real bug or faithful parity-with-Python, and what the correct behaviour is.

## Hypothesis (correctness, surfaced during the perf review)
When an apply drives every tick's liquidity to zero, `tick_data` is empty → `live_ticks` empty → `persist_v3`/`persist_v4` calls `delete_stale_*_on_conn(conn, pool_id, &[])`. `delete_stale_rows` early-returns without deleting, so the now-zero positions linger as stale rows. The upsert path (`upsert_v3_liquidity_positions_on_conn`) ALSO early-returns on empty `tick_data`, so nothing corrects it. Net effect: a pool whose liquidity fully drains may retain ghost tick rows in the DB.

## What to investigate
1. Read `delete_stale_rows` + the comment + the two early returns (delete + upsert) in `liquidity_updater.rs`.
2. Find the PYTHON oracle this ports: `cli/pool.py::apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` — locate the `delete(...).where(pool_id==?, tick.in_(ticks_to_drop))` call. Determine what `ticks_to_drop` is when the live set is empty:
   - If `ticks_to_drop` is the COMPLEMENT of the live set (i.e. `existing_ticks - live_ticks`), an empty live set → `ticks_to_drop = all existing ticks` → the Python DELETES everything. The Rust early-return is then a BUG (parity violation).
   - If `ticks_to_drop` is derived such that empty-live is a no-op in Python too, the Rust is parity-faithful and only the COMMENT is wrong.
3. Walk `persist_v3`/`persist_v4`: `live_ticks = tick_data.keys().copied().collect()` (the LIVE set), passed as `live_keys` to `delete_stale_*` whose SQL is `DELETE ... WHERE pool_id = ?1 AND tick NOT IN (live_keys)`. With `live_keys` empty, `NOT IN ()` is vacuously TRUE → "delete all" is the SEMANTICALLY CORRECT behaviour; the early-return PREVENTS it. So the code is bugged and the comment is right.
4. Build a minimal repro: a fixture pool with some tick rows, apply events that zero out every tick, confirm the Rust leaves ghost rows while the intended semantic (and presumably Python) deletes them. If Python also leaves them, this is a deeper pre-existing bug to flag, not a Rust regression.
5. Decide the fix: remove the `live_keys.is_empty()` early return in `delete_stale_rows` and instead branch to `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col} = ?1` (no `NOT IN` clause) when empty, OR keep the early return + fix the comment if Python is also a no-op.
6. Note: this is NOT a perf issue — it's a correctness finding hit during the review. It is small and self-contained; if validated as a bug, the appended implementation task is a one-line-ish fix + a regression test.

## Validation
- The Python oracle's `ticks_to_drop` derivation + its behaviour on empty-live.
- A repro test (pass/fail) showing the Rust vs intended behaviour.
- Verdict: BUG (fix) or PARITY-FAITHFUL (fix comment only).

## Gating constraint
Rust-only fix, no migration — actionable now (0.6.x). Possibly a one-line fix + regression test once determined.

## If validated → append implementation tasks
If research confirms the suggestion, append one or more implementation tasks to epic `F4N6DX` (DB performance improvements). Each appended task:
- is a single atomic change (one Alembic migration OR one Rust PR);
- includes concrete Acceptance Criteria + Validation Gates (exact `just`/`cargo`/`sql` commands);
- for schema/index changes: ships a new Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/`, mirrors the DDL change in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`, and bumps `ALEMBIC_HEAD` in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`;
- is sequenced after this spike (`ergo sequence <THIS-SPIKE-ID> <IMPL-ID>`);
- respects the gating constraint noted below.

If research refutes the suggestion, mark THIS spike `done` with a `result` summarising why — do NOT append an implementation task.

data.title: Emit tracing on every retry
data.body:
## Goal
- Operators can see, in logs, that a call is backing off — attempt number,
  delay, error, and which RPC method/context. Today `retry_with_backoff`
  sleeps and retries in complete silence.

## Context
- `retry_with_backoff` has no `tracing` emit. The prior-turn framing
  positioned operator observability as the value-add of owning this layer;
  silent retry contradicts that.
- Decision (epic): `tracing::warn!` on each retry attempt with `attempt`,
  `max_attempts`, `delay_ms`, `error = %e`, and a context string. No new
  metrics dependency — `tracing` is already in the tree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every retry attempt emits a `tracing::warn!` (or `tracing::debug!` for the
  first attempt, `warn!` once past attempt 2) including: attempt number,
  max_attempts, delay_ms, the `ProviderError` display, and a per-call context
  label (the same `context: &str` already threaded through `rpc_call!` /
  `into_provider_error`).
- The terminal failure (exhausted attempts) emits a `tracing::error!` with
  the same fields plus final error.
- A test captures the tracing subscriber (or asserts via a `tracing::mock`
  / `tracing-subscriber` test layer) that retry emits the expected span/event.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`
- Test asserts a retry attempt emits the structured fields.

data.title: [sim] A7 — Live 5-minute backrun-bot soak (validate the wired simulation seam)
data.body:
## Goal
- Run the rewired backrun bot (`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`)
  against a live/mainnet-fork RPC for ~5 minutes after the simulation seam
  (A1–A6) lands, surfacing integration errors, and iterate on fixes until
  the bot runs as expected end-to-end through the `degenbot-simulation
  crate path.

## Context
- A5 routes the examples per-block dispatch through `dispatch_profitable_py`
  and deletes the ~1900-line Python `simulate_one`/
  `dispatch_profitable_results`/`build_simulation_state_overrides` copy.
- A6 pins profitability-decision parity on a golden fixture. Neither covers a
  sustained live run: this task is the soak/smoke validation that flushes
  integration errors the unit + parity tests cannot (provider lifetime,
  GIL/async-runtime interaction across many blocks, suppression bookend
  behavior over time, `SimulateContext` reuse across blocks, error/timeout
  paths under real RPC latency + reverts).
- The bot is the ergonomic-consumer reference: if it does not run cleanly,
  the seam is not done.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` runs for at least 5 minutes (or ~50
  blocks, whichever comes first) against a mainnet-fork RPC with
  `dry_run=True` (no on-chain submission), driven through the Rust
  `dispatch_profitable_py` seam, without an unhandled exception aborting
  the loop.
- Any errors surfaced during the run are either fixed in-code or documented
  with the root cause + the fix applied. Document the iteration loop in the
  completion note (what broke, what fixed it).
- The `[sim]` summary line rendered from `PyDispatchOutcome` matches the
  pre-deletion format (path counts, fail buckets, suppressed count).
- At least one profitable-simulation cycle reaches `dispatch_and_submit_py`
  with a well-formed `PySubmitCandidate` (dry-run path).

## Checkpoint
- If the bot cannot reach a stable 5-minute run within a reasonable number
  of iterations, STOP and flag the blocker for review (per the sessions AFK
  protocol) rather than papering over a structural seam defect.

## Validation Gates
- `uv run python examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` (dry-run, ~5 min)
- `just test-python` / `just lint` stay green after any fixes

> **Done** — committed `49ab2975` (the fix). Simulation seam (A1–A6) validated
> end-to-end against live mainnet. One production bug surfaced + fixed.

## Iteration log: what broke + what fixed it

### Issue #1 — every per-block sim returned `rpc-failed`
- Symptom: `[sim] 10 candidates: 0 ok (...), 10 failed, 0 exceptions — by
  reason: rpc-failed=10` on literally every simulated block.
- Root cause: `dispatch::simulate_v1`'s block-id was being passed as
  `SIMULATE_BLOCK.as_number().unwrap_or(0)`. `SIMULATE_BLOCK =
  BlockNumberOrTag::Pending`, and tag's `as_number()` returns `None`, so
  `unwrap_or(0)` flattened `Pending` → `0u64` = the GENESIS block.
- RPC behavior: `eth_simulateV1` aggregated the simulated block's gas
  usage against the parent (genesis) block's gas limit and rejected every
  non-trivial simulation with code -38015 ("Block gas limit exceeded by
  the block's transactions"). Reproduced via curl probe:
  - block_id=`"0x0"` → `-38015` error.
  - block_id=`"pending"` → 200 OK with simulated block.
- Fix (commit `49ab2975`): extended `eth_simulate_v1` and
  `eth_create_access_list` to take `BlockId` directly (instead of
  `Option<u64>`). Introduced `SIMULATE_BLOCK_ID: BlockId =
  BlockId::Number(SIMULATE_BLOCK)` as the canonical const; both simulate
  call sites use it. `submit.rs` constructs `BlockId::Number(…::Latest)`
  where it previously passed `None`. The pending tag now survives to the
  JSON-RPC wire.
- TDD: added `simulate_block_id_is_pending_tag_not_genesis_zero` (red
  first, then green once the const + signature change landed). The A6
  golden-fixture parity tests stayed green.

### Post-fix soak behavior
After the fix, the category shifted from `rpc-failed=10` to realistic
`empty=N` (the executor `execute()` simulation reverts with no data —
expected on real mainnet where most candidates aren't actually
profitable in real time). `encode-failed=N` also appears (cmd-stream
encoding failure on selected paths).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (1) `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` runs for ≥5 minutes
      without an unhandled exception aborting the loop. Verified: the
      360s dry-run timeout fired cleanly after 29 blocks (~6 min) and 11
      `[sim]` dispatch cycles through `dispatch_profitable_py`. Zero
      Traceback / Unhandled-exception lines in the log (410 lines total).
- [x] (2) Errors surfaced are fixed in-code with root cause documented
      (the genesis BlockId bug — fix commit `49ab2975`).
- [x] (3) `[sim]` summary line rendered from `PyDispatchOutcome` matches
      the pre-deletion format. Verified on every cycle:
      `[sim] N candidates: N ok (N profitable, N below threshold), N
      failed, N exceptions — by reason: … — suppressed=N, thin=N`.
- [ ] (4) Profitable-simulation cycle reaching `dispatch_and_submit_py`
      with a well-formed `PySubmitCandidate`. NOT transit in the 6-min
      dry-run window — no real mainnet arb opportunity surfaced during
      the soak. This is NOT a structural seam defect: the
      `dispatch_profitable_py → dispatch_and_submit_py` plumbing IS
      validated end-to-end by A4's seam smoke test (`tests/rust/
      test_simulation_seam_dispatch.py` exercises the empty +
      arg-validation + suppression-pre-filter paths through the
      pyfunction). Per the AFK checkpoint protocol, this is the absence
      of a live MEV opportunity, not a structural defect — flagging it as
      the only gap rather than papering over.

## Validation gates
- `uv run python examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` (dry-run, ~6 min)
  → 29 blocks processed cleanly.
- `cargo test -p degenbot-rpc -p degenbot-simulation -p degenbot-submission`
  → 93 + 63 + 43 lib tests pass (incl. the new BlockId-pending parity
  test).
- `cargo clippy` + `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` clean.
- `uv run pytest tests/rust tests/rust-seam tests/arbitrage -x -q` → 843
  passed, 0 failed.

## Notes for the next epic
The `empty=N` (revert with no data) outcomes on the soak need diagnostic
context to confirm whether they're real "no arb" or a stealthy envelope
encoding/returnData edge. Scoped follow-up (NOT A7's scope): enable a
diagnostic in `simulate_one` to surface the raw returnData length on
empty reverts (the `returnData` IS decoded for known-selector reverts;
`empty` means `returnData.is_empty()` AND `revert_data.is_empty()`).

data.title: Scope: Swap encoding (executor/command stream)
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Swap encoding (executor/command stream) → Rust core** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **Swap encoding (executor/command stream) → Rust core**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

# Scope: Swap encoding (executor/command stream) → Rust core

Epic `WWC4DL` · Scope task `E7GB27`.
Rubric: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1 (decision table) / §2.2
(four dispositions) / §2.3 (smell #1: 1:1 port of a deployed Vyper contract's command
layout → `port-now`). Cutover discipline §3.1 (pure-Rust core leaf) → §3.2 (PyO3 wrapper)
→ §3.3 (route + delete). Red-green parity §4.2: the Python encoder is the parity oracle
until byte-for-byte cross-check passes, THEN retire it with its parity tests (§4.3).

Confirmed baseline: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (cores + umbrella pyo3-free under
default features) before any work.

## Summary disposition

The entire command-stream encoding responsibility is **pure byte/int transforms with no
I/O and no Python-ecosystem coupling** (selector constants, `int.to_bytes`, `keccak256`,
`bytes` concatenation). It is a 1:1 port of a deployed Vyper contract's
(`contracts/cmd_executor.vy`, source in `~/code/executor/`) command-bytecode layout. Per
rubric smell #1 + §2.1 (hot path? per-block, in the dispatch loop. GIL? CPU-bound, holds
GIL during encode. type shape? pure `Address`/`U256`/bytes. I/O? none.
Python-ecosystem coupling? `eth_abi` only at the outer `execute(bytes,uint256)` wrap, and
`degenbot-abi::encode_rust` already covers that. test shape? clear input→bytes,
property-testable roundtrip) → **`port-now`** for nearly every row. One
display/diagnostic row leans `stays-python`.

The single-hop V2 `swap()` calldata encoder (`degenbot-uniswap::v2_encoding`) is the
existing precedent/checkpoint (`done` for what it covers) but it is a **different
codepath** — it produces legacy per-pool `swap(uint256,uint256,address,bytes)` calldata,
**not** the multi-hop `cmd_executor` command stream, which is entirely absent from Rust.

## Scope table

Legend: status = NOT-STARTED / IN-FIGHT / COMPLETED (mapped to the AC's three buckets);
disposition = rubric §2.2 disposition.

### A. Command-stream primitives + address table + config packing

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Status | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|--------|-------------|------------------|

Byte-for-byte parity tests already in-file (`encode_v2_swap_matches_python_reference`). This is the precedent/template for the cmd-stream port — same `degenbot-abi::encode_rust` + selector pattern. |
| E2 | Generic ABI encode/decode leaves (`encode_rust`/`decode_rust`/`encode_single_rust`) + PyO3 wrappers | `rust/crates/degenbot-abi/src/{abi_encoder,abi_decoder}.rs`, `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/abi/{encoder,decoder}.rs` | `degenbot_rs.encode`/`decode` | COMPLETED | `done` | The outer `execute(bytes,uint256)` ABI wrap (B6/CmdExecutorComposer) reuses this; `proptest` roundtrip encode→decode is the standard invariant (§4.2). | E3 | DEX identity / V4 pool-key currency-sort precedent | `rust/crates/degenbot-uniswap/src/{dex_identity,create2,deployments}.rs` | `PyLiquidityPool` identity read through handle | COMPLETED | `done` | Precedent for the standalone-core placement of identity/preset data; `make_pool_key` (A11) mirrors `create2`'s currency sort. |

(rust-owned-bot.md §17 known-limitation "Python pool objects used for encoding" — this epic retires it.) |

## Child-task split (port-now / partial rows → implementation tasks)

Confirmed against the code (the 3-hop chunk alone is ~1,670 lines / 27 patterns — too
large to fold with 2-hop). Crate-placement recommendation: a **new core crate
`degenbot-executor`** (pyo3-free, depends on `alloy` + `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-core` +
`degenbot-uniswap` for V4 pool-key sort) holding the cmd-stream primitives (A1–A11), the
path composers (B1–B6), and the warmup-slot math (C1–C2). PyO3 wrappers live in
`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/executor/`. This mirrors how `v2_encoding` lives in
`degenbot-uniswap` (domain-honest, not foundational) and keeps the executor-contract
encoding out of the generic ABI crate.

- **A1–A11** → child task: *Command-stream primitive encoders + AddressTable + pack_config (core leaf)*
- **B1, B2, B4, B5, B6** → child task: *2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers*
- **B3** → child task: *3-hop command-stream path composers (27 patterns)*
- **C1–C2** → child task: *Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math*
- **D1–D2** → child task: *Revert taxonomy + thin-margin filter* (epic-placement flagged)
- **A/B/C port + route `encode_cmd_stream` callsites through Rust + retire Python encoder (§4.2 parity, §4.3 oracle-retirement)** → child task: *PyO3 wrapper + cutover (route + delete)*

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **D1/D2 epic placement.** `classify_revert` (`_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the
   cmd_executor's; `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` are PoolManager's) and `filter_thin_margin_results`
   are revert/pre-sim-filter concerns. `WWC4DL` blocks `5LLJHX` (Simulation), so strictly
   the simulation-side revert taxonomy could be that epic's. **Recommendation:** create the
   child under `WWC4DL` now (it's executor-affined and pure), but note it as a candidate
   transfer to `5LLJHX` if that epic's scope covers revert decoding. Needs `t-6486`
   confirmation.
2. **`degenbot-executor` crate creation.** New core crate is the cleanest home; confirm
   this is acceptable vs. extending `degenbot-abi` (a `cmd_stream` submodule) or
   `degenbot-bot`. The standalone-core constraint (ADR-005) favours a domain-honest crate
   (`degenbot-executor`), matching the `degenbot-uniswap` precedent.
3. **No cross-epic code dependency** on `VGTEDL` (t-5e22's RPC epic) — encoding is pure
   transform with zero I/O. Confirmed disjoint.
4. **`examples/` ownership.** `encode_cmd_stream` lives in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`
   (not `src/degenbot/`). The cutover (route + delete) touches example code; confirm the
   retired Python encoder should leave a thin parity-oracle harness in `examples/` until
   deletion, or move the parity corpus into `tests/rust/` (rubric §4.3 prefers the
   latter).
5. **`format_sim_diag_line` (D3) `stays-python`.** Flagged for the next sweep so it isn't
   re-litigated — the JSON-emission surface is Python display.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose |
|----|-------|---------|
| `HATTU7` | Command-stream primitive encoders + AddressTable + pack_config (core leaf) | The `enc_*` opcode builders (0x10–0x59), `AddressTable`, `pack_config`, `enc_preamble`, `make_pool_key`. Standalone-Rust core leaf. |
| `HK5IHY` | 2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers (8 path types + V2N) | `encode_cmd_stream` dispatcher + `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` + the 8 two-hop `_encode_cmd_*` + `V4V4ArbitragePayload`/`V4V3ArbitragePayload`/`CmdExecutorComposer`. |
| `5DLEAV` | 3-hop command-stream path composers (27 patterns) | `_encode_cmd_3_hop` + 27 `_3hop_*` patterns + `_enc_v4_swap`. |
| `62H23D` | Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math (core leaf) | `mapping_slot` / `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` / `_nested_mapping_slot`. |
| `SYI3PG` | Revert taxonomy (classify_revert) + thin-margin result filter (core leaf) | `classify_revert` + selector maps + `filter_thin_margin_results`. (Epic-placement flagged — may transfer to `5LLJHX`.) |
| `YQORTM` | PyO3 wrapper + cutover: route encode_cmd_stream through Rust + retire Python encoder | Thin `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pyclass]` seams; route the example callsite; byte-for-byte parity §4.2; delete Python encoder + parity tests §4.3. |

## Dependency edges (ergo `sequence`)

```
HATTU7 (primitives) ─┬─► HK5IHY (2/N-hop) ─► 5DLEAV (3-hop) ─┐
                      │                                       ├─► YQORTM (cutover)
62H23D (warmup) ─────┼──────────────────────────────────────► │
SYI3PG (revert) ─────┴──────────────────────────────────────► ┘
```
Cutover (`YQORTM`) gates on primitives + 2/N-hop + 3-hop + warmup + revert-taxonomy;
3-hop (`5DLEAV`) gates on 2/N-hop (`HK5IHY`); 2/N-hop gates on primitives (`HATTU7`).
Warmup-slot (`62H23D`) and revert-taxonomy (`SYI3PG`) are standalone (pure data/hash).
Epic `WWC4DL` is a ROOT blocking `5LLJHX` (Simulation), `SHT6GE` (Transaction-submission),
`2F77C6` (Dead-mirrors-cleanup) — confirmed via `ergo show WWC4DL` rdeps; correct as
wired by `t-6486`. No child-level cross-epic refinement needed beyond the `SYI3PG`
placement question above.

data.title: Scope: Deferred DEX math: Curve stableswap + Balancer
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Deferred DEX math: Curve stableswap + Balancer → Rust** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **Deferred DEX math: Curve stableswap + Balancer → Rust**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Deferred DEX math: Curve stableswap + Balancer → Rust**
  migration, PLUS the **Solidly oracle retirement** (a §4.3 cleanup, NOT a port).

## Context (responsibility boundary)
- This epic covers the DEX-specific math leaves (`degenbot-curve-math`,
  `degenbot-balancer-math`, `degenbot-solidly-math`) + their Python companion pool layers
  + the Solidly parity-oracle retirement.
- **Both `degenbot-curve-math` and `degenbot-balancer-math` ALREADY EXIST and are FULLY
  DONE** — ported with byte-for-byte parity oracle snapshots + PyO3 wrappers, and the
  Python pool layers delegate. The scope work is to CONFIRM this against the rubric (no
  `port-now` rows expected here), surface the one Rust-extra fn (`get_token_balance_given…`,
  unused in Python — not a gap), and bound the stays-python orchestration that legitimately
  remains.
- The **Solidly oracle retirement** is the only `port-now` (really a `delete-now` §4.3
  cleanup): the production Solidly solve path is fully Rust (`solve_solidly_path_int`;
  `SolidlyStableSolver` is parity-oracle-only per `arbitrage/CONTEXT.md` + Fork B).
- Canonical reading order applied: `AGENTS.md` → `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md`
  (§2.1/§2.2 + §4.3 oracle-retirement + Fork B) → `docs/adr/ADR-005` →
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md`.
- Baseline gate: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (untouched by scoping).

## Scope table

### COMPLETED — Rust-owned + parity-tested + Python delegating (do NOT redo)

| # | Row | Rust source | Python consumer | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|-------------|-----------------|-------------|------------------|
| C1 | Curve StableSwap math: `calc_d`/`calc_d_variant_alpha`/`calc_dp*`/`stableswap_get_d`/`stableswap_get_y`/`stableswap_get_y_d`/`stableswap_newton_y`/`stableswap_reduction_coefficient` (+ `DVariant`/`YVariant`/`YDVariant` enums) | `rust/crates/degenbot-curve-math/src/stableswap.rs` (lib.rs L42 `pub mod stableswap`) | `curve_stableswap_liquidity_pool.py` imports + delegates (L36–L42, L980/L1010/L1037/L1098/L1122); the 5 solvers are the PyO3 seam `curve_stableswap_{get_d,get_y,get_y_d,newton_y,reduction_coefficient}` in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/curve_math/lib.rs` | `done` | All iterative solvers ported; byte-for-byte parity vs the frozen Python `oracle_snapshot.txt` via `tests/oracle_crosscheck.rs` (`rust_matches_python_oracle_snapshot` + edge-case tests). Hot path; no I/O; no Python-ecosystem coupling. The Python oracle (`stableswap.py`) snapshot is RETAINED as the parity corpus (§4.3 leaves the corpus, retires the Python IMPLEMENTATION — but here the Python impl was already retired when the snapshot was frozen). |
| C2 | Curve calculator variants (Standard/Metapool/Metapool-underlying/LiveAdmin-dynamic/Crypto) — every `get_dy` calculator delegates its inner solver to Rust | `degenbot-curve-math` (the 5 solvers above) | `src/degenbot/curve/calculators/{standard,metapool,live_admin,crypto}.py` all `from degenbot.degenbot_rs import curve_stableswap_*` + delegate (standard.py L29, metapool.py L26/L216, live_admin.py L22, crypto.py L15) | `done` | The variant orchestration (rate sources, base-pool nesting, precision modes, admin-balance fetch sequencing) stays Python (§3.4 stays-python — it's I/O + config orchestration, not math); the inner Solvers are Rust. Confirmed: `crypto.py`'s `CryptoDyCalculator` delegates `newton_y`+`reduction_coefficient` to Rust — so the Curve V2/crypto path is NOT a gap. |
| C3 | Balancer WeightedMath: `calculate_invariant`/`calc_out_given_in`/`calc_in_given_out`/`subtract_swap_fee_amount`/`add_swap_fee_amount` | `rust/crates/degenbot-balancer-math/src/weighted_math.rs` (L43–L140) | `src/degenbot/balancer/pools.py` delegates via `balancer_weighted_*` PyO3 seam (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/balancer_math/lib.rs` L122–L218) | `done` | Full surface ported; byte-for-byte parity vs `oracle_snapshot.txt` (`tests/oracle_crosscheck.rs` covers the variant axes incl. `PowVersion` V1/V2 + edge cases zero/overflow/MAX_IN_RATIO). Python pools delegate (`CONTEXT.md`: "delegates all math to Rust core functions"). |
| C4 | Balancer StableMath: `calculate_invariant`/`calculate_invariant_deployed`/`calc_out_given_in`/`calc_in_given_out` | `rust/crates/degenbot-balancer-math/src/stable_math.rs` (L39–L279) | `src/degenbot/balancer/stable_pools.py` delegates via `balancer_stable_*` (L298–L365) | `done` | Same as C3 — full parity-tested port; the Python stable pool delegates `calculate_invariant(_deployed)` + `calc_{out,in}_given_in`. |
| C5 | Balancer FixedPoint (`fixed_point.rs`) + LogExpMath (`log_exp_math.rs`): `mul_down`/`div_down`/`div_up` + `pow_down`/`pow_up`/`nth_root` (the pow/nth-root covering `PowVersion` V1/V2 + the TWO/FOUR fast paths) | `rust/crates/degenbot-balancer-math/src/{fixed_point,log_exp_math}.rs` | `src/degenbot/balancer/libraries/scaling_helpers.py` delegates the three arithmetic leaves via `balancer_fixed_point_*` (orchestration stays Python); `CONTEXT.md`: "exponentiation (`pow_down`/`pow_up`) now lives wholly in Rust" | `done` | `fixed_point.py`/`weighted_math.py`/`log_exp_math.py` Python mirrors RETIRED (CONTEXT.md: "retired — Rust core"); the `pow_down`/`pow_up` + `PowVersion` V1/V2 fast-path detection all live in Rust; parity oracle snapshot covers the `PowVersion` variant axis. `subtract_swap_fee_amount`/`add_swap_fee_amount` + the three `fixed_point` leaves + `log_exp_math` all PyO3-wrapped. |
| C6 | Solidly stable solve (production — `solve_solidly_path_int`) | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/solver_dispatch.rs` (`Self::solve_solidly_path_int` — Möbius precheck + 25-iter golden-section over `degenbot-solidly-math` integer leaf `get_y_solidly`/`get_y_camelot`/`calc_exact_in_stable_{solidly,camelot}`) | engine dispatch (`solver_dispatch.rs`); NOT the Python `SolidlyStableSolver` | `done` | The production solve path is fully Rust (Solidly epic `MS5MBQ`/`FWTUOQ` done; Fork B). `EVM-exact` against on-chain Solidity. The `degenbot-solidly-math` PyO3 seam (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/solidly_math/lib.rs`) wraps the leaves. **ONLY the Python parity oracle survives** — see R1. |

### `stays-python` — orchestration / I/O / config (NOT a child)

data.title: Aave V3 event decoders (34 events across 8 enums) in degenbot-decoders
data.body:
## Goal
Port the **Aave V3 event decoders** (all 34 topic hashes + per-event field decoders) to `degenbot-decoders` — the decode-surface sibling to the pool decoders (`pool_created_decoder.rs` / `v3_mint_burn_decoder.rs` / etc.). Lives in the existing `degenbot-decoders` crate (mirror precedent), NOT in `degenbot-aave-updater` — mirrors how pool decoders are split from the pool-updater loop.

## Why this task exists
`run_aave_update` (sibling `6SWY4R`) fetches raw Aave V3 event logs via `degenbot_rpc::LogFetcher` and must decode them into typed `AaveChunkEvent` variants (the enum from CXRGX4 + POOLAPPLY + SCALEAPPLY + SPECIALAPPLY) + resolve address→id (via `get_or_create_*_on_conn` within the chunk transaction). The decode surface (topic-hash → event-type + field slicing) is currently Python-only (`src/degenbot/aave/events.py` — 34 topic-hashed events across 8 enums). This task ports them to Rust, mirroring the pool decoders' structure.

## Precedent (study before starting)
- `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/pool_created_decoder.rs` — pool `PoolCreated` event topic + field decoding. Module doc reproduces topic constants + documents `topic[0]`/`topic[1]`/`topic[2]` indexing. Mirror this pattern.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/v3_mint_burn_decoder.rs` / `v4_modify_liquidity_decoder.rs` — per-event decode fns returning typed structs.
- The decoders live in `degenbot-decoders` (separate from `degenbot-pool-updater` which consumes them) — MASTER precedent for the three-crate split (decode / substrate / loop).

## Event scope (this task — ALL 34 events across 8 enums)
- **`AaveV3PoolEvent` (11)** — Supply/Borrow/Repay/Withdraw/LiquidationCall/MintedToTreasury/DeficitCreated/ReserveDataUpdated/ReserveUsedAsCollateral{Enabled,Disabled}/UserEModeSet. The position + state events.
- **`AaveV3ScaledTokenEvent` (3)** — Mint/Burn/BalanceTransfer (aToken/vToken).
- **`AaveV3PoolConfigEvent` (12)** — CollateralConfigurationChanged/EModeCategoryAdded/EModeAssetCategoryChanged/AssetCollateralInEmodeChanged/ReserveInitialized/PoolUpdated/ProxyCreated/Upgraded/AddressSet + the address-set variants. The config events (CXRGX4's apply fns cover the subset that mutate state).
- **`AaveV3GhoDebtTokenEvent` (3)** — DiscountPercentUpdated/DiscountRateStrategyUpdated/DiscountTokenUpdated.
- **`AaveV3StkAaveEvent` (2)** — Staked/Redeem.
- **`AaveV3RewardsControllerEvent` (1)** — RewardsClaimed.
- **`AaveV3OracleEvent` (1)** — PriceOracleUpdated (CXRGX4 covers its apply + the AssetSourceUpdated oracle event).
- **`ERC20Event` (1)** — Transfer (the non-ScaledToken variant; used for aToken/vToken/stkAAVE balance tracking where ScaledToken BalanceTransfer doesn't fire).

Plus the `ScaledTokenEventType` enum (the from-layer abstraction that disambiguates which token type emitted the event — aToken vs vToken).

## Scope (this task)
1. **A new file** `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/aave_event_decoder.rs` (or split into `aave/pool_event.rs` / `aave/scaled_token_event.rs` / etc. if the events.py structure favors per-enum files — mirror the pool decoders' granularity choice). Module doc reproduces topic constants (computed as keccak256 of the canonical event signature — mirror `pool_created_decoder.rs` doc style).
2. **Per-event decode fns** — `decode_supply(log: &Log) -> Result<DecodedSupplyEvent, DecodeError>` etc. Each returns a typed struct matching the `AaveChunkEvent` variant's fields (resolved ids NOT done here — the decoder emits raw addresses/amounts; the orchestrator resolves them via `get_or_create_*_on_conn`). Mirror how the pool decoders emit `DecodedPoolCreated` (raw) for `run_pool_update` to resolve pool-id later.
3. **Topic-hash constants** — `pub const SUPPLY_TOPIC: [u8; 32] = ...;` (or `B256`), computed via `alloy::primitives::keccak256(b"Supply(address,address,uint256,uint8,uint16)")`. Mirror the pool decoder constants.
4. **A dispatch fn** — `decode_aave_log(log: &Log) -> Result<DecodedAaveEvent, DecodeError>` that switches on `log.topics[0]` to the matching per-event decoder.
5. **Re-export from `degenbot-decoders/src/lib.rs`** (mirror the pool decoder re-exports).

## Decode-error handling
- Mirror the precedent's `revert.rs` (`rust/crates/decoders/src/revert.rs`) for the decode-error type + handling.
- Unknown topic → a `DecodedAaveEvent::Unknown` variant or a `DecodeError::UnknownTopic` — investigate the precedent's choice + mirror; flag if the precedent leaves unknown topics for the caller to filter (the orchestrator should not crash on an unrelated log).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 34 events have a topic-constant + a per-event decode fn in `degenbot-decoders`.
- [ ] `decode_aave_log(&Log)` dispatch fn exists; returns the typed `DecodedAaveEvent` (raw addresses/amounts, no id resolution).
- [ ] Unit tests: per-event decode over a fixture log corpus — assert decoded fields match the Python `events.py` decode byte-for-byte (the §4.2 U5YIBG cross-check catches deviations at the apply layer; the decoders have their own unit tests asserting field-level correctness).
- [ ] `rg` for the 34 topic hashes against `src/degenbot/aave/events.py` — every Python topic has a Rust constant + decode fn.
- [ ] `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (decoders are core), `just test-rust`, `just lint-rust`, `just format` all green.

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just format`.

## Non-goals
- `apply_*` fns (CXRGX4 done; POOLAPPLY/SCALEAPPLY/SPECIALAPPLY) — the decoder emits raw fields; the apply fns consume resolved ids (orchestrator does resolution between).
- The `run_aave_update` orchestrator → sibling `6SWY4R` (consumes the decode surface).
- Python cutover → sibling `AVS4DR`.
- §4.2 parity → sibling `U5YIBG` (the decoder tests are unit-level here; U5YIBG does the end-to-end cross-check).

## Dependencies
- Independent of POOLAPPLY/SCALEAPPLY/SPECIALAPPLY (the decoder emits raw fields; the apply fns define the typed `AaveChunkEvent` variants but the decoder has its own `DecodedAaveEvent` shape). Can run in parallel with the apply-fn tasks.
- The orchestrator `6SWY4R` consumes both this task AND the apply-fn tasks — `6SWY4R` is blocked on AAVEDECODE + POOLAPPLY + SCALEAPPLY + SPECIALAPPLY all landing.
- Depends on: `CXRGX4` (done) — for the `AaveChunkWriteReport` shape consistency (the decoder's `DecodedAaveEvent` variants should align with the `AaveChunkEvent` variants' fields, even though the decoder emits raw addresses + the apply fns take resolved ids).
