data.title: Rust core: convert_alembic_to_rust_owned + ensure_schema RustOwned branch
data.body:
## Goal
- Close the schema-cutover design gap in `degenbot-db`: add a `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned` operation and extend `ensure_schema` with a `RustOwned { schema_version }` branch so a DB that has crossed the cutover boundary (tables present, `alembic_version` dropped, `_degenbot_db_schema_version` stamped) can be opened.

## Context
- Today `migrate.rs::ensure_schema` returns `Unrecognized` (and `DegenbotDb::open` refuses) for any DB with tables but no `alembic_version` table. That is correct for a foreign SQLite file, but it also **blocks the post-cutover state**: after cutover the `alembic_version` table is gone and `_degenbot_db_schema_version` holds the Rust schema version. The two cases must be distinguished.
- `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned(conn)` is the opt-in cutover op (ADR-010): verify `alembic_version.version_num == ALEMBIC_HEAD`, drop the `alembic_version` table, stamp `_degenbot_db_schema_version` with `RUST_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Refuse if the DB is `AlembicStale` (must upgrade via Alembic first) or `Unrecognized`.
- The cutover writes schema (DROP table + CREATE the version table) — it is the ONE operation that breaks the "Rust never writes schema to an Alembic DB" rule, and only because the DB is leaving Alembic ownership. Document this exception in the function's doc comment.
- Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot-db` consumer must be able to cutover their own DB from Rust. This is core, zero-pyo3.

## Checkpoint
- Produce: an updated `ensure_schema` state-machine sketch (ASCII or bullets) listing every `(tables_present?, alembic_version_present?, _degenbot_db_schema_version_present?)` combination and the resulting `SchemaState`. In particular resolve: does a `FreshStandalone` DB (empty, just DDL'd) also get `_degenbot_db_schema_version` stamped = `RUST_SCHEMA_VERSION` and therefore read back as `RustOwned` on next open? (Today `FreshStandalone` stamps it; confirm `RustOwned` subsumes `FreshStandalone` or remains distinct.)
- Then ask: is the state-machine草图 above correct, and is `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned` refusing `AlembicStale` + `Unrecognized` the right guard surface?
- Do not proceed past this point without user approval — the state machine is the contract every downstream task and the 0.7 retirement depend on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-db` exposes `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned(conn: &Connection) -> Result<RustOwnedInfo, DbError>` with the verification + DROP + stamp behaviour above. Errors: `DbError::AlembicStale` if not at head, `DbError::UnrecognizedSchema` if foreign, `DbError::Sqlite` on DDL failure.
- `SchemaState` gains `RustOwned { schema_version: u32 }`; `ensure_schema` returns it for the post-cutover shape.
- `DegenbotDb::open` opens a `RustOwned` DB normally (no `query_only=on` — it is Rust-owned now; future Rust-owned migrations will write through this connection).
- Unit tests: cutover an `AlembicCurrent` DB → re-open → `RustOwned`; cutover an `AlembicStale` DB → error; cutover a foreign file → `UnrecognizedSchema`; a `FreshStandalone` DB re-opens identically.
- State-machine sketch from the Checkpoint is committed to the ADR-010 appendix or the `migrate.rs` module doc.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`

## Completion note
- Implemented by delegated worker t-f280 (orchestrator t-6ff7 verified; Checkpoint satisfied by accepted ADR-010 §2). Committed as `020dffdf`: `feat(rust): add RustOwned schema state + alembic→rust cutover`.

- `SchemaState` gains `RustOwned { schema_version: u32 }` (migrate.rs).
- `ensure_schema` no-alembic/table_count>0 branch FIXED: now checks `_degenbot_db_schema_version` first — present+row → read version → `RustOwned`; absent → `Unrecognized`; present+no-row → `Unrecognized` (corrupt cutover). This single check fixes both the post-cutover open AND the re-opened-FreshStandalone bug (today both returned `Unrecognized`).
- ALSO (sharp design reading by t-f280, required by ADR-010 §2 row 1): `table_count` query now filters `_degenbot_db_schema_version` (`name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name <> SCHEMA_VERSION_TABLE`) so a bare stamp table counts as 0 tables → FreshStandalone correctly re-applies DDL. Without this, a freshly-stamped empty file would mis-read as RustOwned.
- `convert_alembic_to_rust_owned(conn) -> Result<RustOwnedInfo, DbError>`: on `AlembicCurrent` → DROP `alembic_version` + stamp version table → `RustOwnedInfo{schema_version: RUST_SCHEMA_VERSION}`; `AlembicStale` → `DbError::AlembicStale`; `Unrecognized` → `DbError::UnrecognizedSchema`; `RustOwned`/`FreshStandalone` → idempotent re-stamp. Extracted `stamp_rust_schema_version` helper shared with `apply_fresh_standalone`. `RustOwnedInfo` struct (room for future audit fields).
- `query_only` semantics UNCHANGED as instructed: read handle stays query_only (binding #2); `RustOwned` flows through `finish_open_inner`'s `other => Ok(other)` arm.
- Verified: `cargo test -p degenbot-db migrate` — all 9 migrate tests pass (5 new: rustowned_on_reopen_after_fresh_standalone, convert_alembic_current_to_rust_owned, convert_refuses_alembic_stale, convert_refuses_unrecognized, convert_idempotent_on_rustowned). `just test-rust` green, `just lint-rust` clean, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` OK.
- No kill-list items touched: `ALEMBIC_HEAD`, the AlembicCurrent/AlembicStale branches, `src/degenbot/migrations/`, pyproject deps all unchanged. Only ADDED a variant + a branch + an op.

## Result
rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/migrate.rs

data.title: Surface per-path sim-failure diagnostics in the backrun bot
Typed returns for transaction and receipt; fix storage round-trip
data.body:
## Goal
- `get_transaction` / `get_transaction_receipt` return alloy's typed
  `Transaction` / `Receipt` instead of `Option<serde_json::Value>`, removing
  a serialize-then-reparse round-trip on every call. `get_storage_at` drops
  the pointless `U256`→`B256` byte-array detour.

## Context
- Current `get_transaction`/`get_transaction_receipt` do
  `serde_json::to_value(&tx)` inside the retry closure, returning
  `Option<serde_json::Value>`. Inconsistent with the rest of the API
  (`EthBlock`, `Log`, `FeeHistory`) and wasteful.
- `get_storage_at` does `B256::from(result.to_be_bytes::<32>())` where a
  direct conversion suffices (and may be a no-op if alloy already returns
  `B256`).
- PyO3 wrappers serialize at the FFI boundary if Python needs JSON; the core
  returns typed values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `get_transaction` returns `ProviderResult<Option<Transaction>>` (alloy's
  typed tx type, consistent with `EthBlock`'s `Transaction<TxEnvelope>`).
- `get_transaction_receipt` returns `ProviderResult<Option<Receipt>>` (alloy
  typed).
- `get_storage_at` returns `B256` via a direct conversion — no
  `to_be_bytes::<32>()` detour. If alloy returns `U256`, use
  `B256::from(result)` or document why the detour exists. If alloy already
  returns `B256`, return it directly.
- PyO3 wrapper(s) that consume these updated accordingly (serialize to JSON
  for Python only if a Python caller existed; check `degenbot-python` for
  callers).
- Existing tests updated to assert on typed fields rather than JSON paths.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just test-rust-python` (if PyO3 wrappers change)
- `just lint-rust`

data.title: Rust core: upsert_exchange / set_exchange_active / upsert_pool_manager in degenbot-db
data.body:
## Goal
- Add the Rust-core exchange write substrate to `degenbot-db` that the `exchange activate/deactivate` CLI shells will delegate to: `upsert_exchange`, `set_exchange_active`, and `upsert_pool_manager`.

## Context
- Partial substrate already exists: `read.rs::fetch_exchange` (→ `ExchangeRow`), `discovery.rs::set_exchange_last_update_block`. Mirror their connection-handling + error style.
- `ExchangeTable` columns (`src/degenbot/database/models/base.py`): `id` (PK), `chain_id`, `name`, `active`, `last_update_block` (nullable), `factory` (Address), `deployer` (nullable Address). Unique on `(chain_id, name)`.
- `PoolManagerTable` columns (`src/degenbot/database/models/pools.py`): `id` (PK), `address`, `chain`, `kind`, `state_view` (nullable), `exchange_id` (FK). Unique on `(address, chain)`.
- These functions are **core** (`degenbot-db`) — zero `pyo3`. The PyO3 seam is task 4.
- Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer must be able to register an exchange and seed a V4 pool manager from Rust. This logic cannot live in the PyO3 wrapper.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-db` exposes:
  - `upsert_exchange(conn, chain_id, name, factory, deployer: Option<...>) -> ExchangeRow` — INSERT … ON CONFLICT(chain_id,name) DO UPDATE … RETURNING *, returning the full row (including `id` and `last_update_block`). Idempotent.
  - `set_exchange_active(conn, exchange_id, active: bool) -> ()` — UPDATE exchanges SET active=? WHERE id=?. Raises `DbError` if the row is absent.
  - `upsert_pool_manager(conn, address, chain, kind, state_view: Option<...>, exchange_id) -> PoolManagerRow` — INSERT … ON CONFLICT(address, chain) DO UPDATE … RETURNING *. Idempotent.
- A `PoolManagerRow` typed row is added mirroring `ExchangeRow` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/rows/`).
- Unit tests in `degenbot-db` cover: upsert-then-update exchange; activate/deactivate; pool-manager upsert idempotency; missing-row error path. Tests use an in-memory or temp-file DB created via `ensure_schema` on the fresh-standalone path.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`

## Completion note
- Implemented by delegated worker t-f280 (orchestrator t-6ff7 verified). Committed as `f1e71a78`: `feat(rust): add exchange write substrate to degenbot-db`.
- Three methods on `DegenbotDb` in `discovery.rs`: `upsert_exchange` (SELECT-then-INSERT dedup, returns existing row unchanged, does NOT touch active), `set_exchange_active` (UPDATE; `DbError::MissingRow` on rows_affected==0), `upsert_pool_manager` (ON CONFLICT(address,chain) DO UPDATE … RETURNING). 8 unit tests in `discovery::tests`.
- Key design held: NO unique index added to `exchanges(chain_id, name)` — would force an Alembic migration, out of scope for 0.6.x per ADR-010. Confirmed `MissingRow(String)` is the crate's existing not-found variant — no new variant needed.
- Verified: `just test-rust` green, `just lint-rust` clean, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` OK.
- Drive-by: `cargo fmt` line-wrapped one `.map_err(...)` in `db/pool_read.rs::db_fetch_exchange` (left unformatted by commit 50ebc92f) so the tree passes `fmt-check`. Pure formatting, no logic change.

## Result

data.title: Fix: Rust writer 16496792 bootstrap gaps — PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap (extends O4BOST) + AssetSourceUpdated event-ordering tolerance (Rust-only; Python PRICE_ORACLE assert accepted as cold-boot gap retiring in CZM7TI)
data.body:
## Goal

Fix the writer divergence captured by the JGQHBX harness at mainnet block **16_496_792** (the first `ReserveInitialized` event). Both writers crash at this block on a fresh-market cold-boot — exposing long-standing bootstrap-path + event-ordering gaps that production DBs sidestep via historically-populated rows.

## Captured by

`scripts/aave_replay_diff.py drive --to 16496800` (real mainnet RPC via `$DEGENBOT_RPC_HTTP_CHAINID_1`). Captured by Aave Worker, recorded in HLYWI6's body (`## Tooling` → "First real divergence captured (block 16496792)").

## The dual crash

At mainnet block **16_496_792**:

- **Python `update_aave_market`** → `assert oracle_contract is not None` at `event_handlers.py:667`. The Python path expects the `PRICE_ORACLE` row to already exist in `aave_v3_contracts` when an `AssetSourceUpdated` (or similar price-related) event arrives. The PRICE_ORACLE row is bootstrap-discovered via a `PoolAddressProvider` `AddressSet(id=PRICE_ORACLE, ...)` event; on a fresh-market cold-boot, the assert fires before this bootstrap occurs.

- **Rust `run_aave_update`** → `AssetSourceUpdated: no asset for underlying WETH`. The Rust's `AssetSourceUpdated` handler looks up the asset row by `underlying_address` and errors if missing. The corresponding `ReserveInitialized` event (which WOULD create the WETH asset row) is also in the same chunk — but the Rust processes the `AssetSourceUpdated` event BEFORE the `ReserveInitialized` event, so the asset doesn't yet exist when the price-source event is dispatched.

Note: these are INDEPENDENT bugs that happen to crash at the same block; the writers fail on DIFFERENT events. This is NOT a cutover regression — both writers' fresh-market cold-boot paths have these gaps. They've never hit production because production markets were bootstrapped historically (PRICE_ORACLE row + initial assets already populated by prior Python runs); only a fresh cold-boot exposes them.

## Architectural context

- **AGENTS.md Architectural Vision** — "Rust is the engine; Python is a driver shell, not a co-implementation." Cold-boot is bot functionality, must live in Rust. The RHS (Rust-side) fix is on the critical path. The LHS (Python-side) gap is **ANTI-DIRECTIONAL to fix** (the Python retires in CZM7TI; fixing its PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap would add Python co-implementation of bot functionality that the Rust will eventually own entirely).
- The Python path's PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap is supposed to be replaced by a Rust bootstrap in due course — either this task (RHS only — PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap as part of O4BOST-adjacent work) OR a follow-up bootstrap pass that extends O4BOST's pattern to all PoolAddressProvider-emitted bootstrap events. **DIRECTION**: fix the Rust (both bootstrap-tolerance + event-ordering). Ignore the Python gap (it gets retired).

## This task is NOT a Python fix

This task does NOT fix the Python PRICE_ORACLE assert. That gap is acknowledged + left to retire in CZM7TI. Reasoning:
1. Per the architectural vision, adding Python co-implementation of bot bootstrap is anti-directional.
2. After this task lands + the Rust self-bootstraps + the Rust event-ordering is fixed, the JGQHBX harness's `drive` will see the Python STILL crash at block 16_496_792 (its assert) while the Rust advances past it. That's a known + accepted harness asymmetry, NOT a Rust-vs-Python parity failure — the Python itself is broken-in-cold-boot, the Rust is the canonical fix. The harness note (in HLYWI6's body) should record this: "the Python's PRICE_ORACLE assert at 16_496_792 is a known Python-side cold-boot gap; the Rust has its own bootstrap path that handles this; once the Python is retired (CZM7TI) the harness's `--python-only` flag loses meaning for ranges past 16_496_792."
3. The HLYWI6 verification strategy needs to **shift from "(i) Rust-vs-Python to tip"** (which requires a working Python cold-boot that you don't have + won't fix) **to "(ii) Rust-vs-on-chain truth"** (Rust drives cold-boot to tip, then batch-verify DB state against the Aave contracts via RPC). This is actually architecturally cleaner — on-chain truth is the gold standard, and you don't depend on the broken Python reference.

## Implementation contract (Rust-only)

Two distinct Rust-side fixes — both required for the Rust to drive past 16_496_792 on a fresh-market cold-boot.

### Fix 1 — bootstrap PRICE_ORACLE (and other PoolAddressProvider-discovered contracts)

Conceptually extends O4BOST's bootstrap-pass pattern (which targets `ProxyCreated(id=POOL/POOL_CONFIGURATOR, ...)`). Add to the same bootstrap pass:
- Fetch `AddressSet(id, old, new)` events from `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` over the same bootstrap window.
- For each `AddressSet` whose `id` matches the right-padded ASCII `b"PRICE_ORACLE"` (or other Aave-protocol-recognized contracts: `b"POOL_DATA_PROVIDER"` etc. — confirm by reading the Python `update_aave_market` Phase-1 fetch + dispatch logic at `commands.py:1010–1062` for the full set), insert via `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` (the idempotent helper O4BOST introduced).
- This populates `PRICE_ORACLE` (and any other PoolAddressProvider-discovered contract) BEFORE the chunk loop sees the first price-related event.

### Fix 2 — AssetSourceUpdated event-ordering tolerance (or correct ordering)

Two acceptable designs (pick the one that matches the Python's reference behavior — since the Python path is itself broken here, you can't simply mirror the Python; defer to what's correct):

- **Design I (tolerance)**: the Rust's `AssetSourceUpdated` handler becomes tolerant of a not-yet-existing asset row. Behavior on missing asset: skip the event (with a debug log "deferred: asset missing for {underlying}"); the `ReserveInitialized` event later in the chunk creates the asset. This requires DEFERRING the price-source application — the `ReserveInitialized` handler must apply the price source retroactively (or store the pending `AssetSourceUpdated` for the not-yet-created asset + apply once the asset exists). Both paths are workable; pick the simpler.
- **Design II (ordering)**: enforce strict chronological order within a chunk: sort the chunk's events by `(block, logIndex)` BEFORE dispatching, so `ReserveInitialized` (which precedes `AssetSourceUpdated` on-chain per mainnet logIndex) is dispatched first. **Investigate first**: is the current Rust chunk ordering already logIndex-sorted, or is it tx-grouped only (within-tx-sorted but cross-tx-unordered)? If already sorted by logIndex, this bug isn't an ordering bug — it's that mainnet actually emits AssetSourceUpdated before ReserveInitialized (on-chain) and the Python path sidesteps it differently.

Investigate the mainnet event ordering at block 16_496_792 FIRST (via `scripts/aave_replay_diff.py bisect --to 16496800 --max-blocks 1` — it prints the per-tx events in chronological order) to disambiguate:
- If on-chain, AssetSourceUpdated comes AFTER ReserveInitialized → it's a Rust ORDERING bug → Fix 2a (sort by logIndex + defer-or-buffer).
- If on-chain, AssetSourceUpdated comes BEFORE ReserveInitialized → it's a TOLERANCE bug → Fix 2b (defer the price-source application until after the asset is created).
- If they're in the SAME tx (same transactionIndex) → on-chain ordering has AssetSourceUpdated before ReserveInitialized within the tx (unusual but possible); tolerance fix is the only practical path.

Pick based on what the bisect output of the 16_496_792 events shows. Document the on-chain ordering (verbatim paste) in the completion summary.

## TDD implementation order

1. **Investigate** ordering at block 16_496_792 first (`bisect --to 16496800`, capture the per-tx events). Confirm whether the on-chain order is `ReserveInitialized < AssetSourceUpdated` (an ordering bug) or `AssetSourceUpdated < ReserveInitialized` (a tolerance bug + a Python-bootstrap-gap symptom).
2. **PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap** — extend O4BOST's bootstrap pass to fetch + apply `PoolAddressProvider.AddressSet(id=PRICE_ORACLE)` events. Test: cold-boot a fresh DB → smoke at `--to 16496800` → both `PRICE_ORACLE` row exists + Rust advances to 16_496_800 without crashing on the `oracle_contract is not None`-equivalent Rust path.
3. **AssetSourceUpdated tolerance/ordering** — based on the investigation finding, implement Design I or II. Test: mocked chunk containing both events in the correct on-chain order advances without crashing; the asset row's `price_source` column reflects the eventual `AssetSourceUpdated` once both events have applied.
4. **End-to-end smoke** — `scripts/aave_replay_diff.py drive --to 16496801` (one block past the prior crash point) is GREEN for the Rust side (cand.db advances; no Rust errors). The Python side still crashes (its PRICE_ORACLE assert — accepted as a Python-side cold-boot gap; recorded in the harness). Compare's exit code reflects: 1 (Python crashed; ref.db has divergent-from-cand state OR the harness's compare is GREEN only on the rows both writers DID populate, treating the Python's crash as a keyset diff vs cand — specify in JGQHBX body if not already).
5. **Expand harness coverage** — re-drive at `--to 16_596_000` (10k more blocks). Report GREEN or NEW divergences. Iterate.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT fix the Python's `assert oracle_contract is not None` at `event_handlers.py:667`. (Per the architectural vision + CZM7TI direction.)
- Do NOT add `PRICE_ORACLE` to `aave activate` (no Python changes — Python stays a thin seed). The PRICE_ORACLE row is bootstrap-discovered by the Rust (this task) from `PoolAddressProvider.AddressSet` events, mirroring how O4BOST discovers POOL/POOL_CONFIGURATOR from `ProxyCreated`.
- Do NOT add a `UNIQUE` constraint on `aave_v3_contracts` — idempotency is logic-level (via `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` from O4BOST).
- Do NOT delete the Python writer or the writer_parity tests (CZM7TI's lane).
- Do NOT build the (ii) on-chain-truth verification harness in this task — that's a HLYWI6-strategy follow-up. This task is the Rust write-path fix only.

## Sequencing

- Depends on **O4BOST** (it introduces `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` + the PoolAddressProvider `ProxyCreated` bootstrap pattern that this task extends with `AddressSet`).
- Blocks **HLYWI6** (the cold-boot path can't reach `--to tip` without both the PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap + the AssetSourceUpdated tolerance/ordering).

## Deliverable

- PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap extension to the O4BOST bootstrap pass (commands.py reading not required; the Python is the reference for what events to discover).
- AssetSourceUpdated tolerance or ordering fix in the Rust chunk dispatch.
- A real-RPC smoke test verifying `drive --to 16496801` is GREEN for the Rust side + the harness's compare reports the Python-side crash as a known harness asymmetry (recorded in the JGQHBX body).
- Expand test coverage at `--to 16596000` (or further) — capture GREEN or new divergences.
- Update HLYWI6's body to note: "(i) Rust-vs-Python strategy is INFEASIBLE for full-cold-boot — the Python's fresh-market cold-boot path is broken (PRICE_ORACLE assert gap + others likely). The verification strategy shifts to (ii) Rust-vs-on-chain truth." Flag this to the user via the orchestrator; do not change HLYWI6's strategy text unilaterally.

## Coordination

- `Aave Orchestrator` on pi-link. Ping at:
  - Confirmation of the on-chain ordering at 16_496_792 (Design I vs II decision).
  - On PRICE_ORACLE bootstrap landing (mid-task checkpoint).
  - If the harness's compare behavior needs clarification re: Python-crashed-side handling (does a Python-side crash at block N produce: ref.db has rows up to N-1 only; do we treat that as a "compare is for rows both populated" — needs documenting).
  - On task completion with `drive --to 16596000` smoke result + any newer divergences surfaced by the expanded range.

16496792 bootstrap gaps fixed (Rust-only). Three fixes; all GREEN.

On-chain ordering at block 16496792 (probed via eth_getLogs, tx 357):
  logIdx 409 AssetSourceUpdated (PRICE_ORACLE)      WETH
  logIdx 413 ReserveInitialized (POOL_CONFIGURATOR)  WETH  [creates asset]
  logIdx 419 CollateralConfigurationChanged          WETH
  logIdx 421 PriceOracleUpdated                       WETH
SAME tx; AssetSourceUpdated precedes ReserveInitialized on-chain → Design I
(tolerance), not Design II (events are already logIndex-sorted).

Fix 1b — fresh PRICE_ORACLE lookup (NOT the task body's AddressSet bootstrap).
The AddressSet approach is INFEASIBLE: 0 AddressSet events from the
PoolAddressProvider in [16291071, 16496800]; PRICE_ORACLE is registered via
PriceOracleUpdated at 16291126 (fetched by the chunk loop's address-provider
pass), not AddressSet. Root cause: build_fetch_spec caches oracle_address ONCE
before the loop = None (PRICE_ORACLE registered mid-loop); the spec's stale None
crashed ReserveInitialized. New fetch_aave_oracle_address_on_conn (conn-scoped)
+ the ReserveInitialized dispatch arm falls back to it when the spec's cached
oracle_address is None.

Fix 2b — AssetSourceUpdated tolerance. dispatch_asset_source_updated returns
Result<Option<AaveChunkEvent>> + skips (Ok(None)) when the asset missing. Safe:
the later ReserveInitialized (same tx) creates the asset + its getSourceOfAsset
RPC at block_number recovers the price_source. 2 unit tests.

Fix 2c — intra-dispatch apply. dispatch_config_events applies each AaveChunkEvent
to conn AS it's dispatched (logIndex order), so a later config event's dispatch
sees an earlier event's apply (e.g. CollateralConfigurationChanged at 419 sees
the asset ReserveInitialized at 413 created). Root cause of the
CollateralConfigurationChanged crash: the chunk loop previously dispatched ALL
config events (collecting a Vec) THEN applied in a batch — so during dispatch
the earlier events' writes weren't on conn. Matches the Python's per-event apply.
The chunk loop's batch apply (former step (d)) is removed.

PRICE_ORACLE NOT bootstrapped via a bootstrap pass — the chunk loop's own
PriceOracleUpdated discovery registers it; O4BOST's
apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn is reused idempotently by the existing
PriceOracleUpdated apply. No new bootstrap pass; no AddressSet handling.

Tests: 138 aave-updater lib + 89 degenbot-db lib + 75 writer_parity (byte-IDENTITY
unchanged — the intra-dispatch apply doesn't change any fixture's final state) +
1 cold_boot + 8 replay_diff. clippy clean; core crates pyo3-free.

Real-RPC smoke (fresh DB → cold seed → run_aave_update --to 16496801): GREEN.
21 chunks, 15 events, 5 contracts (POOL/POOL_CONFIGURATOR/POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER/
POOL_DATA_PROVIDER/PRICE_ORACLE), 3 assets (WETH + 2 more bootstrapping
reserves), last_update_block → 16496801.

Harness (JGQHBX) tolerates the Python ref's crash (no re-raise) so the Rust-side
GREEN + the asymmetry are captured: drive --to 16496801 → cand_ok=true, cand_stamp
16496801; ref_ok=false (Python crashes at 16496792, its PRICE_ORACLE assert — known
Python-side cold-boot gap retiring in CZM7TI); compare exit=1, all divergences are
cand_only (ref.db is partial up to the crash).

Step 5 expanded range (--to 16596000) surfaced a NEW divergence at block 16496817:
'malformed Supply event' — decode_supply_pool_event requires 5 topics but the
Aave V3 Supply event has 4. Filed as task 7UFMZX (Rust-only decode bug, sequenced
after I2RHGP, blocks HLYWI6). OUT of I2RHGP's scope (it's a decoder bug, not the
16496792 bootstrap/PRICE_ORACLE/AssetSourceUpdated gap).

HLYWI6 strategy note (flagged to the orchestrator, per task: do NOT change HLYWI6
unilaterally): the (i) Rust-vs-Python strategy is INFEASIBLE for full-cold-boot
past 16496792 — the Python's fresh-market cold-boot path is broken. The
verification strategy should shift to (ii) Rust-vs-on-chain truth (Rust drives
cold-boot to tip, batch-verify DB state against the Aave contracts via RPC).

Commits: ee25d2a1 (I2RHGP fixes), b34f695f + 1cd1bc70 (JGQHBX harness tolerate ref crash).

data.title: Scope: Publisher/subscriber
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Publisher/subscriber → Rust core** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **Publisher/subscriber → Rust core**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

# Scope: Publisher/subscriber → Rust core

Epic `2K2JP4` · Scope task `I7KVKM` · Agent `researcher_1@degenbot`

Status legend: **COMPLETED** = Rust-owned + Python delegating · **IN-FIGHT** = partial (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere) · **NOT-STARTED** = no Rust counterpart; rubric says belongs in Rust.

Rubric (§2.1) criteria shorthand: **hot** (per-block/per-log?) · **GIL** (CPU-bound holds GIL?) · **type** (pure int/tag vs Python obj/WeakSet) · **I/O** (in-process dispatch vs RPC/DB) · **eco** (Python-ecosystem coupling) · **dup** (§2.3 duplication smell) · **standalone** (ADR-005).

## KEY DISTINCTION (orchestrator's): MECHANISM vs CONSUMERS

- **MECHANISM** = the dispatch/listener infrastructure (subscribe/unregister + fan-out `notify`). Rust ALREADY owns a complete one; the Python `PublisherMixin` is a parallel copy. ⇒ `port-now` to bridge (IN-FIGHT convergence), not greenfield.
- **CONSUMERS** = the Python orchestration that subscribes to drive update loops (engine_registry, CLI update hooks, test fakes). ⇒ `stays-python` (orchestration/drivers), with only the *subscribe call* routed through the Rust seam.

## §2.3 duplication smell — CONFIRMED + already partially resolved

A **complete Rust pub/sub mechanism already exists** in `degenbot-bot`, running on `BotState` in the hot pump loop; Python has a **parallel** mechanism on the (being-phased-out) Python pool classes. They are not bridged:

| Layer | Mechanism | Pointer |
|---|---|---|
| Rust (hot path) | `PoolStateSubscriber: Send+Sync` trait + `LogDispatcher::{subscribe(pool_id, Weak<dyn PoolStateSubscriber>), notify(pool_id), dispatch(log, state)}` — `Weak` fan-out with dead-weak skipping, applied AFTER the `BotState` write guard is released (D2 lock order); `EngineSubscriber` adapts it to `UniswapEngine::insert_dirty`; `DrainSink{on_drain,on_send,notify_block}` for the pump drain lifecycle. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs`; `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/engine_subscriber.rs`; `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/drain_sink.rs` |
| Python (parallel) | `Publisher`/`Subscriber` Protocol + `PublisherMixin` (`subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`_notify_subscribers` over a `WeakSet`) + `PoolStateMessage`/`...PoolStateUpdated`. Each Python pool calls `self._notify_subscribers(message=...PoolStateUpdated(self.state))` after a state change. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py`; consumers: `uniswap/{v2,v3,v4}_liquidity_pool.py`, `aerodrome/pools.py`, `balancer/{pools,stable_pools}.py`, `curve/curve_stableswap_liquidity_pool.py` |

The Rust mechanism is the canonical one per the migration vision (Rust owns state → Rust notifies). The work is **bridging** (a `PySubscriberAdapter` so Python consumers can subscribe to Rust `BotState` notifications through `LogDispatcher`), then retiring the parallel Python `PublisherMixin` dispatch on pool types whose state is Rust-owned.

## COMPLETED (Rust-owned, Python delegates)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Pointer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rust pub/sub mechanism** (`PoolStateSubscriber` trait + `LogDispatcher` subscribe/notify/dispatch + `Weak`-fan-out + dead-weak skip + D2 lock discipline) | `done` | hot (per-log in pump); GIL-free (`parking_lot::Mutex`, no Python); type=pure (pool_id u64); standalone (a `cargo add degenbot` consumer subscribes to `BotState` updates directly). Already routes `EngineSubscriber`→engine dirty-mark. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs` |
| **Engine subscriber adapter** (`EngineSubscriber` → `UniswapEngine::insert_dirty`) | `done` | the canonical `PoolStateSubscriber` impl; bridges Rust notify→engine dirty-mark. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/engine_subscriber.rs` |
| **Pump drain lifecycle notifications** (`DrainSink::on_drain`/`on_send`/`notify_block`) | `done` | hot-path drain fan-out; already Rust. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/drain_sink.rs` |

## IN-FIGHT (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale | Python side | Rust side | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Python pool pub/sub dispatch** (`PublisherMixin._notify_subscribers` on V2/V3/V4/Aerodrome/Balancer/Curve pools → `...PoolStateUpdated` messages) | `partial` → bridge + retire | dup (parallel to `LogDispatcher`); hot (per state change). Bridge via a `PySubscriberAdapter` (`#[pyclass] impl PoolStateSubscriber` holding a `Py<PyAny>` Python `Subscriber`/callback; re-acquires GIL on `on_pool_state_updated`); register with `LogDispatcher::subscribe`. Then retire `PublisherMixin` dispatch on Rust-owned pool types. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py::{Publisher,Subscriber,PublisherMixin,_notify_subscribers,PoolStateMessage}`; the `_notify_subscribers(message=...)` callsites in the pool classes | `PoolStateSubscriber`+`LogDispatcher` (done) — needs the PyO3 adapter bridging Python subscribers IN | `ZBD4MS` |

## NOT-STARTED (`port-now` / `stays-python`)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Python side | Rust side | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`PySubscriberAdapter` PyO3 seam** (let a Python `Subscriber`/callback register as a `PoolStateSubscriber` with `LogDispatcher`) | `port-now` | thin translator (rubric §3 B); bridges the two mechanism halves. hot-path-adjacent (re-acquires GIL only when a Python subscriber is present). standalone: a Python-driven MEV bot subscribes to Rust state through this. | n/a (the bridge itself) | (adapter lives in `degenbot-python`; cores stay pyo3-free) | `ZBD4MS` (folds the IN-FIGHT bridge above — one task does both) |
| **Python pub/sub consumers** (subscribe-to-drive-update-loop orchestration: `engine_registry` wiring, CLI update hooks, `FakeSubscriber` test helper) | `stays-python` (route subscribe call only) | eco=Python async/CLI orchestration; the *mechanism* is Rust (sibling). Consumer *reaction* bodies stay Python. | `src/degenbot/arbitrage/engine_registry.py`; CLI; `tests/fakes/subscribers.py` | n/a | `73UJL6` (deps `ZBD4MS`) |
| **Stays-Python (recorded, not ported)** | `stays-python` | | | | |
| └ `TextMessage` (generic text pub/sub message) | `stays-python` | Python-only convenience message with no Rust-state equivalent; only `PoolStateMessage`/`PoolStateUpdated` bridges. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py::TextMessage` | n/a | — |
| └ RPC WebSocket `eth_subscribe` / `subscribe_blocks` / `subscribe_logs` | `stays-python` (out of scope) | RPC pub-sub — a different concern (Epic for `degenbot-rpc`), NOT this in-process message mechanism. | `src/degenbot/bot.py::subscribe_blocks/subscribe_logs`; `engine_registry.subscribe` | n/a | — |
| └ Consumer orchestration *logic* (what `notify` does in each consumer) | `stays-python` | orchestration/drivers (per §2.1 "Keep in Python"). Routed through the Rust seam (subscribe call), bodies unchanged. | `engine_registry`, CLI update loops | n/a | — |

## Child task split (port-now/partial rows → implementation tasks)

| Child | Title | Disposition origin | Deps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ZBD4MS` | Extend Rust `PoolStateSubscriber`/`LogDispatcher` with a `PySubscriberAdapter` seam; retire parallel Python `PublisherMixin` dispatch on Rust-owned pools | mechanism `port-now` + IN-FIGHT bridge | — (Rust mechanism already landed; in-process, no DB/BotState edge to wire) |
| `73UJL6` | Route Python pub/sub consumers (engine_registry/CLI/test fakes) through the `PySubscriberAdapter` seam; consumer reaction bodies stay Python | consumers `stays-python` (subscribe-call routing only) | `ZBD4MS` (intra-epic) |

Route-before-type ordering: `ZBD4MS` (the bridge seam) → `73UJL6` (consumer subscription routing). The Rust mechanism itself is `done` (no ordering edge to a mechanism-build task — it already exists).

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **Cross-epic edges: NONE.** Pub/sub is in-process (no `SLHSM4`/DB edge). `BotState`+`LogDispatcher` are co-located in `degenbot-bot` and already Rust-owned — a `done` reference, not a dep to wire (per your guidance "record as reference if so, no edge"). The `engine_registry`'s `engine.subscribe(node_ws)` is RPC WS-subscribe, unrelated. [RESOLVED — no cross-epic edges to wire.]
2. **Retirement sequencing of `PublisherMixin` on pool classes:** `ZBD4MS` retires the Python dispatch ONLY on pool types whose state is already Rust-owned (`BotState` V2/V3/V4). Pools whose state is still Python-authority (e.g. Balancer/Curve if not yet migrated) keep `PublisherMixin` until their state migrates. `ZBD4MS`'s AC scopes this per-pool-type; flag any pool type whose state isn't yet Rust-owned as "keep Python dispatch" rather than force-retire. [DECIDED — per-pool-type retirement gated on state ownership; non-blocking.]
3. **`PySubscriberAdapter` GIL re-acquisition cost** on the hot path: only fires when a Python subscriber is actually registered for a pool_id (most hot-path pools have only the Rust `EngineSubscriber`, no Python subscriber → no GIL cost). Acceptable; recorded in `ZBD4MS` AC. Non-blocking.
4. **`DrainSink` trait extension for Python consumers?** Decided NO — Python consumers subscribe per-pool via `LogDispatcher::subscribe`, not the `DrainSink` pump-lifecycle trait (which is engine-internal). Keeps the surface minimal. Non-blocking.

## Validation Gates (scope task)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — PASS at baseline (confirmed; no cores touched by the scope pass).
- Scope table written + children created before marking done.
- Child tasks `ZBD4MS` / `73UJL6` created with Goal/Context(cited rubric dispositions + the dup-smell + mechanism-vs-consumer distinction)/AC/Validation-Gates/Non-goals; intra-epic edge (`ZBD4MS→73UJL6`) wired; no cross-epic edges (none needed).

Result pointer: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` (also recorded here; `ergo --json show` `result` field may display `None` per the known gotcha — cosmetic).

data.title: Audit remaining 6f574e07 latent asserts (protect Python gold-standard for future block ranges)
data.body:
# Audit remaining 6f574e07 latent asserts (protect Python gold-standard for future block ranges)

## Context

Commit `6f574e07` ("lint: dead code cleanup", 2026-04-17, BowTiedDevil) added **66 hard `assert` statements across 15 files**, of which **12 are in `src/degenbot/cli/aave/event_handlers.py`** (the Aave event-handler module). The 0.6.0a2 reference code used defensive `if X is None: logger.warning(...); return None` / proper UPSERT-elif patterns; 6f574e07 misread those as dead code and replaced them with hard asserts that crash on legitimate non-initialization mainnet events.

The first of these (the `assert existing_oracle is None` + `assert old_address == ZERO_ADDRESS` pair in `_process_price_oracle_updated_event`) was restored to v0.6.0a2 UPSERT semantics in commit `39eda2af`. That restoration was EMPIRICALLY INERT in the [16291071, 16591070] cold-boot drive range (the second PriceOracleUpdated event lands beyond 16591070), but it is correctness-right regardless and necessary for any future range extension.

## The risk this task prevents

The Python writer is the **gold-standard parity reference** for the Rust cold-boot correctness verification (per the orchestrator's directive "Use the Python code as the gold standard. We must have a match!"). The verified-clean Python reference at block 16591070 was established in the 2026-07-06 thread (full cold-boot + non-fatal `verify_all_positions` PASSED against on-chain truth).

If a future drive past 16591070 hits an un-audited 6f574e07 assert, the Python writer CRASHES and we **lose the gold-standard reference for that range** — collapsing the parity gate exactly where the divergences are most likely to live (post-16591070 is the chunk-12 ~p534 crash range per 44JTVN). This task must run BEFORE any attempt to extend the Python gold-standard drive past 16591070.

## Goal

Audit each remaining 6f574e07 assert (the 11 others in `event_handlers.py` + the 54 across the other 14 files). For each:

1. **Locate** it (the 6f574e07 commit diff is the canonical inventory — `git show 6f574e07` enumerates every added assert).
2. **Compare** against v0.6.0a2's defensive form (`git show v0.6.0a2:<path>` for each affected file).
3. **Classify**: (a) legitimate assertion of a real invariant that v0.6.0a2 also enforced differently (keep, possibly convert to explicit raise), OR (b) 6f574e07 over-tightening that crashes on legitimate mainnet events past the first occurrence (restore v0.6.0a2 warn-and-skip OR UPSERT semantics).
4. **Restore** the (b)-class asserts to v0.6.0a2 form, verbatim (same "copy verbatim" discipline as `39eda2af`). One commit per restored handler (or one commit per file if the asserts in a file are tightly related — the worker's judgment).
5. **Drive-test** each restoration: re-run the Python cold-boot drive past the block where the relevant event class fires, confirming the writer no longer crashes there.

## Sequencing

- PARALLEL to the EIWEPM-divergence resolution work (TYS5MS / SB3XJF / LTGZL6) — does not block them.
- MUST complete BEFORE any range extension past 16591070 of the Python gold-standard drive (i.e., blocks any future chunk-12 Python re-drive — the gold-standard-protection gate for 44JTVN's range).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT bundle restores into a single mega-commit (one per handler/file, per the 39eda2af precedent).
- Do NOT delete the asserts wholesale — some may be legitimate post-6f574e07 invariants. Audit + classify, then restore only the (b)-class over-tightenings.
- Do NOT touch the Rust code path; this is Python-only gold-standard protection.
- Do NOT re-introduce the duplicate-row silent accumulations that pre-6f574e07 code had (e.g., the pre-6f574e07 unconditional INSERT in PriceOracleUpdated). UPSERT (if/elif), not unconditional INSERT.

data.title: fix(db): delete stale liquidity rows on drained pool (parity with Python)
data.body:
# fix(db): delete stale liquidity rows on drained pool (parity with Python)

## This is a CORRECTNESS bug, not a perf issue
Surfaced during the F4N6DX perf review but it is a real data-correctness bug: ghost liquidity rows linger indefinitely on a fully-drained pool, then get re-read into the next apply's `tick_data` with stale non-zero liquidity → wrong base state → **compounding corruption**.

## Validated by spike `DWGD36` (research complete, verdict: INTENT A — real bug, fix the code)

### Root cause
`delete_stale_rows` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs`) early-returns `Ok(())` on `live_keys.is_empty()`, skipping the delete entirely:

```rust
if live_keys.is_empty() {
    // No live keys → delete ALL rows for this pool.
    return Ok(());   // ← DELETES NOTHING — contradicts the comment
}
// ... chunked `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1 AND {key_col} NOT IN (...)`
```

The comment claims "delete ALL"; the code deletes nothing. The pre-built `sql` passed by callers uses `NOT IN ({placeholders})` which would be a syntax error on empty input, so the early-return was likely added to avoid that — but it silently dropped the "delete all" semantic.

### Python parity oracle (the deciding evidence)
`0a431b97^:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py`, `apply_v3_liquidity_updates`:
```python
db_ticks = {position.tick for position in pool_in_db.liquidity_positions}
helper_ticks = set(current_tick_data)
if ticks_to_drop := db_ticks - helper_ticks:
    session.execute(delete(...).where(...pool_id..., .tick.in_(ticks_to_drop)))
```
On a drained pool: `helper_ticks = set()` → `ticks_to_drop = db_ticks - set() = db_ticks` (ALL existing rows) → truthy → **Python DELETES ALL existing tick rows**. Init-maps use the same complement-with-truthy pattern (`words_to_drop := db_words - helper_words`, filtered by `map_.bitmap != 0`). V4 mirrors V3 exactly. **Python deletes all on empty-live; Rust deletes nothing — pure parity violation.** The comment is RIGHT; the code is WRONG.

### Reachability (not a hypothetical edge case)
cl-math prunes zero-gross ticks (`rust/crates/degenbot-cl-math/src/cl_lib/liquidity_mapping.rs:250-253`): `if new_liquidity_gross == U128::ZERO { tick_data.remove(&current_tick); flip_tick(&mut tick_bitmap, ...); continue; }`. A pool fully drained (all positions burned to zero) → every tick removed from `tick_data` → `live_ticks = tick_data.keys().copied().collect()` is EMPTY in `persist_v3` → `delete_stale_v3_positions_on_conn(conn, pool_id, &[])` → the early-return triggers. cl-math's `flip_tick` zeros bitmap bits → empty `live_words` filtered by `bw.bitmap != U256::ZERO` → init-map delete early-returns too. A fully-drained pool is a normal market operation (a pool winding down).

### Downstream effect (compounding corruption)
Ghost rows are read back on the NEXT chunk's apply via `fetch_v3_liquidity_map_on_conn` (`liquidity_updater.rs:295`, `SELECT tick, liquidity_gross, liquidity_net FROM {LIQUIDITY_POSITIONS} WHERE pool_id = ?1`) called at `apply_v3_liquidity_updates_on_conn:444` → ghost rows reconstituted into `tick_data` with stale non-zero `liquidity_gross`/`liquidity_net` → liquidity map is WRONG → next apply mutates a WRONG base → compounding corruption. V4 mirror at line 502. Any swap-simulation / price consumer reading `fetch_v3/v4_liquidity_map` gets ghost ticks with stale liquidity → incorrect swap math.

### Why the existing parity test missed it
`rust/crates/degenbot-db/tests/fixtures/generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py:426-429` exercises a PARTIAL drain (one tick dropped via a 1.3M Burn; the second tick left live) → `live_ticks` non-empty → the early-return does not trigger. The empty-live path has zero coverage.

## The fix (small, self-contained)

Restructure `delete_stale_rows` to branch on `live_keys.is_empty()`:
- **empty** → `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col} = ?1` (no `NOT IN` clause; bind only `id_value`). This is the "delete all rows for this pool" semantic the comment always claimed.
- **non-empty** → the existing chunked `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1 AND {key_col} NOT IN (...)` path (unchanged).

Cleanest minimal shape: change `delete_stale_rows`'s signature to accept `(conn, table, id_col, key_col, id_value, live_keys)` instead of a pre-built `sql` string, and build the appropriate SQL internally. The 4 callers (`delete_stale_v3/v4_positions_on_conn` + `delete_stale_v3/v4_init_maps_on_conn`) already know these identifiers, so they pass table/id_col/key_col instead of a pre-built string. This:
- makes the empty/non-empty branch natural (no syntax-error avoidance),
- removes the `sql_placeholders_for`-replace hack in the chunk loop (a side-benefit overlap with spike `7UVVJI` — note this so 7UVVJI's scope can shrink to whatever remains),
- does NOT touch the `upsert_*_on_conn` early-returns (those ARE correct: empty `tick_data` → nothing to upsert).

### Call sites to change
- The 4 `delete_stale_*_on_conn` fns in `DegenbotDb` impl (`liquidity_updater.rs`): V3 positions, V3 init-maps, V4 positions, V4 init-maps.
- The `persist_v3`/`persist_v4` callers are UNCHANGED — they pass `live_ticks`/`live_words` as before.

### Do NOT touch
- `upsert_v3/v4_liquidity_positions_on_conn` early-return on `tick_data.is_empty()` — CORRECT (nothing to upsert). Only the DELETE path is bugged.

## TDD red-green order (IMPORTANT — do in this order)

1. **First regenerate the parity fixture from Python (the source of truth).** Extend `rust/crates/degenbot-db/tests/fixtures/generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py` with a FULL-DRAIN event sequence: a Mint that initializes 2 ticks, then Burns that drive BOTH ticks' gross to zero → `tick_data` empties → `live_ticks` empty. Regenerate `liquidity_updater_v3_expected.json` + `liquidity_updater_v4_expected.json` — these assert EMPTY positions/init-maps tables for the drained pool (matching the Python oracle's complement-delete-all semantics).
2. **Run the Rust parity test against the regenerated fixture** → it FAILS (ghost rows vs expected empty) — this is the RED.
3. **Apply the Rust fix** (restructure `delete_stale_rows` + 4 callers).
4. **Run again** → PASSES — GREEN.
5. **Add a focused direct in-crate Rust test** (`liquidity_updater.rs::mod tests` or a `tests/` integration test): build an in-memory DB, seed a pool with N tick rows, apply events that zero all ticks (`live_ticks` empty), assert `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM liquidity_positions WHERE pool_id=?` == 0 (and `initialization_maps`). Direct repro of the reachability path, independent of the parity fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `delete_stale_rows` restructured to branch on `live_keys.is_empty()` → empty issues `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE {id_col}=?1`, non-empty uses the chunked `NOT IN` path.
- [ ] Signature changed to `(conn, table, id_col, key_col, id_value, live_keys)`; 4 `delete_stale_*_on_conn` call sites updated.
- [ ] `upsert_*_on_conn` early-returns UNCHANGED (verified by reading the diff — no edits to those fns).
- [ ] Parity fixture regenerated from Python (full-drain event seq) + the regenerated `*_expected.json` assert empty tables for the drained pool.
- [ ] Rust parity test passes post-fix (and was demonstrably RED pre-fix — note the failing-plan output in the completion summary, or regenerate-then-`git stash`-the-fix to prove RED).
- [ ] New direct in-crate repro test: draining a seeded pool to zero → `COUNT(*) == 0` for both `liquidity_positions` and `initialization_maps` (V3 + V4 managed variants).
- [ ] The existing partial-drain parity case (`generate_liquidity_updater_parity.py:426-429`) still passes — no regression.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-db` green (incl. new parity case + new direct repro test).
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater` green (the chunk-atomicity contract test from BHF5BC + no-duplicate-writer from JZLTES — no write-path regression).
- `just test-python` green (`tests/rust/test_liquidity_updater_seam.py` parity test now covers full-drain).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings` clean (CI gate).
- `just test-rust` + `just test-python` + `just lint-rust` + `just format`.

## Sequencing + epic impact
- **Sequence `7UVVJI` (cosmetic rewrite of `liquidity_updater.rs`) AFTER this bugfix lands.** 7UVVJI must rewrite CORRECT code. Additionally, this fix's signature change (pre-built sql → table/id_col/key_col args) overlaps with 7UVVJI's "tidy the chunked placeholder rebuild" scope — note in 7UVVJI's task that the `sql_placeholders_for`-replace hack may already be gone after this fix, so 7UVVJI's scope may shrink.
- This is a correctness bug, not a perf issue, despite living in the F4N6DX perf epic. Small + self-contained (one helper + 4 callers + tests).

## Gating
0.6.x-safe (code fix, no schema change). NOT gated to 0.7. **Higher priority than the perf spikes** — correctness bug that compounds on every drained-pool apply.

data.title: Don't blindly retry eth_sendRawTransaction
data.body:
## Goal
- `eth_send_raw_transaction` no longer route through the generic
  `retry_with_backoff`. On ambiguous outcomes (timeout, connection drop after
  the body was sent) it reconciles via `get_transaction_receipt` before
  deciding to rebroadcast, instead of blindly re-sending the identical
  signed payload.

## Context
- Current code:
  ```rust
  pub async fn eth_send_raw_transaction(&self, encoded_tx: &[u8]) -> ProviderResult<B256> {
      self.retry_with_backoff(|| async {
          let pending = self.inner.send_raw_transaction(encoded_tx).await
              .map_err(|e| e.into_provider_error("eth_sendRawTransaction failed"))?;
          Ok(*pending.tx_hash())
      }).await
  }
  ```
- A `Timeout` means the body may have reached the node; rebroadcasting is a
  guess. Mempools usually dedupe ("already known"), but the right behavior is
  to confirm outcome first.
- Decision (epic): dedicated path. On `Timeout`/`ConnectionFailed`, fetch the
  receipt by the computed tx hash; if present, return the hash (already
  broadcast); if absent, back off and rebroadcast. On `RateLimited`, back off
  and rebroadcast (idempotent). On non-rate-limit `RpcError` ("already known",
  "nonce too low", "replacement underpriced") surface immediately — the tx
  was seen and rejected, retrying won't help.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `eth_send_raw_transaction` does not use `retry_with_backoff` directly; it
  uses a dedicated broadcast-aware helper.
- Outcome branches each covered by a test using `test-utils`:
  - Success on first try → returns hash, no rebroadcast.
  - `RateLimited` → retries, succeeds.
  - `Timeout` → reconciles; receipt present → returns hash without
    rebroadcast; receipt absent → rebroadcasts after backoff.
  - `RpcError` "already known" (-32000/"already known") → surfaces
    immediately, no retry.
- The tx hash is computed locally from the signed payload (so reconciliation
  can happen even when the broadcast response was lost) — verify alloy
  exposes this or compute it; if not computable locally, document the
  limitation and reconcile via the pending-tx hash from a prior successful
  attempt instead.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (mock-provider broadcast tests)
- `just lint-rust`
- Manual: against a local anvil, send a tx that anvil confirms, then trigger
  a synthetic timeout on a second send and confirm no double-inclusion.

data.title: 0.7-gated retirement: drop Alembic dep + migrations + ALEMBIC_HEAD (BLOCKED until 0.7)
data.body:
## Goal
- 0.7-gated placeholder for retiring Alembic. **NOT executed in this epic.** Tracked here so the cutover path has a named termination and so no agent prematurely deletes Alembic mid-0.6.x. This task stays `blocked` until a 0.7 release branch is cut and a production cutover release has shipped giving every `pip` user a path across the boundary.

## Context
- Everything this task removes is on the forbidden-until-0.7 kill list (epic body + ADR-010 + `AGENTS.md`). It may only run after:
  - `degenbot database cutover` has shipped in a 0.6.x release.
  - A deprecation notice has informed users that 0.7 removes the Alembic path and they must cutover.
- This task exists to be the single, named owner of removal so that mid-epic "this import looks unused" cleanups do not strand the migration.

## Acceptance Criteria (when unblocked, in 0.7)
- Remove `src/degenbot/migrations/` and the `alembic` dependency from `pyproject.toml`.
- Remove the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `migrate.rs::ensure_schema` and the `ALEMBIC_HEAD` constant in `schema.rs`.
- Remove the `database upgrade` Alembic fall-back path (the `DatabaseSchemaStale` → `alembic.command.upgrade` shell); `database upgrade` becomes a pure Rust fast-path or is merged into `database cutover`.

## Validation Gates
- Blocked until 0.7. When unblocked: `just test-all`, `just lint`, plus a migration guide under `docs/migration-guides/`.

# 0.7-gated retirement: drop Alembic dep + migrations + ALEMBIC_HEAD (BLOCKED until 0.7)

## Goal
Stand-alone 0.7 debt marker for retiring Alembic — the single named owner of removal so that no agent prematurely deletes Alembic mid-0.6.x and so the `database cutover` path has a named termination. **Not executed in any in-flight epic.** Stays `blocked` until a 0.7 release branch is cut and a production cutover release has shipped giving every `pip` user a path across the boundary.

## Relationship to epic TGIP5N (auto-healed Alembic retirement)
This marker is the **cross-cutting obligation** to retire Alembic in 0.7, independent of the approach. Epic TGIP5N task `OXKANZ` is the **heal-based execution path** for that retirement — it makes the removal non-breaking via the out-of-place `database heal` dump-and-restore. If the TGIP5N heal approach lands, `OXKANZ` executes the removal and this marker is satisfied (closed as duplicate). If TGIP5N is descoped or the heal approach is abandoned, this marker still stands and a different removal approach (e.g. in-place cutover-only, with its own rugpull risk) would be designed at 0.7 time. Tracking it standalone (rather than under any epic) keeps the obligation visible regardless of which approach epic takes the execution work.

## Reason moved out of epic 2Z3Y46
Originally a blocked child of the CLI DB migration epic so the cutover path had a named termination. Now that the `database cutover` command (FF5YGT, `1b66da1f`) is shipped and proven end-to-end (YWN7Z6, `26cc5fac`) and the heal-based retirement epic TGIP5N is filed, holding 2Z3Y46 open for a 0.7-gated task no longer serves the epic's scope. Moved standalone so 2Z3Y46 can close with its substantive work complete; the 0.7 obligation continues independently.

## Context
- Everything this task removes is on the forbidden-until-0.7 kill list (ADR-010 + `AGENTS.md`). It may only run after:
  - `degenbot database cutover` has shipped in a 0.6.x release. ✓ (FF5YGT, `1b66da1f`)
  - `degenbot database heal` has shipped in a 0.6.x release (TGIP5N) — so any legacy DB (head, stale, or unrecognized) can heal into a RustOwned DB regardless of state, making removal non-breaking. (Gates OXKANZ, not this marker, but listed for completeness.)
