data.title: Container summary — placed in epic body via `ergo set`
data.body:
## Goal

Make V2-family pool reserves a typed `U112` (matching on-chain `uint112`)
across the Rust core, and delete the U512 intermediate + narrowing
`assert!` in the V2 swap primitive. This is the deferred "deeper fix"
forward-referenced in commit `19218a2c` and left open by ADR-012.

## Context

ADR-012 (epic `WOYYS2`) landed the *admission* contract — `register_v{2,3,4}_pool`
runtime-validates reserves against `uint112::MAX` and rejects out-of-spec
state. It deliberately left the *storage types* as `U256`, and left the
swap primitive's `U512` upcast → multiply → downcast-with-`assert!` path
in place. The `19218a2c` commit message explicitly names the U512 path as
"a multiply-precision dodge" and defers "the deeper fix."

This epic is that deeper fix: type the reserves `U112` from the
registration boundary, and make the swap primitive's arithmetic
EVM-faithful (`uint256` multiply-with-revert, no extended-precision
intermediate).

## Scope (in)

- `rust/crates/degenbot-pools/src/v2_state.rs` — `V2PoolState`,
  `RegisterV2PoolParams`.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-pools/src/aerodrome_v2_state.rs` — same shape
  (Aerodrome V2 reserves are also on-chain `uint112`).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-pools/src/state_history.rs` — `V2BlockDelta` (the
  reorg journal delta — four `U256` reserve fields).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/v2_sync_decoder.rs` — `SyncEvent` is
  decoded from `Sync(uint112,uint112)`; emit `U112` directly (no upcast).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-v2-math/src/hop_state.rs` — `IntHopState::swap`:
  drop the U512 intermediate; do native `U256` arithmetic with
  overflow-panic matching Solidity `uint256` revert-on-overflow semantics
  (cf. Uniswap V2 `UniswapV2Library.getAmountOut`).
- Cascade across `degenbot-bot` (test helpers + production callsites),
  `degenbot-python` (PyO3 getters), `degenbot` (standalone consumer).

## Scope (out)

- V3/V4 `sqrt_price_x96: U256` (on-chain `uint160`) — separate epic; the
  `sqrt_price_x96` field feeds V3 swap math (`mulDiv` over `uint160`×`uint256`)
  that is a genuinely different code path with its own extended-precision
  requirements. Tracked as a follow-up epic, not folded in here.
- V3/V4 `liquidity: u128` — already typed correctly (ADR-012 noted the
  Rust type itself is the spec bound).
- The Möbius solver's `u512_to_u256_internal` and `isqrt_u512` / U512
  matrix recurrence (`compute_int_mobius_coefficients`) — these are
  legitimate extended-precision for a *multi-hop* matrix product K/M/N
  and an integer square root, respectively; not a single swap primitive.
  Audited in the final task; expected to remain.

## Key decisions

- **`IntHopState::new` keeps `U256` reserves.** This hop type is shared
  between V2 (reserves `≤ uint112::MAX`, upcast once at the construction
  site) and V3/V4 (computed *virtual* reserves that span `~2^224`, natively
  `U256`). Forcing `U112` here would be wrong for V3. The V2 caller's
  single `.to::<U256>()` upcast is the only upcast; the dodgy downcast
  disappears.

- **Swap primitive does `U256` arithmetic, panicking on overflow.**
  Uniswap V2's on-chain `getAmountOut` computes
  `numerator = amountIn * reserveOut * 997` and
  `denominator = reserveIn * 1000 + amountIn * 997` in **`uint256`**,
  reverting on overflow. The current `U512` intermediate silently
  produces a result where Solidity would revert. A panic accurately
  mirrors the on-chain revert; it is unreachable for spec-bound state
  (V2 reserve product `γ * reserve_out * x` with `x ≤ ~2^134` and
  `reserve_out ≤ 2^112` fits in `U256`; `u256_to_u256_internal` and the
  Möbius matrix recurrence stay `U512`).

- **`U112` is `alloy::primitives::aliases::U112`** (a `ruint::aliases::U112`
  = `Uint<112, 2>` re-export). The top-level `alloy::primitives::{…}`
  glob *does not* re-export `U112` (only `U8/16/32/64/128/160/256/512`),
  so the alias path is required. `uint!(…_U112)` literals work and
  enforce the width at compile time. Cross-width conversion uses
  `.to::<U256>()` — the ruint idiom already in use in
  `degenbot-cl-math/cl_lib/tick_math.rs` (`sqrt_ratio.to::<U160>()`).

- **No PyO3 surface change.** Python retains `int`; the PyO3 getters
  `upcast at the seam — `U256::from` is not implemented for `U112`,
  so use `.to::<U256>()` (matches `rust/crates/degenbot-pools/src/v3_state.rs:767`'s
  `sqrt_price_x96.to::<U160>()` pattern).

- **No backwards-compatibility layer.** Per project guidance, the prior
  U512 + narrowing assert is deleted, not feature-gated. Synthetic
  out-of-spec `IntHopState` construction (testing reserves > `uint112::MAX`)
  is a programming error and now produces an overflow panic in the swap
  primitive where it previously silently saturated-then-panicked (the
  `large = U256::MAX / 1000` reserves test in `mobius_int_exact.rs` is
  rewritten to in-spec reserves; the `#[should_panic]` overflow test in
  `hop_state.rs` is updated to feed an overflow-producing *swap input*,
  not out-of-spec reserves).

## Validation strategy

Each task ends `green` on:
- `cargo test -p <affected crate> --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p <affected crate> --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt -p <affected crate> --check`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (only for core-crate tasks).

Epic close: `just test-rust` + `just test-rust-python` + `just lint-rust` green,
ADR-012 addendum committed.

data.title: VerifyProgress contract: add is_final to ChunkProgress/AaveChunkProgress + PyO3 dict
data.body:
## Goal
- Add to BOTH `ChunkProgress` (pool, run.rs) and `AaveChunkProgress` (aave, run.rs): a bool `is_final` (true iff this is the last committed chunk of the run — `chunk_end >= last_block` or `max_chunks` hit).
- Report it through the PyO3 progress dict (`pool/mod.rs`, `aave_updater.rs`).
- Foundation the Python shell needs to observe completion (for the completion-time backup) and a triage field; the Rust completion/interval full-verify computes finality inline but reporting it keeps Python able to fire the backup.

## Context
- Pool `ChunkProgress` (degenbot-pool-updater/src/run.rs): chain_id, chunk_start, chunk_end, pools_written, liquidity_apply_count, committed. Aave `AaveChunkProgress` (degenbot-aave-updater/src/run.rs) adds market_id, events_applied, touched_user_addresses.
- Both loops set `is_final` at the POST-commit `progress.report_chunk` call. Pool: `working_end_block >= last_block`. Aave: `chunk_end >= last_block || max_chunks-hit`.
- ADR-005: zero pyo3 in cores; the dict building is in the pyo3 wrapper crate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ChunkProgress` + `AaveChunkProgress` gain `is_final: bool`.
- Pool loop sets it true on the last committed chunk only; aave loop sets it true on the last committed chunk OR when `max_chunks` cap breaks the loop.
- Existing struct-construction tests updated; no compile breakage.
- PyO3 progress dicts include `"is_final": bool`.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (degenbot-pool-updater, degenbot-aave-updater) — including the PyO3 seam unit tests that assert the progress dict keys (`aave_progress_sink_callback_fires_once_per_chunk`, the pool sibling).
- `just test-rust-python`.

## Completion
- Added is_final: bool to ChunkProgress (pool, run.rs) and AaveChunkProgress (aave, run.rs); wired all progress.report_chunk call sites.
- Pool: rollback path is_final=false; success path is_final = working_end_block >= last_block.
- Aave: two rollback paths is_final=false; success path is_final = chunk_end >= last_block || max_chunks.is_some_and(|limit| chunks_committed+1 >= limit).
- PyO3 dicts (pool/mod.rs progress_report_to_dict + aave_updater.rs aave_progress_report_to_dict) expose is_final; pyo3 unit tests assert the round-trip (first chunk final=true, second false).
- .pyi progress-callback docstring updated.
- Verified: cargo test (cores + pyo3 --features auto-initialize), just lint-rust, just test-rust-python (276 passed).

data.title: [sim] A3 — Extract PathSuppression out of Dispatcher into its own Arc
data.body:
## Goal
- Move `PathSuppression` from an inline field of `Dispatcher` into a standalone
  `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` held by `PyDispatcher` alongside the
  `Arc<Mutex<Dispatcher>>`. Both the submission seam and the sim seam access it
  via this shared handle, so the sim seam never locks the `Dispatcher` across
  its fan-out.

## Context
- `PathSuppression` is currently `path_suppression: PathSuppression` inline in
  `Dispatcher` (dispatcher.rs:236+). `is_suppressed(&mut self, …)` records the
  retry block on read (mutates `last_retry_block`).
- Inside `dispatch_profitable_results`, `&mut path_suppression` is touched only
  at the bookends: step 1 pre-filter (`candidates.retain(|c|
  !path_suppression.is_suppressed(c.path_id, current_block))`) and step 6
  record (`record_success`/`record_failure`). Across the fan-out (steps 2–5,
  `.buffer_unordered().collect().await`) the `&mut` is dormant.
- The submission crate's doc comment on `PathSuppression` (dispatcher.rs:138)
  sanctions ownership by the simulation scope.
- `PyDispatcher` (the pyclass) gains a `suppression_arc()` accessor returning
  `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`.
- Submission access: update any submission-side `path_suppression` touch to use
  the shared `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`. Verify submission tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Dispatcher` no longer has `path_suppression` as an inline field;
  `PyDispatcher` holds `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` as a sibling.
- `core::dispatch_profitable_results` signature takes
  `path_suppression: &Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` (or `&mut` acquired at the
  bookends only, never held across the fan-out `.await`s).
- `is_path_blocked`/`claim_nonce`/`reserve_pools`/`track_task` in the
  submission seam are unaffected (they touch `Dispatcher`, not suppression).
- Submission tests pass; the no-lock-across-awaits convention holds.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (focus: `degenbot-submission` + `degenbot-simulation`)
- `just lint-rust`

> **Done** — committed `5e4d3568`.

## What landed
- `rust/crates/degenbot-submission/src/dispatcher.rs`: removed the `path_suppression: PathSuppression` inline field from `Dispatcher` + the five `record_success`/`record_failure`/`is_suppressed`/`total_suppressed`/`discard_path` delegating methods. Updated the `PathSuppression` doc to describe its standalone-ownership model. Relocated the two suppression-behaviour tests (the proptest state machine + `discard_path_clears_all_tracking`) to exercise `PathSuppression` directly.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/submission/dispatcher.rs`: `PyDispatcher` now holds a second arc `suppression: Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` alongside the `Dispatcher` arc. The five suppression `#[pymethod]` accessors delegate to the suppression arc (not the `Dispatcher` arc). Added `suppression_arc()` accessor for the upcoming A4 sim seam (`dispatch_profitable_py`, QQFTB4) to lock suppression directly without touching the `Dispatcher` lock. `inner_arc()` drops its `#[allow(dead_code)]` (real consumers in the sibling submit/fee/monitor file).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `Dispatcher` no longer holds `path_suppression`; `PyDispatcher` holds `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` as a sibling.
- [x] The sim seam (A4, QQFTB4) will take the suppression arc via `suppression_arc()`; the bookend-only lock pattern is achieved because the `Dispatcher` lock is never touched.
- [x] submission accessors unaffected (they now use the suppression arc).
- [x] submission tests pass (43/43); no-lock-across-awaits convention holds.

## Validation
- `just lint-rust` green (clippy + fmt, all features).
- `cargo test -p degenbot-submission` — 43/43.
- `uv run pytest tests/rust/` — 292/292.

## Notes for A4 (QQFTB4)
- `dispatch_profitable_py` should call `py_dispatcher.suppression_arc()` to get the `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` and pass it to `core::dispatch_profitable_results` (lock at the bookends only, never across the `.buffer_unordered().collect().await` fan-out).
- The `Dispatcher` arc is taken separately via `inner_arc()` for the submit/fee/monitor leaves — suppression and dispatcher now move on independent locks.

## Orphaned/unrelated
- The working tree has unstaged changes in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`, `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`, `tests/arbitrage/test_backrun_config.py`, `tests/arbitrage/test_consumer_block_stream.py` (a dry-run operator-key fix from earlier session work). These were deliberately NOT included in the A3 commit — they belong to a separate concern and should be committed/attributed separately.

data.title: Rust aave update path double-inserts POOL_DATA_PROVIDER contract row (parity-ground-truth diff surfaced)
data.body:
# Rust `aave update` path double-inserts the POOL_DATA_PROVIDER contract row

## Scope

While diffing the Python-written 16591070 DB (live prod after a fresh
`degenbot database reset → aave activate → aave update-py --to-block
16591070` cold-boot) against the Rust-written GREEN reference at the
same block (`${PROD}.postfix-green-bak`, last_update_block=16591070),
the Rust-written DB was found to contain a DUPLICATE row in
`aave_v3_contracts` for `market_id=1, name='POOL_DATA_PROVIDER'`:

| DB                | row count for `aave_v3_contracts` |
|-------------------|------------------------------------|
| Python-written    | 5 (id=4 at `0x7B4EB56E7CD4b454BA8ff71E4518426369a138a3`) |
| Rust-written      | **6** (id=4 + id=6, BOTH at `0x7B4EB56E7CD4b454BA8ff71E4518426369a138a3`) |

Both Rust rows have identical `market_id=1, name='POOL_DATA_PROVIDER'`,
`address=0x7B4EB56E7CD4b454BA8ff71E4518426369a138a3`. The Python writer
correctly emits EXACTLY ONE row for that (market, name) pair.

This is NOT in the 6-position EIWEPM divergence tally (which counted

data.title: Move per-family state structs + PoolEntry/V3FamilyPool/TickInfo/TokenEntry to pools
data.body:
## Goal
- Move the per-family state files + the inline `mod.rs` value types into `degenbot-pools`: `aerodrome_v2_state.rs`, `balancer_stable_state.rs`, `balancer_weighted_state.rs`, `curve_state.rs`, `v3_state.rs`, `v4_state.rs` (each: identity + state + Register*Params + BlockDelta); + `PoolEntry` enum, `V3FamilyPool` trait, `V2PoolIdentity`, `V2PoolState`, `RegisterV2PoolParams`, `RegisterV2PoolError`, `TickInfo`, `TokenEntry` (inline in `bot_core/mod.rs`).

## Context
Per inventory §1 + §2. The bulk of the value surface. State structs hold trait-object fields (task 2 already moved the trait defs, so no cyclic dep). `BotState`/`Bot`/`BlockMetadata` STAY in bot (`BotState` becomes `HashMap<u64, degenbot_pools::PoolEntry>`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All per-family identity/state/Params/Error structs + `PoolEntry` + `V3FamilyPool` + `TickInfo` + `TokenEntry` live in `degenbot-pools`.
- `BotState` in `bot_core/mod.rs` imports `PoolEntry` from `degenbot_pools`; its registry `HashMap<u64, PoolEntry>` updated. `match self.pools.get(&pool_id)? { PoolEntry::V2(..) => ... }` arms compile against the pools-defined enum (no bot-only types in any variant — verify after task 2's trait move).
- `BotState`/`Bot`/`BlockMetadata` STAY in bot.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just test-rust-python`.

## Goal
- Move the per-family pool state structs + their `*BlockDelta` types + `tick_map` + `state_history` + the mis-homed V3 swap-sim value types (currently filed under `solvers/`) into `degenbot-pools`. The `mod.rs` inline registry types (`PoolEntry`, `V3FamilyPool` trait, `V2PoolState`, `TokenEntry`, `RegisterV2*`) STAY in `bot_core/mod.rs` (they reference the moved states via shims; `impl V3FamilyPool for V3PoolState` stays in mod.rs — orphan-OK, `V3FamilyPool` is bot-local).

## Status: IN PROGRESS — in isolated git worktree `/tmp/wt-ltz3tp` (branch `ltz3tp-extraction`), to protect the shared tree during the atomic (non-compiling mid-) move.

## What's already moved (worktree, 6 family files via scripted lib/test split)
- aerodrome_v2_state, v4_state (wholesale); v3_state, curve_state, balancer_stable_state, balancer_weighted_state (lib → pools, `#[cfg(test)]` integration-test mod kept in bot shim — it uses `BotState`). `crate::bot_core::` → `crate::` sed applied (gate-safe: all lib refs point to now-pools symbols; the only `BotState` refs are doc-comment links → rustdoc warnings, not failures).

## Remaining move set (fully mapped)
1. `state_history.rs` → pools wholesale (incl. its 3 `cfg(test)` blocks). lib-code `crate::bot_core::` refs = {balancer_stable, balancer_weighted, curve}_state (all moving) → clean.
2. `tick_map.rs` → pools wholesale (trait + the 2 `impl TickMap for (V3PoolIdentity, V3PoolState)` / `(V4…)` tuple impls + test — now orphan-OK because the trait + both states + the impls all co-locate in pools; the V4 test uses V3/V4 state, both moved).
3. **Mis-homed value types** relocation (spike under-counted these — they're filed under `solvers/` but are pure value, the V3 analogue of v2-math's `IntHopState`):
   - `IntV3TickRangeHop` (struct: u128 + U256×3 + u64×2 + bool) + `IntV3TickRangeSequence` out of `solvers/mobius_v3_int.rs` → pools; `solvers/mobius_v3_int.rs` re-exports them (keeps its solver code).
   - `LiquidityEvent` trait out of `solvers/liquidity_event_buffer.rs` → pools; that file re-exports it. (`BufferedV3LiquidityUpdate` is defined in `v3_state.rs` and `impl`s `LiquidityEvent` — both moving to pools.)
4. Add deps to `degenbot-pools/Cargo.toml`: `parking_lot` (used by V3 state) + `degenbot-decoders` (v4_state uses `v4_swap_decoder::PoolId` — a pyo3-free core crate).
5. Wire `degenbot-pools/src/lib.rs`: declare the new modules + re-export; change moved family files' `use crate::solvers::mobius_v3_int::{IntV3TickRangeHop, …}` → `crate::…`.
6. Validate in worktree: build/clippy/fmt/no-pyo3/test --workspace; then cherry-pick back to `main` as one atomic commit.

## Findings (updates the spike)
- **E0117 orphan rule** (commit a26 = attempted tick_map split): `tick_map` + `state_history` CANNOT be split from the state structs — their trait/generic core + state-coupled impls (tuples violate orphan; inherent impls must be in the defining crate) move together. Hence folded into THIS task.
- **Spike under-count (V3/V4 sim ↔ solvers entanglement)**: the spike called V3/V4 swap sim "value-only", but `v3_state`/`v4_state` use `IntV3TickRangeHop`/`IntV3TickRangeSequence` + `LiquidityEvent` (filed under `solvers/`). These are pure value types mis-homed in `solvers/` — relocating them to `pools` is within the pools mandate (not starting the solvers epic).
- **Mod.rs inline types STAY** (simplification): `PoolEntry`/`V3FamilyPool`/`V2PoolState`/`TokenEntry` are referenced only in `///` prose by the moved family files; they stay in `bot_core/mod.rs` referencing the moved states via shims.

## Validation Gates (per worktree before cherry-picking back)
- `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (in worktree), `just test-rust-python` (on main after cherry-pick + after anvil_fork.py healed by t-cda6).

data.title: Auto-healed Alembic retirement (dump-and-restore cutover)
data.body:
Retire the incoherent, non-forward-buildable Alembic migration chain
(`src/degenbot/migrations/`) without rugpulling users who have built up large
in-place databases of pools and liquidity positions. The mechanism is an
**out-of-place dump-and-restore "heal"**: build a fresh DB at the Rust-DDL
head schema, copy user rows from the old DB into it preserving primary keys
and FK integrity, stamp it `RustOwned` directly (never running any Alembic
code), then atomically swap it into place (old DB preserved as `*.bak`).

Once `heal` ships and is proven, the Alembic dependency, the migrations
directory, and the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `ensure_schema` can be
retired (the 0.7.0 release boundary) **non-breaking-ly**: any legacy DB — at
head, stale, or unrecognized — can `degenbot database heal` into a RustOwned
DB regardless of its old state, so removing Alembic strands nobody.

This epic delivers the durable, rugpull-protected Alembic retirement that the
cutover epic (2Z3Y46 / `cutover` command, `1b66da1f`) deliberately deferred.

## Why out-of-place, not in-place

The existing `database cutover` (`1b66da1f`) is an **in-place** ownership
flip — it assumes the old DB is already at the Alembic head schema (the common
case), so it only drops `alembic_version` and stamps
`_degenbot_db_schema_version`. It is fast and instant, but it cannot repair a
stale or divergent schema.

`heal` is the **general** complement: it reads the old DB as raw SQLite
(whatever columns actually exist there), rebuilds against the coherent Rust
head schema, and applies a **column-mapping table** derived from the migration
history (renames → map, adds → fill default, drops → ignore). It never invokes
`alembic upgrade`, so the non-forward-buildable chain is bypassed entirely.
Both commands coexist: `cutover` for the fast head→RustOwned path,
`heal` as the safe retire / divergent-schema path.

## Non-goals

- **Repairing the Alembic chain in place** (adding the missing
  `add_column`s, guarding the drops, batch-wrapping the alters across all 43
  migrations). The chain is structurally incoherent (e.g. `311beed36e7b`
  "add factory and deployer" alters a `factory` column no migration creates;
  `87fd9fc7ae00` drops `ix_managed_pool_hash` no migration creates). Repair is
  large, fragile, and spent on something about to be deleted. `heal` removes
  the need for forward-buildability; retirement removes the chain.
- **Auto-heal-on-open.** `degenbot database heal` is opt-in through 0.7.0.
  Automatic heal-on-`DegenbotDb::open` (mirroring the eventual automatic
  cutover-on-open) is a 0.8 concern, not built here. Rationale: a full
  out-of-place copy + atomic swap is a surprising, slow operation to trigger
  implicitly; an explicit command lets users back up first and cutover
  deliberately.
- **The `cutover` command itself** (already shipped, `1b66da1f`). This epic
  only adds `heal`; it does not modify `cutover`.

## Constraints

- **Standalone-Rust constraint (AGENTS.md).** The data-copy logic, the
  column-mapping table, the FK-ordered write plan, and the atomic swap all
  belong in `degenbot-db` (zero `pyo3`). A `cargo add degenbot` consumer must
  be able to call `heal_database(path)` directly. The PyO3 wrapper is arg
  extraction → GIL release → core call → result wrap; no logic.
- **Never mutate the old DB in place.** The heal reads the old DB read-only,
  writes a new file at a temp path, and only swaps via `rename`. If any step
  fails, the live DB is untouched. The old DB is preserved as `*.bak`.
- **Preserve primary keys and FK integrity.** Row `id` values are copied as-is
  so foreign-key references survive the rebuild. `sqlite_sequence` is reset
  to the max copied id per table.
- **`heal` must not depend on Alembic at runtime.** Once shipped, retiring
  `src/degenbot/migrations/` and the `alembic` dependency must not break
  `heal`. The column-mapping table is a static Rust constant derived once
  from the migration history, not a runtime call into Alembic.
- **No kill-list items touched other than the explicit retirement task.**
  `src/degenbot/migrations/` is on the 0.6.x kill-list; only the 0.7.0
  retirement task (gated, last) may delete it.

## Architecture (three-layer placement, per ADR-005)

- **Rust core** (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/ops.rs` +
  `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/heal.rs` new module): `heal_database(old_path)
  -> Result<HealReport, DbError>`. Owns: open-old-read-only, schema
  introspection, the static column-mapping table (`COLUMN_MAP: &[(table,
  old_col, new_col, HealAction)]`), FK-ordered copy plan, PK preservation +
  `sqlite_sequence` reset, stamp-as-RustOwned, atomic `rename` swap +
  `*.bak`, row-count verification. The mapping table encodes: added column
  → fill default/NULL, renamed → map read, dropped → ignore. Pure data
  movement; no business logic.
- **PyO3 seam** (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` +
  `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`): `db_heal_database(database_path) -> dict`
  returning `{old_state, rows_copied_per_table, bak_path, new_state}`. Thin
  wrapper — GIL released across the copy.
- **Python shell** (`src/degenbot/cli/database.py` + operations wrapper in
  `src/degenbot/database/operations.py`): `degenbot database heal
  [--dry-run] [--force]` Click command. `--dry-run` reports old state +
  per-table planned row counts + column-mapping diff, writes nothing.
  `--force` skips the confirm prompt. Default (no flag) → `click.confirm`.

## Map of the heal operation

```
old DB (any state)              new DB (fresh Rust DDL)
┌─────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────────┐
│ alembic stamp (any) │         │ full head schema (Rust)  │
│ head-or-stale schema│  copy   │ NO alembic_version table  │
│ user data           │  rows   │ _degenbot_db_schema_     │
│                     │  ────►  │   version = RustOwned     │
└─────────────────────┘         └──────────────────────────┘
         │  preserved as .bak (atomic swap at the end)
         ▼
   old.db.bak
```

1. **Inspect** old DB state (read-only). If `rust_owned`, no-op
   (`already_rust_owned`).
2. **Build** fresh DB at a temp path via Rust DDL
  (`db_create_new_database` — the coherent head schema). This is the same
  primitive `create_new_sqlite_database` uses.
3. **Copy** all rows from old → new, table-by-table in FK-dependency order
   (parents before children: `erc20_tokens` → `exchanges` → `pool_managers`
   → `pools` → `uniswap_v2_pools`/subclass tables → `liquidity_positions` →
   `initialization_maps` → …), applying the column-mapping table per table,
   **preserving PK `id` values** so FK references survive.
4. **Reset** `sqlite_sequence` to max copied id per table (autoincrement
   continues correctly after heal).
5. **Stamp** new DB `RustOwned` directly — no `alembic_version` table is
   created. (The new DB never carried one; `db_create_new_database` stamps
   Alembic-head for back-compat, but heal drops it before stamping RustOwned.
   Alternatively, skip the Alembic stamp entirely on the heal path and go
   straight to RustOwned — cleaner; decide at implementation.)
6. **Verify** per-table row counts: old read count == new read count. Refuse
   the swap on mismatch.
7. **Atomic swap**: `rename(new, live)` then `rename(old, *.bak)` (or copy
   old→bak first if atomic rename isn't safe across the temp dir boundary).
   On any failure mid-heal, the live DB is untouched; partial new file is
   cleaned up.

## Old DB → new DB column-mapping table (static Rust constant)

Derived once from `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/*.py`. Three action
classes:

- **Added-after** (column exists on head/new, may be absent on old):
  `exchanges.factory`, `exchanges.deployer`, `aave_v3_emode_categories.*`,
  `aave_v3_users.*`, `pools.tick_spacing`, `uniswap_v4_pools.*`, …
  → fill with column default / NULL on the new DB.
- **Renamed** (old name → new name): `6a77c4e07151` ("rename_column" —
  `pools.token0_id_` → `pools.token0_id`?), `a4f59783919f` ("rename
  pool_hash_column"), `5c8805573ab3` ("convert_pool_hash_to_text" — type
  change, value-preserving). Map the read.
- **Dropped** (column on old, not on new): `04f858f979a9` ("drop
  factory_column" — but note `factory` still exists on head; verify the
  actual end-state against the Rust DDL, not the migration titles), 
  `901adb947000` ("drop deployer"), `b781499591ed` ("remove
  has_liquidity"), `3199199def8c` ("drop binary pool_hash"). Ignore the
  column on read.

The mapping is **schema-derived, not migration-title-derived**. The
authoritative source is: `PRAGMA table_info` on the old DB vs `PRAGMA
table_info` on a fresh `db_create_new_database` DB. The migration history is
only consulted to disambiguate renamed columns (where a value must be
carried forward under a new name) from dropped columns (where it mustn't).
The implementation should **auto-derive the mapping at heal time** from the
two `PRAGMA table_info` snapshots, with a small explicit override table for
the renamed cases — this is more robust than a hand-maintained 43-entry
constant and survives future head-schema drift.

## Tasks (in dependency order)

### T1 — ADR-011: auto-healed Alembic retirement (design record)

Write `docs/adr/ADR-011-auto-healed-alembic-retirement.md`. Captures: the
out-of-place dump-and-restore decision (vs in-place cutover, vs in-place
chain repair, vs hard retirement); the column-mapping auto-derivation
approach; the atomic-swap + `.bak` guarantee; the relationship to the
existing `cutover` command and to `JFFQV2`; the standalone-Rust placement;
the non-goal of auto-heal-on-open (deferred to 0.8). Update `AGENTS.md` ADR
index to include ADR-011 + the kill-list note that `src/degenbot/migrations/`
retirement is gated on `heal` shipping (not just on 0.7.0 the version).
**Depends on:** nothing. **Unblocks:** T2.

### T2 — Rust core: `heal_database` op + column-mapping auto-derivation

Implement `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/heal.rs` (+ `ops.rs` re-export +
`lib.rs` pub use). `heal_database(old_path) -> Result<HealReport, DbError>`.
Owns the 7-step operation above. The column mapping is **auto-derived at
heal time** from `PRAGMA table_info(old)` vs `PRAGMA table_info(new
db_create_new_database)`, plus an explicit `RENAME_OVERRIDES` constant for the
handful of renamed columns. FK-dependency order is derived from the
`FOREIGN KEY` declarations in the new schema (a static topological sort, also
a Rust constant). PK preservation: copy `id` as-is. `sqlite_sequence` reset.
Stamp RustOwned (do NOT stamp Alembic head on the heal path — go straight to
RustOwned). Verifies row counts; refuses swap on mismatch. Atomic `rename`
swap + `*.bak`. Refuses unrecognized old DB (no `alembic_version` AND no
`_degenbot_db_schema_version` AND tables-present-but-foreign — i.e. a
genuinely foreign file) with a clear error. Returns `HealReport { old_state,
rows_copied: HashMap<String, u64>, bak_path, new_state }`.
Tests: head→heal (rows preserved, alembic_version gone, RustOwned stamped,
FK integrity intact, sqlite_sequence correct), stale→heal (older-revision
old DB reconstructed via the verified `create_new_sqlite_database` + drop-index
+ stamp-rewrite construction from `YWN7Z6`), unrecognized-refusal,
already-rustowned no-op, row-count-mismatch refusal (inject a corrupt old
DB), atomic-swap-keeps-bak (kill mid-copy is impossible by construction,
but verify `*.bak` exists post-heal). **Depends on:** T1.

### T3 — PyO3 seam: `db_heal_database`

`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` + `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`.
Thin: extract `database_path: &str`, `allow_threads(|| heal_database(path))`,
wrap `HealReport` as a `PyObject` dict. No logic. `#[pyfunction]`,
`__all__` entry. Test: round-trip via the seam mirrors the core test.
**Depends on:** T2.

### T4 — CLI: `degenbot database heal [--dry-run] [--force]`

`src/degenbot/cli/database.py` (Click command) + `src/degenbot/database/operations.py`
(thin wrapper `heal_database` + `inspect_heal_plan` for dry-run). `--dry-run`
reports old state + per-table planned row counts + the auto-derived column
mapping (added/renamed/dropped), writes nothing. `--force` skips
`click.confirm`. Default → confirm prompt. Mirrors the `database cutover`
command style (`1b66da1f`). Output: old state, rows copied per table, `.bak`
path, new state. Tests (Click `CliRunner`, mirroring
`tests/cli/test_database_cutover.py`): dry-run-on-alembic-current,
force-heal-on-alembic-current (asserts `*.bak` exists, alembic_version gone,
RustOwned, a pre-written exchange row still reads back — proving
rugpull-protection), force-heal-on-stale, force-heal-on-already-rustowned
no-op, dry-run-on-unrecognized-refusal, confirm-prompt-default. **Depends
on:** T3.

### T5 — pytest: full heal boundary (large-DB rugpull-protection proof)

`tests/cli/test_heal_boundary.py` (or co-located). The contract artifact:
build a representative large old DB (head-stamped, populated with a few
hundred pools + liquidity positions across multiple chains via the existing
PyO3 write seams), then `degenbot database heal --force`, then assert: (a)
every row in every user table survives with identical PKs and FK integrity,
(b) `alembic_version` is gone and `_degenbot_db_schema_version` is stamped
RustOwned, (c) the `.bak` file exists and is openable read-only and still
contains the old data (full recoverability), (d) post-heal writes (a new
exchange/pool upsert) work against the RustOwned DB. This is the artifact
that proves the user-facing promise: no rugpull, full data survival, full
recoverability. **Depends on:** T4.

### T6 — 0.7.0 retirement: drop Alembic dep + migrations dir (gated)

**Gated on T5 passing + an explicit "0.7.0 release" decision.** Delete
`src/degenbot/migrations/` (the kill-listed dir), remove the `alembic` +
`alembic-utils` deps from `pyproject.toml`, remove the
`alembic_version`-reading branch of `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/migrate.rs::ensure_schema`
(AlembicCurrent/AlembicStale states collapse — every DB is either
FreshStandalone / RustOwned / Unrecognized), remove the Alembic fall-back
from `upgrade_existing_sqlite_database` (it becomes `cutover`-or-error, or
better, aliases to `heal` for safety). Update ADR-010 + ADR-011 to mark
retirement complete. Remove the kill-list entry for
`src/degenbot/migrations/` from `AGENTS.md`. This is the
`JFFQV2`-placeholder successor from epic 2Z3Y46, executed now that `heal`
makes it non-breaking. **Depends on:** T5 + 0.7.0-release-decision (human
checkpoint).

data.body:
## Goal
- Port the `Dispatcher` **nonce/pool/task coordination state** to Rust: nonce claim/release
  (`claim_nonce`/`release_nonce` over a `pending_nonces: HashSet<u64>`), pool mutual
  exclusion (`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/`is_path_blocked` against pending+committed
  pools), `active_tasks` (tokio `JoinSet` with auto-discard-on-completion), the
  by-reference `current_block` clock (`Arc<Mutex<u64>>` single-element pattern),
  `block_times` deque, the `block_priority_fees` ring (`FEE_HISTORY_WINDOW` prune +
  `latest_priority_fees`/`record_priority_fees`), and the `PathSuppression` delegation.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), row N3.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure coordination state — `HashMap`/`HashSet` + a
  single-element `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` for the by-ref block clock; hot per-tx; GIL-held today
  across claim/release; property-testable — nonce dedup, pool mutual exclusion, ring
  prune, suppression transitions).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core), `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md`
  §3, `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` (the `next_base_fee` N1 leaf the block clock
  drives).
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `Dispatcher` L579–L678 + the
  `PathSuppression` class L509–L578 (composed; delegated via `record_success`/
  `record_failure`/`is_suppressed`/`is_path_blocked`).
- The `active_tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` + `task.add_done_callback(discard)` Python pattern
  maps to a tokio `JoinSet` (or `task::AbortHandle` set). The `current_block_ref:
  list[int]` single-element mutable-by-reference maps to `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` (read by monitor
  tasks across the consumer/monitor boundary without a per-access lock in Python — Rust
  uses the `Mutex`). The `pending_nonces` `claim_nonce(start)` uses `itertools.count(start)`
  scanning for the first non-pending nonce — Rust: same linear scan over a `HashSet`.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).
  `PathSuppression` is OWNED by the Simulation epic `5LLJHX` D-child (`5FB5MW`) per the
  4JGPDW scope — but `PathSuppression` is COMPOSED into `Dispatcher` here. **Flag:** if
  `5FB5MW` owns `PathSuppression`, this child REFERENCES its struct (compose, no hard
  edge); coordinate with the Simulation epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `pub struct Dispatcher { pending_nonces, pending_pools, active_tasks
  (JoinSet), current_block (Arc<Mutex<u64>>), block_times, block_priority_fees,
  path_suppression }` with `claim_nonce`/`release_nonce`/`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/
  `is_path_blocked`/`release_tx`/`track_task`/`advance_block`/`current_block`/
  `record_block_time`/`record_priority_fees`/`latest_priority_fees` + the `for_block`
  constructor + `PathSuppression` delegation.
- `pending_nonces` claim scans from `start` for the first non-member (matches the Python
  linear scan); `block_priority_fees` prunes to `FEE_HISTORY_WINDOW` on insert (pops the
  min key); `active_tasks` auto-discards on task completion (tokio `JoinSet`/abort-handle).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: nonce dedup/cap, pool mutual exclusion, ring prune,
  by-ref clock read across tasks.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Parity check vs the Python `Dispatcher` behavior (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- `PathSuppression` internals — Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `5FB5MW` (REFERENCE/compose).
- The `next_base_fee` formula — N1 child (`JTLWA3`).
- The submit orchestration + sign + broadcast — N6/N4/N5 siblings.
- The `monitor_pending_transaction` lifecycle — N2 sibling.

## Dependencies
- REFERENCES `5FB5MW` (Simulation `PathSuppression`) for composition — no hard edge
  (compose the struct once it lands).

data.title: spike: VARCHAR(78) → BLOB(32) for uint256 columns (0.7-gated)
data.body:
# spike: VARCHAR(78) → BLOB(32) for uint256 columns (0.7-gated)

## Goal
- Decide whether converting the `VARCHAR(78)` decimal-string uint256 columns to fixed 32-byte `BLOB` is worth it: ~1.5–2.4× smaller for the big tables, better cache density, but touches every encode/decode site + every parity fixture.

## Hypothesis
The uint256 columns (`liquidity_net`, `liquidity_gross`, `bitmap` on the tick/init-map tables; Aave `balance`, `liquidity_index`, `borrow_index`, `liquidity_rate`, `borrow_rate`, `debt_ceiling`, `isolation_mode_debt`, `stk_aave_balance`, `bitmap`) are stored as decimal strings (1–78 bytes, variable). A 32-byte `BLOB` is smaller and fixes width. Trade-off: decimal strings are human-inspectable and the comparison semantics are different (lexicographic-vs-numeric, though these columns are not used in range/order predicates today).

## What to investigate
1. Enumerate EVERY `VARCHAR(78)` column in `schema_head.sql` + its Python model (`src/degenbot/database/models/**`) — the `IntMappedToString` `TypeDecorator`. Categorize: actually-uint256 vs signed (`liquidity_net` is signed → I256 → must encode sign in 32 bytes or keep a separate sign).
2. Enumerate every encode/decode site in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/rows/decode.rs` + the liquidity_updater (`encode_u256`/`decode_u256`/`encode_i256`/`decode_i256`) + the Aave writer. Quantify the blast radius.
3. Check the parity fixtures (`tests/fixtures/*_expected.json`) — they assert VALUES not byte encoding (decimal-string vs BLOB would change the row bytes but the decoded value is identical). Confirm whether the parity harness reads the column via SQL or via the Rust decode (the latter is encoding-agnostic; the former would break).
4. Decide the signed-value encoding for I256 (`liquidity_net`): two's-complement 32-byte big-endian is the natural choice; confirm alloy `I256` round-trips through it.
5. Estimate storage + cache-density win on the largest tables (`liquidity_positions` / `managed_pool_liquidity_positions`) — net/gross are stored as VARCHAR; for typical 128-bit values the VARCHAR is ~39 bytes, vs 32 bytes BLOB; for small values (single-digit net) VARCHAR is ~2 bytes vs 32 bytes BLOB (BLOB is WORSE for small values). Decide whether the win is real for the actual value distributions (gross liquidity is typically large; net can be small).
6. Recommendation: BLOB for `bitmap` (always 32 bytes, big win — VARCHAR(78) for a full uint256 is 78 bytes) + `liquidity_gross` (large values); keep VARCHAR for `liquidity_net` if values skew small. OR skip entirely if the distributions make it a wash.

## Validation
- Per-column verdict: CONVERT / KEEP, with the value-distribution justification.
- The signed-encoding decision for I256 (if converting `liquidity_net`).
- A storage measurement on a representative large fixture for the convert-worthy columns.

## Gating constraint
**Column type change — gated to 0.7** (same reasoning as R8: rides the dump-and-restore cutover). Implementation tasks appended from this spike MUST be blocked behind `JFFQV2`.

## Note
This is a **decision-heavy** spike, not a slam-dunk. The explicit deliverable is the recommendation + per-column verdict, not code.

## If validated → append implementation tasks
If research confirms the suggestion, append one or more implementation tasks to epic `F4N6DX` (DB performance improvements). Each appended task:
- is a single atomic change (one Alembic migration OR one Rust PR);
- includes concrete Acceptance Criteria + Validation Gates (exact `just`/`cargo`/`sql` commands);
- for schema/index changes: ships a new Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/`, mirrors the DDL change in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`, and bumps `ALEMBIC_HEAD` in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`;
- is sequenced after this spike (`ergo sequence <THIS-SPIKE-ID> <IMPL-ID>`);
- respects the gating constraint noted below.

If research refutes the suggestion, mark THIS spike `done` with a `result` summarising why — do NOT append an implementation task.

data.title: Port Aave market activation/deactivation to Rust core (retire last Python ORM writer on Aave path)
data.body:
## Goal
Port `aave activate ethereum_aave_v3` + `aave deactivate ethereum_aave_v3` from SQLAlchemy ORM writes into a Rust core function, exposed via a thin PyO3 seam. This is the LAST remaining Python ORM writer on the Aave path after the CZM7TI writer retirement.

## Context
CZM7TI deletes the Python Aave writer pipeline (event_handlers, transaction_processor, operations_parser, etc.) — the per-event write dispatch is fully Rust-owned. But the ONE-TIME market-activation path still lives in Python (`commands.py::activate_ethereum_aave_v3`, `deactivate_mainnet_aave_v3`):
- `activate`: writes `AaveV3Market` row, `AaveV3Contract` (`POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER`), `AaveGhoToken`, `Erc20TokenTable` (via `db_assets.get_or_create_erc20_token` + `erc20_utils._fetch_erc20_token_metadata`), all via `session.add/flush/commit`.
- `deactivate`: flips `market.active = False` via `session.commit`.

Rust's `bootstrap_pool_contracts` only DISCOVERS `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR`; it does NOT seed the market row, GHO token, or address-provider contract. So activation must run first (from Python today) before `run_aave_update` can bootstrap.

Per AGENTS.md standalone-Rust-core constraint: a standalone Rust consumer (`cargo add degenbot`) must be able to activate an Aave market without Python. This belongs in a core crate (likely a new `degenbot-aave-updater` activation fn or `degenbot-db` helper) behind a PyO3 seam.

## Scope
- Rust core fn: `activate_aave_market(chain_id, market_name, pool_address_provider, gho_token_address, rpc)` -> seeds market + contracts + GHO token + erc20 metadata (RPC name/symbol/decimals fetch), idempotent. One transaction.
- Rust core fn: `deactivate_aave_market(market_id)` -> `active = false`.
- PyO3 seam in `degenbot-python/src/aave_updater.rs` (thin).
- `commands.py::activate_ethereum_aave_v3` / `deactivate_mainnet_aave_v3` become boot + hand-off shells.
- `db_assets.get_or_create_erc20_token` + `erc20_utils._fetch_erc20_token_metadata` retire (the erc20 metadata fetch moves into the Rust core or `degenbot-rpc`).
- `db_assets.py` + `erc20_utils.py` can then be fully deleted.

## Sequencing
- Depends on: CZM7TI (the writer retirement must land first so activation is isolated as the sole remaining writer).
- Does NOT block 0.7 (activation is setup, not the chunk loop). Can land in a 0.6.x point release.

data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **DB-aware pool & lending-market updaters → Rust core** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **DB-aware pool & lending-market updaters → Rust core**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

# Scope: DB-aware pool & lending-market updaters → Rust core

Epic `AZGJUN` · Scope task `MPS3U7` · Agent `researcher_1@degenbot`

Status legend: **COMPLETED** = Rust-owned + Python delegating · **IN-FIGHT** = partial (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere) · **NOT-STARTED** = no Rust counterpart; rubric says belongs in Rust.

Rubric (§2.1) criteria shorthand: **hot/warm** (per-tx vs per-block/bulk) · **GIL** (CPU-bound holds GIL?) · **type** (pure numeric/byte/Address/U256 vs heavy Python obj/ORM) · **I/O** (ORM query/upsert vs pure transform) · **eco** (Python-ecosystem coupling) · **dup** (§2.3 duplication smell).

## Key finding (answers orchestrator's open question)

**The feed-side updaters read/write the DB directly, NOT `BotState`.** `cli/pool.py::apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` reads `pool_in_db.liquidity_positions` via ORM relationships, applies math, writes back via `sqlite_upsert`/`delete`. The in-memory `BotState` liquidity maps (`n_update_by_pool_id` in `degenbot-bot`) are a SEPARATE path (hot-path swap solver) NOT kept in sync with the DB by these updaters. Consequence:
- **Hard DB-substrate dependency on `SLHSM4`** (Epic `VGTEDL`) for the writer children + the read-back child.
- **NO dependency on `QVMWQC`** (builder/construction-time reads — different callsite set, though both consume `SLHSM4` read fns).
- **NO `BotState` edge.**

Also: `UniswapV3/4LiquiditySnapshot` (`v3_snapshot.py`/`v4_snapshot.py`) are **in-memory event-fetchers + `update()` applies to in-memory maps**, NOT DB writers. The real DB writers are `cli/pool.py::apply_*` + `cli/aave/event_handlers.py`. The snapshot *read* half (DB→map) is Epic `VGTEDL` (`WKZ7ID`).

§2.3 duplication smell: liquidity-mapping math exists in TWO places — pure-Python `calculations/concentrated_liquidity.py::apply_liquidity_mapping_update` (DB-updater-only) AND Rust `degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/n.rs::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` (hot path). Lifting into `degenbot-cl-math` gives one shared fn.

## COMPLETED

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale | Pointer |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | No DB-aware updater responsibility is Rust-owned yet. | — |

## IN-FIGHT

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale | Python side | Rust side |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | None. There is no partial Rust updater whose Python callsite is half-routed. The whole updater responsibility is NOT-STARTED (the held `PyBotIo.db` seam from VGTEDL is the staging slot, not an updater port). | — | — |

## NOT-STARTED (`port-now` / `stays-python`)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Python side | Rust side | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Liquidity-mapping math** (`apply_liquidity_mapping_update`, `flip_tick`, `get_tick_word_and_bit_position`) | `port-now` | type=pure int/U256; I/O=none (pure CPU); warm/bulk CPU; §2.3 `dup` (hot path duplicates it in `degenbot-bot::n`). `degenbot-cl-math` has only low-level helpers today (`mulmod`/`to_uint160`/`to_int128`); the tick-bitmap fns have NO Rust counterpart (`rg` empty). Only the DB updater calls the pure-Py version. | `src/degenbot/calculations/concentrated_liquidity.py`; `src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_libraries/tick_bitmap.py`; `src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_functions.py` | (none in cl-math) | `S5YS7U` |
| **V3/V4 DB-aware liquidity updater + pool discovery writers** (apply-and-persist: read pool row+positions → math → upsert positions/init maps + stamp `liquidity_update_block`; PoolCreated scan → upsert pool/config rows + `ExchangeTable.last_update_block`) | `port-now` (apply+persist core) / `stays-python` (driver loop + RPC fetch) | core: type=Address/int/U256; warm/bulk (per-block chunk backfill); §2.3 `dup` (ORM reconstitute + hand-rolled chunked `sqlite_upsert`). driver: orchestration + RPC (`degenbot-rpc` event-fetch port = separate epic). Reads/writes DB directly (see finding). | `src/degenbot/cli/pool.py::{apply_v3_liquidity_updates,apply_v4_liquidity_updates,pool_update,_pool_updater,get_v3/v4_liquidity_events,get_events_from_contract}`; `src/degenbot/cli/pool_updater_configs.py::{update_v2/v3/v4_pools,_get_or_create_token,V2/V3/V4PoolUpdateConfig}` | (none) | `QJSCA5` (deps `S5YS7U` + `SLHSM4`) |
| **Aave V3 lending-market DB writers** (per-event handlers + `get_or_create_*` upserts) | `port-now` (writer/handler core) / `stays-python` (`aave_update` driver + RPC fetch) | type=int/Address/config-bitmaps; warm/bulk; §2.3 `dup` (`session.scalar`→mutate→`session.add` collapses to substrate get-or-create). `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` = pure bit-decode (port alongside). No CL-math dep. | `src/degenbot/cli/aave/**{event_handlers,db_market,db_assets,db_users,db_positions,commands}.py` | (none — Aave row structs land in `SLHSM4`) | `RQXEKH` (deps `SLHSM4`) |
| **Aave V3 rehydrate / read-back** (`DatabasePositionQuery`) | `port-now` (read-back over substrate) | type=Address/big-int; I/O=row→struct (`joinedload` graph); warm (analysis startup/batch). Read companion to the Aave writers. Reads DB directly (see finding). | `src/degenbot/aave/analysis/orchestrator.py::DatabasePositionQuery` | (none) | `OKKMG5` (deps `SLHSM4`) |
| **Stays-Python (recorded, not ported)** | `stays-python` | | | | |
| └ `pool_update` / `aave_update` driver loops + RPC event fetch | `stays-python` | orchestration shell + RPC event fetch (`get_v3/v4_liquidity_events`, `fetch_logs_retrying`, `get_events_from_contract`); RPC port = separate epic. Rust core takes the fetched events as input. | `cli/pool.py::pool_update/_pool_updater`; `cli/aave/commands.py::aave_update` | n/a | — |
| └ `UniswapV3/4LiquiditySnapshot` in-memory event-fetcher/`update()` | `stays-python` *for this epic* | applies events to in-memory maps, not DB; its DB-read half is Epic `VGTEDL` (`WKZ7ID`). | `src/degenbot/uniswap/{v3,v4}_snapshot.py` | n/a | (VGTEDL/WKZ7ID) |
| └ Aave `operations.py`/`extraction.py`/`enrichment/*` in-memory analysis pipeline | `stays-python` | analysis orchestration + domain event→state modeling, separate from DB persistence. | `src/degenbot/aave/{operations,extraction}.py`; `enrichment/` | n/a | — |
| └ `db_verification.py` invariant checks | `stays-python` | verification read-back (consumes Rust-written rows once `RQXEKH` lands; stays a Python read/check). | `src/degenbot/cli/aave/db_verification.py` | n/a | — |
| └ Syncing `BotState` in-memory liquidity maps with the DB | `stays-python` (out of scope) | the hot path owns its own in-memory maps; DB↔BotState sync is a separate concern not in this epic. | n/a | n/a | — |

## Child task split (port-now rows → implementation tasks)

| Child | Title | Disposition origin | Deps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S5YS7U` | Port liquidity-mapping math into `degenbot-cl-math` | math `port-now` | — (pure math, no DB) |
| `QJSCA5` | Port V3/V4 DB-aware liquidity updater + pool discovery writers into Rust over `degenbot-db`; CLI driver stays Python | pool-updater `port-now` | `S5YS7U` (math) + `SLHSM4` (substrate, cross-epic) |
| `RQXEKH` | Port Aave V3 lending-market DB writers into Rust over `degenbot-db`; `aave_update` driver stays Python | aave-writer `port-now` | `SLHSM4` (substrate, cross-epic) |
| `OKKMG5` | Port Aave V3 rehydrate/read-back (`DatabasePositionQuery`) through `degenbot-db` | aave-read-back `port-now` | `SLHSM4` (substrate, cross-epic) |

Route-before-type ordering: `S5YS7U` (pure math core) + `SLHSM4` (substrate, from VGTEDL) land first → `QJSCA5` (needs both) + `RQXEKH` (needs substrate) + `OKKMG5` (needs substrate) fan out. `RQXEKH`/`OKKMG5` are independent of `S5YS7U` (no CL-math dep). `QJSCA5` is the only intra-epic consumer of the math sibling.

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **Cross-epic child-level edges to `SLHSM4` (Epic `VGTEDL`): WIRED** — `SLHSM4 → QJSCA5`, `SLHSM4 → RQXEKH`, `SLHSM4 → OKKMG5`. These are child-level (not epic-level), per the orchestrator's directive. `QJSCA5` has BOTH a cross-epic dep (`SLHSM4`) and an intra-epic dep (`S5YS7U` math). None of the feed-side children depend on `WKZ7ID`/`QVMWQC`/`OP23QV` (the other VGTEDL routing children) — confirmed: the updaters touch their own callsites and share only the substrate read/write *fns* (owned by `SLHSM4`), not the routing children. [RESOLVED — no further action.]

2. **Orchestrator's open question (DB vs `BotState`): RESOLVED.** Feed-side reads/writes the DB directly → hard `SLHSM4` edge; no `BotState` edge; no `QVMWQC` edge. Recorded above. [RESOLVED.]

3. **§2.3 hot-path duplication collapse (degenbot-bot `n` module → shared cl-math fn): NON-BLOCKING follow-up.** `S5YS7U` lands the shared fn in `degenbot-cl-math`; refactoring `degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/n.rs::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` to call it is a separate, non-blocking task for the bot-core maintainers (recorded in `S5YS7U` non-goals). Flagging here so it isn't lost; not a blocker for this epic.

4. **Does `QJSCA5`'s pool-discovery half need its own child?** Considered and folded: discovery (`update_v2/v3/v4_pools` PoolCreated upserts) shares the `pool_update` driver + the `SLHSM4` upsert fns with the liquidity-apply half, so it shares `QJSCA5`. Splittable later if it proves too coarse. [DECIDED — fold.]

5. **`degenbot-updaters` new core module vs `degenbot-db` for the apply-and-persist fns:** left as an impl decision in `QJSCA5`/`RQXEKH` (either lives in `degenbot-db` or a new pyo3-free `degenbot-updaters` core crate consuming it). Both satisfy the standalone + no-pyo3 constraint. No blocker.

data.title: [rpc] O1 — Rust OfflineProvider (alloy Transport) in degenbot-rpc
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the pure-Python `OfflineProvider` (recorded-JSON chain data) into a Rust
  `Provider<Ethereum>` in `degenbot-rpc`, so an offline provider is a real Rust
  provider (no Python round-trip) that any Rust pyclass (`PyBotIo`, `PyAlloyProvider`)
  can hold indistinguishably from a live alloy provider. This is the prerequisite
  for B1 (PZLZE3): PyBotIo can only drop its `Py<PyAny>` provider field once the
  offline test path runs through a real Rust provider.

## Context
- Python source: `src/degenbot/provider/offline_provider.py`. Serves pre-recorded
  JSON: per recorded block `{ "timestamp", "calls": {"<addr_lower>:0x<data_hex>": "0x<result>" | null}, "code": {"<addr_lower>": "0x<bytecode>"} }`.
  Multi-block format wraps blocks under a `"blocks": {"blocknum": {...}}` key;
  single-block format has a top-level `"block_number"`.
- `alloy`'s `Provider` trait methods route through `root().client()` → a
  `Transport`. So a custom in-memory provider must be a custom alloy `Transport`
  (a `tower::Service` over JSON-RPC requests) answering from the recorded map,
  then `RootProvider::new(transport)` → `AlloyProvider::from_provider(Arc)`.
  This is the idiomatic alloy path; `AlloyProvider::from_provider` already
  exists behind the `test-utils` feature (`rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs:1005`).
- The offline provider only needs to answer: `eth_call`, `eth_getCode`,
  `eth_blockNumber`, `eth_getBlockByNumber` (timestamp). The Python impl raises
  `NotImplementedError` for balance / storage / nonce / logs / `make_request` —
  preserve that contract (surface as `ProviderError::Other` /
  `ProviderError::InvalidParams` for the unsupported methods).
- Revert / unrecorded semantics: Python `OfflineDataMissing` (call not recorded)
  and `OfflineCallReverted` (`null` result). Map: unrecorded →
  `ProviderError::ExecutionReverted` or a dedicated variant; `null` →
  `ExecutionReverted`. Decide the mapping and document it.

## Scope
- New module `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/offline.rs` (pyo3-free core):
  - `OfflineProvider` struct holding the parsed recorded data (chain_id, sorted
    block numbers, per-block call/code maps).
  - `from_json_bytes` / `from_json_string` constructors (serde) accepting both
    single-block and multi-block formats (mirrors the Python `from_json_*`).
  - Custom `Transport` impl (or equivalent alloy seam) answering the 4 RPCs.
  - `pub fn as_alloy_provider(self) -> AlloyProvider` (via `from_provider`),
    so callers get an `Arc<AlloyProvider>`-shaped value.
- Unit tests in `offline.rs`: synthetic recorded data exercising each RPC,
  revert/null mapping, block-not-recorded, multi-block lookup, parity with the
  recorded JSON the Python fixtures use (re-use a `tests/golden` chain-data file
  if one is small enough to embed).

## Out of scope
- PyO3 wrapper / Python integration (O2). Keep O1 pure-Rust + unit-tested.
- Balance/storage/nonce/logs (raise like the Python impl).
- PyBotIo cutover (B1) and test migration (O3) — separate tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/offline.rs` exists; `AlloyProvider` built from an
  offline provider answers `eth_call`/`eth_getCode`/`eth_blockNumber`/
  `eth_getBlockByNumber` from recorded data with zero Python.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` stays green.
- Revert (`null`) and unrecorded-call semantics map to documented
  `ProviderError` variants.
- `just lint-rust` + `cargo test -p degenbot-rpc` green with offline unit tests.

data.title: Sync decoder: emit U112 directly
data.body:
## Goal
- `SyncEvent.reserve0` / `SyncEvent.reserve1` become `U112`. The decoder
  produces `U112` from the 32-byte ABI word, validating the high
  20 bytes (bits 112..256) are zero (real `Sync(uint112,uint112)` events
  are left-padded with zeros in the ABI word; non-zero high bits
  indicate a corrupt / synthetic log).
- The decoder currently does `U256::from_be_bytes::<32>(data[..32])`.
  Replace with: decode the `U256`, assert the high 144 bits are zero
  (returning `None` on violation, matching the existing
  "data too short" / "topic mismatch" `None` paths), then narrow to
  `U112` via `.to::<U112>()`.

## Context
- `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/v2_sync_decoder.rs` is the producer
  of `SyncEvent`; consumers (`block_pump`, pools, Aave updater) read its
  fields. After task 1 landed V2PoolState's reserves as `U112`, this
  task makes the decoder–consumer path type-coherent (no implicit
  upcast at the consumer end).
- This task depends on task 1: the `SyncEvent` consumer code in
  `block_pump` / pools reads `sync.reserve0` and assigns to
  `V2BlockDelta.reserve0_after` (now `U112`). If this task lands
  before task 1, the consumer would need a temporary `.to::<U256>()`
  adapter — task ordering avoids the adapter entirely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `SyncEvent.reserve0, reserve1: U112`.
- `decode_sync_log` returns `None` when either ABI word has non-zero
  bits above position 112 (i.e. the `U256` is wider than `U112::MAX`).
  Rationale: a real `Sync(uint112,uint112)` event's data slot is
  left-zero-padded; stray bits are corrupt / synthetic and treated as
  a malformed log (matches the existing short-data `None` path).
- Two new tests: (a) `decode_sync_log_accepts_uint112_max` (the
  `U256` value `2^112 − 1` decodes cleanly), (b)
  `decode_sync_log_rejects_high_bits_set` (a `U256` with bit 112 set
  returns `None`).
- All existing sync-decoder tests updated to feed in-spec `U112`-range
  reserve values; the `make_sync_log` test helper takes `U112`
  reserves (`U256::from(N)` literals become `U112::from(N)`).

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-decoders --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-decoders --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt -p degenbot-decoders --check`

data.title: CLI: cutover exchange activate/deactivate to the Rust seam
data.body:
## Goal
- Cut `src/degenbot/cli/exchange.py`'s `activate_*` / `deactivate` commands over to the task-4 Rust seams, making each command a thin delegating shell (path resolve → `db_upsert_exchange` / `db_set_exchange_active` / `db_upsert_pool_manager` → logging).

## Context
- Today `exchange.py` is ~1200 lines of repetitive SQLAlchemy: each `activate_ethereum_*` / `activate_base_*` / … does `session.scalar(select(ExchangeTable)...)`, sets `active=True` (or inserts a new row with `factory` + `last_update_block=None`), and for V3/V4 also upserts `PoolManagerTable`. `deactivate` mirrors it.
- The V3/V4 activate paths also seed a `PoolManagerTable` row (address, chain, kind, state_view, exchange_id) — use `db_upsert_pool_manager`.
- The `deployer` column is nullable; most activate paths pass the factory address only. Preserve each command's existing argument surface.
- Disposition per the rubric: CLI orchestration (arg parsing, logging, exit codes) = **stays-python**; the DB write = **port-now** (Rust-owned).
- Red/Green TDD: write a CLI test (Click `CliRunner`) per DEX family asserting the exchange row + pool-manager row land in the DB via a fresh Rust readback (`db_fetch_exchange`) before gutting the Python body.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No `session.add` / `session.commit` / `session.scalar` against `ExchangeTable` or `PoolManagerTable` remains in `src/degenbot/cli/exchange.py`. The file imports `degenbot_rs` for the three task-4 seams (plus the existing `db_fetch_exchange` for the already-active guard).
- Every `activate_*` / `deactivate` command behaves identically to before: same row shapes, same idempotency (activating an already-active exchange is a no-op logged, not an error), same exit behaviour.
- The V4 pool-manager seeding survives: after `activate_ethereum_uniswap_v4`, `db_fetch_exchange` returns the exchange and a `pool_managers` row exists for the manager address.
- `DatabaseSessionManager` is no longer imported by `exchange.py` (the SQLAlchemy session is gone from this path). It remains elsewhere — do NOT delete it (forbidden-until-0.7 kill list).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (CLI exchange tests, including the new TDD cases)
- `just test-rust-python`
- `uv run ruff check src/degenbot/cli/exchange.py`
- Smoke: `uv run degenbot database reset --force && uv run degenbot exchange activate ethereum_uniswap_v2` succeeds and a subsequent `pool update` discovers V2 pools.

## Completion note
- Implemented by delegated worker t-f280 (orchestrator t-6ff7 verified). TWO commits:
  - `424949a6` `feat(rust): add fetch_exchange_by_name substrate + PyO3 seam` — prerequisite close-the-gap: `DegenbotDb::fetch_exchange_by_name` in `read.rs` (mirror of `fetch_exchange`) + `degenbot_rs.db_fetch_exchange_by_name` PyO3 seam + `.pyi`/`__all__` + Rust unit test + Python round-trip test.
  - `e4a91ef6` `refactor(python): cutover exchange CLI to the Rust seams` — rewrote all ~30 `activate_*`/`deactivate` commands in `src/degenbot/cli/exchange.py` (~1412 lines churned, net -786/+851) to delegating shells: `db_upsert_exchange` → check `row.active` → `db_set_exchange_active` → (V4) `db_upsert_pool_manager`. `exchange.py` no longer imports `sqlalchemy.select`/`ExchangeTable`/`PoolManagerTable`/`bot.db()`; imports `degenbot_rs`. 7 new CLI tests in `tests/cli/test_exchange.py`.
- Design held: `upsert_exchange` inserts `active=False` → shell always calls `set_exchange_active(True)` unless already active. V4 `db_upsert_pool_manager` called unconditionally on activate — idempotent reassert (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), produces identical DB state to the original's new-exchange-only seeding (documented as intentional safe deviation in commit body).
- Verified independently: `just test-rust` green, `just test-rust-python` 260 passed, `uv run ruff check exchange.py degenbot_rs.pyi` clean, `just test-python` exchange tests pass (7/7). NOTE: `tests/test_config_rpc.py::test_fallback_beats_config` fails in this environment but is PRE-EXISTING/environmental — fails identically with the pre-cutover exchange.py checked out; unrelated to this task.
- End-to-end smoke: `database reset → activate ethereum_uniswap_v2 → deactivate → already-deactivated → activate ethereum_uniswap_v4` all succeed; V4 seeds `pool_managers` row (EXISTS=1); re-activate idempotent ("already activated"); V4 manager id stable across deactivate/re-activate (idempotent reassert verified).

data.title: PyO3 seam: db_heal_database
data.body:
## Goal
Expose `heal_database` over PyO3 as `db_heal_database`.

## Body
`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` + `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`. **Thin wrapper only — no business logic** (ADR-005):
- `#[pyfunction] fn db_heal_database(database_path: &str) -> PyResult<PyObject>`
- Extract `database_path: &str`, `py.allow_threads(|| heal_database(path))` (GIL released across the copy — it's the slow part), wrap `HealReport` as a `PyObject` dict `{old_state: str, rows_copied: dict[str,int], bak_path: str, new_state: str}`.
- `SchemaState` → label string (`alembic_current`/`alembic_stale`/`rust_owned`); `DbError` → Python exception (`DatabaseSchemaStale`/`UnrecognizedSchema` via the existing `db_err_to_py` helper).

Mirror the existing seam style in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` (e.g. `db_convert_alembic_to_rust_owned` from `1b66da1f`).

Add to `__all__` in the `.pyi`.

## Test
Round-trip via the seam mirrors the core `head_to_heal` test: build head DB, write an exchange row via `db_upsert_exchange`, call `db_heal_database`, assert the returned dict's `new_state == "rust_owned"`, `bak_path` exists, `rows_copied["exchanges"] == 1`, and the exchange row still reads back via `db_fetch_exchange_by_name`.

## Depends on
T2.

## Completion note
- Implemented by delegated worker t-f280 (orchestrator t-6ff7 verified). Committed `67691f7c`: `feat(python): add db_heal_database PyO3 seam` (3 files, +153).

### Artifacts
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` (+50) — `db_heal_database` `#[pyfunction]` returning `Py<PyDict>` (the PyO3 dict-return idiom used in this codebase). Thin: extract `database_path: &str`, `py.detach(|| ops::heal_database(&path))` (GIL released across the copy), wrap `HealReport` as a dict `{old_state, rows_copied, bak_path, new_state, warnings}` via `schema_state_label` for the state fields. Registered in `add_db_module`.
- `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi` (+27) — type stub + `"db_heal_database"` added to `__all__`.
- `tests/rust/test_db_file_ops.py` (+76) — `test_heal_round_trips_through_seam`: head DB + an exchange row → `db_heal_database` → asserts `new_state=="rust_owned"`, `bak_path` exists, `rows_copied["exchanges"]==1`, exchange row still reads back via `db_fetch_exchange_by_name`.

### Gates (all green)
- `cargo test -p degenbot_rs` (the PyO3 crate name — brief said `degenbot-python` but the actual crate is `degenbot_rs`; t-f280 resolved): 39 tests pass incl. the new seam round-trip test.
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot_rs -- -D warnings`: clean.

- Import check: `db_heal_database` in `m.__all__`; the .so rebuilt on `uv run` (cache-keys caught the Cargo.toml/src changes) and loads cleanly.

### Thin-wrapper invariant (ADR-005) holds
No business logic in the seam — arg extraction → GIL release (`py.detach`) → core call (`ops::heal_database`) → result wrap (dict via `schema_state_label` + `db_err_to_py` for errors). All logic stays in `degenbot-db` core (FCA2HP/`ca782237`).
