data.title: 6. Wire the pre-commit gate into `run_pool_update` (degenbot-pool-updater)
data.body:
## Goal
- Insert compute → verify(mode) → persist into `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn`'s V3/V4 per-pool loop, mirroring the aave `--verify-chunk` pattern: divergence drops `tx` (rollback), no `last_update_block` advance, returns `RunError::Verification { pool, chunk_start, chunk_end, divergences }`.
## Context
- `run_pool_update` already has the `AlloyProvider` (rpc_url). Add a `verify_mode: VerifyMode` param (`None` default → no gate, backward compat — the existing `run_pool_update` callers that pass no mode keep working).
- In `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn` (site: `rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/run.rs` ~lines 320–360): replace each `apply_v3_liquidity_updates_on_conn(conn, …)` with `compute_v3` → (if verify_mode != None) `rt.block_on(verify_v3_liquidity_map_on_chain(provider, …, &tick_data, &tick_bitmap, chunk_end, scope))` → if divergences return `Err(Verification{..})` (the outer loop already drops `tx` on `apply_chunk_writes_on_conn` Err, lines ~1545/1560). On GREEN → `persist_v3`. V4 mirror.
- The `scope` for `Touched` = the `touched_ticks` from `compute_*`. For `Full` = All. The touched set derivation makes Touched cheap + correct for this-chunk errors.
- Re-export `RunError::Verification` (mirror `degenbot-aave-updater::RunError::Verification`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- With `verify_mode = VerifyMode::None`, behavior is byte-identical to today (the 6SRJRL full-drain tests + parity tests + `no_duplicate_writer`/chunk-atomicity tests stay GREEN unchanged).
- With `VerifyMode::Touched`/`Full`, a deliberately-wrong in-memory map (a tampered `tick_data` in a unit test) → the chunk's `tx` is rolled back + `last_update_block` NOT advanced + `RunError::Verification` returned with the named divergences.
- The 6SRJRL-class base-read corruption is caught under `Full` (the strongest net): a poisoned reconstituted base diverges at the gate before persist.
## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater` (incl. the new rollback-on-divergence test using a mock provider feeding a synthetic `extsload`/`ticks` return — the `multicall3_batch` fallback path + the pure mapping helper make this offline-testable).
- `just test-rust` (no regressions in the broader pool-updater / db suite).

Pre-commit gate wired into run_pool_update. apply_chunk_writes_on_conn now takes Option<&VerifyCtx> (provider+rt+block_number+v4_manager_addresses); when Some, V3+V4 per-pool loops run compute → verify_v3/v4_liquidity_map_on_chain (FULL in-memory map at block_number=chunk_end) → persist only on GREEN; a divergence returns RunError::Verification{pool, block_number, divergences} → the chunk loop drops tx (rollback) + does NOT advance last_update_block (the restart-invariant holds — next run re-processes the chunk). When None, the fused compute→persist path is byte-identical to before (backward-compat; all 52 existing tests unchanged).

VerifyCtx threaded via run_pool_update(verify: bool). Chunk loop collects v4_manager_addresses (pool_hash → spec.factory the PoolManager addr) during the V4 fetch. RunError::Verification variant added (mirrors aave). PyO3 seam + .pyi updated: run_pool_update now has verify: bool = False (default off for backward-compat — task 7 will expose a CLI/standalone-entry).

TDD: RunError::Verification carries pool+block_number+the named divergences (tested). verify=None backward-compat: all existing chunk-atomicity + no-duplicate-writer + rollback tests GREEN. Full Rust suite exit 0; workspace clippy --all-features --deny warnings clean; no-pyo3 clean.

data.title: Aave V3 operations parser: apply dispatch glue (process_transaction entry)
data.body:
# HQF5NQ-C — Aave V3 operations parser: the apply dispatch glue

> **Split sibling of HQF5NQ (the single-shot OPERATIONSPARSER).**
> Deps on HQF5NQ (A: parser-core + standard builders) + HQF5NQ-B (liquidation
> engine) — needs A's `Operation` types + the `parse()` scaffold AND B's
> `Operation { operation_type: Liquidation, ... }` builder. Ships LAST
> (after A + B). This is the per-tx entry point the orchestrator (6SWY4R)
> calls — the bridge from parsed `Operation`s to substrate `AaveChunkEvent`
> variants dispatched via `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`.

## Goal

Port the `transaction_processor._process_transaction` dispatch + the
`Operation`→`ScaledTokenProcessor`→`AaveChunkEvent` variant construction +
the GHO-discount-lookup machinery. The parser (A + B) produces an
`Operation` sequence; this task consumes that sequence + writes through the
substrate apply fns (CXRGX4/UR7QNL/5Z3QQ2/RYKCC4) on the caller's chunk
Connection. This is where the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) is
exercised end-to-end — U5YIBG (§4.2) is the final arbiter.

## Scope (this task)

### 1. `process_transaction(conn, tx_events: &[DecodedAaveEvent], ctx: &TxContext) -> Result<()>`
The per-tx entry point the orchestrator (6SWY4R) calls. Instantiates the
`OperationsParser` (A's struct) with the tx context + calls `parse()` to
get the `Operation` sequence + dispatches each Operation's constituent
ScaledToken events to the substrate apply fns. Mirror the Python
`transaction_processor._process_transaction`.

### 2. `Operation`→`AaveChunkEvent` variant construction (1 path per `ScaledTokenEventType`)
For each Operation, construct the `AaveChunkEvent` variant(s) + dispatch via
`apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` (CXRGX4's dispatch). The paths:
- `CollateralMint` → `ScaledTokenProcessor::collateral(rev).process_collateral_mint(&event_data)` → `AaveChunkEvent::ScaledTokenMint { position: Collateral, position_id, balance_delta, new_index }`.
- `CollateralBurn` → `process_collateral_burn` → `ScaledTokenBurn`.
- `CollateralTransfer` → `ScaledTokenTransfer { from_position_id, to_position_id, scaled_amount, transfer_index }`.
- `DebtMint`/`DebtBurn`/`DebtTransfer` → the vToken equivalents.
- `GhoDebtMint`/`GhoDebtBurn` → the GHO-vToken equivalents (coordinate with RYKCC4).
- The **Mint-as-burn interest-exceeds-repayment edge case** for WITHDRAW/REPAY_WITH_ATOKENS (the §4.2-drift edge — the SCALEAPPLY 3-branch reconciliation's interest-exceeds-deposit arm fires; verify the `balance_delta` sign). This is where the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) is exercised on the edge branches.
- The **GHO_LIQUIDATION debt-burn vs COLLATERAL transfer** in DeficitCoverage (the burn-pair check in `_create_deficit_coverage_operations`).
- The **GHO_DEBT_INTEREST vToken handling** in the LiquidationCall builder's output (from B).

### 3. The GHO-discount-lookup machinery (mirror `transaction_processor._process_transaction` L73-192)
The `discount_updates_by_log_index` map + `get_effective_discount_at_log_index` path — the GHO-payoff-before-LiquidationCall machinery that needs the stkAAVE balance first. Coordinate with RYKCC4's `apply_stk_aave_staked_on_conn`/`apply_stk_aave_redeem_on_conn` for the stkAAVE-transfer pre-processing (the discount is computed from the user's stkAAVE balance at the LiquidationCall's log index, so the stkAAVE transfers must be applied BEFORE the LiquidationCall's GHO discount is read). Flag if the ordering constraint needs an explicit log-index sort.

### 4. Integration test: per-tx fixture corpus → asserted chunk-write sequence
1 tx → multiple `Operation`s → multiple `AaveChunkEvent`s → the `AaveChunkWriteReport`. The end-to-end exercise of the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1).

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged)

ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Every apply writes through `_on_conn` on the caller's tx. On `Err`, whole-chunk revert. The `process_transaction` fn takes a `&Connection` (the chunk's tx) — the caller (orchestrator) owns the tx lifecycle.

## Architectural calls I own (escalate, don't guess)

- **The plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) on edge branches:** if the integration test reveals a divergence between SCALEAPPLY's `ScaledTokenProcessor::process_*` (taking `ScaledTokenEventData`) and the Python enrichment's `calculate(raw_amount, index)` on the WITHDRAW/REPAY_WITH_ATOKENS/GHO_LIQUIDATION edge branches, escalate — do NOT paper over it. The right fix may be a thin `ScaledTokenProcessor::calculate(raw_amount, index, event_type)` bridge fn mirroring `ScaledAmountCalculator.calculate`, OR confirming the existing surface is plumbing-equivalent. U5YIBG (§4.2) is the final arbiter.
- **The stkAAVE-transfer-before-LiquidationCall ordering:** if the log-index sort + the discount-lookup ordering is subtle, flag.
- **The `PoolUpdated` mid-tx revision mutation:** the parser reads revision once at parse-start (A's design). If a `PoolUpdated` config event appears mid-tx, the revision mutation is the orchestrator's (6SWY4R) concern — C's `process_transaction` does NOT re-read the revision mid-tx. If the integration test reveals a mid-tx-revision case, escalate (the right fix is orchestrator-side, not parser-side).

## Validation gates (paste tail in callback)

- `just test-rust` (new integration test + all prior tests still green — A's parser-core + B's liquidation engine must remain green)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact)
- `just lint-rust` (clippy --deny warnings)
- `just format`

## Not touched (per non-goals)

- The parser-core + standard builders → HQF5NQ (A).
- The liquidation engine → HQF5NQ-B.
- The orchestrator (`run_aave_update`) → 6SWY4R (this task's `process_transaction` is the entry point 6SWY4R calls, but 6SWY4R owns the chunk loop + the RPC fetch + the event filtering).
- Python cutover → AVS4DR.
- §4.2 parity → U5YIBG (the §4.2 cross-check is the final arbiter for the plumbing-equivalence caveat).
- Python `transaction_processor.py` — unchanged (AVS4DR deletes).

## Operating rules

1. You own implementation; I own sequencing/state/architectural calls.
2. **No `git commit` without my explicit authorization.** Make changes; run gates; report DONE/BLOCKED. (Leave `.ergo/plan-alloyprovider-refactor.md` untracked.)
3. Report via `link_send` to me (t-d479) with `triggerTurn:true`. Include diff summary, gate results, open questions, flagged decisions.
4. Root AGENTS.md is the canonical ref.

data.title: Rust wrong raw_amount word for Supply/Borrow
data.body:
## Goal

`extract_raw_amount_for_event` (rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/transaction_processor.rs, ~line 280) returns `extract_pool_amount_word0(pool_event)` for ALL non-liquidation standard operations (Supply/Withdraw/Borrow/Repay). That's WRONG for Supply + Borrow: their ABI encoding puts `user` at data word 0, with `amount` at word 1. Result: every Supply's CollateralMint balance_delta is the user ADDRESS interpreted as a U256 (~10^48-10^57), NOT the supply amount.

## Impact (NOT a crash — a silent wrong-value divergence)

* Users' collateral balances are wrong by a factor of ~10^27 (160-bit address vs 18-decimal amount). Always positive -> no negative-balance crash.
* Surfaced while pulling together the YUPSIB parity fixture (`test_standalone_transfer_then_withdraw_parity.py`): Rust's SENDER post-supply balance = `0xe4`x20-as-int = `1306754405142924962158588791605147170515892626660`; Python's = the actual supply amount.
* This is the "~10^69 scaling oddity" the orchestrator flagged for the W2S3WH test tightening — it was never an aToken scaling oddity; it is a word-extraction bug in the standard path.
* Did NOT crash the W2S3WH + YUPSIB real-RPC re-drive to 16596000 — every Supply blats the user-as-int uniformly; end-state balance is uniformly wrong but never negative, so the "doesn't crash" gate held. Re-drive result is technically wrong (no value-correctness gate was watching); the cold-boot path HLYWI6 must revisit balance correctness AFTER this fix lands.

## Python reference

`src/degenbot/aave/extraction.py::RawAmountExtractor` (the oracle):
* `extract_supply`: `abi_decode(["address","uint256"], data)` -> returns word 1.
* `extract_borrow`: `abi_decode(["address","uint256","uint8","uint256"], data)` -> returns word 1.
* `extract_repay`: `abi_decode(["uint256","bool"], data)` -> returns word 0. Rust correct.
* `extract_withdraw`: `abi_decode(["uint256"], data)` -> returns word 0. Rust correct.

So Python switches extractor per event-type via `EVENT_EXTRACTORS`; Rust collapses them to a single word0.

## Fix

In `extract_raw_amount_for_event`, for the non-liquidation branch, switch on `op.operation_type`:
* `OperationType::Supply | OperationType::Borrow` -> `extract_pool_amount_word1(pool_event)`.
* `OperationType::Repay | OperationType::RepayWithAtokens | OperationType::Withdraw` -> `extract_pool_amount_word0(pool_event)` (unchanged).

## Test plan (Red/Green)

RED-first: the YUPSIB parity fixture I just wrote (`test_standalone_transfer_then_withdraw_parity.py`) currently fails with the 10^57 divergence — that is the RED state for this task. After the fix, both paths write byte-identical collateral_positions (SENDER end-state = 0: supplied `_AMOUNT` then standalone-transferred out; USER end-state = 0: received then withdrew).

GREEN regression guards:
* `test_supply_same_chunk_as_reserve_init_lands_collateral` (W2S3WH) tightened from `> 0` to `== _SUPPLY_AMOUNT` (the Mint credits the supply amount; liquidityIndex=RAY=1.0 makes scaled == underlying).
* The YUPSIB standalone test (`test_standalone_transfer_then_withdraw.py`) tightened to `== 0` on both positions.

## Out of scope

* Why the mainnet re-drive to 16596000 didn't catch this — NONE of the existing tests assert on Supply balance values; they're all existence-only.
* The cold-boot path HLYWI6 — file a separate revisit AFTER this fix lands so the re-drive can be re-evaluated against Python on values, not just "doesn't crash".

data.title: Rust-owned AnvilFork via alloy node-bindings (replace web3 subprocess glue)
Fix: Rust run_aave_update cold-boot bootstrap — self-discover POOL/POOL_CONFIGURATOR via ProxyCreated (replace Python Phase-1 bootstrap; unblock HLYWI6 fresh-market hand-run)
data.body:
## Goal

Make `run_aave_update` (`rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/run.rs:1025`) cold-boot a fresh Aave V3 market on its own: when `aave_v3_contracts` lacks the `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows that `build_fetch_spec` (run.rs:919–947) requires, the updater must self-bootstrap them by fetching `ProxyCreated` events from the (already-seeded) `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` contract, mirroring the Python `update_aave_market` Phase-1 bootstrap (`commands.py:1010–1062` + `event_handlers.py:982 _process_proxy_creation_event`).

This closes the production blocker that surfaced during JGQHBX (harness construction): a fresh-market first run `aave activate ethereum_aave_v3` → `aave update` currently hard-errors at `build_fetch_spec` with `ValueError: POOL contract row not found for market {market_id}` — reproduced on real mainnet RPC. See the worker's JGQHBX finding + the orchestrator's reproduction (committed alongside this task's creation, ephemeral script `/tmp/rust_fresh_boot_check.py` shape).

## Architectural context (read before implementing)

- **AGENTS.md Architectural Vision** — "Rust is the engine; Python is a driver shell, not a co-implementation." Cold-boot of a fresh market is **bot functionality**, not driver-shell orchestration; it must live in the Rust core. A standalone Rust consumer (`cargo add degenbot`) must bootstrap a fresh market without any Python pre-step (apart from the one-line PoolAddressProvider-address seed in `activate`, which is fine — it's a constant address, pure config).
- **ADR-005 / ADR-003** — the Rust core owns everything a functional bot needs; the Python layer's `activate` becomes a thin seed (`POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` constant + market row + GHO token), not a bootstrap implementation.
- **Migration-guide §4.3** — the Python `_process_proxy_creation_event` retires in CZM7TI; this task's Rust bootstrap replaces it. The Python Phase-1 bootstrap is the DELETING-Python's responsibility, but its replacement must already exist (HERE) before deletion can fire.

## Current state (what's broken)

1. `aave activate ethereum_aave_v3` (`commands.py:160`) seeds:
   - `AaveV3Market` row with `last_update_block = 16_291_070`
   - `AaveV3Contract` row `name="POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER"` (constant address `EthereumMainnetAaveV3.pool_address_provider`)
   - GHO token + `AaveGhoToken` row
2. `run_aave_update` (`run.rs:1025`) immediately calls `build_fetch_spec` (`run.rs:919`) BEFORE entering the chunk loop.
3. `build_fetch_spec` calls `db.fetch_aave_contracts(market_id)` (db: `aave.rs:428`) and **hard-errors** if `POOL` / `POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows are missing (`run.rs:930–941`).
4. The chunk dispatcher already HAS a `ContractInserted` arm (run.rs:710–722 → `apply_contract_inserted_on_conn` at `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs:1420`) that handles `ProxyCreated` events during a chunk — but only AFTER `build_fetch_spec` passes. So the boot events that would create the `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows are reachable ONLY AFTER the rows are required → circular for a cold boot.

## Implementation contract

### Behavior on cold boot (fresh market, only `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` seeded)

After `run_aave_update` returns from a cold-boot run covering `[last_update_block+1, to_block]` over mainnet:
- The DB has exactly ONE `POOL` contract row (address matches mainnet's Aave V3 Pool; revision fetched via `POOL_REVISION()` RPC).
- The DB has exactly ONE `POOL_CONFIGURATOR` contract row (same shape, `CONFIGURATOR_REVISION()` RPC).
- The DB has the `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` row (unchanged from `activate`).
- `PRICE_ORACLE` may or may not exist — both Rust + Python paths treat it as `Option` (`run.rs:941`); the bootstrap does NOT need to create it. (It's discovered dynamically via chunk events on both paths — keep parity with Python.)
- `last_update_block` advanced to `to_block`.
- All per-tx/user/asset state written as the chunk loop normally would.

### Idempotency (the subtlety)

**The same `ProxyCreated` event must NOT produce two contract rows.** The chunk dispatcher's `ContractInserted` arm will re-encounter the `ProxyCreated(POOL)` event at block 16_291_127 during chunk processing (it's part of the chunk's events). If a bootstrap pass ALSO applies it, you get a duplicate row.

The Python path is reference: it produces exactly ONE `POOL` row per `ProxyCreated` event — Phase-1 processes it (`_process_proxy_creation_event` at `commands.py:1031/1039`), Phase-3 chronological dispatch does NOT re-process ProxyCreated (no `PROXY_CREATED` arm in `transaction_processor.py`'s per-tx dispatch — verified via grep). So Python = 1 row per ProxyCreated.

Two acceptable designs for the Rust to match this (pick one, justify in the task completion summary):

**Design α — bootstrap pass + idempotent chunk dispatch.** Before `build_fetch_spec`, if `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows are missing, fetch `ProxyCreated` events from the `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` address over `[last_update_block+1, last_update_block + bootstrap_window]` (default window ~2k blocks; mainnet lands at +56/+59/+65, well within), apply each via a NEW `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` (idempotent variant: `INSERT` only if no row with `(market_id, name, address)` exists). Then proceed with normal chunk loop; the chunk's `ContractInserted` arm must use the SAME idempotent variant (so the bootstrap-applied row is not re-inserted).

**Design β — deferred/lazy `build_fetch_spec`.** Hoist the `build_fetch_spec` call to per-chunk (re-evaluated after each chunk's bootstrap events apply), and have the chunk `ContractInserted` arm be the SOLE creator of `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows. The first chunk containing the boot ProxyCreated events creates the rows; subsequent per-chunk `build_fetch_spec` calls see them. Risk: changes the chunk loop's structure; more invasive; possibly affects reserves/asset resolution which depends on the fetch spec.

**Recommendation: Design α** — smaller surface, the bootstrap-pass is a one-shot RPC-fetch + apply, the idempotency change to `apply_contract_inserted_on_conn` is localized to the bootstrap-name path (only `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR`), and the chunk loop structure is unchanged.

### Idempotency for ONLY the bootstrap contracts — NOT generic

The idempotency check applies to `name IN ("POOL", "POOL_CONFIGURATOR")` only. Other `ContractInserted` events (`AddressSet`-driven, `PoolDataProviderUpdated`-driven, etc.) MUST stay unconditional INSERT (matching the Python which also unconditional-appends them). Hardcoding the bootstrap-name whitelist is acceptable here — these names are protocol constants (the right-padded ASCII bytes32 ids `b"POOL"`/`b"POOL_CONFIGURATOR"`).

## TDD implementation order

1. **Idempotent insert helper.** Add `DegenbotDb::apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn(conn, market_id, name, address, revision) -> Result<bool, DbError>` (returns `true` if inserted, `false` if pre-existing). Tests in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs`:
   - Cold: no prior row → inserts one → returns `true`.
   - Warm: prior row with same (market_id, name, address) → no-op → returns `false` → row count unchanged.
   - Different address same name → inserts (idempotency key is `(market_id, name, address)`, NOT `(market_id, name)`).
   - Different revision same (market_id, name, address) → no-op (the revision stays as-is — matching the Python's "Phase-1 wins" semantics; the row from the first ProxyCreated event is canonical).
2. **Bootstrap pass + chunk-dispatch wiring.** In `run.rs::run_aave_update`, BEFORE `build_fetch_spec`:
   - Read `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` row from `aave_v3_contracts` (filter by `name`). If it does NOT exist, propagate a `NotBootstrapped`-style error (caller must seed via `activate`).
   - If `POOL` OR `POOL_CONFIGURATOR` is missing: RPC-fetch `ProxyCreated` events from `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER.address` over `[last_update_block+1, last_update_block+1+BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW]` (default `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW = 2000`).
   - For each `ProxyCreated` event, decode the `id` (bytes32, right-padded ASCII), match against `b"POOL"` / `b"POOL_CONFIGURATOR"`; for matches, decode the `proxy` address (topics[2]) + `implementation` address (topics[3]); RPC-call `POOL_REVISION()` / `CONFIGURATOR_REVISION()` on the implementation; insert via `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn`.
   - If after this pass `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` is STILL missing (e.g., the bootstrap window was too small for a non-mainnet market), raise a `BootstrapFailed` error.
3. **Chunk dispatch idempotency.** The `ContractInserted` arm (run.rs:710–722) currently calls `apply_contract_inserted_on_conn` unconditionally. Change it to use `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` for `name IN ("POOL", "POOL_CONFIGURATOR")`; keep `apply_contract_inserted_on_conn` (unconditional) for all other contract names. Add a test: feeding the SAME `ProxyCreated` event in a chunk twice (or via bootstrap-pass + chunk) yields ONE row, not two.
4. **End-to-end cold-boot test in Rust.** A `#[test]` in `run.rs` that mocks the ProxyCreated RPC response (you can pattern off the writer_parity harness's mock-JSON-RPC server at `tests/aave/writer_parity/harness.py`) and asserts: call `run_aave_update` on a fresh DB seeded only with the market row + `POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER` row → both `POOL` and `POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows are created with correct addresses + revisions → `last_update_block` advances → no duplicate rows.
5. **Verify against Python parity.** Run the existing writer_parity test suite (`just test-rust-python` or `uv run pytest tests/aave/writer_parity/`) — all 75 fixtures must stay GREEN (the idempotency change должен NOT change the byte-IDENTITY results the fixtures already assert; if a fixture's mock RPC happens to feed a duplicate `ProxyCreated` event, the previous behavior was 2 rows + the Python apparently also produced 2 — confirm before changing fixture expectations; if it changes, write a new fixture that documents the idempotency intent explicitly).

## Out of scope

- Do NOT change `aave activate ethereum_aave_v3` (`commands.py:160`) — it stays the thin seed (PoolAddressProvider + market + GHO). No Python changes.
- Do NOT touch the `aave_v3_contracts` schema (`schema_head.sql:59`) — no `UNIQUE` constraint added. The idempotency is logic-level (read-then-insert), not schema-level. (Adding a `UNIQUE(market_id, name, address)` would be a schema migration gated on ADR-010/011; out of scope here. Logic-level idempotency is the right scope.)
- Do NOT bootstrap `PRICE_ORACLE`. The Python path treats it as `Option`; the Rust must too.
- Do NOT retire the Python `_process_proxy_creation_event` here — that's CZM7TI's lane (still gated on HLYWI6).
- Do NOT delete the JGQHBX harness's `_bootstrap_rust_contracts` workaround in THIS task — that's JGQHBX's responsibility once the worker returns to it. (After this task lands, JGQHBX deletes its workaround since the Rust self-bootstraps; the symmetric-dup wart disappears; the known blind-spot in [16291071, 16291136] becomes validated.)

## Deliverable

- `apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn` in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs` + unit tests.
- Bootstrap pass in `run_aave_update` (run.rs) wiring the PoolAddressProvider fetch + decode + idempotent inserts.
- Idempotency in the chunk dispatcher's `ContractInserted` arm for `name IN ("POOL", "POOL_CONFIGURATOR")`.
- At least one Rust `#[test]` for cold-boot end-to-end + one for idempotency (no duplicate when same ProxyCreated appears via bootstrap-pass AND chunk).
- The writer_parity suite stays GREEN (no existing-byte-IDENTITY test changes; if any do, write a NEW fixture documenting the idempotency intent and link it here).
- Reproduction script behavior: `/tmp/rust_fresh_boot_check.py`-style "fresh DB → activate-shape seed → update --to 16296000" no longer raises; a smoke against real RPC at `--to 16296000` produces `POOL`/`POOL_CONFIGURATOR` rows with mainnet-correct addresses + revisions + advances `last_update_block` to 16_296_000. (The worker can run this smoke directly — they have the RPC envvar + the devcontainer's `host.containers.internal:8545` archive node.)

  - First sign that Design β is preferable to Design α (the spec recommends α; the worker may find β cleaner given the code structure — if so, ping before committing).
  - On completion with the cold-boot smoke-test result (paste the post-run row dump: `SELECT name, address, revision FROM aave_v3_contracts` + `SELECT last_update_block FROM aave_v3_markets`).
- After this task is done, JGQHBX (the harness) resumes; the worker deletes its `_bootstrap_rust_contracts` workaround as the first JGQHBX update.
- HLYWI6 (the full-sync gate) was blocked on JGQHBX; it is now ALSO blocked on THIS task (sequencing applied at task creation).

Design α landed (bootstrap pass + idempotent chunk arm).

Deliverables:
- apply_contract_inserted_if_absent_on_conn (degenbot-db/write.rs): idempotent
  INSERT keyed on (market_id, name, address); Phase-1 wins (revision not
  overwritten). 4 unit tests (cold-insert, warm-same-key no-op, different-
  address inserts second, different-revision-same-key no-op).
- bootstrap_pool_contracts (aave-updater/run.rs): before build_fetch_spec, if
  POOL/POOL_CONFIGURATOR missing, fetch ProxyCreated from POOL_ADDRESS_PROVIDER

## Goal
- Port the Aave V3 **state rehydrate / read-back** path — `aave/analysis/orchestrator.py::DatabasePositionQuery` (reads `AaveV3User` + joined `AaveV3CollateralPosition`/`AaveV3DebtPosition` + `AaveV3Asset`/`AaveV3AssetConfig`/`AaveV3EModeCategory` + `AaveGhoToken` from the DB) — through `degenbot-db` via a PyO3 seam, converting the SQLAlchemy `joinedload` query into a typed-row read.

## Context
- Scope task: `MPS3U7` (Epic `AZGJUN`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (read-back over substrate).
- §2.1 criteria: type=Address/big-int/int; I/O=row→struct transform (the `joinedload` chains are pure relational reads); warm path (analysis-pipeline startup / per-analysis-batch, not per-tx). This is the read companion to the Aave writers (sibling task): it rehydrates the very rows the writers persist. Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer running Aave analysis must read lending-market state from a Rust crate.
- **Cross-epic read-dependency answer (orchestrator's question):** the lending-market feed reads the **DB**, not `BotState`. `DatabasePositionQuery` holds a `Session` and runs `select(AaveV3User).where(market_id).joinedload(...)` — a hard DB-substrate dependency on `SLHSM4` (the Aave read fns). NO `BotState` edge; NO `QVMWQC` edge (different callsite set; QVMWQC is pool builders).
- Deps: `SLHSM4` (substrate Aave row structs + read fns). NO dep on the writer sibling (reads are independent of how rows were written). NO dep on the liquidity-math sibling.
- `aave/analysis/orchestrator.py` orchestration surrounding the query = **stays-python** (analysis-pipeline orchestration is a shell concern; the Rust seam owns the query + typed-row materialization).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-db` (or a `degenbot-updaters` read module) exposes `fetch_aave_users_by_market(conn, market_id) -> Vec<AaveUserRow>` + `fetch_collateral_positions(conn, user_id) -> Vec<CollateralPositionRow>` (+ asset/config/e-mode joins) returning typed row structs; the `joinedload` graph materialized in Rust.
- PyO3 seam (`#[pyclass] PyDatabasePositionQuery` or `#[pyfunction]`s) wraps the reads; `py.detach()` for DB I/O; registered in `c_api.rs`.
- Python `DatabasePositionQuery` delegates; the `select(...).joinedload(...)` bodies deleted.
- Parity (§4.2): read a fixture Aave DB through the Rust seam → identical user/position/asset graph as the prior Python path (Py as oracle until green, retire per §4.3).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (aave analysis + `db_verification` suite), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `SLHSM4` substrate (Epic `VGTEDL`).
- The Aave writers (sibling task).
- The analysis pipeline's in-memory modeling (`aave/operations.py`, `extraction.py`, `enrichment/handlers/*`) — stays Python (analysis orchestration + domain logic).
- Pool rehydrate-on-startup (`v3/v4_snapshot.py::DatabaseSnapshot`) — that is Epic `VGTEDL` (`WKZ7ID`).

data.title: cache Aave get_or_create lookup statements (prepare_cached)
data.body:
# impl-4: cache Aave get_or_create lookup statements (prepare_cached)

## Validated by spike-7 — ADOPT (`prepare_cached` one-line swap, shape a)

## Goal
Convert the 5 `existing_*` lookup fns in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs`
from `conn.query_row(<sql>, ...)` (which prepares+runs+finalizes a statement each
call) to `conn.prepare_cached(<sql>)?.query_row(...)` — caching the compiled
statement across calls. **4.07–4.40× speedup** per lookup (the strongest result
in the F4N6DX epic).

## Why this is NOT the rejected JO64LY (do not carry over that rejection)
JO64LY rejected `prepare_cached` for the liquidity-updater hot loop because the
**dynamic-SQL upsert** (variable `chunk.len()` placeholders per pool) fragmented
the cache → 0.947× slowdown. The Aave lookup SQLs are a DIFFERENT shape: constant
single-row `SELECT ... WHERE <unique> = ?` queries, called per Aave event. The
cache key (SQL text) is identical every call → `prepare_cached` hits every time.
The JO64LY rejection does NOT transfer.

## The 5 sites (all constant-SQL, all the same one-line swap)
In `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/write.rs`:

| Site | line | SQL (constant) | Lookup key |
|---|---|---|---|
| `existing_emode_category` | ~800 | `SELECT id FROM aave_v3_emode_categories WHERE market_id = ?1 AND category_id = ?2` | (market_id, category_id) UNIQUE |
| `existing_asset_config` | ~815 | `SELECT id FROM aave_v3_asset_configs WHERE asset_id = ?1` | asset_id (UNIQUE) |
| `existing_user_collateral_config` | ~828 | `... WHERE user_id = ?1 AND asset_id = ?2` | (user_id, asset_id) UNIQUE |
| `existing_user` | ~843 | `... WHERE market_id = ?1 AND address = ?2` | (market_id, address) UNIQUE |
| `existing_erc20_token` | ~857 | `SELECT id FROM erc20_tokens WHERE chain = ?1 AND address = ?2` | (chain, address) UNIQUE |

### The swap (mechanically identical, observationally identical)
```rust
// before:
conn.query_row("SELECT id FROM ... WHERE ...", params![...], |r| r.get(0)).optional()

// after:
let mut s = conn.prepare_cached("SELECT id FROM ... WHERE ...")?;
s.query_row(params![...], |r| r.get(0)).optional()
```
~3 lines each (the `let mut s = ...; s.query_row(...).optional()` two-liner replaces
the `query_row(...).optional()` one-liner). NO signature changes (the fns still take
`&Connection` + return `Result<Option<i64>, DbError>`). Block-scoped (the `s` drops
at the fn's `}`) → safe.

## Benchmark (spike-7, reused JO64LY harness, 5 runs median)
| N events | baseline (query_row) | prepare_cached | hoisted | speedup (cached) | speedup (hoisted) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 500 | 0.0051s (2.05µs/lookup) | 0.0012s (0.46µs) | 0.0008s | 4.40× | 6.06× |
| 5000 | 0.0510s (2.04µs) | 0.0122s (0.49µs) | 0.0088s | 4.19× | 5.78× |
| 50000 | 0.5411s (2.16µs) | 0.1330s (0.53µs) | 0.1017s | 4.07× | 5.32× |

`prepare_cached` captures 4× of the 5.5× available; the hoist adds only ~1.3-1.4×
over `prepare_cached` (NOT worth the invasive restructure — threading a
`LookupStmts` struct through call sites / driver-loop transaction). The one-line
swap is the right cost/benefit tradeoff.

## Honest framing / when this matters (preserve in impl notes)
**The absolute CPU saved is small right now** because:
- The Rust `get_or_create_*` are NOT yet in any production hot loop. The
  `degenbot-python/src/aave/` module is empty (no PyO3 exposure). The Rust
  `get_or_create_*` are called only from `writer_parity.rs` tests.
- The **only production caller** is `existing_erc20_token` via
  `get_or_create_erc20_token_on_conn` in `discovery.rs:189/197/288/296/375/383` —
  per-pool at registration (pool discovery, a cold/sparse path). Tiny immediate benefit.
- Aave event processing is still Python SQLAlchemy ORM (`cli/aave/db_users.py`,
  `db_positions.py`, `db_assets.py`). The Rust ports are waiting for the migration.

**So this is a forward-looking optimization** — bank the 4× for when the Aave
migration ports the Python event handlers to the Rust `get_or_create_*` path.
At ~5 lookups/event × ~500 events/chunk that's ~4ms/chunk saved post-migration.
The change is zero-risk (parity tests pin correctness) + cheap (5 one-line swaps,
no restructure, no behavior change), so ship now rather than re-discovering this
when the migration lands.

## Safety (verified)
Per the JO64LY borrow-check proof (block-scoped stmts drop before next acquire;
rusqlite's cache is interior-mutable via `&Connection`), the swap is safe. Spike-7
re-verified the `existing_*` `fn(&Connection, ...) -> Result<...>` shape: prototyped
on `existing_user`, compiles clean. Sequential `existing_*` calls on a
`&Connection` (Transaction-borrowed) + commit-after-runs all OK. Multiple sequential
`prepare_cached` of the SAME SQL = cache hit (previous released before re-acquire).
No `CachedStatement` held across `commit()` (all drop at the per-call fn boundary).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 5 `existing_*` fns in `write.rs` swapped from `conn.query_row(...).optional()` to `conn.prepare_cached(...)?.query_row(...).optional()`.
- [ ] Function signatures UNCHANGED (still `fn(&Connection, ...) -> Result<Option<i64>, DbError>`).
- [ ] `writer_parity.rs` tests pass UNCHANGED (the swap is observationally identical — these tests pin correctness).
- [ ] No `CachedStatement` held across `commit()` (verified by reading the diff — block-scoped drops).

## Optional (out of scope, don't expand)
- `aave.rs:310` `fetch_aave_oracle_address` (`query_row` on `aave_v3_contracts WHERE market_id = ?1 AND name = 'PRICE_ORACLE'`) is the same shape, constant SQL, single-row. Currently called per-market-init (low priority). Could be swapped as a 6th site if desired, but NOT required — it's not in a hot loop. Flag for the Aave migration task.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-db` (incl. `writer_parity.rs` — MUST pass unchanged).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings` (CI gate).
- `just test-rust` + `just lint-rust` + `just format`.
- Optional: a microbench in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/benches/` asserting the 4× (low priority — the scratch bench shape transfers; given the change is a tested one-liner, the bench is Nice-to-Have).

## Revisit note
If the Aave migration (when it lands) restructures the `get_or_create_*` path to
introduce a hoisted-statement struct (`LookupStmts`), revisit — the hoist gave
5.3-6.1× in the bench, ~1.3-1.4× over `prepare_cached`. For now, the one-line
swap is the right tradeoff.

## Gating
0.6.x-safe (code change, no schema change). NOT gated to 0.7. NOT blocked on any
other task. Forward-looking (banks 4× for the future Aave-migration hot path).

## Goal
- Port the SQLite **file operations** (`create_new_sqlite_database`, `backup_sqlite_database`, `compact_sqlite_database`, `upgrade_existing_sqlite_database` in `src/degenbot/database/operations.py`) into `degenbot-db` (sibling `SLHSM4`), and convert the Click CLI (`src/degenbot/cli/database.py`: `backup`/`reset`/`upgrade`/`compact`) into a delegating shell over the Rust seam.

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL`). Rubric split:
  - The SQLite file ops (create-with-WAL/`VACUUM`/Alembic stamp, `sqlite3.Connection.backup`, `VACUUM`, `command.upgrade`) = **port-now** — pure SQLite/file I/O with no Python-ecosystem coupling beyond the Alembic `command` shim; a standalone Rust consumer needs DB create/upgrade/backup/compact.
  - The Click CLI commands (`cli/database.py`) = **stays-python** — CLI orchestration is a Python shell concern (rubric §2.1 "Keep in Python": orchestration).
- §2.1 for the ops: hot path = construction/CLI only; type shape = file path + pragma strings; I/O shape = sqlite file ops. Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer must be able to create/upgrade/back up its DB from Rust.
- Depends on `SLHSM4` (the migration runner + connection the ops use).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-db` exposes `create_new_database(path)`, `backup_database(src,dst)`, `compact_database(path)`, `upgrade_database(path)` (the Rust core already owns connection + migration runner from `SLHSM4`).
- A `#[pyfunction]` seam in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/` wraps each op (registered in `c_api.rs`); `py.detach()` for the file I/O.
- `cli/database.py`'s four commands delegate to the Rust seam; the inline `create_engine`/`sqlite3.connect`/`command.upgrade` bodies in `operations.py` deleted (functions kept as thin Python wrappers or removed if the CLI calls Rust directly).
- `backup_sqlite_database`'s integrity-check assertions (`PRAGMA integrity_check`) preserved in Rust.
- Parity (§4.2): `degenbot database create/backup/compact/upgrade` against a fixture DB produces an equivalent file (WalMode, stamped to head, byte-stable backup) — keep Python path as oracle until green, retire per §4.3.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (CLI database tests), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `degenbot-db` crate itself (sibling `SLHSM4`).
- The `DatabaseSettings` config / path resolution (`config.py`) — stays Python (config loading is a shell concern; the Rust core takes a resolved path).
- The Alembic migration **authoring** toolchain — stays Python (Alembic autogenerate is a Python-ecosystem dev tool); only the runtime migration **runner** ports (in `SLHSM4`).

data.title: Goal
data.body:
## Body
`tests/cli/test_heal_boundary.py` (or co-located in `test_database_heal.py` if preferred). **Larger than the unit tests in T4** — this is the end-to-end proof.

## Setup
Build a representative large old DB — head-stamped, populated with a few hundred pools + liquidity positions across multiple chains, using the existing PyO3 write seams (`db_upsert_exchange`, `db_upsert_pool`/whatever the pool-write seam is, `db_upsert_erc20_token`, etc.). The point is realistic volume + FK graph depth, not a single row.

## Assertions (post `degenbot database heal --force`)
- (a) **every row in every user table survives** with identical PKs.
- (b) **FK integrity intact**: every `_id` column's values resolve to an existing row in the referenced table.
- (c) `alembic_version` table GONE; `_degenbot_db_schema_version` stamped RustOwned.
- (d) **full recoverability**: the `.bak` file exists, is openable read-only (assert a `sqlite3.connect` succeeds in read-only mode), and still contains the old data (row counts match the pre-heal counts).
- (e) **post-heal writes work** against the RustOwned DB: a new exchange/pool upsert succeeds and reads back.

## Docstring
State this is the artifact for ADR-011 + epic TGIP5N — proves the heal operation is non-destructive and fully recoverable, which is the precondition for the 0.7.0 retirement (T6) being non-breaking.

## Depends on
T4.

data.body:
# Cut `cli/aave/db_*` `get_or_create_*` to delegating shells over the Rust seam (Sub-step C, slice 1)

## Goal
- Sub-step C slice 1 of the Aave-writer port: convert the **4 small writer-helper modules** (`cli/aave/db_market.py`, `db_assets.py`, `db_users.py`, `db_positions.py`) from inline SQLAlchemy `session.scalar(select(...))` → mutate → `session.add` ORM bodies into **delegating shells** over the `RQXEKH` Sub-step-B `db_get_or_create_*` PyO3 seam. Delete the inline ORM bodies (no back-compat layer — per root AGENTS.md).

## Context
- **Premature close recap.** RQXEKH's acceptance criterion — "*Python `_process_*` handlers + `get_or_create_*` become delegating shells; inline `session.scalar/select`/`session.add` bodies deleted*" — is unmet. This sibling is the smallest, cleanest first cut of Sub-step C.
- **Current state evidence.** ORM-session call counts in the 4 target files (`session.add`/`scalar`/`commit`/`flush`/`execute`):
  - `db_market.py`: 6 calls (160 lines)
  - `db_assets.py`: 6 calls (173 lines)
  - `db_users.py`: 5 calls (150 lines)
  - `db_positions.py`: 3 calls (92 lines)
- **The seam each shell calls.** Sibling `<ID_B>` (2QPBUJ) lands the `#[pyfunction]`s `db_get_or_create_e_mode_category`, `db_get_or_create_asset_config`, `db_get_or_create_user_collateral_config`, `db_get_or_create_user`, `db_get_or_create_erc20_token`, `db_get_or_create_collateral_position`, `db_get_or_create_debt_position` taking `database_path` + the caller-supplied `Option` params (per the RPC-coupling carve-out: the Python driver stays the RPC authority for name/symbol/decimals/GHO discount).
- **The `Session` becomes vestigial for these writes.** Each `db_*` helper currently takes `session: Session` to resolve the SQLAlchemy `engine.url.database` (the `.db` file path) + run the get-or-create. After cutover, the shell takes `database_path` (or keeps `session` for path resolution + hands `database_path` to the Rust seam) — the ORM `add`/`scalar` bodies are deleted. The Python `AaveV3Market` etc. ORM classes are NOT deleted (they're still used for read-back + the `aave_update` driver's `market.last_update_block` mutation); only the `get_or_create_*` write paths are cut over.
- **Rubric (§2.1).** I/O=substrate upsert (Rust owns get-or-create); GIL=`py.detach()` in the seam already; type=matches the Rust core; hot=warm (per-block chunk backfill in `aave_update`). Shell has no business logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cli/aave/db_market.py`: every `get_or_create_*` fn (e.g. `get_or_create_market`, `get_or_create_aave_contract`) calls the corresponding `db_get_or_create_*` Rust seam fn (sibling 2QPBUJ); inline `session.scalar`/`session.add`/`session.flush` bodies deleted.
- [ ] `cli/aave/db_assets.py`: `get_or_create_asset`, `get_or_create_asset_config`, `get_contract` etc. delegate to Rust; ORM bodies deleted (a caller may still mutate the returned ORM for non-write purposes — that's read-back, not in scope).
- [ ] `cli/aave/db_users.py`: `get_or_create_user` + `get_or_create_user_collateral_config` delegate; ORM bodies deleted.
- [ ] `cli/aave/db_positions.py`: `get_or_create_collateral_position` + `get_or_create_debt_position` delegate; ORM bodies deleted.
- [ ] The SQLAlchemy `Session` arg remains on the shell signatures (callers unchanged — the `bot.db()` context manager returns one) but is used only to resolve `database_path` + for the `market.last_update_block` end-of-chunk mutation (which is `aave_update` driver-side, separate).
- [ ] `rg -n "session\.add\b" src/degenbot/cli/aave/db_{market,assets,users,positions}.py` returns empty (no inline ORM writes left in these 4 files).
- [ ] `aave update --dry-run` over a fixture Aave event sequence produces the same commit-time DB state as pre-cutover (proves the shell preserves behavior end-to-end — the §4.2 red-green against the Python oracle is owned by the parity-gate sibling, not this task).
- [ ] Cross-check: file diff shows ONLY deletions + delegate calls (`from degenbot_rs import db_get_or_create_*`); no new logic.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` — the `cli/aave/` test suite passes (the existing parity tests assert the same DB state; they were always passing via the ORM, must still pass via the Rust seam).
- `just lint-python` (ruff + ty) — the new `from degenbot_rs import ...` resolves via the `.pyi` stub.
- `just test-rust-python` — if any `tests/rust/` test exercises these shells.
- `just format`.

## Non-goals
- The PyO3 seam itself (sibling 2QPBUJ — Sub-step B).
- The `event_handlers.py::_process_*` handlers (sibling Sub-step C slice 2 — those consume the `apply_*` seam, different fn set).
- The `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch — `stays-python`.
- The `transaction_processor.py` / `operations_parser.py` / `token_processor.py` residual ORM callsites — Sub-step C slice 3 (sibling).
- The §4.2 red-green parity gate (sibling — final close-out).

## Sequencing
- **Depends on:** sibling 2QPBUJ (the Sub-step B seam — these shells call its pyfunctions).
- **Unblocks:** the handler-shell cut (slice 2 — reads via the same `db_get_or_create_*` shells transitive) + the processor-callsite audit (slice 3 — depends on the db_* shells having landed to know which residual callsites are real writes).

data.title: 0.7.0 retirement: drop Alembic dep + migrations dir (gated on heal + release)
data.body:
## GATED — do not start without explicit "0.7.0 release" decision + T5 passing.

## Goal
Execute the 0.7.0 Alembic retirement, made non-breaking by `heal` (T1-T5). Successor to the `JFFQV2` placeholder from epic 2Z3Y46.

## Body
Once `heal` ships + is proven (T5) and the 0.7.0 release decision is made:
- Delete `src/degenbot/migrations/` (the kill-listed dir).
- Remove `alembic` + `alembic-utils` deps from `pyproject.toml`.
- Remove the `alembic_version`-reading branch of `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/migrate.rs::ensure_schema` — `AlembicCurrent`/`AlembicStale` states collapse; every DB is `FreshStandalone` / `RustOwned` / `Unrecognized`.
- Remove the Alembic fall-back from `upgrade_existing_sqlite_database` (`src/degenbot/database/operations.py`): it becomes `cutover`-or-`heal`-or-error. Preferred: alias `database upgrade` → `database heal` for safety (heal is strictly more general; any legacy DB heals regardless of state).
- Update ADR-010 + ADR-011 to mark retirement complete.
- Remove the kill-list entry for `src/degenbot/migrations/` from `AGENTS.md` (it's gone).

## Why non-breaking
Any legacy DB — head, stale, or unrecognized — can `degenbot database heal` into a RustOwned DB regardless of its old state, so removing Alembic strands nobody. `heal` doesn't depend on Alembic at runtime (the column mapping is a static Rust constant + auto-derivation), so deleting the migrations doesn't break it.

## Acceptance
- `just test-all` green.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green.
- No references to `alembic` remain in `pyproject.toml` or `src/degenbot/`.
- A pre-0.7 DB (built before this release) heals cleanly via `degenbot database heal`.

## Depends on
T5 + human "0.7.0 release" decision (checkpoint).

data.title: Aave V3 operations parser: apply dispatch glue (process_transaction entry)
data.body:
# HQF5NQ-C — Aave V3 operations parser: the apply dispatch glue

> **Split sibling of HQF5NQ (the single-shot OPERATIONSPARSER).**
> Deps on HQF5NQ (A: parser-core + standard builders) + HQF5NQ-B (liquidation
> engine) — needs A's `Operation` types + the `parse()` scaffold AND B's
> `Operation { operation_type: Liquidation, ... }` builder. Ships LAST
> (after A + B). This is the per-tx entry point the orchestrator (6SWY4R)
> calls — the bridge from parsed `Operation`s to substrate `AaveChunkEvent`
> variants dispatched via `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`.

## Goal

Port the `transaction_processor._process_transaction` dispatch + the
`Operation`→`ScaledTokenProcessor`→`AaveChunkEvent` variant construction +
the GHO-discount-lookup machinery. The parser (A + B) produces an
`Operation` sequence; this task consumes that sequence + writes through the
substrate apply fns (CXRGX4/UR7QNL/5Z3QQ2/RYKCC4) on the caller's chunk
Connection. This is where the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) is
exercised end-to-end — U5YIBG (§4.2) is the final arbiter.

## Scope (this task)

### 1. `process_transaction(conn, tx_events: &[DecodedAaveEvent], ctx: &TxContext) -> Result<()>`
The per-tx entry point the orchestrator (6SWY4R) calls. Instantiates the
`OperationsParser` (A's struct) with the tx context + calls `parse()` to
get the `Operation` sequence + dispatches each Operation's constituent
ScaledToken events to the substrate apply fns. Mirror the Python
`transaction_processor._process_transaction`.

### 2. `Operation`→`AaveChunkEvent` variant construction (1 path per `ScaledTokenEventType`)
For each Operation, construct the `AaveChunkEvent` variant(s) + dispatch via
`apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` (CXRGX4's dispatch). The paths:
- `CollateralMint` → `ScaledTokenProcessor::collateral(rev).process_collateral_mint(&event_data)` → `AaveChunkEvent::ScaledTokenMint { position: Collateral, position_id, balance_delta, new_index }`.
- `CollateralBurn` → `process_collateral_burn` → `ScaledTokenBurn`.
- `CollateralTransfer` → `ScaledTokenTransfer { from_position_id, to_position_id, scaled_amount, transfer_index }`.
- `DebtMint`/`DebtBurn`/`DebtTransfer` → the vToken equivalents.
- `GhoDebtMint`/`GhoDebtBurn` → the GHO-vToken equivalents (coordinate with RYKCC4).
- The **Mint-as-burn interest-exceeds-repayment edge case** for WITHDRAW/REPAY_WITH_ATOKENS (the §4.2-drift edge — the SCALEAPPLY 3-branch reconciliation's interest-exceeds-deposit arm fires; verify the `balance_delta` sign). This is where the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) is exercised on the edge branches.
- The **GHO_LIQUIDATION debt-burn vs COLLATERAL transfer** in DeficitCoverage (the burn-pair check in `_create_deficit_coverage_operations`).
- The **GHO_DEBT_INTEREST vToken handling** in the LiquidationCall builder's output (from B).

### 3. The GHO-discount-lookup machinery (mirror `transaction_processor._process_transaction` L73-192)
The `discount_updates_by_log_index` map + `get_effective_discount_at_log_index` path — the GHO-payoff-before-LiquidationCall machinery that needs the stkAAVE balance first. Coordinate with RYKCC4's `apply_stk_aave_staked_on_conn`/`apply_stk_aave_redeem_on_conn` for the stkAAVE-transfer pre-processing (the discount is computed from the user's stkAAVE balance at the LiquidationCall's log index, so the stkAAVE transfers must be applied BEFORE the LiquidationCall's GHO discount is read). Flag if the ordering constraint needs an explicit log-index sort.

### 4. Integration test: per-tx fixture corpus → asserted chunk-write sequence
1 tx → multiple `Operation`s → multiple `AaveChunkEvent`s → the `AaveChunkWriteReport`. The end-to-end exercise of the plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1).

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged)

ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Every apply writes through `_on_conn` on the caller's tx. On `Err`, whole-chunk revert. The `process_transaction` fn takes a `&Connection` (the chunk's tx) — the caller (orchestrator) owns the tx lifecycle.

## Architectural calls I own (escalate, don't guess)

- **The plumbing-equivalence caveat (Finding 1) on edge branches:** if the integration test reveals a divergence between SCALEAPPLY's `ScaledTokenProcessor::process_*` (taking `ScaledTokenEventData`) and the Python enrichment's `calculate(raw_amount, index)` on the WITHDRAW/REPAY_WITH_ATOKENS/GHO_LIQUIDATION edge branches, escalate — do NOT paper over it. The right fix may be a thin `ScaledTokenProcessor::calculate(raw_amount, index, event_type)` bridge fn mirroring `ScaledAmountCalculator.calculate`, OR confirming the existing surface is plumbing-equivalent. U5YIBG (§4.2) is the final arbiter.
- **The stkAAVE-transfer-before-LiquidationCall ordering:** if the log-index sort + the discount-lookup ordering is subtle, flag.
- **The `PoolUpdated` mid-tx revision mutation:** the parser reads revision once at parse-start (A's design). If a `PoolUpdated` config event appears mid-tx, the revision mutation is the orchestrator's (6SWY4R) concern — C's `process_transaction` does NOT re-read the revision mid-tx. If the integration test reveals a mid-tx-revision case, escalate (the right fix is orchestrator-side, not parser-side).

## Validation gates (paste tail in callback)

- `just test-rust` (new integration test + all prior tests still green — A's parser-core + B's liquidation engine must remain green)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact)
- `just lint-rust` (clippy --deny warnings)
- `just format`

## Not touched (per non-goals)

- The parser-core + standard builders → HQF5NQ (A).
- The liquidation engine → HQF5NQ-B.
- The orchestrator (`run_aave_update`) → 6SWY4R (this task's `process_transaction` is the entry point 6SWY4R calls, but 6SWY4R owns the chunk loop + the RPC fetch + the event filtering).
- Python cutover → AVS4DR.
- §4.2 parity → U5YIBG (the §4.2 cross-check is the final arbiter for the plumbing-equivalence caveat).
- Python `transaction_processor.py` — unchanged (AVS4DR deletes).

## Operating rules

1. You own implementation; I own sequencing/state/architectural calls.
2. **No `git commit` without my explicit authorization.** Make changes; run gates; report DONE/BLOCKED. (Leave `.ergo/plan-alloyprovider-refactor.md` untracked.)
3. Report via `link_send` to me (t-d479) with `triggerTurn:true`. Include diff summary, gate results, open questions, flagged decisions.
4. Root AGENTS.md is the canonical ref.

data.title: Cascade: degenbot-bot + degenbot-python + standalone consumer
data.body:
## Goal
- Update every callsite that constructs `RegisterV2PoolParams`,
  `RegisterAerodromeV2PoolParams`, `V2BlockDelta`, or reads
  `.reserve{0,1}` from a `V2PoolState` / `AerodromeV2PoolState`, across
  `degenbot-bot` (production + ~50 test callsites — see MSTAT2 for the
  precedent of how the `-> Result` cascade was sized), `degenbot-python`
  (PyO3 getters), and `degenbot/examples/standalone_consumer.rs`.

## Context
- Same mechanical ripple as task `MSTAT2` (the
  `register_v2_pool -> Result` cascade). Inventory the sites with:
  `rg 'reserve[01]' rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src rust/crates/degenbot-python/src rust/crates/degenbot/examples`.
- Two classes of change:
  1. **Struct-literal construction sites** with `reserve0: U256::from(N)`
     → `reserve0: U112::from(N)` (or `uint!(N_U112)` for compile-time
     check, preferred where `N` is a literal). The
     `register_v2_pool(&RegisterV2PoolParams { reserve0: U256::from(1000), … })`
     test-helper form goes through this.
  2. **Read sites** that feed `state.reserve0` (now `U112`) to a `U256`
     API: PyO3 getters like `reserve0(&self) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>>`
     return `U256` to Python (Python keeps `int`); they now do
     `s.reserve0.to::<U256>()`. Sites feeding `reserve0` to
     `IntHopState::new` already need `.to::<U256>()` after task 1; if
     task 1 already landed those, this task picks up the stragglers
     outside `degenbot-pools` (in particular the
     `solver_dispatch.rs:522,667` and `diagnostic.rs:172` sites).
- The PyO3 getters in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/pool.rs` at
  `reserve0`/`reserve1`/`aerodrome_reserve0`/`aerodrome_reserve1` and
  the `snapshot` helpers go through class 2.
- `standalone_consumer.rs` constructs a `RegisterV2PoolParams` — class 1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` green (no type-mismatch
  errors at struct-literal sites; no `U112` values flowing to `U256`
  APIs without an explicit `.to::<U256>()`).
- No `U256` → `U112` *downcast* is silently truncating anywhere in
  the cascade — every such conversion is via the spec-bound validator
  or `.try_to::<U112>()` with a typed error (audit: there should be
  *none* of these in production paths — V2 state only flows from
  `SyncEvent` → `V2BlockDelta`/`V2PoolState`, all `U112` after tasks
  1 + 3).
- PyO3 `reserve0`/`reserve1`/`aerodrome_reserve{0,1}` getters still
  return Python `int` (the conversion `.to::<U256>()` happens in the
  getter body before `Py<PyAny>` materialization; no `.pyi` change).
- Test-helper `register_v2_pool(&RegisterV2PoolParams { reserve0: U256::from(N), … })`
  sites now read `U112::from(N)` (or `uint!(N_U112)`); the
  `.expect("test setup: V2 registration")` cascade from MSTAT2 is
  untouched.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot -p degenbot-python --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-bot -p degenbot-python --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt -p degenbot-bot -p degenbot-python --check`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (PyO3 stays out of cores).
- `cargo build -p degenbot` (standalone consumer builds).

## Context
