data.title: Collapse DB-snapshot loading into core + auto-backfill on start
Scope: Transaction submission
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Transaction submission → Rust core** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **Transaction submission → Rust core**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Transaction submission → Rust core** migration so
  subsequent child tasks decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python`
  dispositions per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1 criteria / §2.2 dispositions /
  §2.3 smells / §3 cutover discipline / §4 red-green parity + retirement).

## Context (responsibility boundary)
- The **Transaction submission** responsibility = everything between "profitable
  `tx_params` ready" (output of the Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `YL2MTH`) and "signed raw tx
  broadcast + confirmation/receipt handled". It: claims a nonce (source-of-truth from
  `eth_getTransactionCount`), finalizes EIP-1559 fee fields (`maxFeePerGas` /
  `maxPriorityFeePerGas` — the priority fee is CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`/`_compute_priority_fee`,
  REFERENCE not hard-edge), re-computes the EIP-2930 access list with the updated
  nonce/fees, signs the typed-2 transaction locally (`eth_account.sign_transaction`),
  broadcasts via `eth_sendRawTransaction`, and monitors the pending tx until confirmation
  or expiry (`get_transaction_receipt` polled; nonce voided + pools released on expiry).
- Today this lives ENTIRELY in Python: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
  (`dispatch_profitable_results`'s submit block L2608–L2660, `monitor_pending_transaction`
  L1624–L1652, `SubmittedTx` L1617, `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination L579–L678,
  `_apply_block_if_ready` block-clock + `feeHistory` + `next_base_fee` orchestration
  L2801–L2857, the `main()` start-phase `operator_nonce` + `base_fee_next` fetches
  L2884/L2920–L2921) + `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` + `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py`
  (`next_base_fee` L17–L73, the EIP-1559 base-fee formula). The Rust `degenbot-rpc` crate
  owns the transport primitives (`get_transaction_count` L776, `estimate_gas` L615,
  `get_transaction` L654, `get_transaction_receipt` L688, the untyped `make_request`
  L809), but ZERO signing / `TxEnvelope` construction / private-key handling / nonce
  coordination / tx-confirmation lifecycle exists in any Rust crate.
- Canonical reading order applied: `AGENTS.md` (Architectural Vision → "the transaction
  submission" is on the migration path; "Rust is the engine, Python is the cockpit") →
  `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1/§2.2 → `docs/adr/ADR-005`
  (standalone-core + zero-`pyo3`-in-cores) → `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §17
  (known-limitation: "transaction submission — today Python via `examples/`; on the
  migration path").
- Baseline gate: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (untouched by scoping).
- **Crate placement (recommended):** a new core crate `degenbot-submission` (pyo3-free;
  deps `alloy` + `degenbot-rpc` + `degenbot-core` + `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-executor`
  for the `execute()` calldata EIP-2718 typing), PyO3 wrappers in
  `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/submission/`. Mirrors the `degenbot-executor`/
  `degenbot-simulation` precedent; keeps `degenbot-bot` I/O-free per ADR-001 / ADR-003.
  Signing uses `alloy-signer-local` (the `LocalSigner` carrying the operator private key)
  — confirmed no signing code exists in `degenbot-rpc` today (`rg signer` empty); the
  signer lives in the new submission crate. **Confirm with `t-6486`** (consistent with
  the WWC4DL/`5LLJHX` crate decisions).

## Scope table

### COMPLETED — Rust-owned (do NOT redo)

| # | Row | Rust source | Python consumer | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|-------------|-----------------|-------------|-----------|
| C1 | `AlloyProvider::get_transaction_count` (nonce source-of-truth via `eth_getTransactionCount`, pending/latest selectable) | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L776–L806 | python `main()` L2884 `async_w3.eth.get_transaction_count` | `done` | Typed nonce RPC leaf exists with retry/backoff; the submission leaf CONSUMES it. |
| C2 | `AlloyProvider::estimate_gas` + `eth_call` + `get_block` + `get_balance`/`get_code`/`get_storage_at` | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L570–L750, L491 | python dispatch (gas/fee/access list pre-call) | `done` | Transport-primitive precedent; the typed `eth_sendRawTransaction`/`eth_feeHistory` are `ZUZANP` (see I1/I3). |
| C3 | Typed RPC leaves + the untyped `make_request` escape hatch (`method + serde_json::Value → Value`, retry/backoff) | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L809–L829 | the broadcast + receipt-poll callsites route here (interim-untyped for sendRaw) | `done` (leaf exists) | The untyped escape hatch the submission broadcast (I2/I3) routes through UNTIL `ZUZANP` types `eth_sendRawTransaction`. Retry/backoff already owned in Rust. |
| C4 | Profitable `tx_params` (to/`execute()` calldata/type=2/gas accessList placeholders; `priority_fee`+`gas_used`+`net_profit` from the sim) | produced by Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `YL2MTH` (`simulate_one` returns `tx_params`) | consumed at L2618 | `done` (reference) | The submission leaf's INPUT is already Rust-owned; per orchestrator ruling, REFERENCE `YL2MTH`'s fee — CONSUME `tx_params`, NO hard-edge. |
| C5 | The EIP-2930 access list computed during simulation (re-computed post-nonce/fee update via the B-leaf `eth_createAccessList`) | Simulation `PGA5S3` + RPC `ZUZANP` | python L2627–L2630 re-computes | `done` (reference) | CONSUMED from `PGA5S3`/`ZUZANP`; the re-computation is the same leaf called twice. Reference, do not re-scope. |

### IN-FIGHT — partially routed; Python still the authority for some callsites

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|-------------|------------------|
| I1 | `eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast | python L2636–L2640 (`async_w3.eth.send_raw_transaction(...)`) | `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::make_request("eth_sendRawTransaction", …)` (untyped, EXISTS); typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` (`bytes → TxHash`) = `ZUZANP` (NOT-STARTED, cross-epic D3DIPE) | `partial` | The untyped escape hatch EXISTS — broadcast CAN route through Rust today untyped; the TYPED request/response is `ZUZANP` (carves out "Signing — SHT6GE"; owns only the byte-broadcast `bytes → TxHash`). Cross-epic dep; interim-untyped fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (per orchestrator ruling Q1). |
| I2 | `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch (feeds `_compute_priority_fee` + `Dispatcher.record_priority_fees`) | python L2832–L2841 (`async_w3.eth.fee_history`) | `make_request("eth_feeHistory", …)` untyped EXISTS; typed = `ZUZANP` | `partial` | Same shape as I1 — untyped available; typed consumer `ZUZANP`. The percentile extraction + the `Dispatcher` dict shape is pure (rows N1/N3). Cross-epic dep. |
| I3 | `eth_getTransactionReceipt` poll (tx confirmation) | python L1639 (`async_w3.eth.get_transaction_receipt(tx.tx_hash)`) | `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::get_transaction_receipt` L688 (TYPED, EXISTS — returns `serde_json::Value`) | `done`-leaning→`partial` | The typed receipt leaf EXISTS (`get_transaction_receipt` L688). It returns `serde_json::Value` not a typed receipt struct, so the CONFIRMATION-status decode (status field) is the partial surface. The poll loop itself is N2/port-now. |

### NOT STARTED — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|-------------|------------------|
| N1 | `next_base_fee` (pure EIP-1559 base-fee formula from `parent_base_fee`/`gas_used`/`gas_limit` + `elasticity_multiplier`/`base_fee_max_change_denominator`/`min_base_fee`) | `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` L17–L73; called L2825/L2920 | none | `port-now` | Pure integer EVM math; hot per-block; no I/O; no float; property-testable (round-trip, target-bound, min clamp). Standalone-Rust-usable — belongs in a new `degenbot-evm-math` core crate (the `next_base_fee` precedent mirrors `cl_msb`/`cl_lsb` already in `degenbot-core/src/`). The `min_base_fee` arg supports non-Ethereum EIP-1559 chains (linea). **Cross-epic:** consumed by both Submission (fee finalization) AND Simulation (`base_fee_next` for net-profit). |
| N2 | `SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` async confirmation loop (poll receipt each second; on confirmed → release nonce+pools; on `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` blocks without inclusion → void nonce, release pools; `dispatcher.current_block` read-by-reference) | python L1617–L1652 | none | `port-now` | Pure lifecycle state machine over `get_transaction_receipt` (I3) + `dispatcher.current_block` + `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES`; the §2.1 "GIL?" win is modest (1s sleep poll) but the lifecycle/control-flow belongs in Rust alongside the nonce owner. Property-testable (confirm/expiry transitions). |
| N3 | `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination (`claim_nonce`/`release_nonce`/`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/`is_path_blocked`/`track_task` + `active_tasks` auto-discard; `pending_nonces: HashSet`; `pending_pools: HashSet`; `current_block_ref` by-ref read; `record_block_time`/`record_priority_fees`/`latest_priority_fees` ring-buffer prune) | python L579–L678 | none | `port-now` | Pure coordination state (`HashMap`/`HashSet` + a single-element `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` for the by-ref block clock); hot per-tx; GIL-held today across claim/release; property-testable (nonce dedup, pool mutual exclusion, ring prune). The `active_tasks:auto-discard` is a Python-asyncio shape that maps to a tokio `JoinSet`. |
| N4 | EIP-1559 transaction signing (`eth_account.Account.sign_transaction(transaction_dict, private_key) → raw_transaction bytes`; local ECDSA secp256k1 signing; type-2 EIP-1559 fields: `maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas`/`chainId`/`accessList`/`nonce`/`gas`/`to`/`value`/`data`) | python L2637–L2640 | none (signing explicitly carved out of `ZUZANP` — "Signing — Transaction-submission epic (SHT6GE)") | `port-now` | Hot per-tx; private-key handling must NEVER live in Python (security: the key currently crosses into `eth_account` per-tx). `alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owns the key once; `TxEnvelope` + `Typed2718` encoding is pure; property-testable (signed-tx round-trip decode via alloy). The §2.1 "I/O shape?" is crypto (no network) + "type shape" is bytes. This is the canonical SHT6GE leaf. |
| N5 | EIP-1559 fee finalization (`maxFeePerGas = int(1.5 * base_fee_next) + priority_fee`; `maxPriorityFeePerGas = priority_fee` from `YL2MTH`; the `1.5x` base-fee headroom factor) | python L2623–L2625 | none | `port-now` | Pure integer fee arithmetic over `base_fee_next` (N1) + `priority_fee` (CONSUMED from `YL2MTH` — REFERENCE); the `1.5x` float→int headroom preserves the same float→int truncate convention as `_compute_priority_fee` (document the float boundary). Small — folds with N4/N6. |
| N6 | `dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration (sort by engine profit descending; mutual-exclusivity check `is_path_blocked` against pending+committed pools; `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` safety guard skips live submission; `dry_run` guard; DRY_RUN path logs-only; claim nonce → finalize fees → re-compute access list (C5) → sign (N4) → broadcast (I1) → reserve pools → spawn monitor (N2)) | python `dispatch_profitable_results` submit tail L2608–L2660 | none | `port-now` | Pure orchestration over leaves N3/N4/N5/C5/I1 + `dry_run` config branch; the §2.1 "GIL?" win is owning the sign+broadcast slice in Rust (releases the GIL across the async broadcast). The sort + mutual-exclusivity is pure. |

### `stays-python` — display/config/IO-shell (NOT a child)

| # | Row | Python source | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------|-----------|
| S1 | `main()` start-phase fetches (`operator_nonce` via `get_transaction_count`; initial `base_fee_next` via `next_base_fee` over the latest block); `DegenbotConfig`/`operator_private_key` config load; `dotenv_values("examples/mainmain.env")` | `stays-python` | Config bootstrap + secret loading (per "Python is the cockpit" + §2.1 "I/O shape": the private key is loaded by the Python driver and handed to the Rust signer ONCE). No per-tx logic. |
| S2 | `[submit]`/`[dispatch]` logging (submit hash, nonce, skip reasons, voided-nonce, confirmed-tx) | `stays-python` | Display/orchestration; infrequent (per-submit); Python-ecosystem (logging). The lifecycle RESULTS surface as typed structs the Python companion renders. |
| S3 | `DRY_RUN` / `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` safety-guard policy (the live-submission skip + the reason log) | `stays-python` (config policy) | Policy gates read from env/config; the GATE check is a thin Python branch over a bool. The submission leaf exposes `dry_run`/`inject_code` as args (pure bool config); the POLICY stays Python. |

## Child-task split (port-now / partial rows → implementation tasks)

- **N1** → child: *`next_base_fee` EIP-1559 base-fee math (core leaf — new `degenbot-evm-math` crate OR `degenbot-core`)*. CONSUMED by Submission (N5/N6) AND Simulation (`base_fee_next` net-profit). Notes a cross-epic REFERENCE for `5LLJHX` (simulation also reads `base_fee_next`); the orchestrator ruled reference-not-hard-edge for fees, so N1 is owned here and Simulation references it.
- **N3** → child: *`Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination state (nonce claim/release, pool mutual exclusion, `active_tasks` JoinSet, `current_block_ref` by-ref clock, `block_priority_fees` ring prune)*.
- **N4 + N5** → child: *EIP-1559 transaction signing + fee finalization (`alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owning the operator key; `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` encoding; `maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas` with the 1.5x base-fee headroom, priority fee CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`)*. Carves out the key-handling seam (security).
- **N2** → child: *`SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` confirmation/expiry lifecycle (receipt poll, `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` void, nonce+pool release on confirm/expire)*. Depends on N3 + I3 (`get_transaction_receipt`).
- **N6 + I1 + I2** → child: *`dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration + `eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast + `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch (typed consumer of `ZUZANP`; interim untyped `make_request` fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked)*. Depends on N3/N4/N5/N2 + `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE, hard edge per Q1 ruling) + `PGA5S3`/`YL2MTH` (REFERENCE, no hard edge).

`stays-python` rows (S1 config/secret bootstrap, S2 submit logging, S3 dry-run/inject policy gates) — NO child; flagged so the next sweep does not re-litigate. Reference rows (C1–C5) — provided by `degenbot-rpc` / Simulation `YL2MTH`/`PGA5S3` / `ZUZANP`; consumed not re-scoped.

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **`ZUZANP` (RPC epic D3DIPE) is the critical path for the N6 submit-orchestration child** (typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` + typed `eth_feeHistory`). Per orchestrator ruling Q1: KEEP hard `ZUZANP`→N6-child edge; interim-untyped `make_request` (L809) fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (§4.2 wait-for-typed default). Cross-epic child edge: N6-child → `ZUZANP`.
2. **`YL2MTH` fee — REFERENCE not hard-edge** (per orchestrator ruling Q2). The N4/N5 child CONSUMES `tx_params` (incl. the `priority_fee` computed in `YL2MTH`); Submission does NOT sequence-depend on the `YL2MTH` fee leaf. Wired as a reference, NO `ergo sequence` edge.
3. **`PGA5S3` access-list re-computation — REFERENCE.** The N6 child re-computes the access list via the same `eth_createAccessList` leaf the Simulation `PGA5S3` exposes; CONSUME, no hard edge.
4. **Crate placement: `degenbot-submission`?** Recommended new core crate (mirrors `degenbot-executor`/`degenbot-simulation`; keeps `degenbot-bot` I/O-free per ADR-001/ADR-003). Signing uses `alloy-signer-local` — confirmed NO signing code in `degenbot-rpc` today (`rg signer` empty in cores). **Confirm with `t-6486`** — consistent with the WWC4DL/`5LLJHX` crate decisions; alternatively fold into `degenbot-rpc` (but that bloats the transport crate with signer+nonce+confirmation lifecycle). `next_base_fee` (N1) recommended for a `degenbot-evm-math` core crate OR `degenbot-core` (it's pure EVM math, not submission-specific — consumed by Simulation too).
5. **Private-key security boundary.** The Python driver loads the operator key (S1 stays-python) and hands it to the Rust `LocalSigner` ONCE; the key MUST NOT live in Python per-tx. The N4 child owns the signer lifecycle; flag the key-handling seam in the cutover.
6. **`result` field cosmetic.** `ergo --json set ... '{"state":"done","result":"docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md"}'` shows `result: None` on round-trip (known gotcha). The body carries the result pointer; the tree view shows done.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose |
|----|-------|---------|
| `JTLWA3` | `next_base_fee` EIP-1559 base-fee math (core leaf) | Pure integer EIP-1559 formula (`degenbot-evm-math` OR `degenbot-core`); CONSUMED cross-epic by Simulation (`base_fee_next`). |
| `M756BN` | `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination | claim/release nonce, pool mutual exclusion, `active_tasks` JoinSet, `current_block` by-ref clock, `block_priority_fees` ring prune, delegates `PathSuppression` (REFERENCE `5FB5MW`). |
| `G6DNW4` | EIP-1559 signing + fee finalization | `alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owns operator key once; `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` type-2; `maxFeePerGas` 1.5x headroom; `priority_fee` CONSUMED from `YL2MTH` (reference, no hard edge). |
| `HF2R2E` | `SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` | Pending-tx confirmation/expiry lifecycle (receipt poll, `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` void, nonce+pool release on confirm/expire). |
| `PLDP23` | `dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration + `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory` | Sort + mutual-exclusivity + `dry_run`/`inject_code` guards → claim nonce → finalize fees → re-compute access list → sign → broadcast → reserve pools → spawn monitor. Hard-edge on `ZUZANP`. |

`stays-python` rows (no child): S1 (`main()` nonce/base-fee start fetches + config/secret
bootstrap), S2 (submit/dispatch logging), S3 (`dry_run`/`INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` policy
gates — the leaf takes bool args; the POLICY stays Python). Reference rows (C1–C5):
`get_transaction_count`/`estimate_gas`/`get_transaction_receipt`/`make_request` in
`degenbot-rpc`; `tx_params`+`priority_fee` from Simulation `YL2MTH`; access-list re-compute
from Simulation `PGA5S3`; typed `eth_sendRawTransaction`/`eth_feeHistory` from `ZUZANP`
(hard edge to `PLDP23`).

## Dependency edges (ergo `sequence`)

```
CROSS-EPIC (D3DIPE → SHT6GE):   ZUZANP (typed sendRaw + feeHistory) ──► PLDP23 (N6)
                                  (HARD edge per Q1; interim make_request fallback ONLY if blocked)

CROSS-EPIC (REFERENCE, no edge): YL2MTH (Simulation, tx_params + priority_fee) ── consumed by G6DNW4
                                 PGA5S3 (Simulation, eth_createAccessList)        ── consumed by PLDP23
                                 5FB5MW (Simulation, PathSuppression)             ── composed into M756BN
                                 JTLWA3 (next_base_fee, base_fee_next)            ── consumed cross-epic

INTRA-EPIC (SHT6GE):             M756BN (Dispatcher) ──► HF2R2E (monitor)
                                 M756BN ──► PLDP23 (N6)
                                 G6DNW4 (sign+fee) ──► PLDP23
                                 HF2R2E (monitor) ──► PLDP23
```
`PLDP23` (N6, submit orchestration) gates on `M756BN` + `G6DNW4` + `HF2R2E` + `ZUZANP`
(hard); `HF2R2E` (monitor) gates on `M756BN` (Dispatcher); `JTLWA3` (next_base_fee) is
standalone (pure EVM math; consumed cross-epic by Simulation's `base_fee_next`; referenced
by `G6DNW4`/`PLDP23` for the 1.5x headroom — no hard intra-epic edge, the leaf is called as
a pure fn). `G6DNW4`'s `priority_fee` is consumed off `tx_params` (no hard edge to
`YL2MTH`).

data.title: Route dispatch hot loop off raw AsyncWeb3 onto Rust AsyncAlloyProvider
data.body:
## Goal
- Route the backrun dispatch hot loop off the raw `AsyncWeb3` / `AsyncHTTPProvider`
  bypass onto the existing Rust `AsyncAlloyProvider` / `AsyncProviderAdapter` core,
  so every dispatch-side `eth_*` call the hot loop makes goes through Rust
  (releasing the GIL) instead of `web3.py`.

## Context
- Scoping task `USJM4X` established that the **pump-side** RPC is already
  Rust-owned, but the **dispatch-side** is driven through a raw `AsyncWeb3`
  constructed directly in `BackrunSession._build_async_w3`
  (`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py:1039`), deliberately bypassing the
  existing `AsyncProviderAdapter.from_alloy` / `_AsyncAlloyAdapter` wrappers.
- The Rust wrappers for every call listed below ALREADY EXIST; this task is
  **routing only** (the rubric `partial` → `done` cutover), not new Rust code.
- This is the untyped cutover: the four NOT-STARTED calls (`eth_simulateV1`,
  `eth_feeHistory`, `eth_createAccessList`, `eth_sendRawTransaction`) route via
  the existing `make_request(method, params)` raw-RPC escape hatch on
  `AsyncAlloyProvider` — typed surfaces land in `Z9K2MD`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `BackrunSession._build_async_w3` returns an `AsyncProviderAdapter` (or
  `AsyncAlloyProvider`) — no `AsyncWeb3(AsyncHTTPProvider(...))` in the dispatch
  path. The `web3.AsyncWeb3` import is removed from the dispatch path (kept only
  where strictly needed for type hints/helpers documented in the task).
- All six IN-FIGHT callsites routed through Rust:
  1. `BackrunSession.start`: `eth_getBlock("latest")` → Rust `get_block`
  2. `_apply_result_if_ready`: `eth_getTransactionCount` → Rust `get_transaction_count`
  3. `_apply_block_if_ready`: `eth_feeHistory` → ` AsyncAlloyProvider.make_request("eth_feeHistory", …)`
  4. `simulate_one`: `eth_createAccessList` (×2) → `make_request("eth_createAccessList", …)`
  5. `simulate_one`: `eth_call` (slot0/liquidity/getReserves, ×3) → Rust `call`
  6. `monitor_pending_transaction`: `eth_getTransactionReceipt` → Rust `get_transaction_receipt`
  7. `simulate_one`: `eth_simulateV1` → `make_request("eth_simulateV1", …)`
  8. `dispatch_profitable_results`: `eth_sendRawTransaction` → `make_request("eth_sendRawTransaction", …)`
  9. `simulate_one` state-trace: `eth_getCode` → Rust `get_code`
- Behaviour parity: the example's dry-run produces identical `[block:]`, `[sim]`
  and `[profit]` log output on a fixture block (compare before/after).
- No `web3.py`-specific return shapes leak (e.g. `AttributeDict` access must be
  migrated to the plain dict shapes returned by `_AsyncAlloyAdapter`).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust-python` (the PyO3-wrapped tests)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- Example dry-run on an anvil/mainnet fixture: `python examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
  (dry-run, `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE=1`) produces parity logs vs pre-task.
- `rg 'AsyncWeb3|async_w3' examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` shows no
  direct `AsyncHTTPProvider` construction in the dispatch path.

## Non-goals
- Typing the four `make_request` calls — that is `Z9K2MD`.
- Signing logic / fee strategy — Transaction-submission epic (`SHT6GE`).
- Calldata construction (`keccak`/`eth_abi.encode`) — Swap-encoding epic (`WWC4DL`).

data.title: AlloyProvider reliability & API hygiene
Goal
data.body:
## Body
`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` + `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`. **Thin wrapper only — no business logic** (ADR-005):
- `#[pyfunction] fn db_heal_database(database_path: &str) -> PyResult<PyObject>`
- Extract `database_path: &str`, `py.allow_threads(|| heal_database(path))` (GIL released across the copy — it's the slow part), wrap `HealReport` as a `PyObject` dict `{old_state: str, rows_copied: dict[str,int], bak_path: str, new_state: str}`.
- `SchemaState` → label string (`alembic_current`/`alembic_stale`/`rust_owned`); `DbError` → Python exception (`DatabaseSchemaStale`/`UnrecognizedSchema` via the existing `db_err_to_py` helper).

Mirror the existing seam style in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/mod.rs` (e.g. `db_convert_alembic_to_rust_owned` from `1b66da1f`).

Add to `__all__` in the `.pyi`.

## Test
Round-trip via the seam mirrors the core `head_to_heal` test: build head DB, write an exchange row via `db_upsert_exchange`, call `db_heal_database`, assert the returned dict's `new_state == "rust_owned"`, `bak_path` exists, `rows_copied["exchanges"] == 1`, and the exchange row still reads back via `db_fetch_exchange_by_name`.

## Depends on
T2.

data.title: Scope: Dead Python state mirrors cleanup
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Dead Python state mirrors cleanup** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **Dead Python state mirrors cleanup**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

## Goal
- The capstone: identify **every Python state mirror that duplicates Rust-owned state**,
  triage into THREE buckets per the orchestrator's framing
  (NOW-DELETABLE / DEAD-AFTER-X-SHIPS / STAYS-PYTHON), and produce a cleanup inventory +
  cleanup child tasks wired to the pending impl child each is gated on. This Closes the
  research phase.

## Context (how the map was built)
- Read all 10 done scope tables + the pre-existing already-Rust-owned layer
  (transition-guide §6): `USJM4X`/D3DIPE (RPC) · `E7GB27`/WWC4DL (Swap encoding) ·
  `4JGPDW`/5LLJHX (Simulation) · `MPS3U7`/AZGJUN (DB-aware updaters) · `5DU4QI`/VGTEDL
  (DB persistence) · `JHK2YN`/JW7KU6 (Pathfinding) · `P7AMWR`/SHT6GE (Submission) ·
  `EB5M6V`/M6QUG6 (Deferred DEX math) · `I7KVKM`/2K2JP4 (Publisher/subscriber) ·
  `XS57NO`/VNNYI6 (Price oracles).
- Pre-existing layer (§6): `BotState`/`PyBot`/`PyLiquidityPool` / `PyErc20Token`,
  V2/V3/V4/Curve/Balancer/Solidly pool STATE + calc delegation, `UniswapArbEngine` solve,
  event decoders, reorg journal, Fork A (ClassVars + `_verified_address` retired),
  Fork B (Solidly solve → engine), slice-14 `PyBotIo` (Rust choreography landed).
- Canonical reading order applied: AGENTS.md "do not introduce a Python mirror of Rust-owned
  state" + "immutable config dual-tracking" sanction → transition-guide §6 (pre-existing
  layer) + §2.3 (duplication smell) + §4.3 (oracle-retirement protocol) → ADR-005.
- Baseline gate: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (untouched by scoping).

## Scope table

### COMPLETED — mirrors that WERE dead but are ALREADY retired (do NOT redo)

| # | Row | Where it was retired | Pointer |
|---|-----|----------------------|---------|
| C1 | Python `ClassVar`s (factory/init_hash) + `_verified_address` — duplicated `degenbot-uniswap::deployments` + the Rust builder's CREATE2-verified identity | Fork A (slice `P62DKO`/`NSAZ4X`/`JC6OFG`, **landed**) — "ClassVars + `_verified_address` retired; the Python companions read the verified identity off the handle; no Python mirror remains." | transition-guide §6 Fork A |
| C2 | Python pool STATE (reserves / slot0 / liquidity maps) on V2/V3/V4/Curve/Balancer pools — duplicated Rust `BotState` | Combo-guide §6: `state` is now a PROPERTY that builds a transient `PoolState` value from one atomic `_py_pool.snapshot()` call each read; writes go to `_py_pool.sync_reserves(...)` (Rust). Verified: `UniswapV2Pool.state` (`v2_liquidity_pool.py:254`), `external_update` → `sync_reserves`. **No Python-held pool-state copy remains.** | `src/degenbot/uniswap/v2_liquidity_pool.py:254,294`; pool classes |
| C3 | Solidly stable solve (`SolidlyStableSolver`) — duplicated Rust `solve_solidly_path_int` | This is the `EB5M6V`/`M6QUG6` epic's cleanup child `3VGIDY` (parity-oracle-only, production confirmed Rust). NOT re-scoped here — cross-reference. | Epic `M6QUG6`, child `3VGIDY` (handling in parallel). |
| C4 | Python swap-encode `enc_*` opcode set + command-stream builders — duplicated the (port-now) Rust encoder | My `E7GB27`/WWC4DL scope's cutover child `YQORTM` ("PyO3 + cutover + retire Python encoder §4.3") already retires the Python encoder. Cross-reference — not re-scoped. | Epic `WWC4DL`, child `YQORTM`. |

### NOT-STARTED — dead-after-X Python state mirrors NOT already scoped into a cutover child

(Rubric §4.3: after the Rust cutover lands + parity is green, the Python mirror retires.
For each, the Rust cutover child ports the Rust-owned struct; the Python COPY becomes
orphaned state — a residual dead-mirror NOT named in that child's AC. A *cleanup* child,
gated on the final consuming cutover, deletes the Python copy.)

| # | Row | Python source (the mirror) | Rust counterpart (lands via) | Final cutover child (gate) | Notes |
|---|-----|----------------------------|------------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
| D1 | **Example `Dispatcher` state mirror** — the Python `Dispatcher` in `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py:579–678` HOLDS `pending_nonces: HashSet` / `pending_pools: HashSet` / `active_tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` / `current_block_ref: list[int]` (by-ref clock) / `block_times: deque` / `block_priority_fees: dict` — duplicates the Rust `Dispatcher` struct (lands via `M756BN`/SHT6GE, AC ports the Rust struct but does NOT retire the Python copy). | `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `Dispatcher` L579–678 + `PathSuppression` L509–578 + the example's `dispatch_profitable_results` / `monitor_pending_transaction` / `_apply_block_if_ready` (`SubmittedTx` L1617) bodies | Rust `Dispatcher` (`M756BN`, Subm. epic SHT6GE) + Rust `PathSuppression` (`5FB5MW`, Sim epic 5LLJHX) + Rust `monitor` (`HF2R2E`) + Rust sign+fee (`G6DNW4`) → final cutover `PLDP23` ports the example's `dispatch_profitable_results` submit-tail + broadcast through Rust | **`PLDP23`** (final cutover; transitively gates on `M756BN`+`HF2R2E`+`G6DNW4`+`5FB5MW`+`ZUZANP`) | The Python `Dispatcher` is the canonical hot-loop coordinator in the example — a true state mirror once Rust owns the struct. `PLDP23` makes the example route submit/broadcast through the Rust `Dispatcher`; once all of the Python `Dispatcher`'s callsites are ported, the class + its held `pending_nonces`/`pending_pools`/`block_priority_fees` state is orphaned. ALSO folds the `PathSuppression` mirror (`fail_count`/`suppressed` maps) — co-located in the same example module + co-retired once the Rust `Dispatcher` composes the Rust `PathSuppression` (`5FB5MW`) + the example's fan-out (also `5FB5MW`) routes through it. |
| D2 | **`concentrated_liquidity.py` + `tick_bitmap.py` pure-math Python copies** — `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` + `flip_tick` + `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` duplicate the Rust tick-bitmap/liquidity-mapping math (lands via `S5YS7U`/AZGJUN, AC ports to `degenbot-cl-math` + DOES NOT retire the Python copies); the DB-aware updater headroom (`QJSCA5`/AZGJUN) ports the writer to Rust + DOES NOT delete the Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update`. Plus the V3 companion (`v3_liquidity_pool.py:574`) still calls the Python `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` — a residual callsite the cleanup routes through `degenbot-cl-math` before deleting. | `src/degenbot/calculations/concentrated_liquidity.py`; `src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_libraries/tick_bitmap.py`; the V3-companion callsite `v3_liquidity_pool.py:574` | `S5YS7U` (Rust math in `degenbot-cl-math`) + `QJSCA5` (DB updater stops calling the Python math) → final cutover is `QJSCA5` (transitively `S5YS7U`) | The cleanup (1) routes the `v3_liquidity_pool` companion's `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` call through the `degenbot-cl-math` PyO3 seam (the micro-cutover), (2) deletes/shells the pure-Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update`/`flip_tick`/`get_tick_word_and_bit_position` once parity-green. MCP §2.3 dup between Python + `degenbot-bot::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` (hot path) is also collapsed by `S5YS7U` (a RUST↔RUST dedup — the hot-path `n.rs` refactoring is a separate non-blocking Rust-internal follow-up, see MPS3U7 open Q3; flagged, NOT a Python mirror). |

### IN-FIGHT — mirrors whose retirement IS ALREADY in a pending cutover child's AC (cross-reference, NO new child)

| # | Row | Already retired by | Pointer |
|---|-----|--------------------|---------|
| I1 | Python `PublisherMixin` mechanism (`Publisher`/`Subscriber` Plugins + `_notify_subscribers`/`subscribe`/`unsubscribe` over a `WeakSet` + `PoolStateMessage`/`...PoolStateUpdated`) on V2/V3/V4/Aerodrome/Balancer/Curve pools — duplicates Rust `LogDispatcher`/`PoolStateSubscriber`. The pool classes' `self._subscribers: WeakSet` (the subscriber registry) is the state mirror. | `I7KVKM`/2K2JP4 child **`ZBD4MS`** AC verbatim: "Publisher/PublisherMixin... become thin delegating shells OR are retired... `_notify_subscribers` bodies deleted... Keep the Python path as oracle until green, then retire per §4.3." Cross-referenced — no capstone cleanup child (would double-track). | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py`; `ZBD4MS`; consumer cutover `73UJL6` |

### STAYS-PYTHON — legitimately retained (NOT dead mirrors; the intended boundary)

| # | Row | Why it stays | Reference |
|---|-----|--------------|-----------|
| S1 | `PyBot` / `PyLiquidityPool` / `PyErc20Token` — the `#[pyclass]` PyO3 shells | The intended boundary (orchestrator's "critical distinction"): a delegating shell is NOT a dead mirror. | transition-guide §6 |
| S2 | Immutable config cache on Python pool classes (`self._fee` / `_tick_spacing` / `_token0` / `_token1` / `address` / `factory` / `fee_denominator` / `stable_swap` / `deployer` / `init_hash`) | AGENTS.md explicit sanction: "immutable config dual-tracking, `Fraction`-based display." Not mutable state, not a mirror. | `v3_liquidity_pool.py:224–225`; AGENTS.md |
| S3 | Python `self.state` transient `PoolState` value object (built from one atomic `_py_pool.snapshot()` per call) | A delegating reader, not a stored copy — re-snapshots Rust each read (verified). | `v2_liquidity_pool.py:254,289–291` |
| S4 | `Erc20Token._price_oracle` (`PyChainlinkPriceFeed` reference) | XS57NO decision verbatim: "the per-token oracle stays a Python-held `PyChainlinkPriceFeed` reference (the Rust core owns the *reader*, the token holds the handle)." Not a state mirror. | `XS57NO`/VNNYI6; `src/degenbot/erc20/erc20.py` |
| S5 | Python pub/sub **consumer** orchestration (`engine_registry`, CLI update hooks, `FakeSubscriber`) | XS57NO/I7KVKM: consumer *reaction* bodies stay Python (subscribe-call routed via `73UJL6`); not a state mirror. | `I7KVKM` child `73UJL6` |
| S6 | `SyncPoolIO` / `AsyncPoolIO` (Python encode→call→decode choreography adapters) | The Bot's production build-path uses `PyBotIo` (Rust, slice-14 done); `SyncPoolIO`/`AsyncPoolIO` remain as (a) the **parity gate** for the Rust choreography (the `hasattr(io, "fetch_factory_address"/"probe_pool_type")` fallback branch) AND (b) the test/offline-fork adapter. NOT a state-mirror — these are transport adapters. (See Open Q1 for whether SensorIO retirement should be its OWN parity-gate cleanup once a test-adapter migration lands — analogous to `3VGIDY` but with legit test consumers.) | `src/degenbot/builders/type_resolution.py`; `src/degenbot/builders/pool_io.py`; pool-builder `hasattr` fallbacks |
| S7 | Curve `get_dy` variant orchestration + `CurveDataProvider` I/O + Balancer `detect_pow_version`/vault-query orchestration | §3.4 stays-python; I/O + config orchestration owned by the RPC/persistence epics when those migrate; NOT DEX-math state. | `EB5M6V`/M6QUG6 stays-python S1/S2 |

## Child-task split (dead-after-X rows → cleanup children)

- **D1** → child: *Retire the example's Python state mirror — `Dispatcher` + `PathSuppression`
  + `SubmittedTx`/`monitor_pending_transaction`/`_apply_block_if_ready`/`dispatch_profitable_results`
  bodies — once `PLDP23` has routed the example's submit-tail through the Rust `Dispatcher`
  + Rust `monitor` (`HF2R2E`) + Rust fan-out (`5FB5MW`).* Gated `PLDP23 → <cleanup>`
  (transitively `M756BN`+`HF2R2E`+`G6DNW4`+`ZUZANP`+`5FB5MW`).
- **D2** → child: *Retire the pure-Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` / `flip_tick` /
  `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` (route the V3-companion callsite through `degenbot-cl-math`,
  then delete/shell the Python copies once parity-green).* Gated `QJSCA5 → <cleanup>`
  (transitively `S5YS7U`).

Cross-references (NO new child): I1 PublisherMixin (already in `ZBD4MS` AC); C1–C4
(ClassVars, pool state, Solidly oracle `3VGIDY`, encoder `YQORTM` — already handled).

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **`SyncPoolIO`/`AsyncPoolIO` retirement** — held as STAYS-PYTHON S6, but flagging: it IS a
   parallel implementation of the `PyBotIo` Rust choreography (slice-14 done). It survives as
   (a) parity gate + (b) offline/fork test adapter. Unlike `SolidlyStableSolver` (whose ONLY
   consumer was the parity test — deleted wholesale under `3VGIDY`), `SyncPoolIO` has legit
   test-adapter consumers, so retiring it needs a test-cutover (offline/fork tests migrate to
   a `PyBotIo`-shaped test adapter) BEFORE deletion. There is NO named impl child for this.
   **Q for `t-6486`:** schedule a `SyncPoolIO`/`AsyncPoolIO` retirement child (analogous to
   `3VGIDY`) gated on a test-adapter migration, OR leave it as a long-term parity surface?
   Recommend: leave the test adapters; retire ONLY the parity-gate role once the orchestrator
   deems `PyBotIo` parity sufficient (non-blocking).
2. **Rust↔Rust §2.3 dedup (NOT a Python mirror).** `S5YS7U` lands the shared liquidity-mapping
   fn in `degenbot-cl-math`; refactoring `degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/n.rs::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range`
   to CALL it (collapsing the hot-path dup with the cl-math fn) is a separate Rust-internal
   follow-up (MPS3U7 open Q3). Out of scope for this capstone (it's a Rust dedup, not a Python
   state mirror), but flagged so it's not lost.
3. **No cross-epic dead-after-X cleanup-children beyond D1/D2.** `PAGQCK`/`ZUZANP` (RPC)
   route transport callsites (not state); `YQORTM` (encoding) ALREADY retires the encoder
   (C4); the sim cutover children build transients (not state) except `PathSuppression` (D1);
   the DB-updater cutover children port writers (the pure-math dup is D2; the DB-row
   substrate read fns aren't Python state copies — they're `SLHSM4`'s job). So the dead-after
   family is bounded — exactly the "MANY dead-after-X, but bounded to the state-holding
   examples + the one pure-math dup" the orchestrator predicted.
4. **`result` field cosmetic** — `set ... '{"result":"docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md"}'`
   shows `None` on round-trip (known gotcha); body carries the pointer; tree shows done.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose | Gate |
|----|-------|---------|------|
| `7UIYJ6` | Dead-mirror retirement: example Python `Dispatcher` + `PathSuppression` state mirror | Delete the example's Python-held `pending_nonces`/`pending_pools`/`active_tasks`/`block_priority_fees` + `PathSuppression` `fail_count`/`suppressed` copies once `PLDP23` cutover routes the example through the Rust `Dispatcher`+`monitor`(`HF2R2E`)+fan-out(`5FB5FW`)+sign/fee(`G6DNW4`). | hard `PLDP23 → 7UIYJ6` (cross-epic SHT6GE→2F77C6) |
| `ZJEL3N` | Dead-mirror retirement: pure-Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` + `flip_tick` + `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` | Routes the V3-companion `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` callsite to the `degenbot-cl-math` seam, then deletes the pure-Python copies once the DB-updater `QJSCA5` cutover (transitively `S5YS7U`) makes them orphaned. | hard `QJSCA5 → ZJEL3N` (cross-epic AZGJUN→2F77C6) |

**No NOW-DELETABLE children** created under `2F77C6` — the pre-existing state-layer
mirrors were ALREADY retired (Fork A `ClassVars`+`_verified_address`; combo-guide §6
pool-state → `_py_pool.snapshot()`/`sync_reserves`). The only now-deletable cleanups
already exist as their own epics' children: Solidly oracle `3VGIDY` (M6QUG6), encoder
`YQORTM` (WWC4DL — retires the Python encoder in its AC). Cross-referenced, not re-scoped.

**IN-FIGHT cross-references (already-scoped, NO new child):** `PublisherMixin` mechanism +
`PoolStateMessage`/`...PoolStateUpdated` message retirement = `ZBD4MS` (I7KVKM, 2K2JP4)
AC verbatim ("become thin delegating shells OR retired... retired per §4.3"). Wiring a
capstone cleanup child for the PublisherMixin would double-track — cross-referenced only.

## Dependency edges (`ergo sequence`)
```
CROSS-EPIC (SHT6GE → 2F77C6, HARD):  PLDP23 ──► 7UIYJ6   (example Dispatcher state mirror)
CROSS-EPIC (AZGJUN → 2F77C6, HARD):   QJSCA5 ──► ZJEL3N   (concentrated_liquidity Python math)
                                        (transitively: QJSCA5 gates on S5YS7U which this child's
                                         V3-companion cutover reuses for the cl-math PyO3 seam)
```
Both cleanup children are hard-gated on their cross-epic implementation child; no intra-epic
edges (the two cleanups are independent — example state mirror vs. library math). No epic-level
edges (retired — the orchestrator removed epic-level routing in favor of child-level). The
PublisherMixin retirement rides inside `ZBD4MS` (cross-reference). The successor-impl
`degenbot-bot::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` Rust↔Rust dedup (MPS3U7 open Q3) is NOT wired
here (out of scope: a Rust-internal §2.3 follow-up, not a Python state mirror).

data.title: Surface per-path sim-failure diagnostics in the backrun bot
data.body:
# Goal

`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` reports simulation failures with an
aggregate-only `[sim] … by reason: <bucket>=<count>` line. That collapse loses
the per-path attribution the operator needs to identify WHICH path reverted,
selector-encoded WHY (which custom error / Error(string) message), at which
call index in the 7-call vector, against which pools.

The Rust `simulate_one` leaf already has the full revert data + `first_failure`
index in hand at the failure point but discards both when it converts them into
a bare bucket string for `FailBuckets`. The Python companion already ships
two UNUSED diagnostic helpers — `_hop_token_summary` and
`format_sim_diag_line` in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` — designed for
this exact surface but never wired because the per-failure record doesn't
cross the FFI.

# Non-goals

- Auto-state/drift attribution (the `format_sim_diag_line` `hops` /
  `engine_state` / `onchain_state` block) — out of scope; only emit the
  fields the existing core data surfaces.
- Changing the `[sim]` summary line.
- Loosening the path-suppression / thin-margin filters.

# Disposition (three-layer rubric)

- Rust core (`degenbot-simulation`): `port-now` — own the failure detail
  struct + the per-path push.
- PyO3 wrapper (`degenbot-python`): `port-now` — thin getter.
- Python companion (`eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` + `eth_backrun_helpers.py`):
  `stays-python` — rendering only.

data.title: Simulation RPC dispatch leaf: 7-call balanceOf + execute() calldata + SimulateV1Payload + eth_simulateV1/eth_createAccessList/eth_feeHistory (typed consumer of ZUZANP)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **simulation RPC dispatch leaf** to Rust: the balance-call calldata builders
  (WETH9 `balanceOf`, ETH getBalance folded into the call vector, ERC6909 `balanceOf`),
  the `execute(bytes,uint256)` calldata shape (CONSUMED from WWC4DL `YQORTM`), the
  `eth_simulateV1` `blockStateCalls` payload (7-call pattern), the
  `eth_createAccessList` (EIP-2930) dispatch, and the `eth_feeHistory` consumer surface.
- Routes through `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::make_request` (untyped, EXISTS) UNTIL the
  typed `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList`/`eth_feeHistory` surfaces land in `ZUZANP`
  (RPC epic D3DIPE); then swaps to the typed RPC.

## Context
- Scope task: `4JGPDW` (epic `5LLJHX`), rows B1/B3/B4/B5.
- Rubric dispositions: B1 `port-now` (pure ABI calldata via `degenbot-abi::encode_rust`
  + executor selectors); B3/B4/B5 `partial` (the untyped `make_request` escape hatch
  EXISTS in `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider` L809 — so dispatch CAN route through Rust today
  untyped; the TYPED request/response structs are `ZUZANP`, cross-epic D3DIPE).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1 (core leaf)
  + §3.2 (PyO3) + §4.2 (parity), `docs/adr/ADR-005` (standalone-core + zero-pyo3),
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §3, `rust/CONTEXT.md` {AlloyProvider}/{make_request}.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` — `encode_balanceof_calldata`
  L372–L386, the `SimulateV1Payload`/`BlockStateCallV1` 7-call vector L2028–L2048, the
  `create_access_list` call L2007–L2010, `Dispatcher` feeHistory population feeding
  `_compute_priority_fee` L1570–L1615. The `eth_simulateV1` call: L2021–L2049.
- Rust precedent: `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::make_request` (L809, with retry/backoff),
  `eth_call`/`estimate_gas`/`get_balance` typed leaves (L570–L806) — the template shape
  the typed `ZUZANP` surfaces + this consumer mirror.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-simulation` core crate (deps `degenbot-rpc` +
  `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-executor`); confirm with `t-6486`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust calldata builders for the 3 balance calls (WETH9 `balanceOf(address)`,
  ERC6909 `balanceOf(address,uint256)` with the executor's WETH/native ids) via
  `degenbot-abi::encode_rust`.
- A `SimulatePayload` builder assembling the 7-call `blockStateCalls` vector
  (3 pre-balance reads, `execute()` call, 3 post-balance reads) + `stateOverrides`
  (from the sibling A-child) + `block_identifier="pending"`.
- `async fn simulate_v1(&self, payload) -> ProviderResult<SimulateResult>` dispatching via
  `make_request("eth_simulateV1", …)` UNTYPED (with a TODO/feature to swap to the typed
  `ZUZANP` surface); `async fn create_access_list(&self, tx, block) -> …` via
  `make_request("eth_createAccessList", …)`; an `eth_feeHistory` typed-consumer surface
  returning the percentile dict `_compute_priority_fee` consumes.
- The dispatch owns NO business logic (encode + state-override construction live in
  sibling crates); this leaf only shapes the RPC request + parses the response into typed
  structs (`returnData: Vec<Bytes>`, `gasUsed: u64`, `status`, revert `error.data`).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: the wire-shape of the `eth_simulateV1` JSON params + the
  response parse match the Python web3.py `simulate_v1` round-trip (use a mock transport).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example callsite.
- Mock-transport parity vs the web3.py `simulate_v1`/`create_access_list` wire shape.

## Non-goals
- Typing `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList`/`eth_feeHistory` request/response structs
  at the `degenbot-rpc` level — `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE). This leaf CONSUMES them when
  ready (interim: untyped `make_request`).
- The `execute(bytes,uint256)` cmd-bytes — `YQORTM` (cross-epic WWC4DL).
- The `stateOverrides` dict — sibling A-child (`TCTUAW`).
- The `simulate_one` orchestration + profit computation — sibling C-child.

## Dependencies
- Depends on `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE, typed RPC surfaces — hard dep for the typed
  path; the untyped `make_request` interim is already available so work can start on
  the consumer shape immediately, swapping to typed when `ZUZANP` lands).
- Depends on `YQORTM` (cross-epic WWC4DL, the `execute()` cmd-bytes + composer).

data.title: 4. PyO3 seam: `verify_v3_liquidity_on_chain` + `.pyi`
data.body:
## Goal
- Expose `verify_v3_liquidity_on_chain_on_conn` through a PyO3 seam in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/` (new `pool_updater.rs` module or extend the nearest existing `db/` module — match where the aave seam lives), mirroring `verify_all_positions_on_chain`'s signature + GIL-release + runtime-strategy (`Handle::try_current` + `block_in_place` vs own multi-thread rt) + divergence-dict-building.
## Context
- Copy the aave seam's runtime strategy verbatim (`Handle::try_current` → `block_in_place` + `handle.block_on`, else build own multi-thread rt; `AlloyProvider::new(rpc_url, 5)` inside the chosen runtime). The GIL is released across the whole call; zero SQL writes (open via `DegenbotDb::open`).
- Signature: `degenbot_rs.verify_v3_liquidity_on_chain(database_path, rpc_url, chain_id, pool_address, block_number, ticks=None) -> list[dict]`. Each divergence dict carries `pool_address`, `block_number`, a `field` (`"tick_gross"`/`"tick_net"`/`"bitmap_word"`/`"extra_db_tick"`/`"missing_db_tick"`), `tick` or `word`, `expected`, `actual` — the shape a Python compare harness (or pytest) can assert on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `degenbot_rs.pyi` declares the function with the full signature.
## Validation Gates

- `just test-rust` (the PyO3 crate's `#[cfg(test)]` seam-shape tests, if any).
- `just lint` (ruff checks the `.pyi`).

data.title: [rpc] B2 — Adopt sol! static ABI in degenbot-rpc for fetcher ABIs
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace `PyBotIo`'s hand-rolled selector + byte-decode fetchers with
  `sol!`-macro-typed contract calls, per the alloy static-ABI guide. The fetchers
  (`fetch_v2_reserves`/`fetch_v3_slot0_liquidity`/`fetch_v4_slot0_liquidity`/
  `fetch_token_balance`/`fetch_token_allowance`/`fetch_token_total_supply`)
  become typed `sol!`-generated calls.

## Context
- Guide: https://alloy.rs/guides/static-dynamic-abi-in-alloy/ —
  `sol! { function getReserves() external returns (uint112, uint112, uint32); }`
  + `#[sol(rpc)] contract IUniswapV2Pair { … }` gives
  `IUniswapV2Pair::new(addr, provider).getReserves().call().await`.
- New module `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/abi.rs` with `sol!` definitions for
  the handful of fetcher ABIs. `degenbot-rpc` is a core crate — pyo3-free.
- `PyBotIo`'s fetchers call these typed methods, removing the manual
  `keccak(text=…)[ :4]` + `eth_call` + `bytes.fromhex(…)[a:b]` decode.
- The example's 4 sim-fail diagnostic sites (A5 may leave them routing to
  `make_request`; this task reroutes them to the typed fetchers, eliminating
  the last `web3.keccak` in the example if not already done).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/abi.rs` exists with `sol!` definitions for the
  fetcher ABIs used by `PyBotIo`.
- `PyBotIo` fetchers use the typed calls; no hand-rolled selector computation
  in `PyBotIo`.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` stays green.
- Fetcher return values are byte-identical to the pre-refactor hand-rolled
  decode (parity test on a fork).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (fetcher parity on a fork)
- `just lint-rust`

data.title: dispatch_profitable_results submit orchestration + eth_sendRawTransaction broadcast + eth_feeHistory percentile fetch (typed consumer of ZUZANP; interim make_request fallback, dry_run/inject_code guards)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **`dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration** + the
  **`eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast** + the **`eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch** to
  Rust: sort candidates by engine profit descending; mutual-exclusivity check
  (`is_path_blocked` against pending+committed pools); `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE`/`dry_run`

  (N3) → finalize fees (N5) → re-compute access list (C5/`PGA5S3`) → sign (N4) →
  broadcast via `eth_sendRawTransaction` (I1/`ZUZANP`) → reserve pools (N3) → spawn the
  monitor task (N2). Plus the `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch feeding the `Dispatcher`
  `block_priority_fees` ring.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), rows N6 + I1 + I2.
- Rubric dispositions: N6 `port-now` (pure orchestration over leaves N3/N4/N5/N2 + C5 +
  I1; the §2.1 "GIL?" win — owning the sign+broadcast slice in Rust releases the GIL
  across the async broadcast; the sort + mutual-exclusivity is pure). I1 `partial`
  (`eth_sendRawTransaction` — untyped `make_request` EXISTS in `degenbot-rpc` L809 so
  broadcast CAN route through Rust today; the TYPED `bytes → TxHash` is `ZUZANP`
  cross-epic D3DIPE). I2 `partial` (`eth_feeHistory` — same shape; typed consumer `ZUZANP`).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§3.2 (PyO3)
  /§4.2 (parity), `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core),
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §3.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `dispatch_profitable_results`
  submit tail L2608–L2660 (the `dry_run` guard L2608, `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` guard L2612,
  claim nonce L2622, finalize fees L2623–L2625, re-compute access list L2627–L2630,
  sign+broadcast L2636–L2640, reserve pools L2648, spawn monitor L2650–L2656) + the
  `_apply_block_if_ready` `feeHistory` fetch L2832–L2841.
- **Cross-epic (hard edge, per orchestrator ruling Q1):** `ZUZANP` (D3DIPE) types exactly
  `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory` — KEEP hard `ZUZANP`→this-child edge; interim
  untyped `make_request` (L809) fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (§4.2 wait-for-typed
  default).
- **Cross-epic (REFERENCE, no hard edge):** the `tx_params` (+ `priority_fee`) CONSUMED
  from `YL2MTH` (Simulation); the access-list re-computation CONSUMED from `PGA5S3`
  (Simulation `eth_createAccessList`). Per orchestrator ruling Q2, Submission does NOT
  sequence-depend on `YL2MTH`.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `async fn dispatch_and_submit(gas_profitable: Vec<SimResult>, dispatcher,
  provider, signer, base_fee_next, current_block, inject_code: bool, dry_run: bool) ->
  SubmitOutcome` orchestrating: sort by engine profit desc → for each: mutual-exclusivity
  guard → `dry_run`/`inject_code` guard (RETURN a typed Skip reason, don't submit) → claim
  nonce (`M756BN`) → finalize fees (`G6DNW4`) → re-compute access list via
  `eth_createAccessList` → sign (`G6DNW4`) → broadcast via `eth_sendRawTransaction`
  (`ZUZANP` typed; interim `make_request` untyped) → `reserve_pools` → spawn
  `monitor_pending_transaction` (`HF2R2E`) tracked by `Dispatcher::track_task`.
- `async fn fetch_fee_history(provider, block_number, percentiles) -> FeeHistory` typed
  consumer of `eth_feeHistory` (`ZUZANP` typed; interim `make_request`) feeding
  `Dispatcher::record_priority_fees`.
- `dry_run`/`inject_code` are passed as `bool` args from the Python driver (S3 policy
  gate) — the leaf exposes them as config, NOT as Python policy.
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: submit order (profit-desc), mutual-exclusivity skip,
  `dry_run`/`inject_code` skip, nonce-fee-access-sign-broadcast sequence; mock the
  provider + signer.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example.
- Parity check vs the Python `dispatch_profitable_results` submit tail (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- Signing + fee finalization — N4/N5 child (`G6DNW4`).
- `Dispatcher` coordination — N3 child (`M756BN`).
- `monitor_pending_transaction` lifecycle — N2 child (`HF2R2E`).
- `_compute_priority_fee` (the `priority_fee` value) — Simulation `YL2MTH` (consume off
  `tx_params`, reference not hard-edge).
- `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList` typed RPC — `ZUZANP` (this child CONSUMES
  `eth_createAccessList` + `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory`).
- The `dry_run`/`INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` policy (the live-submission skip as a POLICY) —
  stays Python (S3); the leaf takes them as bool config.
- The `next_base_fee` formula — N1 child (`JTLWA3`).

## Dependencies
- Depends on N3 `M756BN` (Dispatcher), N4/N5 `G6DNW4` (sign+fee), N2 `HF2R2E` (monitor).
- Hard edge: `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE, typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` +
  `eth_feeHistory` — interim untyped `make_request` fallback ONLY if blocked).
- REFERENCE (no hard edge): `YL2MTH` (Simulation, `tx_params`+`priority_fee`) +
  `PGA5S3` (Simulation, `eth_createAccessList`).

data.title: [rpc] B1 — PyBotIo native alloy bodies (slice 14b/14c)
data.body:
## Goal
- Complete the 14b/14c cutover: `PyBotIo` holds `AlloyProvider` directly and
  runs native Rust method bodies for every `PoolIO` method, dropping the
  `Py<PyAny>` provider + `call_kw` GIL round-trip for the alloy path.

## Context
- `PyBotIo` today:
  ```rust
  #[pyclass(name = "PyBotIo")]
  pub struct PyBotIo { /* holds Py<PyAny> provider */ fn new(provider, db, database_path) }
  ```
  Each of ~10 methods (`get_block_number`/`get_block`/`get_code`/`get_balance`/
  `call`→`eth_call`/`call_raw`/`get_logs`/`get_transaction_count`/
  `get_storage_at`) round-trips via `self.call_kw(py, "method", …)`.
- `AlloyProvider` (degenbot-rpc, pyo3-free) exposes every primitive natively:
  `get_block_number`/`get_block` (returns `EthBlock` with header.timestamp)/
  `get_code`/`get_balance`/`eth_call`/`get_logs`/`get_transaction_count`/
  `get_storage_at`. `get_block_timestamp` derives from
  `get_block(n).header.unix_timestamp()`.
- After B2, the fetchers (`fetch_v2_reserves` etc.) call `sol!`-typed methods
  instead of hand-rolled `eth_call` + byte-slice.
- `degenbot-rpc` stays pyo3-free; native bodies live in `degenbot-python`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PyBotIo` holds `AlloyProvider` (cloned arc) directly; the `Py<PyAny>`
  provider field + `call_kw` machinery is removed.
- Every `PoolIO` method has a native body (no Python round-trip).
- `get_block_timestamp` returns the block header timestamp without a separate
  RPC.
- Existing `PyBotIo` tests pass (pool-build choreography unchanged from the
  caller's view).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (focus: `degenbot-python` PyBotIo tests)
- `just lint-rust`

data.title: crash #5 followup: pare 3,366 divergences after 18M drive completes
data.body:
## Goal

Fix the remaining 3,366 divergences between the Rust `run_aave_update`
18M drive and the Python oracle, after crash #4 resolution (commit 68334031).

The 16591070→18M drive now completes without crash (141 chunks committed,
234,043 events applied in 241s), but `compare_dbs` (`scripts/aave_replay_diff.py`)
reports 3,366 total divergences from the Python oracle:

| bucket | count | class |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `aave_v3_users.stk_aave_balance` | 381 | Rust `NULL` vs Python's value (mixed: ~most are Rust NULL vs Python `0`, but several are Rust NULL vs Python nonzero on-chain balance — e.g. `1012356973342319609` for user `0x0029Ab...`, `950000000000000000` for `0x03AA12...`) |
| `aave_v3_debt_positions.balance` | 48 | GHO debt position scaled balance drift |
| `aave_v3_users.gho_discount` | 6 | discount column drift |
| row_count (users) | 1 | Python ref: 17,291 users vs Rust: 14,361 (≈3,000 extra Python users) |

The exact `0` cases on Python's side suggest that Python's
`get_or_init_stk_aave_balance` backfilled from chain where Rust's
`dispatch_stk_aave_transfer_with_backfill` didn't run (e.g. users Rust
doesn't see a Staked/Redeem/Transfer event for but Python created via the
GHO borrow path's user lookup). And the nonce-zero Python values
(1012356973342319609 etc.) for users that have NO stkAAVE events in the drive
suggest Python backfilled from chain via `_refresh_discount_rate` AND the
post-borrow `get_or_init_stk_aave_balance` call.

## Plan (TDD, narrow cross-sections). Each child targets one divergence class.

Children:

1. **users-null-vs-py-zero** — Rust's `get_or_create_user_on_conn` is called
   from BOTH the StkAaveTransfer dispatch AND the (C) refresh's lookup. Python
   has the same flow. Trace the ~381 NULL-vs-zero cases; if Python's
   `get_or_init_stk_aave_balance` runs as a side-effect of the GHO borrow
   handler (NOT just the (C) refresh), the Rust GHO borrow handler is missing
   the matching backfill. Add a per-tx pre-pass for GHO active users whose
   balance column is None: backfill once per tx in the START of
   process_transaction (mirror Python's `tx_context.user_lookup` lazy init).
2. **users-missing-in-cand** — Rust has ~3,000 fewer user rows than Python.
   Identify why Python creates them (`get_or_create_user` side-effect of a
   GHO event handler that touches an address Rust doesn't create users for).
   Probably a Transfer/Swap event Rust treats as type-only-no-user but Python
   treats as user-creating.
3. **debt-positions-balance-mismatches** — 48 debt-position scaled balance
   mismatches. Probably 1-wei rounding issues (`CEIL` vs `HALF_UP` mint/burn)
   OR the `actual_repay_amount` isn't being threaded from paired Repay events
   in some specific cases. Compare-cand-vs-ref per-position with the event
   history.
4. **gho_discount-6-cases** — 6 discount mismatches. These are likely
   downwind from the stk_aave_balance issues above; close after #1 lands.

## Recovery context

- Drive harness: `/tmp/c_reverify_18m.py` (cold-boot source
  `/home/dev/.config/degenbot/degenbot.db.rust-coldboot-16591070-bak` + Python
  gold `/tmp/python_gold_18m_drive.db`).
- Full drive log: `/tmp/c_reverify_18m_v5.log`.
- Pure compare_dbs-only invocation (no drive): see the discussion in `_reverify`
  bash script — pass limit=5000 to see all 3,366 divergences (default limit
  clamps to 50).
- Compare-DBs signature: `compare_dbs(ref_path, cand_path, *, limit=50) ->
  {"exit_code": int, "total_divergences": int, "divergences": [...]}`.

data.title: Port V3/V4 DB-aware liquidity updater + pool discovery writers into Rust over degenbot-db; CLI driver stays Python
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the V3/V4 **DB-aware liquidity updater** (`cli/pool.py::apply_v3_liquidity_updates` / `apply_v4_liquidity_updates` — read pool row + positions → apply liquidity-mapping math → upsert positions + init maps + stamp `liquidity_update_block`/`liquidity_update_log_index`) and the **pool discovery writers** (`cli/pool_updater_configs.py::update_v2/v3/v4_pools` — scan PoolCreated, upsert pool/config rows, stamp `ExchangeTable.last_update_block`) into a Rust apply-and-persist core over `degenbot-db` + `degenbot-cl-math`, exposed via a PyO3 seam. The Python `pool_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch stay as the shell.

## Context
- Scope task: `MPS3U7` (Epic `AZGJUN`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (the apply-and-persist core) / **stays-python** (the driver loop + RPC fetch).
- §2.1 criteria (apply-and-persist core): type=Address/int/U256; I/O= substrate read (pool row + `liquidity_positions` + `initialization_maps`) + math + substrate write (upsert/delete positions + init maps, set stamps); warm/bulk path (per-block chunk backfill, not per-tx hot loop). §2.3 smell: the apply function reconstitutes a `PoolLiquidityMap` from DB rows via ORM relationships, calls the (pure-Py, soon-Rust) math, then hand-writes chunked `sqlite_upsert(...).on_conflict_do_update` + `delete(...)` — a Rust typed-row substrate (`SLHSM4`) collapses the ORM reconstitution + the hand-rolled chunked upsert into one seam.
- **Orchestrator open question answered:** the feed-side updater reads/writes the **DB directly** (`pool_in_db.liquidity_positions`, `session.execute(sqlite_upsert(...))`), NOT `BotState`. The in-memory `BotState` liquidity maps (`n_update_by_pool_id` in `degenbot-bot`) are a SEPARATE path (hot-path swap solver) NOT synced by these updaters. Therefore: **hard DB-substrate dependency on `SLHSM4`; NO dependency on `QVMWQC`** (builder/construction reads — different callsite set, though both use `SLHSM4` read fns); **NO dependency on a BotState child**.
- Driver loop `pool_update` + `_pool_updater` + `get_v3/v4_liquidity_events`/`get_events_from_contract`/`fetch_logs_retrying` = **stays-python** (CLI orchestration shell + RPC event fetch; `degenbot-rpc` event-fetch port is a separate concern not in this epic).
- Deps: `SLHSM4` (substrate: `fetch_liquidity_map`, `upsert_liquidity_positions`, `set_liquidity_update_marker`, `upsert_pool_row`, pool-row upsert for discovery) + sibling math task (lifted `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` in `degenbot-cl-math`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rust core (in `degenbot-db` or a new `degenbot-updaters` core module) exposes `apply_v3_liquidity_updates(conn, pool_address, liquidity_events, chain_id)` and `apply_v4_liquidity_updates(...)` over `degenbot_db::SqliteConnection` + `degenbot_cl_math::apply_liquidity_mapping_update`; the ORM reconstitution + chunked `sqlite_upsert`/`delete` bodies replaced by substrate calls (`upsert_liquidity_positions(pool_id, &positions)`, `upsert_initialization_maps(...)`, `delete_stale_positions(pool_id, &ticks)`, `set_liquidity_update_marker(pool_id, block, log_index)`).
- Pool discovery writers `update_v2/v3/v4_pools` route PoolCreated upserts through `degenbot_db::upsert_pool_row` / `upsert_erc20_token` / `set_exchange_last_update_block`.
- PyO3 seam (`#[pyfunction]` in `degenbot-python/src/updaters/` or `db/`) wraps each apply/discovery fn, registered in `c_api.rs`; `py.detach()` for the DB I/O.
- Python `apply_v3_liquidity_updates`/`apply_v4_liquidity_updates`/`update_v2/v3/v4_pools` become delegating shells; the inline SQLAlchemy `session.scalar/select`/`sqlite_upsert`/`delete` bodies deleted.
- The block/log-index ordering invariants (the `assert blockNumber >= last; logIndex > last` guards) preserved in Rust (return/panic on violation, matching current assertion behavior).
- Parity (§4.2): apply a fixture event sequence against a fixture DB → identical resulting `liquidity_positions`/`initialization_maps` rows + `liquidity_update_block` stamp as the prior Python path (Py as oracle until green, retire per §4.3). The SQLite 32766-variable chunking behavior preserved (or superseded by a substrate batch fn that respects the limit).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`cli/pool.py` + `pool_updater_configs` updater tests), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The liquidity-mapping math itself (sibling math task in `degenbot-cl-math`).
- The `SLHSM4` substrate (Epic `VGTEDL`).
- The `pool_update`/`_pool_updater` driver loop + RPC event fetch (`get_v3/v4_liquidity_events`, `fetch_logs_retrying`) — stays Python (orchestration + RPC, RPC port is another epic).
- The `UniswapV3/4LiquiditySnapshot` in-memory event-fetcher/`update()` classes (`v3_snapshot.py`/`v4_snapshot.py`) — they apply events to in-memory maps, not DB; their DB-read half is Epic `VGTEDL` (`WKZ7ID`).
- Aave lending-market writers (sibling task).
- Syncing `BotState` in-memory liquidity maps with the DB (separate concern; the hot path owns its own).

## QJSCA5 §4.3 — liquidity-updater slice landed

Path (a): Rust owns the reconstitute→apply-math→persist pipeline; Python shells decode + delegate.

- PyO3 seam (`db/liquidity_updater.rs`): `LiquidityUpdateEvent` pyclass + `db_apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` + `db_fetch_pool_row` (V3 scope precondition).
- Python `apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates` → delegating shells. Retired `_apply_liquidity_mapping_via_rust` + ORM helpers.
- 2 seam parity tests vs the §4.2 JSON oracle. §4.2 Rust parity unchanged, green.

Deferred: pool-discovery writers (`update_v2/v3/v4_pools`) need NEW substrate fns (`upsert_pool_row`/`set_exchange_last_update_block`) — not yet in `degenbot-db`.

PRE-EXISTING LINT FAILURE: `just lint` is RED on `pathfinding.py` (`build_path_graph` imported from degenbot_rs but no .pyi stub — ZX5JBH residual) + `async_adapter.py` ty issues. NOT from this slice (files unmodified by me). Needs the `build_path_graph` pyfunction stub.

data.title: [sim] A4 — dispatch_profitable_py pyfunction
data.body:
## Goal
- Implement the `dispatch_profitable_py` async pyfunction that wraps the core
  `dispatch_profitable_results`, joining `SimResult → PySubmitCandidate` at
  result-wrap time, and returns `PyDispatchOutcome`. GIL discipline mirrors
  `dispatch_and_submit_py` exactly (arg-extract → `py.detach` → core call →
  wrap).

## Context
- Signature (Python-facing):
  `async def dispatch_profitable_py(candidates: list[PyDispatchCandidate],
  context: PySimulateContext, dispatcher: PyDispatcher, current_block: int,
  min_profit_net: int, min_profit_margin_bps: int) -> PyDispatchOutcome`.
- Internally: build `SimulateContext` borrowing from `PySimulateContext`;
  build `DispatchCandidate`s from `PyDispatchCandidate`s; call
  `core::dispatch_profitable_results(&candidates, &ctx, suppression_arc,
  current_block, …) → DispatchOutcome<SimResult>`; join each surviving
  `SimResult` → `PySubmitCandidate` (executor_address from `SimulateContext`,
  path_pools from the originating candidate's `path_info.hops` — the exact
  derivation at example L1719/L2476); assemble `PyDispatchOutcome`.
- `gas_used` source: confirm whether `PySubmitCandidate` expects raw sim
  `gasUsed` or the 1.5× `inflated_gas()`. `SimResult` exposes both — pick
  whichever `dispatch_and_submit` consumes (30-second lookup at impl time).
- Register as `#[pyfunction]` in `simulation/dispatch.rs`; wire into `mod.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `dispatch_profitable_py` registered as a pyfunction; appears in the `.pyi`.
- The function releases the GIL for the duration of the core call.
- The `SimResult → PySubmitCandidate` join produces candidates whose fields
  match what `dispatch_and_submit_py` consumes (verified by a handoff test).
- No business logic in the wrapper — pure delegation.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (pyo3 seam test: mock core, verify join + GIL release)
- `just lint-rust`

> **Done** — committed `52c3eb04`.

## What landed

### `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/simulation/dispatch.rs` (NEW)
The `dispatch_profitable_py` pyfunction — the PyO3 shell over the core
`dispatch_profitable_results` fan-out. GIL discipline mirrors
`dispatch_and_submit_py` exactly:
1. GIL-held arg extraction: walk `list[PyDispatchCandidate]`, clone each held
   `DispatchCandidate` into the input batch + snapshot `path_id -> PathInfo`
   into a join map. Resolve `Option<BlockPriorityFees>` from the
   dispatcher's priority-fee ring (ports the Python
   `block_priority_fees[max(...)]` + `.get(10)/.get(50)` lookup the cockpit
   did inline pre-A4). Take the suppression arc.
2. `future_into_py` releases the GIL across the per-tx `eth_simulateV1` /
   `eth_createAccessList` RPCs. The async block is `Send`: `SimulateContext`
   borrows a moved `Arc<AlloyProvider>` (block-local `'a` borrow);
   `executor_address` is `Copy`; the suppression arc is passed by reference
   (the core locks at bookends only — no guard across any `.await`).
3. Pure-Rust join (no GIL needed): `join_sim_result` maps each surviving
   `SimResult` -> `SubmitCandidate`; `derive_path_pools` derives the
   mutual-exclusion `path_pools` set (V4 -> `pool_id_hex`; V2/V3 -> the
   EIP-55 checksummed `pool_address` Display form, ports example L2476-L2478).
   `gas_used` is the raw `gasUsed` UN-inflated (1.5x `inflated_gas()`
   computed downstream at submit time).
`PyDispatchOutcome::from_join(joined, &outcome)` stores core types +
builds wrappers on getter access.

### `rust/crates/degenbot-simulation/src/dispatch_profitable.rs` (CORE change)
`dispatch_profitable_results` signature changed from
`path_suppression: &mut PathSuppression` to
`path_suppression: &Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>` — the A3 acceptance
criterion #2 (which A3 left incomplete). The lock is scoped at the two
bookends only (step 1 pre-filter `.retain`, step 6 outcome-record loop):
`let mut s = arc.lock().expect(...); ...; ` guard dropped at block close.
**This is the fix for `future cannot be sent between threads safely`** — a
`std::sync::MutexGuard` is not `Send`, so holding it across the
`buffer_unordered().collect().await` fan-out made the wrapper's future
non-`Send` (and `future_into_py` requires `Send + 'static`). Bookend-only
scoping drops the guard before any `.await`. Core tests updated to wrap
`PathSuppression` in `Arc::new(Mutex::new(...))` + lock for assertions.

### `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/simulation/mod.rs`
Register the pyfunction via `wrap_pyfunction!` + add the `dispatch` submodule.

### `src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`
The `dispatch_profitable_py` signature (returns
`Coroutine[Any, Any, PyDispatchOutcome]`) + the `__all__` entry.

### `tests/rust/test_simulation_seam_dispatch.py` (NEW)
7 smoke tests: registration, the empty-candidate short-circuit (proves GIL
release + `future_into_py` async wiring + `PyDispatchOutcome` join shape
end-to-end, no RPC), arg-validation (non-candidate list element +
non-list), the `gas_profitable` getter list-construction shape, and a
suppression-pre-filter propagation (a path suppressed past the threshold is
dropped pre-sim, `suppressed_count=1` — the dead-URL provider never dials).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `dispatch_profitable_py` registered as a pyfunction; appears in the `.pyi`.
- [x] The function releases the GIL for the duration of the core call
      (`future_into_py`, the test `test_empty_candidates_releases_gil_across_await`).
- [x] The `SimResult -> PySubmitCandidate` join produces candidates whose
      fields match what `dispatch_and_submit_py` consumes (verified structurally:
      `SubmitCandidate` is the exact core type `dispatch_and_submit` reads;
      the join populates every field; the empty + suppressed seam tests
      exercise the plumbing. The full handoff with a real SimResult is A6's
      parity-test domain.)
- [x] No business logic in the wrapper — pure delegation (arg extract +
      bookend-resolution + join, all ported-from-python lookups).

## Validation
- `just lint-rust` green (clippy + fmt, all features).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` OK (core stayed pyo3-free).
- `cargo test -p degenbot-simulation` -- 61/61.
- `cargo test -p degenbot-submission` -- 43/43 + doc.
- `uv run pytest tests/rust/` -- 299/299 (292 prior + 7 new).

## Notes for A5 (T56NNZ) — route the example through the seam
- The cockpit swaps its `await dispatch_profitable_results(...)` Python call
