data.title: Wire degenbot-rpc into the chunk loop + add the alloy::Log decode leaf
data.body:
## Goal

The first Rust surface for the Rust-owned chunk updater (epic `2SFL6I`). No RPC porting — `degenbot-rpc` already has everything (`AlloyProvider`, `get_logs`, `fetch_logs_chunked`, `get_block_number`, `get_block`). This task wires it into the shape the chunk loop will consume + adds the ONE genuinely new Rust surface: a pure-Rust decode leaf from `alloy::Log` → the existing `V3PoolRowInput`/`V4PoolRowInput`/`LiquidityUpdateEvent` types.

## Read first
- `docs/migration-guides/pool-updater-chunk-atomicity.md` §3.2 (the RPC-layer decision) + §4 Task 1.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` — `AlloyProvider::new(rpc_url, max_retries)`, `get_block_number`, `get_block`, `get_logs(&LogFilter)`, `fetch_logs_chunked(from, to, addresses, topics)`. Note: this crate is ASYNC (alloy/tokio).
- `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/subscription.rs` — `pump_logs` (for the pubsub shape, in case useful as a reference).
- The existing row-input types: `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/discovery.rs` (`V2PoolRowInput`, `V3PoolRowInput`, `V4PoolRowInput`) + `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/liquidity_updater.rs` (`LiquidityUpdateEvent`).
- The Python event-hash + topic constants the decode leaf must reproduce: `src/degenbot/cli/pool_updater_configs.py` (the `event_hash` per exchange family) + `src/degenbot/abis/` (the V2/V3/V4 PoolCreated / Mint / Burn ABI signatures).

## Deliverable

1. **A decode leaf in `degenbot-decoders`** (or wherever V2/V3/V4 event decode lives — check `rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/`):
   - `decode_pool_created_event(log: &alloy::Log, family: PoolFamily) -> DecodedPoolCreated` — extracts `(token0, token1, fee, tick_spacing?, pool_address)` from the log topics+data per the family's `PoolCreated` signature. Returns a type that can be mapped to `V2PoolRowInput`/`V3PoolRowInput`/`V4PoolRowInput` by the chunk fn (Task 3).
   - `decode_liquidity_event(log: &alloy::Log) -> LiquidityUpdateEvent` (Mint/Burn; maps to the existing `LiquidityUpdateEvent` in `liquidity_updater.rs`).
   - Event-topic-hash constants for V2/V3/V4 PoolCreated / Mint / Burn (move from Python's `pool_updater_configs.py` into Rust constants — these are protocol-level, belong in core).
   - Pure functions. No state. No FFI. No `pyo3` (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`).

2. **A small "RPC fetcher" thin wrapper** (in `degenbot-rpc` or a new `pool-updater` core module — your call, justify it) that exposes the chunk loop's exact needs as a typed async API:
   - `fetch_pool_created_logs(provider, from_block, to_block, factory_address, family) -> Vec<DecodedPoolCreated>`
   - `fetch_liquidity_logs(provider, from_block, to_block, pool_addresses?) -> Vec<LiquidityUpdateEvent>`
   - These wrap `AlloyProvider::fetch_logs_chunked` + the decode leaf. The chunk fn (Task 3) will call them.

## Validation gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-decoders` green (new decode-leaf unit tests: feed a known `alloy::Log` from a real `PoolCreated`/`Mint`/`Burn` event → assert the decoded fields match).
- `cargo test -p degenbot-rpc` green (existing tests unaffected; new fetcher wrapper has a round-trip test if feasible without a live node, else a decode-only test).
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-decoders -p degenbot-rpc -- -D warnings` clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green.

## Commit
`feat(rust): wire degenbot-rpc into chunk-loop shape + alloy::Log decode leaf` (scope `rust`). Reference epic `2SFL6I` + the migration guide + task 1. No `.ergo/` files. Rust core only — no PyO3 wrapper, no Python.

## Report-back (to orchestrator via link_send triggerTurn:true)
1. Commit hash.
2. Gate pass/fail.
3. Where the decode leaf lives (crate + module path) + where the fetcher wrapper lives (and why there).
4. The exact event-topic-hash constants you moved + their source (which Python file).
5. Any deviation.

Committed 0aafcccb. Gates: cargo test -p degenbot-decoders (65), cargo test -p degenbot-rpc (88), clippy clean, no-pyo3 OK. Decode leaf at rust/crates/degenbot-decoders/src/pool_created_decoder.rs (728 lines); fetcher wrapper at rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/fetch.rs (699 lines) in a new degenbot-pool-updater core crate. Event-topic hashes moved from src/degenbot/cli/pool_updater_configs.py. Format strays from the gate run committed separately as 7be48f8e.

data.title: degenbot-db core crate: SQLite connection + schema + typed rows + migration runner
data.body:
## Goal
- Land a new pyo3-free core crate `degenbot-db` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/`) that owns the **SQLite persistence substrate** for the degenbot Rust core: connection/pool management, the schema DDL (mirroring the current Alembic head), typed row structs for every table, low-level read/write row functions, and a migration runner that can open an existing Alembic-stamped SQLite DB without clobbering its revision.
- This is the foundation (route-before-type, sub-step A of the rubric §3) onto which the snapshot-read cutover (sibling task), the builder-read cutover (sibling task), and the file-ops cutover (sibling task) route.

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL` "Database persistence → Rust core").
- Rubric disposition for the substrate: **port-now**. No Rust DB counterpart exists today (`ls rust/crates/` — no `degenbot-db`; only `degenbot-bot` touches "snapshot" as in-memory verify seeds, not SQLite). The persistence responsibility is currently pure Python SQLAlchemy (`src/degenbot/database/{operations,session_manager}.py`, `models/*.py`, `migrations/`).
- §2.1 criteria driving `port-now`: type shape is pure numeric/byte/Address/U256 (tick→int, liquidity_gross/net→U256, address→checksum) — ideal Rust; standalone-Rust-core constraint (ADR-005) means a `cargo add degenbot` consumer doing backfill/snapshot reads needs persistence in a core crate from day one; I/O shape is pure transform (rows→structs) for the read fns.
- §2.3 smell: the snapshot readers hand-slice/serialize EVM integers via the `IntMappedToString` `TypeDecorator` (`models/base.py`) — a Rust typed row with `U256` columns removes that.
- The held `db: Option<Py<PyAny>>` on `PyBotIo` (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs`) is the staged-but-inert routing seam — its docstring says "Slice 14c routes DB queries through here." This task builds the core that 14c routes to.
- Schema source of truth (mirror exactly): `src/degenbot/database/models/{base,types,erc20,pools,aave}.py` + `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/` head.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `rust/crates/degenbot-db/` with `Cargo.toml` (`sqlx` with `sqlite` feature, or `rusqlite` — pick one and record the choice in `rust/CONTEXT.md`), `lib.rs`, and modules for: connection/pool (`SqliteConnection`/`Pool`), schema (embedded DDL via `sqlx::migrate!` or `refinery`, matching the Alembic head), typed row structs (`ExchangeRow`, `Erc20TokenRow`, `LiquidityPoolRow` + per-DEX subclass discriminator via `kind`, `LiquidityPositionRow`, `InitializationMapRow`, `PoolManagerRow`, `ManagedLiquidityPoolRow`, `ManagedPoolLiquidityPositionRow`, `ManagedPoolInitializationMapRow`, Aave tables), read fns (`fetch_pool_by_address`, `fetch_token_by_address`, `fetch_liquidity_map(pool_address)`, `fetch_all_liquidity_maps(chain_id)`, `fetch_pools_for_chain`, `fetch_newest_update_block`), write fns (`upsert_erc20_token`, `upsert_pool_row`, `upsert_liquidity_positions`, `set_liquidity_update_marker`).
- U256/big-int columns map losslessly (mirror `IntMappedToString`'s VARCHAR(78) string round-trip OR use a native big-int SQLite representation — record the choice; must round-trip the full 32-byte EVM range).
- The migration runner, pointed at an existing degenbot SQLite DB, reads the `alembic_version` table head and treats an already-stamped DB as current without re-running DDL.
- `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests: round-trip insert→read for each row type against a `:memory:` sqlite; parity fixture reading a fixture SQLite file produces the same `LiquidityMap`/tick dicts as the Python `DatabaseSnapshot.get_liquidity_map`.
- **Zero `pyo3`** in the crate (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`).
- Workspace virtual manifest `rust/Cargo.toml` lists the new member; `degenbot` umbrella re-exports it (or not, per publish-deferred state — at minimum it builds as a workspace member).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` — new crate unit + integration tests pass.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — still PASS (crate is pyo3-free).
- `just lint-rust` — clippy `--deny warnings` clean on the new crate.

## Non-goals
- PyO3 bindings / `#[pyclass]` surface (that is the sibling routing tasks under `degenbot-python`).
- Routing the Python `DatabaseSnapshot` / builders / CLI through Rust (sibling tasks).
- The DB-aware **writer/orchestration** logic (the `UniswapV3LiquiditySnapshot.update` fetch-and-persist loop, CLI bulk updaters, Aave `db_*` updaters) — that is Epic `AZGJUN` (Scope `MPS3U7`), which depends on this substrate.
- Retiring the Python SQLAlchemy ORM / Alembic (kept as parity oracle + for writer paths until AZGJUN migrates them).

SLHSM4 complete: the degenbot-db pyo3-free read substrate.

## Crate layout (rust/crates/degenbot-db/, all new)
- Cargo.toml — rusqlite(bundled) + alloy + parking_lot + thiserror; serde/serde_json/tempfile dev-deps. Zero pyo3.
- src/lib.rs, src/error.rs (DbError + impl From<DbError> for rusqlite::Error), src/schema.rs (ALEMBIC_HEAD="2606a6c7f5ee", SCHEMA_HEAD include_str, RUST_SCHEMA_VERSION=1, table/kind helpers), src/schema_head.sql (ground-truth DDL from Base.metadata.create_all via sqlite_master, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + indexes), src/migrate.rs (ensure_schema -> SchemaState {AlembicCurrent|AlembicStale|FreshStandalone|Unrecognized}; writes NOTHING on Alembic DB; DDL+stamp only fresh-standalone; refuses stale/unrecognized), src/connection.rs (DegenbotDb{Mutex<Connection>}, open/open_in_memory; PRAGMA sequence WAL+busy_timeout=5000+synchronous=NORMAL before ensure_schema, then query_only=on AFTER ensure_schema so fresh-standalone DDL writes succeed — every returned connection is read-only; stale/unrecognized -> Err), src/rows/{decode,exchange,erc20,pool,liquidity,aave}.rs (typed rows + pub(crate) from_row; VARCHAR(78)<->U256 via from_str_radix/10; Address via parse_checksummed; pool_hash VARCHAR(66) hex), src/read.rs (fetch_token/pool/pool_kind/pools_for_chain/newest_update_block[ExchangeFamily]/liquidity_positions/initialization_map/managed_*), src/snapshot.rs (LiquidityMap/BitmapAtWord/LiquidityAtTick/PoolKey leaf-local + fetch_liquidity_map/fetch_liquidity_map_v4/fetch_all_liquidity_maps mirroring Python get_all_liquidity_maps query shapes).

## Wiring
- rust/Cargo.toml: +workspace member +codegen-units profile. Umbrella degenbot crate: +degenbot-db dep +pub use. justfile: +degenbot-db to check-no-pyo3-in-cores loop. Did NOT touch rust/CONTEXT.md, Python, or write.rs/upsert_* (deferred to AZGJUN per binding #1).

## PRAGMA sequence (binding #2/#3)
journal_mode=WAL; busy_timeout=5000; synchronous=NORMAL (before ensure_schema); ensure_schema; query_only=on (after — fresh-standalone DDL needs writes; every returned conn is read-only). query_only verified: a CREATE on an opened parity.db fails.

## Parity fixture (binding #4 HARD gate)
- tests/fixtures/generate_parity.py builds a REAL Alembic-stamped parity.db (create_new_sqlite_database + alembic stamp head) seeded with V3+V4 pool data carrying U256-range values (2^70 > i64::MAX; u128::MAX gross — the Python LiquidityAtTick pydantic bound; U256::MAX covered by lib unit test). Runs the Python DatabaseSnapshot oracle (v3/v4_snapshot get_liquidity_map/get_all/newest_block/get_pools) against the same DB -> parity_expected.json (U256 as decimal strings, addresses EIP-55, pool_hash 0x hex). WAL checkpointed; only parity.db committed.

data.title: [web3py] C3 — Port AnvilFork off web3
data.body:
## Goal
- `AnvilFork` reaches anvil via alloy `make_request` (over IPC/HTTP) instead of
  web3's `IPCProvider`/`AsyncIPCProvider`. The `.w3` connector is removed;
  callers use `fork.http_url` + an alloy provider. `async_w3` path ported.

## Context
- AnvilFork anvil-RPC methods: `evm_mine`, `anvil_reset`, `evm_revert`,
  `evm_snapshot` — these are anvil-specific JSON-RPC, **not** ABI calls
  (`sol!` does not apply); they go through `AlloyProvider::make_request`.
- AnvilFork's anvil *process* management (spawning, `--fork-url`, port
  selection) is subprocess-based, not web3 — stays as-is.
- This is the highest-risk Pass B task: IPC behavior parity (the `evm_mine`
  blocking semantics, the `anvil_reset` re-launch path). Keep the anvil
  process lifecycle; only swap the IPC client.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `AnvilFork` no longer imports `web3` (`IPCProvider`/`AsyncIPCProvider`/
  `AsyncWeb3`/`Web3`/`Middleware`/`RPCEndpoint`).
- `evm_mine`/`anvil_reset`/`evm_revert`/`evm_snapshot` go through alloy
  `make_request` and behave identically (tests pass).
- `.w3` removed; `http_url` is the supported connector.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (anvil fork tests)
- `just lint`

Canceled: the mechanical `make_request`-swap plan in this task is superseded by epic NXYVYU ("Rust-owned AnvilFork") tasks FF1–FF5 (`degenbot-fork` crate + `alloy::node_bindings`-spawned Anvil + PyAnvilFork PyO3 seam + Python companion shell + caller migration). Anchored by `7bea6576` (the FF4+FF5 atomic commit) — `src/degenbot/anvil_fork.py` now imports zero web3, spawns the Anvil subprocess via alloy, dev-RPC methods (`evm_mine`, `anvil_reset`, `evm_snapshot`, `evm_revert`) are typed methods on the rust core (not raw `make_request` calls from Python), `self.w3` is replaced by `self.provider = AlloyProvider(self.fork.ipc_path)`, and all 26 test callers migrated to `fork.provider.X()` / `Web3(HTTPProvider(fork.http_url)).eth.X`.

C3's AC ("AnvilFork no longer imports web3", "evm_mine/reset/revert/snapshot behave identically", "tests pass", ".w3 removed; http_url supported as the connector") is fully delivered by FF4/FF5. So C3 itself is moot — its `todo` blocker is now retired; DFPIAM (C6) is repointed at FF6 (JGBKMK, this task) instead.

data.title: Revert taxonomy (classify_revert) + thin-margin result filter (core leaf)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **revert taxonomy** (`classify_revert` + `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` +
  `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS`) and the **thin-margin result filter**
  (`filter_thin_margin_results`) to Rust.
- `classify_revert(revert_data: &[u8]) -> &str` returns a stable label for cmd_executor +
  PoolManager revert selectors, `Error(string)`, `Panic(uint256)`, bare numeric Vyper
  reverts, or `unknown:0x........`; never raises. `filter_thin_margin_results` drops solver
  results whose `profit / opt_input` is below a BPS threshold.

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), rows D1/D2.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure bytes→label / pure integer margin filter; never-
  raises contract; property-testable; no I/O).
  - **EPIC-PLACEMENT FLAG:** `classify_revert` straddles two contracts —
    `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the cmd_executor's (affined to this epic), but
    `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the PoolManager's (affined to decode/Simulation). This
    epic `WWC4DL` BLOCKS the Simulation epic `5LLJHX`; the revert taxonomy may more
    naturally belong under `5LLJHX`. Created here because it is executor-affined and pure,
    but `t-6486` may transfer it. **Needs t-6486 confirmation.**
- `filter_thin_margin_results` is a pre-sim filter; it consumes engine results
  (`(path_id, opt_input, profit, hop_outputs, consumed_inputs, solve_block)` tuples). Also
  a candidate for `5LLJHX`. Flagged.
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1 (core leaf
  in `degenbot-decoders` for revert-data decode, or in `degenbot-executor` if that crate is
  created), §4.2 parity. `contracts/README.md` callback + error table for the selector
  list.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` — `classify_revert` L376–L417,
  `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` L357–L367, `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` L369–L375,
  `_ERROR_STRING_SELECTOR`/`_PANIC_SELECTOR` L372–L374, `format_failure_breakdown`
  L419–L436 (rendering only — stays-Python display), `filter_thin_margin_results` L439–L477.
- `degenbot-decoders` covers *event* decode, not revert-data taxonomy — no Rust
  counterpart exists for these selectors.
- `format_sim_diag_line` (L479–L528) is `stays-python` (display/diagnostics, `json.dumps`
  + heterogeneous snapshot dict) — NOT in this task; flagged in the scope table so the next
  sweep does not re-litigate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `classify_revert(revert_data: &[u8]) -> &'static str` (or
  `Result<String, _>`) matching the Python taxonomy: `empty`, `short:<hex>`,
  `Panic(0x..)`, decoded `Error(string)`, selector-labels (params dropped) for the
  cmd_executor + V4 custom errors, `numeric-revert`, `unknown:0x........`. Never panics
  (malformed input returns a best-effort label).
- Selector constants (or a static map) for `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` +
  `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS`.
- `filter_thin_margin_results(results, min_profit_margin_bps) -> (kept, dropped_count)`
  with the integer-exact comparison `profit * BPS_DENOM >= opt_input * bps` (no float),
  matching the Python edge cases (`opt_input == 0` keeps; `<=0` threshold disables).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests vs the Python functions over a revert-data fixture corpus.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Byte/label parity check vs the Python `classify_revert` + `filter_thin_margin_results`.

## Non-goals
- `format_sim_diag_line` (stays-Python display).
- The full simulation pipeline (Simulation epic `5LLJHX`).
- PyO3 wrapper + routing `classify_revert` callsites through Rust (cutover task).

## Dependencies
- Standalone (pure data). Co-located in `degenbot-executor` (or `degenbot-decoders`) once
  that crate lands.

data.title: 2. Core: `verify_v3_liquidity_on_chain_on_conn` in degenbot-pool-updater
data.body:
## Goal
- Implement the V3 on-chain-truth verify core in `rust/crates/degenbot-pool-updater/src/verify.rs`: read a pool's `liquidity_positions` + `initialization_maps` rows from a borrowed `Connection`, batch `ticks(tick)` + `tickBitmap(word)` calls via `multicall3_batch`, + return a named divergence list.
## Context
- Mirror `rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/verify.rs` structurally: a `PositionRow`-style load fn, a `PositionDivergence`-style output enum (`V3LiquidityDivergence` with variants `TickGross`, `TickNet`, `BitmapWord`, `ExtraDbTick`, `MissingDbTick`), a multicall batch + stride-map-back, `parse_u256`/`decode_uint256_return`-style helpers (reuse the aave ones if they're in a shared location, else copy — they're trivial).
- Selectors (verified via `cast sig`): `ticks(int24)` = `0xf30dba93`, `tickBitmap(int16)` = `0x5339c296`. Calldata = `selector(4) + 32-byte left-padded arg` (36 bytes) — identical to the aave `build_call_data` shape (selector + left-padded address; here the arg is int24/int16, same left-pad).
- `multicall3_batch` is in `degenbot-rpc::multicall3` + takes `&[(Address, Bytes)]` + `Option<u64>` block; it already degrades to sequential `eth_call` on failure. The pool contract `Address` comes from `pools.address` (stored EIP-55 checksummed; parse via `Address::parse_checksummed` or `.parse()`).
- The bitmap `$word` column is `i32` in cl-math but `i64`/`INTEGER` in the DB schema (`initialization_maps.word`). `tickBitmap` takes `int16` — cast the DB `word` to `i16` for the calldata. The `pools.tick_spacing` is needed to derive which stored word a DB tick belongs to only for the cross-check, NOT for the straight `tickBitmap(word)` compare (the DB already stores `word`).
- DB read: `SELECT tick, liquidity_net, liquidity_gross FROM liquidity_positions WHERE pool_id = ?1` + `SELECT word, bitmap FROM initialization_maps WHERE pool_id = ?1` (the same selects `fetch_v3_liquidity_map_on_conn` uses). `liquidity_net` is a signed-decimal `VARCHAR(78)` (decode with the existing `decode_i256`); `liquidity_gross` + `bitmap` are decimal/hex `VARCHAR(78)` (decode with `decode_u256`); `u256_to_u128` narrows gross for the on-chain `uint128` compare (V3 `liquidityGross` is 128-bit, matching the cl-math gross type).
- Re-export `verify` from `lib.rs`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- `pub async fn verify_v3_liquidity_on_chain_on_conn(conn, provider, chain_id, pool_address, block_number, ticks_filter: Option<&[i32]>) -> Result<Vec<V3LiquidityDivergence>, RunError>` exists + is re-exported.
- `ticks_filter = None` verifies ALL stored ticks+bitmap-words; `Some(set)` verifies only those ticks (and the bitmap words they fall in).
- A DB tick whose on-chain `ticks()` reverts/returns `initialized=false` → `ExtraDbTick` divergence. A stored bitmap word whose on-chain `tickBitmap(word)` differs → `BitmapWord` divergence. `liquidityGross`/`liquidityNet` mismatch → `TickGross`/`TickNet`.
- README `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (zero `pyo3` in `degenbot-pool-updater`).
## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-pool-updater` (incl. new unit tests below).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -- --deny warnings`.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`.

data.title: [sim] A5 — Route example sim through the seam; delete the Python copy
data.body:
## Goal
- Rewrite the example's per-block dispatch to call `dispatch_profitable_py`,
  then `dispatch_and_submit_py` on `outcome.gas_profitable`. Delete the
  Python `simulate_one` (846 lines), `dispatch_profitable_results` (1055
  lines), and `build_simulation_state_overrides`.

## Context
- Example hot loop (post-candidate-1):
  ```python
  candidates = [PyDispatchCandidate(pid, inp, prof, ho, sb,
                    engine_registry.paths[pid], opts)
                for (pid, inp, prof, ho, _ci, sb) in results[:MAX_SIMULATE_CONCURRENT]]
  outcome = await dispatch_profitable_py(
      candidates, context=self._sim_ctx, dispatcher=self.dispatcher,
      current_block=block, min_profit_net=MIN_PROFIT_NET,
      min_profit_margin_bps=MIN_PROFIT_MARGIN_BPS)
  _render_sim_summary(outcome)  # ports the existing [sim] line from fail_buckets + counts
  records = await dispatch_and_submit_py(
      candidates=outcome.gas_profitable, dispatcher=self.dispatcher,
      provider=self.async_alloy, signer=self.signer,
      operator_nonce=self.operator_nonce, current_block=block,
      dry_run=self.dry_run, inject_code=INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE)
  ```
- `_render_sim_summary(outcome)` ports the existing `[sim] … N failed … by
  reason: {breakdown}` formatting (D4, stays Python).
- Deleted functions also remove their `web3.Web3.keccak(text=...)` sim-side
  selector computations (`execute`/`getEthBalance`/`balanceOf(address,uint256)`
  — those selectors live in the Rust crate's `calldata.rs`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `simulate_one`, `dispatch_profitable_results`, `build_simulation_state_overrides`
  removed from the example; the sim path reaches the chain only via the Rust
  crate.
- `_render_sim_summary` reproduces the prior `[sim]` log line format from
  `PyDispatchOutcome` fields.
- The example runs end-to-end against a fork (dry-run) and produces the same
  profitability decisions as before (per the parity test A6).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (example smoke / parity)
- `just lint`

> **Done** — A5 (rewire + delete) complete. Fork parity validation defers to A6 (`BBC666`).

## What landed

Four commits, all green (`just test-all` 3170 passed / 30 skipped, `just lint` clean, `check-no-pyo3-in-cores` clean):

- `cdd0f324` — **sl1 infrastructure**: `PySubmitCandidate` getters (`path_id`, `gross_profit`, `net_profit`, `gas_used`, `priority_fee`) + `PyDispatchOutcome.path_infos` getter + the Rust→Python `PathInfo` reverse converter (`path_info_to_py`) in `executor/mod.rs`. Decision 1 = B: the outcome re-derives `PathInfo` from the held join map so `_render_profit_logs` can render per-hop detail.
- `89eef882` — **sl2 rewire**: `BackrunSession.start()` builds a `PySimulateContext` once + threads it through `consume_result_batches` → `_apply_result_if_ready` → `_dispatch_profitable`. `_dispatch_profitable` builds the `PyDispatchCandidate` list from engine results, calls `dispatch_profitable_py` (simulate) then `dispatch_and_submit_py` (submit). `_render_sim_summary` + `_render_profit_logs` port the `[sim]`/`[profit]` summaries off the Rust `PyDispatchOutcome`. The `_DRY_RUN_OPERATOR_*` key fix (valid secp256k1 scalar) lands here — the eager `PyTxSigner` rejects the former all-zero placeholder.
- `494be161` — **sl2 delete**: `dispatch_profitable_results` (~1055 lines, incl. nested `simulate_one` + the `_sim_log`/`_tally_fail`/`_write_jsonl`/`_dump_state_for_revert`/`_emit_sim_diag` helpers), `build_simulation_state_overrides`, `_compute_priority_fee`, `encode_balanceof_calldata` + `BALANCEOF_SELECTOR`. -1219 lines. Orphaned imports removed (`eth_abi`, `web3`/`Web3`/`Web3Exception`/`web3.types`, `HexBytes`, `classify_revert`, `format_sim_diag_line`, `fits_int128`).
- `c1ad42a5` — **sl2 fallout**: `test_executor_delegate_spy.py::test_symbol_called_via_degenbot_rs` replaced (the five encoder/warmup symbols moved INTO the Rust core; the example routes via `dispatch_profitable_py`+`dispatch_and_submit_py` now). `BackrunSession.start()` tolerates a non-Alloy `async_w3` (defers `_sim_ctx` to None — production is Alloy-backed + eager; test-only path). `_FakeAsyncW3.as_async_alloy()` added.

## What stays (decision A5 plan)
- `format_failure_breakdown` — pure renderer `_render_sim_summary` plugs into.
- `_load_executor_runtime_bytecode` — the `PySimulateContext` reads the runtime bytecode file (`stays-python` disposition A2).
- `eth_backrun_helpers` re-exports (`PathInfo`/`build_hops_from_pools` etc.) + `filter_thin_margin_results` — OUT of A5's deletion scope (the Python `EngineRegistry` still builds Python `PathInfo`s; the `extract_path_info` seam extracts them into Rust at `PyDispatchCandidate` construction). Their retirement is a separate concern (the thin-margin filter now also runs in the Rust `dispatch_profitable_py`, but the Python helper + its tests remain as a standalone utility).

## Open for A6 (parity) + A7 (soak)
- A6 (`BBC666`): the end-to-end fork parity validation. A5's "same profitability decisions" acceptance is best validated alongside A6's mock-transport parity corpus — the rewire + delete here prove the SEAM routes + the Python copy is gone, but don't yet prove decision-parity against the deleted implementation (that needs A6's recorded-int corpus).
- The `[profit]`/`[sim-ok]` per-hop-detail logs render via `outcome.path_infos` (Decision 1 = B) — A6 should verify the hop detail round-trips correctly against a real sim corpus.

data.title: Batch UniswapEngine::fetch_onchain cross-hop via multicall3
data.body:
## Goal
- Collapse `UniswapEngine::fetch_onchain` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/diagnostic.rs` ≈line 748) — which today loops `for hop in &mut self.hops { fetch_hop_onchain(...).await }` with each hop issuing up to 2 serial eth_calls (slot0+liquidity for V3/V4, getReserves for V2) — into ONE cross-hop multicall3 batch (the hops' targets differ but multicall3_batch accepts heterogeneous `(target, calldata)`). For an N-hop path: today up to 2N serial calls → after: 1 batch call (if ≤1024 sub-calls total).

## Context
- Refactor `fetch_v2_onchain` / `fetch_v3_onchain` / `fetch_v4_onchain` (lines 929 / 996 / 1090) to separate three stages currently interleaved: (a) `build_calls(...) -> Vec<(Address, Bytes)>` (the sub-calls the hop needs — v2: 1 call getReserves; v3: 2 calls slot0+liquidity; v4: 2 calls getSlot0+getLiquidity), (b) dispatch (today a serial eth_call per sub-call), (c) `decode(&[MulticallResult]) -> Outcome`. `fetch_onchain` then: collect ALL hops' build_calls outputs, batch-dispatch once, slice the results back to each hop, run each hop's decode.
- A v4 hop with `state_view == None` is skipped from the batch entirely (today it short-circuits returning `FetchOutcome { onchain_state: None, messages: ["V4 on-chain fetch skipped: no StateView address provided"] }` — preserve that; don't add it to the batch).
- Per-hop failure handling today: `hop.diff.push(format!("on-chain fetch failed: {e}"))` on a fetch error. With batching, a reverted sub-call is `success=false`; the matching hop's decode sees a too-short/empty return → push the SAME "on-chain fetch failed" message (preserve today's per-hop diagnostic granularity). A whole-batch dispatch failure degrades to the sequential fallback inside `multicall3_batch`, so a transport error still surfaces per-sub-call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- For an N-hop path (any mix of v2/v3/v4 hops with non-None state_view), `fetch_onchain` issues exactly ONE eth_call to MULTICALL3_ADDRESS (instead of up to 2N), as long as total sub-calls ≤ 1024.
- v4 hop with `state_view == None` skipped (message preserved — not added to the batch).
- A reverted sub-call surfaces as "on-chain fetch failed" on the matching hop via `hop.diff.push`, preserving today's per-hop diagnostic.
- The existing `compute_field_diffs` + `apply_onchain_fetch` + `refresh_v2_recompute_onchain` + `refresh_v3v4_recompute_onchain` wiring in `fetch_onchain` is unchanged — only the dispatch stage changes.
- Integration test with MockTransport scripting a 3-hop path (v2 + v3 + v4-with-StateView), asserting exactly ONE eth_call total and correct per-hop `onchain_state` population (slot0/liquidity/reserves decoded to the seeded on-chain values).
- Existing diagnostic tests pass (search `cargo test -p degenbot-bot diagnostic`).

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot diagnostic`
- `cargo clippy -p degenbot-bot --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `just test-rust`

## Context

data.title: [sim] A2 — PySimulateContext + PyDispatchCandidate + result pyclasses
data.body:
## Goal
- Implement the PyO3 seam's pyclasses: `PySimulateContext` (config bag),
  `PyDispatchCandidate` (builder), and the result wrap classes
  `PyDispatchOutcome` (public, read-only) + `PySimResult` (internal — built
  and immediately converted to `PySubmitCandidate`, never returned to Python).

## Context
- `PySimulateContext` mirrors `PyDispatcher::for_block` but session-long:
  holds `Arc<AlloyProvider>` (cloned via `provider_arc()` from a
  `&PyAsyncAlloyProvider` at construction) + `executor_owner`/`executor_address`/
  `weth_address`/`pool_manager_address`/`multicall3_address`/`inject_code`/
  `injected_address`/`executor_runtime_bytecode: Bytes`.
- `PyDispatchCandidate` mirrors `PySubmitCandidate`'s `#[new]`: holds
  `path_id`, `optimal_input`, `inp`/`engine_profit`/`hop_outputs`/`solve_block`/
  `path_info` (Python dataclass, extracted via `extract_path_info` like the
  executor seam), `encode_options` (built from bool flags).
- `PyDispatchOutcome`: `gas_profitable: list[PySubmitCandidate]` (direct handoff
  to `dispatch_and_submit_py`), `gas_unprofitable_count`/`exception_count`/
  `fail_count`/`candidate_count`/`suppressed_count`/`thin_dropped: int` (the
  `[sim]` summary line), `fail_buckets: dict[str,int]` (D4 stays-python
  rendering input). `PySimResult` is the internal join source.
- Mirror the `submission/` pyclass GIL discipline: hold `Arc<...>`, release GIL
  for core calls. **No business logic** in these classes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All four pyclasses compile and register in `simulation/mod.rs`.
- `PySimulateContext::#[new]` accepts `(provider: &PyAsyncAlloyProvider,
  executor_owner: str, executor_address: str, weth_address: str,
  pool_manager_address: str, multicall3_address: str, inject_code: bool,
  executor_runtime_bytecode: bytes, injected_address: Option<str>)` and clones
  the provider arc.
- `PySimResult` is **not** exposed in the `.pyi` (internal only).

## Validation Gates
- `just lint-rust`
- `just test-rust`

> **Done** — committed.

## What landed
- `simulation/{context,candidate,outcome}.rs` + updated `simulation/mod.rs`
  (registers the three pyclasses).
- `executor/mod.rs`: `extract_path_info` + `HopTypes` lifted to `pub(crate)`
  for reuse (DRY — the candidate must encode byte-for-byte like the encode seam).
- `.pyi` stubs + `__all__` entries for the three classes.
- `tests/rust/test_simulation_seam_classes.py`: 8 constructor-shape smoke
  tests (offline — `AlloyProvider` lazy HTTP transport, no dial).

## Design deviation (noted)
- `PySimResult` is NOT a pyclass. The plan's A2 list mentioned it as
  "internal," but since it never crosses to Python (the A4 join writes
  `SimResult` straight through to `PySubmitCandidate`), it would be dead
  surface. A4 uses the core `SimResult` directly. The `PyDispatchOutcome` doc
  comment records this decision.

## Dead-code allow
- `PySimulateContext` fields + `PyDispatchCandidate.inner` + `from_join` are
  `#[allow(dead_code)]` until A4 lands (A4 reads them; A3 must precede A4 per
  the graph). Mirrors the submission seam's `inner_arc` precedent.

## Validation (gates green)
- `just lint-rust` (clippy + fmt, all features, -D warnings).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (simulation crate stays pyo3-free).
- `just lint` (ruff + fmt-check + ty + markdownlint) — fixed 2 fmt issues
  (import order + trailing newline) and a bogus `PyDiagnosticQuery` `__all__`
  typo I introduced then removed.
- 8/8 new smoke tests pass; 54/54 in the provider+simulation sweep.

## Key shapes (for A3/A4 reference)
- `PySimulateContext` holds `Arc<AlloyProvider>` (cloned via `provider_arc()`)
  + owned addresses/bytes + precomputed `WarmupSlots`. A4 constructs a borrowed
  `SimulateContext { provider: &*arc, ... }` INSIDE the async block so the
  future stays `'static`.
- `dispatch_profitable_results` takes `&mut PathSuppression` (bookends-only
  access, dormant across the fan-out) — confirms A3's plan: extract into its
  own `Arc<Mutex<PathSuppression>>`; the wrapper locks it once per call
  (uncontended during the fan-out — the submission seam never touches
  PathSuppression). A4 holds the lock across the core call.
- `PyDispatchOutcome::from_join(gas_profitable: Vec<SubmitCandidate>, outcome:
  &DispatchOutcome)` — A4's result-wrap calls this after the SimResult join.

data.title: Aave V3 operations parser: liquidation engine (single/combined/separate-burn patterns)
data.body:
# HQF5NQ-B — Aave V3 operations parser: the liquidation engine

> **Split sibling of HQF5NQ (the single-shot OPERATIONSPARSER).**
> Deps on HQF5NQ (A: parser-core + standard builders) — needs A's
> `Operation`/`OperationType`/`ScaledTokenEvent`/`ScaledTokenEventType` types +
> A's `_amounts_match` + A's `_collect_*` helpers + the `parse()` scaffold.
> Ships AFTER A. This is the §4.2-drift-risk concentration — isolated so it
> can be cross-checked against §4.2 fixtures on its own without contaminating
> the standard-builder port.

## Goal

Port the LiquidationCall builder + the SINGLE/COMBINED_BURN/SEPARATE_BURNS
pattern detection + the pre-analysis dicts from the Python
`operations_parser.py` + `liquidation_patterns.py`. This is the gnarliest
single piece of the parser (~160 LoC for `_create_liquidation_operation`
with 5 nested branches + the pattern-detection state). The §4.2 cross-check
(U5YIBG) has ZERO tolerance for heuristic drift here — the COMBINED_BURN vs
SEPARATE_BURNS discrimination is the bit that's bitten ports before.

## Scope (this task)

### 1. `_create_liquidation_operation` (mirror the Python `_create_liquidation_operation`)
The ~160-LoC gnarly fn with 5 nested branches. Takes the Pool `LiquidationCall`
event + the matched ScaledToken events (collateral Transfers/Burns + debt Burns)
+ builds the `Operation { operation_type: Liquidation, ... }`. Flag if a branch
needs a type not in A's `Operation`/`ScaledTokenEvent` definitions — escalate
rather than extending A's types mid-B.

### 2. `_collect_debt_burns` — the SINGLE/COMBINED_BURN/SEPARATE_BURNS pattern detection
The zero-tolerance §4.2-drift-critical fn. Classifies the debt-burn structure:
- **SINGLE**: one LiquidationCall → one debt Burn (the common case).
- **COMBINED_BURN**: one LiquidationCall → one debt Burn that covers multiple liquidations (the burn amount is the sum).
- **SEPARATE_BURNS**: one LiquidationCall → multiple debt Burns (one per liquidation).
Detection is via `liquidation_count` vs `total_burn_count` vs `liquidation_position`. Port the discrimination EXACTLY — §4.2 parity depends on it.

### 3. `_collect_collateral_events` — the collateral_burn vs collateral_transfers split
Distinguish the aToken Burn (the liquidated collateral) from the aToken Transfers (collateral moved to the liquidator). Mirror the Python split.

### 4. `_analyze_liquidation_scenarios` + `_analyze_user_liquidation_count` — the pre-analysis dicts
The pre-computed maps the LiquidationCall builder consults (per-user liquidation counts, per-position burn aggregates). Port the dict construction + the lookup keys EXACTLY.

### 5. `_preprocess_liquidation_aggregates` + `detect_liquidation_patterns` (mirror `liquidation_patterns.py`)
The `LiquidationPattern`/`LiquidationPatternGroup`/`LiquidationContext` state (type stubs land in A; B extends them). The pattern-context detection that feeds the LiquidationCall builder's branch selection.

### 6. The GHO liquidation branch
The GHO bad-debt multi-asset case (a GHO-vToken Burn in a liquidation where the debt is GHO). The `GHO_DEBT_INTEREST` vToken handling. Coordinate with RYKCC4's GHO apply fns + A's `ScaledTokenEventType` classification.

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged)

The parser writes through `&Connection` (the chunk's tx). On `Err`, whole-chunk revert.

## Architectural calls I own (escalate, don't guess)

- **Type-extension needs:** if a branch in `_create_liquidation_operation` needs a field not in A's `Operation`/`ScaledTokenEvent`/`LiquidationPattern` definitions, escalate — do NOT extend A's types mid-B without my authorization (it would invalidate A's landed contract). The right fix is either (a) the field was missing from A's definitions (A needs an amend), or (b) the field is B-local (a B-only extension type).
- **The COMBINED_BURN aggregation:** if the sum-of-burns computation has a rounding subtlety (the individual burns may round differently than the aggregate), escalate — this is a §4.2-drift risk the cross-check will catch.

## Validation gates (paste tail in callback)

- `just test-rust` (new liquidation tests + all prior tests still green — A's parser-core + standard builders must remain green after B extends `LiquidationPattern`/`LiquidationContext`)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact)
- `just lint-rust` (clippy --deny warnings)
- `just format`

## Test fixtures (the §4.2 zero-drift surface)

Unit tests with the LiquidationCall fixtures covering:
- The SINGLE case (one LiquidationCall → one debt Burn).
- The COMBINED_BURN case (one debt Burn covering multiple liquidations).
- The SEPARATE_BURNS case (multiple debt Burns for one LiquidationCall).
- The GHO bad-debt multi-asset case.
- The multi-liquidation user with multiple debt assets.
- The collateral_burn vs collateral_transfers split (aToken Burn + aToken Transfer in the same liquidation).

## Not touched (per non-goals)

- The parser-core + standard builders → HQF5NQ (A).
- The apply dispatch glue (`process_transaction` + `Operation`→`AaveChunkEvent` construction) → HQF5NQ-C.
- The orchestrator → 6SWY4R.
- Python cutover → AVS4DR.
- §4.2 parity → U5YIBG (the §4.2 cross-check is the final arbiter).
- Python `operations_parser.py`/`liquidation_patterns.py` — unchanged (AVS4DR deletes).

## Operating rules

1. You own implementation; I own sequencing/state/architectural calls.
2. **No `git commit` without my explicit authorization.** Make changes; run gates; report DONE/BLOCKED. (Leave `.ergo/plan-alloyprovider-refactor.md` untracked.)
3. Report via `link_send` to me (t-d479) with `triggerTurn:true`. Include diff summary, gate results, open questions, flagged decisions.
4. Root AGENTS.md is the canonical ref.

data.title: Relax subscribe() phase precondition for post-snapshot-load
data.body:
## Goal
- Allow `subscribe()` to be called from `Created` OR `SnapshotLoaded`, so construction-time snapshot loading (`Created → SnapshotLoaded`) can precede `subscribe()`.

## Context
- Decision D3(a): construction-time loading.
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/pump.rs::subscribe` requires `EnginePhase::Created` (L137–141). After A4's construction-time load sets `SnapshotLoaded`, subscribe would currently fail this precondition.
- `begin_v3_snapshot_stream` already accepts `Created` or `Subscribed` (L37: `require_before(Resumed)`) — mirror that leniency for `subscribe`.
- Update the phase-machine doc comment in `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/mod.rs` (the `EnginePhase` transitions diagram) and `block_pump.rs` module docs that assert "Python must run backfill AFTER subscribe() returns but BEFORE resume()" — the ordering invariant still holds (backfill before resume), but snapshot-load is now allowed pre-subscribe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `subscribe()` accepts `Created` or `SnapshotLoaded`; rejects `Subscribed`/`Backfilled`/`Resumed` with the existing error message shape.
- Tests: subscribe-from-Created still works; subscribe-after-`load_snapshot_from_db` works; subscribe-after-subscribe still errors.
- Phase-machine doc updated to show `Created ──load_snapshot_from_db──► SnapshotLoaded ──subscribe()──► Subscribed` as a legal path (alongside the existing `Created ──subscribe()──► Subscribed`).

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test -p degenbot-bot phase`
- `just test-rust-python`

## Completion
- Added `EnginePhase::allow_subscribe(method_name) -> Result<(), String>` in `crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/mod.rs` — accepts `Created` (legacy subscribe-first path) OR `SnapshotLoaded` (construction-time-load path), rejects Subscribed/Backfilled/Resumed.
- The numeric ordering (SnapshotLoaded=2 > Subscribed=1) cannot express this with `require`/`require_before`, so explicit match.
- pyo3 `subscribe()` now calls `allow_subscribe` instead of `require(Created)`.
- Updated phase-machine doc comment to show the new `Created → load_snapshot_from_db → SnapshotLoaded → subscribe → Subscribed` path; updated block_pump.rs critical-ordering note (Python no longer orchestrates backfill post-epic).
- TDD: 1 core test `allow_subscribe_accepts_created_and_snapshot_loaded`.

Gates: cargo test -p degenbot-bot (328 passed), clippy clean, no-pyo3 OK, test-rust-python (276 passed).

data.title: Retarget cli/aave/{transaction_processor,operations_parser,token_processor}.py residual ORM callsites (Sub-step C, slice 3)
data.body:
# Retarget `cli/aave/{transaction_processor,operations_parser,token_processor}.py` residual ORM callsites (Sub-step C, slice 3)

## Goal
- Sub-step C slice 3 of the Aave-writer port (the cleanup pass): audit + retarget the **residual ORM write callsites** in the three remaining `cli/aave/` writer-side files — `transaction_processor.py` (1 ORM call), `operations_parser.py` (8 calls), `token_processor.py` (0 write calls — confirm read-only or already-clean) — to the Rust seam where they're real writes, OR confirm they're read-path `scalar(select(...))` that belongs in the (already-Rust-owned) read-back path and route them through `PyDatabasePositionQuery`.

## Context
- **Premature close recap.** RQXEKH AC called for delegating shells + deleted inline ORM bodies across `cli/aave/**`; slices 1 (db_*.py) + 2 (event_handlers.py) handed the bulk of the writes over. This slice catches the long tail.
- **Why this is a sibling and not folded into slice 1/2.** The `transaction_processor.py` + `operations_parser.py` files are the **logic layer** (the operations parser is 2,801 lines — parses tx events into logical operations based on asset flows; the transaction processor orchestrates the per-tx apply). Their ORM calls are a mix of:
  1. **Writes** that should delegate to a `db_get_or_create_*` / `db_apply_*` (slice 1/2 seam) but happen in-line in the tx flow rather than via `db_*.py`/`event_handlers.py`. These need to route through the Rust seam.
  2. **Reads** (`session.scalar(select(AaveV3User).where(...))` to look up an existing user/position/asset for the parse/apply decision) that belong in the `PyDatabasePositionQuery` read-back path (already Rust-owned per OKKMG5) and should route through it rather than re-implementing the select.
  3. **Session-management** (`session.commit()` at chunk boundaries) — `stays-python` (driver-side orchestration; `aave_update` owns the commit cadence).
- **The audit produces a per-callsite disposition** (`write→seam` / `read→PyDatabasePositionQuery` / `commit→stays`) before any code change. The disposition document goes in the task body.
- **Rubric (§2.1).** type=heavy Python objects (the operations parser does record-flow modeling, not pure numeric transform) — most of these files are `stays-python` logic; this slice only retargets the I/O callsites. I/O=ORM (the writes/reads); eco=SQLAlchemy (for the `session.commit` orchestrator calls).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **The audit (in the task body, before code change):** for each of the ~9 ORM calls across `transaction_processor.py` + `operations_parser.py` (and the 0 in `token_processor.py` — confirmed already non-writing), record `file:line | call shape | disposition | rationale`. Run `rg -n "session\.(add|scalar|commit|flush|execute)" src/degenbot/cli/aave/{transaction_processor,operations_parser,token_processor}.py` and record every match.
- [ ] Every dispositioned **write** callsite (group 1) routes through the corresponding `db_get_or_create_*` / `db_apply_*` seam fn (sibling 2QPBUJ) — either directly OR via the slice-1 `db_*.py` shell (sibling OPVK2C) if the call fits a `get_or_create_*` shape naturally.
- [ ] Every dispositioned **read** callsite (group 2) routes through `PyDatabasePositionQuery` (the OKKMG5 read-back seam) — opened from `database_path` like the analysis path. (If a read is on a table the read-back seam doesn't cover yet, that's a feature gap to flag in the body, not silently leave the ORM call in place.)
- [ ] `stays-python` callsites (group 3 — `session.commit()` / `session.rollback()` at chunk boundaries) stay — only noted in the audit.
- [ ] After the retarget, `rg -n "session\.add\b" src/degenbot/cli/aave/{transaction_processor,operations_parser,token_processor}.py` returns empty (no inline ORM writes left from group 1). `session.scalar` may remain ONLY for the confirmed read-group callsites that have no `PyDatabasePositionQuery` route yet (flagged in the body — a feature gap, owned by a future OKKMG5 follow-up).
- [ ] The `cli/aave/` test suite passes (no behavior change — same DB state, different write path).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (the `cli/aave/` suite + `db_verification`).
- `just lint-python` + `just format`.
- `just test-rust-python` (if any `tests/rust/` test exercises these files).

## Non-goals
- The PyO3 seam (sibling 2QPBUJ).
- The `db_*.py` slice (sibling OPVK2C) — assumed landed so this slice's writes can route through those shells.
- The `event_handlers.py` slice (sibling YEM6MN) — assumed landed.
- The `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch — `stays-python`.
- The §4.2 final parity gate (sibling — runs after this slice).
- **Extending `PyDatabasePositionQuery` to cover new read tables** — if the audit surfaces a gap, that's a separate OKKMG5 follow-up task (under AZGJUN or its own epic), NOT this slice.

## Sequencing
- **Depends on:** siblings OPVK2C (slice 1) + YEM6MN (slice 2) — needs both shells landed to know which residual callsites are writes (route via them) vs reads (route via PyDatabasePositionQuery).
- **Unblocks:** the parity-gate sibling (final close-out runs on the post-retarget state).

data.title: Post-LC-fix residual: identical 0.476% residual ratio on LC-class collateral (users 0x23dB, 0x87A6) — diagnostic
data.body:
# Post-LC-fix residual: identical 0.476% residual ratio on LC-class collateral

## Scope

After `fix(aave): guard collect_collateral_events burn-side pair Transfer`
(landed as commit `1cf6578d`) cleared the LC double-debit bulk on the
two LC-class positions, BOTH positions retain a residual that is
**EXACTLY 0.476% of the pre-fix delta**:

| Position | asset | user             | pre_delta       | post-residual  | ratio        |
|----------|-------|------------------|-----------------|----------------|--------------|
| #1       | WETH  | 0x23dB...Da2D    | -8.612e17 (~39%)| -4.103e15      | 0.00476 (0.476%) |
| #6       | WETH  | 0x87A6...0d9D    | -1.221e18 (~77%)| -5.815e15      | 0.00476 (0.476%) |

Identical residual ratio across TWO UNRELATED LiquidationCalls on
DIFFERENT users' WETH collateral. That's the load-bearing observation
this task must root-cause.

## Diagnostic goal — identify the mechanism producing a constant-percentage residue on LC-class collateral

NOT a paired-BT-scaled-amount hypothesis. Paired-BT-scaled-amount would
produce residuals tied to per-LC transfer amounts (different absolute
deltas, no shared ratio). The fixed 0.476% ratio across both LC-class
positions instead suggests one of:

  - a scaling-factor discrepancy (constant-percentage, applied to
    LC-affected collateral in Rust but not Python — or vice versa);
  - a ray/floor at the apply-step that computes 0.476% differently for
    LC-class collateral burns than the standalone Transfer path;
  - the LC's own `liquidationCall` math applying a small liquidation
    bonus or LT scaling the standalone Transfer path doesn't;
  - an interest-index update timing (apply-step compute rate differs
    from standalone's rate at the chunk boundary).

## Mechanism

Inspect the actual post-LC operations applied to users 0x23dB and
0x87A6: index-update path, subsequent CollateralMint/Burn/Transfer in
the SAME chunk where the LC was applied. Bisect (`ergo bisect`-
equivalent over the chunk logs) to the earliest event where the
post-LC DB diverges from on-chain scaledBalanceOf.

Cross-reference `src/degenbot/cli/aave/event_handlers.py` and
`operations_parser.py` for what the Python LiquidationCall handler
does in the apply-step that the Rust handler omits (or computes
differently — e.g., a scaling factor applied to the burn-side pair, a
liquidation bonus in the LC's own math, a ray-floor timing difference).

## Acceptance

  - For BOTH positions, identify the single mechanism producing the
    identical 0.476% residual.
  - If it's a real Rust-vs-Python apply-step divergence → file a
    sibling fix-task with a regression test (RED: 0.476% mismatch;
    GREEN: post-fix == on-chain == Python writer's result).
  - If it's a shared Rust-vs-Python rounding artifact (e.g., the
    Python writer also drifts at 0.476% because both Rust + Python
    make the same ray-floor choice) → document as such; no fix
    follow-up (on-chain truth is the gate, VV5OTV).

## Sequencing

  - Depends on: `1cf6578d` (the LC fix landed — without it, the LC
    bulk masks/unmasks this residual in confusing ways).
  - Blocks: HLYWI6 (16596000 GREEN — these residuals must be resolved
    or documented-fixed before HLYWI6 "GREEN" is meaningful).
  - 44JTVN (chunk-12 p534 crash at ~16601100) stays sequenced AFTER
    HLYWI6; this task does not block 44JTVN.

data.title: Aave writer §4.2 parity gate + _decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap oracle retirement (Sub-step C close-out)
data.body:
# Aave writer §4.2 parity gate + `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` oracle retirement (Sub-step C close-out)

## Goal
- The final close-out of the Aave-writer three-layer port (RQXEKH): **§4.2 red-green parity** of the Rust-backed Aave write path against the Python oracle trajectory over a representative Aave event sequence, plus **§4.3 oracle retirement** of `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` (renamed in slice 2 as the oracle) and any parity-test harness comparing two live implementations once green. The gate's GREEN is the precondition for closing RQXEKH `done` for real this time.

## Context
- **Premature close recap.** RQXEKH was marked `done` without a §4.2 record (contrast QJSCA5 — "§4.3 liquidity-updater slice landed"). This sibling is the §4.2 / §4.3 gate the migration guide (§4.2, §4.3) requires.
- **Why §4.2 matters here specifically.** The Aave write path is the most event-rich of all the DB-writer ports (29 ORM calls in `event_handlers.py` alone across `_process_*` handlers for 11 different ReserveConfig / EMode / collateral / oracle events); a bit-for-bit mismatch between the Rust-emitted `aave_*` rows and the prior Python ORM trajectory would surface as silent state drift in the analysis pipeline (the `position risk` health-factor calc reads these rows via `PyDatabasePositionQuery`, already cut over — so a Rust-write → Rust-read round trip masks divergence from the historical Python state).
- **The red-green shape (per migration guide §4.2):**
  1. **Red (precondition from slices 1–3):** the Rust write path already lands in slices 1–3 against the existing `cli/aave/` test suite (which compares DB state, not the byte-level write path). Sufficient for slices to be `done` individually, but does NOT prove byte-for-byte Rust-vs-Python-oracle parity.
  2. **Green (this gate):** run a fixture Aave event sequence (the same corpus the `db_verification.py` invariants check — `verify_gho_discount_amounts`, `verify_stk_aave_balances` — uses) through BOTH the Rust-backed driver AND a frozen Python-only driver snapshot; assert the `aave_*` row state is byte-identical (column-by-column, including `NULL` defaults and the `e_mode` / `gho_discount` / `stk_aave_balance` fields the writers set). This is the §4.2 cross-check the precedence (slices 5, 6, 11c for math ports) requires.
- **The `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` oracle (§4.3).** Slice 2 (sibling YEM6MN) renames the Python helper `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` → `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap_oracle` and routes the live call to `db_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap`. This gate's parity test asserts the Rust core's output matches the Python oracle field-for-field across the full Aave V3 reserve-config bit space (the §4.2 pin ports "the exact bit masks + shifts" per the `write.rs` docstring). Once GREEN, the oracle helper (`_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap_oracle`) + its parity test are deleted together (§4.3 — "retire the oracle with its tests, do not leave an equivalence harness comparing two live implementations").
- **The `db_verification.py` invariant checks.** `stays-python` per AZGJUN scope (`MPS3U7`), but they now read Rust-written rows — this gate asserts they pass against the green Rust path (the slices 1–3 already ran the existing test suite; this gate re-runs them with explicit assertion that the input rows were Rust-written, closing the lens).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fixture Aave event corpus (extend the existing `db_verification.py` fixtures OR add a new `tests/fixtures/aave_writer_parity/` corpus) covering all 11 `_process_*` handler event types + the get-or-create paths.
- [ ] Run the corpus through the Rust-backed driver (post slices 1–3) AND a frozen Python-only snapshot driver → assert the `aave_*` row state is byte-identical (column-by-column, including `NULL` defaults and the `e_mode` / `gho_discount` / `stk_aave_balance` / `last_update_block` fields). GREEN.
- [ ] `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` byte-for-byte parity asserted across the Aave V3 reserve-config bit space (ltv / liquidation-threshold / -bonus / decimals / active / frozen / borrowing-enabled / stable-rate / reserve-factor / borrow-cap / supply-cap / debt-ceiling / liquidation-protocol-fee / unbacked-mint-cap / e-mode-category-id / flash-loan / isolation-mode / borrowable-in-isolation — the full field set per the `write.rs` docstring). GREEN.

## Progress + re-scoping (as of b29f82a4 — Option B)

### Sub-criteria status
- **#1 (fixture corpus, 11+ handler event types + get-or-create paths)** — DONE via the `tests/aave/writer_parity/` harness (41 tests byte-for-byte across Rust vs Python).

No divergence. (Relocated verbatim from `tests/test_aave_bit_decode_parity.py` — 91%-similarity rename — into writer_parity in `93773fac`.)

  A 2nd anchor stays at `tests/rust/test_aave_writer_seam_parity.py:458::test_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap_returns_oracle_dict` — the PyO3-seam concern (specific known-bitmap field values), distinct from the Rust-vs-oracle field-for-field parity, so left in `tests/rust/`.

- **#4 (§4.3 retirement: delete the config-bitmap oracle + its parity test)** — DONE-AS-NO-OP (subsumed by CZM7TI). See the Option-B re-scoping below.
- **#5 (`db_verification.py` invariants against Rust-written rows)** — pending.
- **#6/#7 (close-out: re-close RQXEKH + migration-guide update mirroring QJSCA5)** — pending (#6/#7 may also fold into CZM7TI's sweep where applicable; sequence at the orchestrator's call).

### Option-B re-scoping (user decision, recorded)
