data.title: GHO rev-5 scaled-balance overshoot (×RAY stray multiply)
data.body:
## Goal
Pin and fix the single root cause of the 60-position GHO rev-5 (`variableDebtEthGHO`, vToken 0x786dBff3) scaled-balance overshoot surfaced by the clean 22.63M→23.1M re-drive against march_py.db@23.1M.

## Symptom (clean throwaway drive reverify_78358.db, from verified-clean 22.63M baseline)
- 60/5478 GHO rev-5 debt positions diverge; Rust balance ALWAYS too high; `last_index` matches Python/on-chain byte-exact (index tracking correct — only balance diverges).
- Magnitude: Rust ~1e51 vs Python ~1e22 (ratio ~1e28–1e30, non-constant ⇒ accumulated per event). 3099/5478 GHO positions end at exactly 0 in both (full-repayment guard masks the bug; that is why spot-checks of fully-repaid positions are meaningless).
- Repro position: user 0x71927529167fDE40EbD4D2aCdAbFc88afD340f35, GHO vToken 0x786dBff3, position_id 65158 (in reverify_78358.db): Rust 6803422951803914840226900798581461830281460821988, Python 38298601274558820130607, last_index 1143775633777399963731283945 (identical).
- Confirmed NOT: fixture poisoning (clean verified baseline), broken ray primitive (degenbot-evm-math::ray_mul is standard a*b/RAY), scaled-vs-actual confusion (index≈1.14, would be ~1.14× not 1e27×), routing (GHO correctly routes to gho_processor.rs via build_gho_chunk_event).

## Hypothesis (from orchestrator + contract verification)
A STRAY RAW INTEGER MULTIPLY by RAY (1e27) or by the index (1.14e27) on the GHO delta/apply path where `ray_mul` (= a*b/RAY) or `ray_div` (= a*RAY/b) was intended. Per-event ~1e47–1e48 ⇒ ~1e51 clustering over heavy borrowers. Suspect sites: (i) enrichment scaled_amount compute/path in build_gho_chunk_event (transaction_processor.rs:1105+), (ii) accrue_debt_on_action / get_discounted_balance discount_scaled in gho_processor.rs, (iii) the apply site that writes balance_delta to running/committed balance. The V5 no-discount burn/mint branches (gho_processor.rs ~358–405 mint, ~505–578 burn) use event_data.scaled_amount + self.ray_div/ray_mul (correct primitives) — feed-through would be clean.

## Constraints (inviolable)
- Fix at the EVENT-PROCESSING level only. NEVER edit/patch a DB value. Throwaway /tmp DBs only; re-drive from verified boundary to verify. No compare-harness changes; no rounding-band-aids; single root cause only.
- Distinct from crash #10 (crash #10 = baseline poisoning, already resolved as branch (a)).
- Flag the exact root-cause line for orchestrator review BEFORE changing processing code.

## Plan
1. Per-event trace on pos 65158 (throwaway build+DB): log event log_index/etype, ev.amount(value), balance_increase, index, enriched scaled_amount, prev_balance, prev_index, effective_discount, computed balance_delta (I256), running balance before+after. Drive 22.63M→23.1M.
2. Correlate against Python per-event deltas (Python on-chain-correct) for the same position; find FIRST divergent event.
3. Pinpoint the stray ×RAY line; propose (unwritten) fix; escalate to orchestrator for review before writing it.
4. On approval: implement fix (event-processing level), re-drive throwaway, verify 0 GHO rev-5 divergences vs march_py.db@23.1M, 0 NEW divergences elsewhere.

## ROOT CAUSE PINNED (airtight; no code changed yet)

**Line:** `rust/crates/degenbot-aave-updater/src/transaction_processor.rs`, `build_gho_chunk_event` (~line 1130):
```rust
let raw_amount = pool_event.map_or(ev.amount, extract_pool_amount_word0);
```
Uses `extract_pool_amount_word0` (word0) unconditionally for the GHO `scaled_amount` enrichment. For a GHO **BORROW** (`GhoDebtMint` / `op=GhoBorrow`) the paired `Pool.Borrow` event encodes the amount at **word1** (word0 = the borrower address). So `scaled_amount = ray_div(borrower_address, index)` ≈ 5.67e47 (bogus), instead of `ray_div(borrow_amount, index)` ≈ 4.44e20 (on-chain-correct).

**Proof (computed from the trace, blowup event logidx=700, GhoDebtMint):**
- value=503727852887279541202, bal_inc=3727852887279541202, index=1143532071192526597534024499
- scaled_amount=566999464514235617502525849100508903005499793313, delta=566999464514235617502525849100508903005499793313 (delta == scaled_amount → V5 CEIL branch used it)
- inferred raw_amount = scaled_amount × index / RAY = **0x71927529167fde40ebd4d2acdabfc88afd340f35** (the borrower address, 40 nibbles). 
- Correct scaled_amount would be ray_div(borrow_amount, index, Ceil) ≈ 4.44e20 (matches Python/on-chain).

**Why GHO-rev5-only + latent-then-activated:** the V5 BORROW branch (`gho_processor.rs:382`) `if !supports_discount && rounding.mint==Ceil && scaled_amount.is_some()` uses `scaled_amount` as the delta. rev4 (mint=HalfUp → condition false → `ray_div(value−bal_inc, index)` fallback) computes correct deltas, so the bogus `scaled_amount` is computed-but-UNUSED in rev4. rev5 (mint=Ceil → condition true) USES the bogus `scaled_amount` as the delta → first rev5 borrow after the rev4→rev5 cutover blows the balance. This explains: GHO-rev5-only, ~constant-e47 scaled_amount (= address÷index, constant numerator), `last_index` byte-exact (set from event.index, never multiplied), accumulated over subsequent borrows.

**Sanity for surrounding tables:** accounts for ALL 60 GHO rev-5 divergences + the 3,099 that masked to 0 (full-repayment guard). The 438 non-GHO +1..+14-wei divergences are a SEPARATE issue (standard processor path) — not addressed by this fix.

## PROPOSED FIX (unwritten; flagging for review before writing)
In `build_gho_chunk_event`, extract `raw_amount` per-op-type mirroring `extract_raw_amount_for_event` (`Supply|Borrow|GhoBorrow => extract_pool_amount_word1`; `Repay|RepayWithAtokens|Withdraw|GhoRepay => extract_pool_amount_word0`) instead of unconditional `extract_pool_amount_word0`. Verify the exact formula against Python's enrichment handler (`src/degenbot/aave/extraction.py` + `enrichment/handlers/borrow.py`) before writing. Does NOT change rev4 behavior (scaled_amount unused there). Trace instrumentation is env-gated (`DEGENBOT_TRACE_GHO`) + position-id-gated, OFF by default — will remove before the fix commit.

data.title: ADR-011: auto-healed Alembic retirement design record
data.body:
## Goal
Write `docs/adr/ADR-011-auto-healed-alembic-retirement.md` and update `AGENTS.md`.

## Body
Captures the **out-of-place dump-and-restore "heal" decision** — the durable, rugpull-protected Alembic retirement mechanism. Records the four alternatives considered and why heal-wins:

1. **In-place chain repair** (add missing `add_column`s, guard drops, batch-wraps alters across all 43 migrations) — large, fragile, spent on a retirement-bound artifact. Rejected.
2. **Squash to a single coherent baseline** — legitimate but mid-sized effort on something about to be deleted; `heal` makes forward-buildability irrelevant. Rejected as bridge.
3. **Hard retirement** (just delete Alembic + migrations) — strands every legacy DB at a stale/unrecognized state. Rejected (rugpull).
4. **Out-of-place heal** (this ADR) — read old DB read-only as raw SQLite, rebuild against the Rust head schema, copy rows preserving PKs + FK integrity + column mapping, stamp RustOwned directly (never runs Alembic code), atomic swap with `*.bak` backup. Selected.

## Decision record must capture
- The **column-mapping auto-derivation** approach: map derived at heal-time from `PRAGMA table_info(old)` vs `PRAGMA table_info(new db_create_new_database)`, plus an explicit `RENAME_OVERRIDES` constant for the handful of renamed columns (from `6a77c4e07151`, `a4f59783919f`, `5c8805573ab3`). NOT a hand-maintained 43-entry constant — survives head-schema drift.
- The **atomic-swap + `.bak` guarantee**: heal reads old read-only, writes new at temp path, swaps via `rename`; any failure leaves live DB untouched. Old preserved as `*.bak` for full recoverability.
- **Relationship to `cutover`** (`1b66da1f`, epic 2Z3Y46): `cutover` = fast in-place ownership flip assuming head schema; `heal` = general out-of-place rebuild, schema-agnostic. Both coexist. `heal` is the canonical Alembic-retirement mechanism for the 0.7.0 retirement task (T6).
- **Standalone-Rust placement** (ADR-005): heal logic + mapping + FK-order + swap all live in `degenbot-db` core; PyO3 seam is thin. `cargo add degenbot` consumers can call `heal_database(path)` directly.
- **Non-goal: auto-heal-on-open.** Opt-in through 0.7.0 via `degenbot database heal`. Auto-heal-on-open (mirroring eventual auto-cutover-on-open) deferred to 0.8 — a full out-of-place copy is too slow/surprising to trigger implicitly.

## AGENTS.md update
- Add ADR-011 to the ADR records list.
- Update the kill-list note for `src/degenbot/migrations/`: retirement is gated on **`heal` shipping + proven** (T5), not just on the 0.7.0 version bump. Reference this epic (TGIP5N) and T6.

## Acceptance
- `docs/adr/ADR-011-auto-healed-alembic-retirement.md` exists, follows the ADR format of ADR-010 (`020dffdf`/`48656121`).
- `AGENTS.md` ADR index includes ADR-011; kill-list entry for `src/degenbot/migrations/` notes the heal-gate.
- Markdown lint passes.

## Depends on
Nothing. Unblocks T2.

## Completion note
- Implemented by delegated worker t-f280 (orchestrator t-6ff7 verified). Committed `794ed97f`: `docs(adr): add ADR-011 auto-healed Alembic retirement` (2 files, +256/-2).

### Artifacts
- `docs/adr/ADR-011-auto-healed-alembic-retirement.md` (NEW, 254 lines) — design record mirroring ADR-010's format. Captures: the migration chain's structural incoherence (`311beed36e7b` alters a `factory` column no migration creates; `87fd9fc7ae00` drops `ix_managed_pool_hash` no migration creates; bare `op.alter_column` unsupported on SQLite) + empirical verification (forward-build fails at `87fd9fc7ae00`) + root cause (migrations as model-mirrors, not self-contained schema ops; only "worked" for incremental upgraders carrying pre-Rust-DDL state).
- The decision: out-of-place dump-and-restore heal, selected over in-place chain repair / squash / hard-retirement. Records all four + rationale.
- The 7-step heal operation + map diagram, the column-mapping auto-derivation (PRAGMA-derived + small RENAME_OVERRIDES constant, NOT 43-entry hand-maintained), the atomic-swap + `.bak` guarantee, consequences, ADR-010 relationship, non-goals (no auto-heal-on-open through 0.7.0), three-layer placement.

### AGENTS.md edits
- ADR index line (line 83): appended "ADR-011 Auto-healed Alembic retirement (dump-and-restore cutover)".
- Kill-list entry for `src/degenbot/migrations/` (line 92): updated to gate retirement on `heal` shipping + proven (epic TGIP5N, T2-T5) AND the 0.7.0 release decision (T6/OXKANZ), not just the 0.7.0 version bump; references ADR-011.

### Validation
- Markdown lint (prek, run independently): Passed.
- `uv run ruff check`: not applicable (no Python touched); ran pre-commit markdown lint via prek — both hooks pass.

## Result
docs/adr/ADR-011-auto-healed-alembic-retirement.md, AGENTS.md

data.title: Fix: GHO discount dispatch must validate emitter == GHO vToken (§4.2 divergence #2 found by U5YIBG)
data.body:
# Fix: GHO discount dispatch must validate the event emitter == the GHO vToken

## The divergence (found by U5YIBG §4.2 parity)
The `fetch_discount_config_logs` fetch is chain-wide ("no address filter — the events emit from any contract": `aave_fetch.rs:210`, passes `None` for the address filter). The Python oracle guards against spurious chain-wide discount events:
- `event_handlers.py:738` & `:773`: `if gho_asset.v_token is None or gho_asset.v_token.address != event["address"]: return`

The Rust **omits** this guard:
- `config_dispatch.rs:661`: `DecodedAaveEvent::DiscountTokenUpdated(ev) => gho_token_id.map(|id| dispatch_discount_token_updated(id, ev))` — the dispatch takes `gho_token_id` resolved from the MARKET context (the single chain-unique GHO asset, `run.rs:988 build_fetch_spec`), NOT from the event emitter.
- `dispatch_discount_token_updated`/`dispatch_discount_rate_strategy_updated` (`config_dispatch.rs:313/326`) receive only `(gho_token_id, decoded_event)` — no emitter address, no `gho_vtoken_address` to validate against.

The Rust HAS `gho_vtoken_address` available at the run-loop level (`run.rs:990`). The fix is to validate the emitter against it. The open question is whether the decoded `DiscountTokenUpdatedEvent`/`DiscountRateStrategyUpdatedEvent` structs carry the emitter (log.address) — if the decoder strips it, the fix requires either carrying it in the decoded struct OR validating at a layer that still has the raw log.

## Why this is a DEFECT (not "Rust is more correct")
- The fetch is chain-wide → spurious events CAN appear (any contract emitting these topic0 signatures). The Python guard is load-bearing, not defensive redundancy.
- Without the guard, the Rust applies ANY chain-wide `DiscountTokenUpdated`/`DiscountRateStrategyUpdated` event against the market's single GHO asset → could write bogus GHO discount config from a spurious event.
- This is the inverse of divergence #6 (EModeCategoryAdded zero-oracle, where Rust=NULL is canonical + Python had a latent bug). Here the Python has the correct guard + the Rust omits it.

## Goal
Add GHO discount event emitter validation to the Rust dispatch, mirroring the Python's `gho_asset.v_token.address != event["address"]` guard. Decide the placement (decoded-struct-carries-emitter vs a layer that has the raw log). The `gho_vtoken_address` is available at the run-loop level.

## §4.3 retirement gate
CZM7TI (the retire) MUST NOT delete the Python emitter guard until this fix lands. Sequenced: U5YIBG → this task → CZM7TI.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the fetch to address-filter (the fetch is chain-wide by design — discovery mode; the emitter isn't known upfront, same as the Python).
- Do NOT touch divergence #3 (PriceOracleUpdated get-or-update — ACCEPTED: Rust get-or-update is canonical + more robust than the Python's INSERT-only-assert; the UPDATE branch should get a Rust-internal `#[cfg(test)]`, separate from the parity harness since the Python can't reach it).

# Fix: GHO discount dispatch must validate the event emitter == the GHO vToken

## RESOLVED (verified post-finding — the open question is answered)
**The decoded structs DO carry the emitter.** `DiscountTokenUpdatedEvent`/`DiscountRateStrategyUpdatedEvent` carry `v_token_address: Address` (= `log.address()`, the emitter) — `aave_event_decoder.rs:708-714` + the decode fns set `v_token_address: log.address()`.

**The fix placement is RESOLVED:** add the emitter-validation guard INSIDE `dispatch_discount_token_updated`/`dispatch_discount_rate_strategy_updated` (`config_dispatch.rs:313/326`) by comparing `decoded.v_token_address` against `gho_asset.v_token_address`. The Rust already threads `gho_asset` into `dispatch_config_events`, so the inputs are available. The guard mirrors the Python's `if gho_asset.v_token is None or gho_asset.v_token.address != event["address"]: return` (`event_handlers.py:738` & `:773`).

## The divergence (found by U5YIBG §4.2 parity)
`fetch_discount_config_logs` is chain-wide ("no address filter — the events emit from any contract": `aave_fetch.rs:210`, passes `None`). The Python guards against spurious chain-wide discount events (`event_handlers.py:738/773`).

The Rust OMITS the guard: `config_dispatch.rs:661` takes `gho_token_id` from MARKET context (the single chain-unique GHO asset), not the emitter. Without the guard, the Rust applies ANY chain-wide `DiscountTokenUpdated`/`DiscountRateStrategyUpdated` event against the market's GHO asset → could write bogus GHO discount config from a spurious event.

## Why DEFECT (not "Rust is more correct")
The fetch is chain-wide → spurious events CAN appear. The Python guard is load-bearing. This is the inverse of divergence #6 (EModeCategoryAdded zero-oracle, where Rust=NULL is canonical + Python had a latent bug): here the Python has the correct guard + the Rust omits it.

## Goal
Add the emitter-validation guard inside the two discount dispatch fns: `if decoded.v_token_address != gho_asset.v_token_address { return None }` (mirror the Python's `None`-v_token guard too). Add a `#[cfg(test)]` asserting a non-matching-emitter discount event is ignored.

## §4.3 retirement gate
CZM7TI (the retire) MUST NOT delete the Python emitter guard until this fix lands. Sequenced: U5YIBG → ULDUAC → CZM7TI.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the fetch to address-filter (chain-wide by design — discovery mode).
- Do NOT touch divergence #3/#7 (PriceOracleUpdated get-or-update — ACCEPTED; already `#[cfg(test)]`-covered by `apply_price_oracle_updated_inserts_then_updates` at `write.rs:3247`).

data.title: spike: drop low-selectivity boolean index ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled
data.body:
# spike: drop low-selectivity boolean index ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled

## Goal
- Confirm `ix_aave_user_collateral_config_enabled` (an index on a BOOLEAN column of `aave_v3_user_collateral_configs`) is never used by the planner and can be dropped.

## Hypothesis
A boolean column has ~50% selectivity; the SQLite planner will always prefer a full table scan over such an index, so it is pure write-amplification with no read benefit.

## What to investigate
1. Confirm the index exists in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`.
2. Grep `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/**/*.rs` for any predicate on the `enabled` column of `aave_v3_user_collateral_configs` (e.g. `WHERE enabled`, `WHERE enabled = 1`). Note any.
3. Check the Python side (`src/degenbot/**`) for any query filtering on `enabled` that the Rust port would need to mirror.
4. Build a representative fixture DB (or reuse `tests/fixtures/aave_parity.db`) with a non-trivial row count and run `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT ... WHERE enabled = 1` to confirm the planner does a full scan (not the index). Vary row count (100 / 1000 / 10000) — boolean selectivity can shift planner choice at small N.

## Validation
- Verdict: DROP (planner never uses it across representative N) or KEEP (planner uses it at some N / a predicate depends on it).
- The EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN outputs.

## Gating constraint
Index drop = new Alembic migration + `schema_head.sql` mirror + `ALEMBIC_HEAD` bump — allowed in 0.6.x.

## If validated → append implementation tasks
If research confirms the suggestion, append one or more implementation tasks to epic `F4N6DX` (DB performance improvements). Each appended task:
- is a single atomic change (one Alembic migration OR one Rust PR);
- includes concrete Acceptance Criteria + Validation Gates (exact `just`/`cargo`/`sql` commands);
- for schema/index changes: ships a new Alembic migration under `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/`, mirrors the DDL change in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema_head.sql`, and bumps `ALEMBIC_HEAD` in `rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/schema.rs`;
- is sequenced after this spike (`ergo sequence <THIS-SPIKE-ID> <IMPL-ID>`);
- respects the gating constraint noted below.

If research refutes the suggestion, mark THIS spike `done` with a `result` summarising why — do NOT append an implementation task.

data.title: Aave Pool position/state apply fns (Supply/Borrow/Repay/Withdraw/Liquidation/ReserveData/etc.) + AaveChunkEvent variants
data.body:
## Goal
Port the **canonical Aave V3 Pool position/state apply fns** to `degenbot-db/src/write.rs` + extend `AaveChunkEvent` in `degenbot-aave-updater` — the position-state sibling to CXRGX4 (which landed the 8 config-event apply fns). Pure `write.rs` substrate (`_on_conn` variants, fixture-testable atomicity), mirroring CXRGX4's shape exactly.

## Why this task exists
CXRGX4 (done) covered only the 8 config/oracle/UserEMode apply fns. The orchestrator `6SWY4R` (`run_aave_update`) cannot ship until ALL Aave V3 event categories have Rust apply fns — §3.4 two-writer hazard (config-in-Rust + position-in-Python = same hazard that killed OPVK2C). This task ports the canonical Pool position-state apply fns; siblings `SCALEAPPLY` (ScaledToken) + `SPECIALAPPLY` (GHO/stkAAVE/Rewards/ERC20) cover the rest.

## Event scope (this task)
The `AaveV3PoolEvent` position/state events — the events that mutate user balances + asset indices + treasury/deficit state. From `src/degenbot/aave/events.py::AaveV3PoolEvent` (11 events total; CXRGX4 already covered `UserEModeSet`; the remaining ~10 are in scope):
- `Supply(reserver, user, amount, referralCode)` — increment the user's collateral position balance for the asset; update `scaled_balance` via the asset's `liquidity_index`.
- `Borrow(user, reserve, amount, borrowRateMode, borrowRate, referralCode)` — increment the user's debt position; update `scaled_balance` via `borrow_index`.
- `Repay(reserve, user, repayer, amount, useATokens)` — decrement debt position; handle `useATokens` variant (repay from aToken balance).
- `Withdraw(reserve, user, to, amount)` — decrement collateral position.
- `LiquidationCall(collateralAsset, debtAsset, user, debtToCover, liquidatedCollateralAmount, liquidator, receiveAToken)` — the complex one: select collateral + debt positions, apply bonus, handle deficit; mirror the Python `liquidation_processor.py` + `operations_parser.py` liquidation logic exactly.
- `ReserveDataUpdated(reserve, liquidityRate, stableBorrowRate, variableBorrowRate, liquidityIndex, variableBorrowIndex)` — update `aave_v3_assets.{liquidity_index, liquidity_rate, borrow_index, borrow_rate}` (the index that scales all balances).
- `MintedToTreasury(reserve, amount)` — increment the treasury's aToken balance (treasury is a synthetic user).
- `DeficitCreated(reserve, amount)` + the deficit tracking.
- Plus the missing `AaveV3PoolConfigEvent::ReserveInitialized` (asset initialization write — CXRGX4's config slice skipped it; it belongs here as it seeds the asset row that position events mutate). Flag if `ReserveInitialized` is better a separate config-task (your call; default: include here since position events depend on the seeded asset).

## The math (port from operations_parser.py, exactness required)
The Python `operations_parser.py` (~2,801 lines) implements:
- **Ray math** — `rayMul(a, b) = a * b / 1e27`, `rayDiv(a, b) = a * 1e27 / b`. Aave V3 uses 27-decimal ray for indices/rates. Port as pure fns over `u128`/`U256` (mirror how `degenbot-cl-math` handles WAD/RAY — check if a ray-math primitive already exists in a core crate; reuse, don't reinvent).
- **Scaled balance** — `scaledBalance = balance * index / RAY` (or its inverse). The position stores `scaled_balance`; the user-facing balance = `scaled_balance * current_index / RAY`. Updates on each event use the asset's CURRENT `liquidity_index`/`borrow_index` (which `ReserveDataUpdated` advances).
- **Liquidation** — collateral/debt position selection (by user + asset), bonus calculation (the liquidation bonus % from the asset's config), deficit handling (the `DeficitCreated` companion event). Mirror the Python flow exactly — §4.2 parity (U5YIBG sibling) will cross-check Rust-written rows vs the Python oracle, so any deviation bites there.

## Scope (this task)
1. **`apply_*` fns in `write.rs`** for each event above, each as `_on_conn(conn: &rusqlite::Connection, ...)` + a thin `&self` lock-and-delegate wrapper (mirror CXRGX4's extraction pattern). Idempotent where the Python is idempotent; UPDATE-or-INSERT where appropriate.
2. **Extend `AaveChunkEvent` enum** in `degenbot-aave-updater/src/run.rs` with one variant per position event (carrying resolved `asset_id`/`user_id` + the event's typed fields — amounts as `U256`, indices as `u128`/`U256` per the ray-math convention).
3. **Extend `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`'s dispatch match** to handle the new variants. Update `AaveChunkWriteReport`'s per-event-type counts.
4. **Ray-math helpers** — if not already in a core crate (`degenbot-cl-math`/`degenbot-core`/`degenbot-evm-math`), add `ray_mul`/`ray_div` to the appropriate crate (flag the chosen home — don't reinvent if it exists).

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged from CXRGX4)
ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Every new `apply_*` writes through `_on_conn` on the caller's tx. On `Err`, whole-chunk revert. Unit tests assert commit-vs-rollback all-or-nothing for the new variants (mirror CXRGX4's `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn_rolls_back_on_injected_failure`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `apply_supply_on_conn` / `apply_borrow_on_conn` / `apply_repay_on_conn` / `apply_withdraw_on_conn` / `apply_liquidation_on_conn` / `apply_reserve_data_updated_on_conn` / `apply_minted_to_treasury_on_conn` / `apply_deficit_created_on_conn` (+ `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn`) exist in `write.rs`; `&self` wrappers preserved (2QPBUJ path still compiles).
- [ ] `AaveChunkEvent` extended with one variant per position event; `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` dispatches them.
- [ ] Ray-math helpers reused from an existing crate OR added with a flag noting the home.
- [ ] Unit tests: per-event apply correctness (fixture event → asserted DB row state) + one new rollback atomicity test covering a position-event variant.
- [ ] `rg "session\.(add|scalar)" src/degenbot/cli/aave/operations_parser.py` STILL shows the Python (this task does NOT touch Python — that's AVS4DR's cutover). The Rust fns are added alongside, not yet routed.
- [ ] `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact), `just lint-rust`, `just format` all green.

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust` (new apply-fn tests + CXRGX4 tests still green)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ path intact — the `&self` wrappers preserved)
- `just lint-rust`, `just format`

## Non-goals
- ScaledToken (aToken/vToken Mint/Burn/Transfer) apply fns → sibling `SCALEAPPLY`.
- GHO/stkAAVE/Rewards/ERC20-Transfer apply fns → sibling `SPECIALAPPLY`.
- Event decoders (topic hashes + field decoding) → sibling `AAVEDECODE`.
- The `run_aave_update` orchestrator → sibling `6SWY4R` (after this + SCALEAPPLY + SPECIALAPPLY + AAVEDECODE).
- Python cutover → sibling `AVS4DR`.
- §4.2 red-green parity → sibling `U5YIBG` (cross-checks ALL apply fns together).
- Touching the Python `operations_parser.py` — this task adds Rust alongside; AVS4DR deletes Python.

## Dependencies
- `CXRGX4` (done) — the `_on_conn` extraction pattern + `AaveChunkEvent` enum + `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` dispatch this task extends.
- Depended on by: `6SWY4R` (the orchestrator calls the full apply surface).

## Goal — RE-SCOPED 2026-07-04 to Option A (the only direct-write Pool events)
Port the **two Aave V3 Pool events that write DB rows directly**: `apply_reserve_data_updated_on_conn` + `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn` to `degenbot-db/src/write.rs`, + extend `AaveChunkEvent` in `degenbot-aave-updater` with their variants.

## Architectural finding (why this task shrank)
Investigation (2026-07-04, verified by orchestrator) revealed the Pool events Supply/Borrow/Repay/Withdraw/LiquidationCall/MintedToTreasury/DeficitCreated do NOT have per-event apply fns in Python — they're consumed by `operations_parser.py` to GROUP ScaledToken events into `Operation` objects; the actual balance mutations ALL happen in `token_processor.py` via ScaledToken events (sibling SCALEAPPLY's domain). Only `ReserveDataUpdated` + `ReserveInitialized` are direct Pool-event DB writes. So this task reduced to those two fns. The parser-matching bulk is sibling `OPERATIONSPARSER`.

## Event scope (this task — 2 events)
- **`ReserveDataUpdated(reserve, liquidityRate, stableBorrowRate, variableBorrowRate, liquidityIndex, variableBorrowIndex)`** — `event_handlers.py:794-847`. Updates `aave_v3_assets.{liquidity_rate, borrow_rate, liquidity_index, borrow_index, last_update_block}`. Pure substrate write; clean port to `apply_reserve_data_updated_on_conn(asset_id, liquidity_rate, variable_borrow_rate, liquidity_index, variable_borrow_index, block_number)`. No ray-math (stores raw indices/rates as-is).
- **`ReserveInitialized(asset, aToken, stableDebtToken, variableDebtToken, interestRateStrategyAddress)`** — `event_handlers.py:555-687`. Seeds the `aave_v3_assets` row (underlying/a/v token ids + revisions + `liquidity_index=0`/`liquidity_rate=0`/`borrow_index=0`/`borrow_rate=0` + RPC-resolved `price_source`). The apply-side `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn(market_id, underlying_asset_id, a_token_id, a_token_revision, v_token_id, v_token_revision, price_source)` is a clean get-or-create-asset on `(market_id, underlying_asset_id)`. **Note: the RPC-resolved revisions + price_source resolutions happen in the orchestrator (6SWY4R); the apply fn takes pre-resolved fields** (mirrors CXRGX4's design decision #1). The GHO cross-link setup if the asset IS the GHO token is `RYKCC4` (SPECIALAPPLY)'s concern, NOT this task's.

## Scope (this task)
1. **`apply_reserve_data_updated_on_conn` + `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn`** in `write.rs` — `_on_conn` + thin `&self` wrappers (mirror CXRGX4's extraction pattern). Idempotent (get-or-create for ReserveInitialized; unconditional UPDATE for ReserveDataUpdated).
2. **Extend `AaveChunkEvent` enum** with `ReserveDataUpdated` + `ReserveInitialized` variants (carrying resolved `asset_id: i64` + the event's typed fields — rates/indices as `U256`, addresses as `String`/`Option<String>`).
3. **Extend `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn`'s dispatch match** to handle the 2 new variants. Update `AaveChunkWriteReport`'s per-event-type counts.
4. **Unit tests**: per-event apply correctness (fixture event → asserted DB row state, including the index/rate/seed values) + one rollback atomicity test covering a Pool-event variant.

## §3.4 atomicity invariant (unchanged from CXRGX4)
ONE `Connection`, ONE `Transaction` per chunk. Every apply writes through `_on_conn` on the caller's tx. On `Err`, whole-chunk revert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `apply_reserve_data_updated_on_conn` + `apply_reserve_initialized_on_conn` exist in `write.rs`; `&self` wrappers preserved (2QPBUJ path still compiles).
- [ ] `AaveChunkEvent` extended with `ReserveDataUpdated` + `ReserveInitialized` variants; `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` dispatches them; `AaveChunkWriteReport` counts updated.
- [ ] Unit tests: per-event apply correctness + one new rollback atomicity test covering a Pool-event variant.
- [ ] `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ smoke intact), `just lint-rust`, `just format` all green.

## Validation gates
- `just test-rust` (new apply-fn tests + CXRGX4 tests still green after the `AaveChunkEvent`/dispatch extension)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `just test-rust-python` (2QPBUJ path intact)
- `just lint-rust` (clippy --deny warnings), `just format`

## Non-goals
- The parser-matching for Supply/Borrow/Repay/Withdraw/Liquidation/MintToTreasury → sibling `OPERATIONSPARSER`.
- ScaledToken apply fns + ray-math + TokenMath → sibling `SCALEAPPLY`.
- GHO/stkAAVE/Rewards/ERC20-Transfer → sibling `RYKCC4`.
- Event decoders → sibling `ECFB5C`.
- The orchestrator → sibling `6SWY4R`.
- Python cutover → sibling `AVS4DR`.
- §4.2 parity → sibling `U5YIBG`.
- Touching the Python `event_handlers.py` — this task adds Rust alongside; AVS4DR deletes Python.

## Dependencies
- `CXRGX4` (done) — the `_on_conn` extraction pattern + `AaveChunkEvent` enum + `apply_aave_chunk_writes_on_conn` dispatch this task extends.
- Depended on by: `SCALEAPPLY` (reads the asset indices this task updates), `OPERATIONSPARSER` (dispatches the asset-row apply fns), `6SWY4R`.

data.title: Research: define the chunk-atomicity invariant + scope the Rust-owned chunk updater
data.body:
## Goal

Produce a precise write-up that (1) states the exact invariant the pool updater must hold, (2) names the concrete approach to restore it in the current Rust-core architecture, and (3) decomposes that approach into implementation tasks to attach to this epic. **The write-up IS this task's deliverable** — no code changes.

## Direction (already endorsed by the orchestrator)

**The whole chunk loop may move into Rust.** If the entire chunk (fetch events, upsert pools, apply liquidity updates, stamp `last_update_block`) is one Rust call, then Rust owns one connection + one transaction and the write/stamp desync is **structurally impossible** — there's only one writer. The PyO3 seam becomes something like `run_pool_update_chunk(database_path, chain_id, exchange specs, start_block, end_block, ...) -> ChunkReport`. This is the strongly-preferred direction (ADR-005: Rust is the engine; Python is a thin shell).

The research must confirm whether this is the right approach vs the partial fix (thread a single connection through the existing `db_*` seams without rewriting the loop) and name the trade-offs.

## What the write-up must establish

### 1. The invariant (state it precisely)

Pin down the exact contract, by reference to `main`:
- A "chunk" is a batch of blocks `[working_start_block, working_end_block]` processed atomically.
- **Atomicity invariant:** at chunk commit, EITHER (a) every pool row from `PoolCreated` events in the chunk + every liquidity update from `Mint`/`Burn` events in the chunk + the `last_update_block = working_end_block` stamp are ALL durably persisted (single transaction commit), OR (b) NONE of them are (single transaction rollback). No intermediate state is observable — including across an interrupt or crash.
- **Restart invariant:** `last_update_block` is a strict upper bound on the block range whose pool + liquidity data is durably committed. Restarting from `last_update_block + 1` re-processes only work that was NOT committed — never re-applies committed work.
- **No-duplicate-writer invariant:** at most one connection holds a write transaction on the DB during a chunk. (The current code violates this with multiple short-lived `DegenbotDb` connections + a SQLAlchemy session all writing concurrently.)

Reference the exact lines on `main` (git show main:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py) where the invariant was held by construction: the shared `session` threaded through every updater, the ORM-dirty `exchange.last_update_block` stamp, the single `session.commit()` at chunk end.

### 2. The current regression (cite the code)

Document precisely how the invariant is broken in the current tree:
- `db_upsert_v3_pools` (and v2/v4) → own connection via `open_for_writes`; `upsert_v3_pools` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/discovery.rs`) does per-row autocommit `execute()` with NO `transaction()` wrapper — pool rows durable mid-chunk, separate connection from the stamp.
- `db_apply_v3_liquidity_updates` / `db_apply_v4_liquidity_updates` — confirm the same pattern (separate connection; own writes). Read `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/*.rs` for these seams.
- `db_set_exchange_last_update_block` — separate connection again.
- The SQLAlchemy `session.commit()` only commits SQLAlchemy-owned state, not the Rust writes.
- Net: writes + stamp live in separate transactions on separate connections → interrupttroduces write/stamp desync → the observed `UNIQUE constraint failed: pools.address, pools.chain`.

### 3. The approaches (name + evaluate)

Evaluate these in the write-up; pick one as THE approach (with rationale); the others are documented as considered-and-rejected:

**A. Move the whole chunk loop into Rust (preferred direction — confirm).** A Rust function (e.g. `pool_update_chunk(database_path, chain_id, exchange_specs, start_block, end_block, ...) -> ChunkReport`) owns the single connection + single transaction for the chunk: fetches events (or accepts pre-fetched events), upserts pools, applies liquidity updates, stamps `last_update_block`, commits once or rolls back. The PyO3 seam is one call; Python no longer holds a write-bearing session. This is the maximal Rust ownership answer and the structurally-safest.

  - Sub-questions to resolve in the write-up:
    - Does the chunk loop fetch RPC events in Rust or Python? (The current loop fetches via `get_events_from_contract` / `get_v3_liquidity_events` / `get_v4_liquidity_events` in Python, then passes results to the Rust write seams.) Recommend: keep RPC fetching in Python (it's I/O orchestration, the legitimate Python-shell responsibility), pass the decoded events INTO the Rust chunk function, and let Rust do all the DB writes + the commit in one transaction. The chunk function's signature should accept the decoded event payloads, not do RPC itself.
    - OR: push RPC into Rust too (bigger — needs the RPC crate work; only do if it's clearly the right call for atomicity, which it probably isn't — RPC is I/O, not DB state). Document.
    - How are the per-exchange `new_pool_events` + the cross-exchange `liquidity_events` batches combined into one transaction? (They're currently separate calls; the chunk function must accept them all + commit once.)

**B. Thread a single DegenbotDb connection through the existing `db_*` seams.** Expose a connection-scoped handle (e.g. a `DegenbotDb` clone or a `&Connection`-bearing wrapper) at the PyO3 level so the chunk loop can open one connection, pass it to `upsert_v3_pools` / `apply_v3_liquidity_updates` / `set_exchange_last_update_block`, and commit at chunk end. Smaller change than A.

  - Trade-off: the PyO3 seam gets more complex (connection handle is a new `#[pyclass]`); still leaves the chunk loop's orchestration in Python (which is fine for ADR-005's "thin shell" reading); must ensure a single transaction spans all calls (either explicit `BEGIN`..`COMMIT` or rusqlite `transaction()`).
  - Sub-question: is this even achievable cleanly given the current `DegenbotDb` is `Mutex<Connection>` and the `db_*` seams open-and-close per call? May need a "borrow connection" seam.

**C. Make the individual writes idempotent (`INSERT OR IGNORE` / `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) without fixing the transaction structure.** Rejected as a real fix: it papers over the duplicate-pool-insert symptom but leaves the write/stamp desync — `last_update_block` would still lag the committed pool data, and `apply_*_liquidity_updates` would double-apply Mint/Burn events (stateful — not idempotent — unlike pool inserts). Record as "considered and rejected: doesn't restore the invariant."

**D. Keep the chunk in Python, wrap everything in one DB-level `BEGIN`..`COMMIT`.** E.g. a PyO3 seam `db_begin_transaction(database_path) -> TxHandle` + `db_commit_transaction(tx)`. Rejected: leaking SQLite transaction handles across the PyO3 boundary is fragile (what if Python raises mid-chunk? the tx leaks; rollback semantics get murky). Record as considered-and-rejected.

### 4. The implementation task decomposition

After picking the approach (likely A), decompose into implementation tasks to file as children of this epic. Each task should be ~1 commit, with clear gates. For approach A, likely tasks (use as a starting sketch; refine in the write-up):

1. `pool_update_chunk` Rust core function — owns the single connection + transaction, accepts decoded events (new_pool_events per exchange + liquidity_events), does the pool upserts + liquidity updates + stamp + commit/rollback. Reuses existing `upsert_v*_pools` / `apply_*_liquidity_updates` / `set_exchange_last_update_block` logic but bound to the passed-in connection.
2. PyO3 seam — thin wrapper; GIL released across the chunk. Define the event-payload types (or accept the raw decoded values Python already produces).
3. Python chunk loop refactor — keep RPC fetching (the `get_events_*` calls) in Python; replace the per-exchange `pool_updater(...)` + per-pool `apply_*_liquidity_updates(...)` + the stamp loop with a single `run_pool_update_chunk(...)` call per chunk. Drop the SQLAlchemy `session.commit()` (the Rust function owns the commit now).
4. Remove the now-redundant standalone `db_upsert_v*_pools` / `db_apply_*_liquidity_updates` / `db_set_exchange_last_update_block` seams IF the chunk function supersedes them (or keep them for standalone testing + have the chunk function call into the same core logic without going through the seam). Decide + document.
5. A regression test that reproduces the bug: interrupt mid-chunk (mock the interrupt) → assert the chunk is fully rolled back → restart re-processes cleanly with no `UNIQUE constraint` failure. This is the contract artifact for the invariant.
6. (Maybe) a test that proves the no-duplicate-writer invariant: the chunk function holds a write transaction; a concurrent `DegenbotDb::open_for_writes` during the chunk blocks/refuses rather than producing concurrent writers.

These tasks should be filed as children of this epic with the dependencies sequenced. The orchestrator will create them from the write-up's decomposition.

## Deliverable

A markdown file at `docs/migration-guides/pool-updater-chunk-atomicity.md` capturing:
- The invariant (§1).
- The current regression (§2, with code citations).
- The approaches + the chosen approach + rationale (§3).
- The implementation task decomposition (§4) — concrete enough that the orchestrator can file the tasks directly from it.

Commit it as `docs(migration): define pool-updater chunk atomicity invariant + fix approach`. Reference epic `2SFL6I`. Reference `main`'s chunk loop as the contract source of truth.

## Constraints

- **Read `main` first** (`git show main:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py`) — that's the contract. The current tree is the regression; `main` is the reference.
- Read the current Rust seams (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/*.rs`) + core (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/src/discovery.rs`, `connection.rs`) to cite the exact breakage points.
- No code changes in this task — the write-up is the deliverable. The implementation tasks (filed separately after this lands) do the code.
- Read ADR-005 (`docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`) + the migration guide (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md`) to ground "Rust is the engine" in the project's own architecture language.

## Report-back (to orchestrator t-6ff7 via link_send triggerTurn:true)

1. Commit hash of the write-up.
2. The chosen approach (A/B/C/D) + one-paragraph rationale.
3. The list of implementation tasks you decomposed (titles + one-line summaries) — so the orchestrator can file them as epic children.
4. Any sub-question from §3 you couldn't resolve + why.

## Result

Committed `35624d6f` — `docs(database): pool-updater chunk atomicity invariant + fix`. Markdown lint passes.

### Chosen approach
**A — move the whole update loop into Rust.** Anchored in AGENTS.md §Architectural Vision: "the database (persistence), RPC interaction, ... the DB-aware pool ... updater" are all explicitly on the migration path; the standalone-Rust-core constraint forbids stranding the loop logic on the Python side. Python becomes a driver shell (boot + progress), not a co-implementation.

### RPC-layer decision
**REUSE `degenbot-rpc` — no port in scope.** Inventory confirmed (cross-checked by orchestrator): `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/` is a mature core crate with `AlloyProvider::new(rpc_url, max_retries)`, `get_block_number()`, `get_block(n)`, `get_logs(&LogFilter)`, and `fetch_logs_chunked(...)` (built-in big-range pagination + concurrency, on alloy 2.0 with transport-throttle). The only genuinely new Rust surface is a pure-Rust decode leaf (`alloy::Log` → `PoolCreated`-row input / `LiquidityUpdateEvent`) belonging in `degenbot-decoders` (decode-only, no state, no FFI).

### Implementation task decomposition (filed separately by orchestrator as children of `2SFL6I`)
1. Wire `degenbot-rpc` into the chunk loop's RPC needs + the decode leaf (no port). ← depends on nothing
2. `ExchangeSpec` + event-config types in Rust (Rust reads the `exchanges` table). ← depends on 1
3. `run_pool_update` Rust core fn: chunk loop, single conn + `transaction()` per chunk, cancel-poll at chunk boundaries. ← depends on 1+2
4. PyO3 seam + `ProgressCallback`. ← depends on 3
5. Python CLI refactor: `pool_update` = boot + hand-off. ← depends on 4
6. Regression test: chunk interrupt → full rollback → restart clean (the contract). ← depends on 5
7. No-duplicate-writer test. ← depends on 3

### Notable nuance (for Task 3)
`degenbot-rpc` is async (alloy/tokio); `degenbot-db` is sync (rusqlite). `run_pool_update` must bridge these (likely a tokio runtime inside the chunk fn, or `block_on` per RPC fetch into the sync write path). Orchestrator will flag this in the Task 3 brief.

## References
- docs/migration-guides/pool-updater-chunk-atomicity.md (the write-up)
- AGENTS.md §Architectural Vision; ADR-005; rust/AGENTS.md (GIL discipline)
- git show main:src/degenbot/cli/pool.py (the contract source of truth)

data.title: Scope: RPC dispatch layer
data.body:
## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **RPC dispatch layer → Rust core** migration so subsequent child tasks
  decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python` dispositions
  per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Context
- This epic is a container for the migration of one responsibility area from
  Python into the Rust core (the AGENTS.md Architectural Vision). Before any
  implementation task is created, this task must produce a scope inventory so
  later decomposition is grounded, not improvised.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`,
  the rubric §2 + smell checklist §2.3, the cutover discipline §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A scope table committed into this task body (via `ergo set`) listing, for
  **RPC dispatch layer → Rust core**:
  - **COMPLETED** — Rust-owned + Python already delegating (cite file/crate +
    the landed slice if known).
  - **IN-FIGHT** — partially routed; Python still the authority for some
    callsites (cite both sides).
  - **NOT STARTED** — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust.
- Each row carries the rubric disposition (`done`/`partial`/`port-now`/
  `stays-python`) and a one-line rationale using §2.1 criteria (hot path? GIL?
  type shape? I/O shape? Python-ecosystem coupling? test shape?).
- Open dependency / blocking questions surfaced (e.g. depends on the RPC or
  persistence epic).
- After the scope table lands, child implementation tasks are split out from
  this epic (one per `port-now`/`partial` row), each with AC + validation gates.

## Validation Gates
- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task
  is created under this epic.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` still passes (no cores touched by the scoping
  itself, but confirms the baseline).

## Status: RESEARCH COMPLETE — scope table below; child tasks split out.

## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **RPC dispatch layer → Rust core** migration
  so subsequent child tasks decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` /
  `stays-python` dispositions per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.2).

## Findings — the dispatch seam today

The **pump-side** RPC is already Rust-owned and runs on the shared tokio
runtime (`degenbot-rpc::provider::AlloyProvider` + `subscription::pump_*`,
dual-WS newHeads+logs). The **dispatch-side** RPC in the hot loop is, by
contrast, driven through a **raw `AsyncWeb3(web3.AsyncHTTPProvider)`** that the
backrun example constructs directly in `BackrunSession._build_async_w3`
(`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py:1039`) — it bypasses the
`AsyncProviderAdapter` / `AsyncAlloyProvider` Rust wrappers that already exist
and ARE wired for the rest of the codebase (`src/degenbot/provider/__init__.py`
imports `RustAlloyProvider`/`AsyncAlloyProvider`; `_AsyncAlloyAdapter` wraps
them). So the work is *not* "build a Rust RPC core" (it exists) — it is "route
the dispatch hot loop through the existing Rust core, fill the gaps the core
doesn't cover, then delete the raw-`AsyncWeb3` bypass."

The backrun example makes exactly these `async_w3.eth.*` dispatch calls
(exhaustive grep):

| Call | Count | Site |
|---|---|---|
| `eth_call` (`slot0`/`liquidity`/`getReserves` per-hop state inspection) | 3 | `_emit_sim_diag` / state-trace block in `simulate_one` |
| `eth_createAccessList` | 2 | `simulate_one` + `dispatch_profitable_results` (re-warm) |
| `eth_simulateV1` (7-call profit pattern) | 1 | `simulate_one` |
| `eth_sendRawTransaction` | 1 | `dispatch_profitable_results` |
| `eth_getTransactionReceipt` | 1 | `monitor_pending_transaction` |
| `eth_getTransactionCount` | 1 | `_apply_result_if_ready` |
| `eth_getCode` | 1 | V3 state-trace (presence check) |
| `eth_getBlock` ("latest") | 1 | `BackrunSession.start` |
| `eth_feeHistory` | 1 | `_apply_block_if_ready` |
| `eth.contract(...)` (ABI-bound executor handle) | 1 | `dispatch_profitable_results` |
| `web3.Web3.keccak(text=...)` + `eth_abi.abi.encode(...)` | many | selector + calldata construction throughout |

Plus dispatch-side **helpers**: `web3.Web3.to_checksum_address`, `Web3.to_bytes`,
the `EXECUTOR_ABI` literal, `HexBytes`. These belong to the **Swap encoding**
epic (`WWC4DL`) / ABI work, not the RPC transport itself — but they are how the
dispatch loop currently produces the byte payloads it hands to `eth_call` /
`eth_simulateV1`.

---

## Scope table — COMPLETED / IN-FIGHT / NOT STARTED

Per the rubric §2.1 criteria. Disposition legend:
`done` = Rust-owned + Python delegating · `partial` = Rust counterpart exists,
Python still authority for some callsites · `port-now` = no Rust counterpart,
belongs in Rust · `stays-python` = rubric says keep in Python.

### COMPLETED

| Sub-area | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Pointers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pump-side dual-WS subscription (newHeads + logs) | `done` | Hot path / pure transform / no Python-ecosystem coupling — already the production path. The `UniswapEnginePump` owns event receipt + backfill; Python only reads `block_stream()` + result batches. | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/subscription.rs::pump_blocks`/`pump_logs`; `degenbot-bot/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine_pump.rs`; `examples/...py::_tee_block_stream` |
| `eth_getBlockNumber` / `eth_getChainId` | `done` | Sync + async PyO3 wrappers exist, delegating to `AlloyProvider`. Not hot-loop but used at startup. | `degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs:422,435`; PyO3 `provider.rs:251,263`, `async_provider.rs:100,111` |
| `eth_getBlock` | `done` | Wrapper exists sync + async; consumed by `BackrunSession.start` (raw `async_w3.eth.get_block("latest")` — *should* route through Rust, see IN-FIGHT). | `provider.rs:491`; PyO3 `provider.rs:278`, `async_provider.rs:157` |
| `eth_getLogs` (backfill) | `done` | `LogFetcher::fetch_logs_chunked` + `AlloyProvider::get_logs`; used by the pump's timeout/empty-block backfill. | `provider.rs:893,444`; PyO3 `provider.rs:154`, `async_provider.rs:120` |
| `eth_getCode` | `done` | Wrapper exists sync + async; the example calls it for V3 presence-check. Not yet routed through Rust at that site (IN-FIGHT). | `provider.rs:463`; PyO3 `provider.rs:225`, `async_provider.rs:209` |
| `eth_call` (generic) | `done` | Wrapper exists sync + async (`provider.rs:570`, PyO3 sync `provider.rs:191` + async `async_provider.rs:185`). Used for `slot0`/`getReserves` per-hop inspection in the example — NOT yet routed through Rust at those sites (IN-FIGHT). | `provider.rs:570`; PyO3 sync `provider.rs:191`, async `async_provider.rs:185` |
| `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getTransaction`, `eth_getTransactionReceipt` | `done` (exists) / `partial` (not routed) | Wrappers exist for all four. `get_transaction_receipt` is the one the dispatch loop calls (`monitor_pending_transaction`) — exists but not routed at that site. | `provider.rs:750,722,654,688`; PyO3 sync `provider.rs:452,420,365,391`, async `async_provider.rs:348,298,275,324` |
| `eth_getTransactionCount` | `done` (exists) / `partial` (not routed) | Wrapper exists; dispatch loop calls it (`_apply_result_if_ready`) through raw `AsyncWeb3` instead. | `provider.rs:776`; PyO3 `provider.rs:479`, `async_provider.rs:372` |
| `eth_estimateGas`, `eth_getGasPrice` | `done` | Wrappers exist; not on the dispatch hot path (the example pulls `gasUsed` off the simulation, not a separate `estimateGas`). | `provider.rs:599,615` |
| Raw-RPC escape hatch `make_request(method, params)` | `done` | Both sync + async PyO3 wrappers release the GIL and return untyped JSON. This is the **bridge** that lets `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_feeHistory`/`eth_createAccessList`/`eth_sendRawTransaction` route through Rust *today*, untyped. | `provider.rs:809`; PyO3 `provider.rs:512`, `async_provider.rs:396` |

### IN-FIGHT (Rust counterpart exists; Python still the authority at dispatch sites)

| # | Sub-area | Disposition | What's Python-only at the callsite | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IF-1 | **Route `BackrunSession._build_async_w3` off raw `AsyncWeb3`** | `partial` | The example constructs `AsyncWeb3(AsyncHTTPProvider(...))` directly (`:1039`), bypassing `AsyncProviderAdapter.from_alloy` which already wraps `AsyncAlloyProvider`. Switch the session to build an `AsyncProviderAdapter` (or raw `AsyncAlloyProvider`) so dispatch calls hit Rust. Hot path? yes per block. GIL? I/O — already releases via async. Ecosystem coupling? pure transport — no `web3.py` semantics needed for `eth_*` primitives. | `PAGQCK` |
| IF-2 | **Route `eth_call` per-hop state inspection** through Rust | `partial` | The 3 `async_w3.eth.call` sites in `simulate_one` / `_emit_sim_diag` (slot0/liquidity/getReserves). The Rust `call` wrapper exists. | folds into `PAGQCK` |
| IF-3 | **Route `eth_getCode` (V3 presence)** through Rust | `partial` | Single site in the V3 state-trace; Rust wrapper exists. | folds into `PAGQCK` |
| IF-4 | **Route `eth_getBlock("latest")`** through Rust | `partial` | `BackrunSession.start` reads latest block via raw `async_w3`. Rust wrapper exists. | folds into `PAGQCK` |
| IF-5 | **Route `eth_getTransactionCount`** through Rust | `partial` | `_apply_result_if_ready` calls it via raw `async_w3`. Rust wrapper exists. | folds into `PAGQCK` |
| IF-6 | **Route `eth_getTransactionReceipt`** (`monitor_pending_transaction`) through Rust | `partial` | `monitor_pending_transaction` polls receipt via raw `async_w3`. Rust wrapper exists. | folds into `PAGQCK` |

### NOT STARTED (no Rust first-class surface; only the untyped `make_request` escape hatch)

| # | Sub-area | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NS-1 | **`eth_simulateV1`** (7-call profit pattern) | `port-now` | Hot path per dispatch · pure JSON↔struct transform (stateOverrides, blockStateCalls, returnData) — no Python-ecosystem coupling · testable input→output. Reaches Rust via `make_request` untyped today; needs a typed core surface. **Depends on the Simulation epic (`5LLJHX`) only for the orchestration; the transport primitive itself is this epic.** Typing note: web3.py's `SimulateV1Payload`/`BlockStateCallV1`/`StateOverride`/`AccountOverride` shapes are the spec. | `ZUZANP` |
| NS-2 | **`eth_feeHistory`** | `port-now` | Hot path per block · pure numeric return (baseFeePerGas, reward percentiles) · no coupling. Used by `_apply_block_if_ready` for priority-fee percentiles (consumed by the Transaction-submission epic's fee strategy). `make_request`-reachable today, needs typed surface. | `ZUZANP` |
| NS-3 | **`eth_createAccessList`** | `port-now` | Hot path per simulate · pure transform (TxParams → AccessList) · no coupling. Two sites in `simulate_one` + `dispatch_profitable_results`. `make_request`-reachable today. | `ZUZANP` |
| NS-4 | **`eth_sendRawTransaction`** | `port-now` | Hot path per dispatch · pure (signed bytes → tx hash) · no coupling. Single site in `dispatch_profitable_results`. **Note:** signing itself is in the Transaction-submission epic (`SHT6GE`); this task is the transport primitive only. | `ZUZANP` |
| NS-5 | **`debug_traceCall`** (offline repro of reverts) | `stays-python` | Not on the hot path; invoked only for offline manual debug (referenced in comments only). Not on the migration path for v1 — keep Python. | none |
| NS-6 | **`web3.Web3.keccak` + `eth_abi.abi.encode` calldata construction** | `stays-python` (here) → belongs to `WWC4DL` | Pure byte transforms (selectors + ABI encode) — but they are the **Swap encoding** epic's concern, not the RPC transport. `degenbot-abi` already covers encode/decode; routing those callsites is tracked under `WWC4DL`. Recorded here so it isn't re-litigated. | — (see `WWC4DL`) |

---

## Open dependency / blocking questions (resolved)

1. **Simulation orchestration vs RPC primitive.** The 7-call
   `eth_simulateV1` *orchestration* (pre/post balance reads, profit math, state
   overrides, revert decoding) belongs to the **Simulation** epic (`5LLJHX`),
   which already depends on this epic. This epic owns only the **transport
   primitive** (`eth_simulateV1` typed request/response through `degenbot-rpc`).
   Edge already wired: `D3DIPE` → `5LLJHX`. ✓
2. **Signing vs send.** `eth_account.sign_transaction` is the
   Transaction-submission epic (`SHT6GE`); `eth_sendRawTransaction` (signed
   bytes → hash) is here. Edge already wired: `D3DIPE` → `SHT6GE`. ✓
3. **Untyped bridge as the cutover seam.** Because `make_request` already
   releases the GIL and returns JSON, the routing child (`PAGQCK`) can land
   *before* the typed primitives (`ZUZANP`) — route the dispatch loop through
   `make_request` first (untyped), then type. This matches the rubric §3
   ordered sub-steps and de-risks the cutover.

## Proposed child-task split (created under this epic)

| ID | Title | Disposition | AC summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PAGQCK` | Route dispatch hot loop off raw `AsyncWeb3` onto the Rust `AsyncAlloyProvider` | `partial` (IF-1…IF-6) | `BackrunSession._build_async_w3` returns an `AsyncProviderAdapter`/`AsyncAlloyProvider`; all 6 IN-FIGHT callsites call through Rust wrappers; raw `AsyncWeb3` import removed from the dispatch path; `just test-rust-python` + example dry-run green. |
| `ZUZANP` | Add typed Rust surfaces for `eth_simulateV1` / `eth_feeHistory` / `eth_createAccessList` / `eth_sendRawTransaction` | `port-now` (NS-1…NS-4) | New core fns in `degenbot-rpc` (zero `pyo3`, gated by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`); PyO3 thin wrappers in `degenbot-python/src/rpc/`; the routing child's untyped `make_request` calls replaced by typed ones; parities vs web3.py shapes asserted. |

`PAGQCK` precedes `ZUZANP` (route untyped first, then type) — edge to be wired.

`stays-python` items (NS-5, NS-6) get no child task; their disposition is
recorded above so the next sweep doesn't re-litigate (NS-6 flows to `WWC4DL`).

## Validation Gates (baseline, per task AC)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` → **PASS** (verified 2026-07-02; no cores touched by scoping).
- `ergo list` shows `PAGQCK` ready, `ZUZANP` blocked on `PAGQCK`.

# Database persistence → Rust core

## Scope
Migrate the SQLAlchemy-based persistence layer from a Python implementation
into a Rust-owned core crate, so a standalone Rust consumer (`cargo add
degenbot`) has full DB persistence without Python.

## In-scope (per `AGENTS.md` Architectural Vision: "the database (persistence,
not just ORM calls)")
- ORM models: `src/degenbot/database/models/{pools,aave,erc20,types}.py`
- `src/degenbot/database/session_manager.py` + `operations.py`
- Alembic migrations: `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/`
- Snapshot DB readers feeding the engines (`uniswap/v3_snapshot.py`,
  `uniswap/v4_snapshot.py` — `DatabaseSnapshot` classes)
- Per-chain DB path resolution (`config.py` `DatabaseSettings`)

## Non-goals
- Rust ownership of the pump/RPC/WS subscription (tracked in their own epics).
- Deleting Python ORM call sites before the Rust persistence layer has parity
  and the snapshot loaders route through it.

## Constraints
- Apply the ADR-005 three-layer transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2) — one disposition
  per sub-module (`done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python`).
- Standalone-Rust-core constraint: any persistence a `cargo add degenbot`
  consumer needs lands in a core crate from day one.
- Each cutover sub-step leaves all `just` gates green; no Python mirror of
  Rust-owned state (no back-compat layer).

data.title: Build minimal per-chunk verify-positions-on-chain-truth gate (BE474R first slice) for JGQHBX drive
data.body:
# Build minimal per-chunk verify-positions-on-chain-truth gate (BE474R first slice) for the JGQHBX drive harness

## Context — why this NOW (the reassessment-trigger retarget)

The cold-boot re-drive is a CRASH gate (it detects divergences that underflow balances) but NOT a VALUE-CORRECTNESS gate. Two systematic value bugs surfaced only because the W2S3WH test-tightening happened to add value-equal assertions:

- **NMWPI6** (catastrophic + systematic): `extract_raw_amount_for_event` returned `extract_pool_amount_word0` for ALL standard ops. For Supply/Borrow the ABI is `abi.encode(user, amount)` → word0 = the user's ADDRESS (~10^48-10^57) used as the amount. **Every Supply/Borrow balance the Rust writer produced was wildly wrong** — always positive, never underflowed → the re-drive to 16596000 was "GREEN" while writing garbage for every Supply/Borrow. The re-drive + existence-only tests structurally cannot detect this.
- **3MF5QM**: `dispatch_balance_transfer` used the ERC20 CollateralTransfer's UNDERLYING amount as `scaled_amount` with `transfer_index=0` instead of the paired BalanceTransfer's scaled value + index. Systematic for every standalone transfer.

The crash-gate is the wrong SHAPE for value correctness in steady-state history. Masked wrong balances accumulate silently. The Python has the missing functionality: `verify_positions_for_users` (per-chunk/per-block on-chain balanceOf verification) — bot functionality that belongs in the Rust core per AGENTS.md regardless.

**The user greenlit (R1):** build the minimal per-chunk verify-positions-on-chain-truth gate as BE474R's first slice, sequenced BEFORE HLYWI6 (it becomes part of what clears HLYWI6). Use the Python's verification loop as inspiration (it's "fully functional and very robust" per the user).

## Inspiration — Python's verification.py (src/degenbot/cli/aave/verification.py, 243 lines)

- `verify_positions_for_users` (verification.py:62) — per-chunk/per-block verify of touched users (called from commands.py:1232/1258/1273 with `users_modified_this_block` / `users_modified_this_chunk`). Verifies: scaled-token positions (collateral + debt) + stk_aave_balances + gho_discount_amounts.
- `verify_all_positions` (verification.py:115) — market-wide (`user_addresses=None`); the full soundness verification the user mentioned.
- `verify_scaled_token_positions` (verification.py:152) — **the core to port**: scans DB positions (filtered by `user_addresses`), for each position: RPC `scaledBalanceOf(user)` + `getPreviousIndex(user)` at `block_number`, `assert actual == position.balance` + `assert actual == position.last_index`. Skips `DEAD_ADDRESS`/`ZERO_ADDRESS`.
- `cleanup_zero_balance_positions` (verification.py:27) — deletes zero-balance positions (the Rust chunk apply may leave zero-balance stubs; this mirrors the Python's cleanup).

## Goal — the minimal slice (R1)

Port a Rust `verify_positions_for_users`-equivalent (`verify_touched_positions_on_chain` or similar) in the Rust core (degenbot-aave-updater). The MINIMAL slice = `verify_scaled_token_positions` only (collateral + debt, via `scaledBalanceOf` + `getPreviousIndex` RPC at a block, compare to DB `balance` + `last_index`). Use the Python's exact assertion contract (scaled balance + last_index equality). The stk_aave + gho_discount verifications are a SECONDARY slice (follow-up; not blocking the debugging gate).

Wire it into the JGQHBX drive harness (`scripts/aave_replay_diff.py`) as a per-chunk verification step: after each chunk commits, call `verify_touched_positions_on_chain(db, provider, market_id, chunk_end_block, touched_users)`. On mismatch, emit a NAMED divergence (user, asset, position_id, expected vs actual balance/index) — same shape as the harness's compare divergences, so they're bisect-able.

## Architectural placement (per AGENTS.md)

- The verify fn lives in the Rust CORE (degenbot-aave-updater) — it's bot functionality (verification), not driver-shell orchestration. ZERO pyo3.
- The fn is callable from BOTH: (a) the JGQHBX harness (the debugging gate — per-chunk verify of touched users), + (b) `run_aave_update` (production — expose a `verify_chunk: bool` flag as a follow-up, NOT blocking this task). For this task, the harness-level wiring is sufficient + the production flag is a noted follow-up.
- Use the existing `AlloyProvider` (run.rs) for the RPC `scaledBalanceOf`/`getPreviousIndex` eth_calls. Per-position calls are fine for the touched-users-per-chunk case (small set). For the market-wide (BE474R-full, post-cutover), batch via multicall3 — note the design so the market-wide verify is the natural extension.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A Rust `verify_positions_for_users`-equivalent fn (minimal slice: scaled-token collateral + debt positions) in the core, mirroring verification.py:152's assertion contract (scaledBalanceOf + getPreviousIndex equality at block_number).
2. Wired into the JGQHBX drive harness as a per-chunk verification step (touched users, chunk_end block). Mismatches emit named divergences (user/asset/position_id/expected-vs-actual) bisect-able like the compare divergences.
3. **Validation**: re-drive past 16596000 with the gate ACTIVE. The gate MUST surface the 44JTVN divergence (the current crash) + any masked wrong balances (NMWPI6/3MF5QM-class) as named divergences BEFORE they would have crashed — proving the gate catches what the crash-gate cannot. If the gate surfaces the NMWPI6/3MF5QM-class masked bugs that are ALREADY fixed, that confirms the gate's detection power (the fixes mean the gate passes for those now; the test is that the gate WOULD have caught them pre-fix — add a red test that reverts a fix + shows the gate catches it).
4. The gate, once active, makes the re-drive a VALUE-CORRECTNESS gate — "reaches 16596000 cleanly" now means "no position mismatches vs on-chain truth at any committed chunk," not just "no crash."

## Sequencing + HLYWI6 strategy change

- This task → HLYWI6 (BE474R's full version, BE474R, stays post-HLYWI6 as the market-wide + stk_aave/gho_discount + config-getter hardening follow-up).
- **HLYWI6's gate UPDATED**: clearing HLYWI6 now requires the re-drive to tip with the value-correctness gate ACTIVE + GREEN (no position mismatches), not just crash-free + Python-parity. The (ii)-slice (this task) is what makes the cold-boot path past the Python ref's crash (16496792) VALIDATABLE — without it, "GREEN to tip" was green-on-garbage.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT build the stk_aave + gho_discount verification (secondary slice, follow-up).
- Do NOT build the market-wide verify or the multicall3 batching (BE474R-full, post-HLYWI6).
- Do NOT add the `verify_chunk: bool` flag to `run_aave_update`'s public API (production follow-up; the harness-level wiring is sufficient for this task).
- Do NOT fix 44JTVN directly — the gate is the tool to surface it (+ other masked bugs) as named divergences; root-cause each the gate surfaces (the 44JTVN classification question informs the fix once the gate names the diverging user/asset).

data.title: Python CLI: unify verify args (pool verify-chunk default on + verify-all/interval; aave delete verify-block + backup-interval, repurpose verify-all)
data.body:
## Goal
- `src/degenbot/cli/pool.py pool_update`: replace `--verify/--no-verify` with `--verify-chunk/--no-verify-chunk` (default TRUE), add `--verify-all/--no-verify-all` (default FALSE) + `--verify-all-interval` (default 1_000_000, envvar `DEGENBOT_VERIFY_ALL_INTERVAL`, show_envvar). Keep `--verify` as a hidden deprecated alias mapping to verify_chunk.
- `src/degenbot/cli/aave/commands.py aave_update`: delete `--verify-block`; keep `--verify-chunk` (default TRUE); repurpose `--verify-all` (default FALSE) to map to BOTH interval + completion (verify_all_interval + verify_all_at_completion); add `--verify-all-interval` (default 1_000_000, envvar `DEGENBOT_VERIFY_ALL_INTERVAL`); delete `--backup-interval` (backup is completion-only now); keep `--backup` (runs after the completion verify when on).
- Wire all new Rust params through the `run_pool_update` / `run_aave_update` Python calls.
- Aave post-run: DROP the redundant post-run `rs_verify_all_positions_on_chain` (Rust now runs the completion full-verify pre-commit — stronger). KEEP the post-run `rs_cleanup_zero_balance_positions` + the `--backup` backup (writes that don't belong on the pre-commit verify tx).
- Update docstrings to be honest; remove all "not honored by the Rust core" / "not supported" warnings for the surviving flags.

## Context
- Depends on: 5AI7WL (PyO3 seam exposes the new params) and YWEUIR (Rust behavior).
- Resolves the cutover-loss: aave's old mid-loop interval verify+backup interleaving was lost in the Rust cutover (commands.py docstring at ~line 240 admits it). We RESTORE the interval verify (mid-loop, pre-commit, in Rust) but keep backup completion-only (a backup mid-loop on a possibly-rolled-back chunk isn't useful).
- The per-chunk touched verify stays default-ON for both updaters (the existing aave behavior is the target for pool).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pool update --help` shows: verify-chunk (default on), verify-all (default off), verify-all-interval (default 1,000,000, envvar). `--verify` still accepted as alias.
- `aave update --help` shows: verify-chunk (default on), verify-all (default off), verify-all-interval (default 1,000,000, envvar), backup. NO verify-block, NO backup-interval.
- `--backup` still backs up at completion (aave) when on.
- No "not supported by the Rust core" warnings remain for surviving flags.
- Envvars honored.
- `aave update-py` (legacy) unchanged (it has its own verify flags).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (any CLI tests); `just lint`; `just test-all`.

## Completion
- Pool pool update: --verify/--no-verify renamed to --verify-chunk/--no-verify-chunk (default ON, was OFF); --verify kept as hidden deprecated alias (--no-verify too). Added --verify-all/--no-verify-all (default OFF) + --verify-all-interval (default 1_000_000, envvar DEGENBOT_VERIFY_ALL_INTERVAL). Wires to Rust seam verify_all_interval (None when --verify-all is off; the interval when on) + verify_all_at_completion (= verify_all).

Repurposed --verify-all (default OFF, was ON+post-run) to wire the Rust pre-commit FULL gate (verify_all_interval + verify_all_at_completion). Cleanup runs unconditionally.
